The templates ruling and the 9 October afternoon ruling block only the INS dashboard's summary information: the INS home's 'Create new' and the type question go ahead on today's INS home.

The older end-to-end traces show the earlier start, where the dashboard's create button posted to /live-animals/notifications and landed on the new notification's origin page with no type question (trace-e2e-p4-001, trace-animals-fit-p5-001).

requirements.statement: The notification type page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' and the heading 'What are you importing?' set as the radios' fieldset legend (h1), with the caption 'About the consignment' inside the heading.
requirements.why: The target design's copy for the page.

requirements.statement: The notification type question offers radio options in this order, with no hint text and none pre-selected on a new start: Live animals; Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos); Plants for planting; Potatoes (seed and ware); Wood products. Live animals continues to the animals frontend's live-animals start, which creates the GBN-AG draft with the live-animals category and lands on its origin page. Germinal products continues to the start of the germinal products set, the live-animals set's sibling in the animals frontend, which creates its own GBN-AG draft with the germinal products category and lands on that set's origin page. Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products continue to the start of the high-risk plants journey in trade-imports-plants-frontend, which creates a plants draft in that service's own reference format and lands on plants' own first page.
requirements.why: The target design's options and order, with each type sent to the real service or set that takes it: the real services split journeys by type, each creating its own draft and reference (c-007). The 9 October ruling offers Germinal products second and makes it start the germinal products set, each set passing its category when it creates the draft, and lets the link land ahead of the set. The templates ruling gives plants the same entry from the INS type question.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the question offers four options, Live animals, Plants for planting, Potatoes (seed and ware) and Wood products, with no Germinal products option and no hints, each option already sent to its own service (repo-tests-p14-043, repo-tests-p14-044, repo-tests-p14-046, repo-tests-p14-095), so only the Germinal products option and its place second in the list are added.

requirements.statement: Answering No to the region of origin code question clears any saved region code, so the notification view shows 'Not applicable' for it and answering Yes again offers an empty box.
requirements.why: The target design drops the code when the user says there is none.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-034 and repo-tests-p1-038 show No clearing the saved code, the view showing it as not applicable and Yes offering an empty box; the older traces show the code kept and still shown on review (trace-animals-fit-p5-048, trace-animals-fit-p5-049).

requirements.statement: The region of origin code question may be left unanswered on save; only an answer other than Yes or No is refused, with 'Select a valid option'.
requirements.why: The target design defines no missing-answer error, and the V4 data page makes the region of origin code requirement mandatory to submit rather than mandatory to proceed, so neither save button refuses a blank answer to it; the invalid-option check is server validation the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p5-046 shows an unanswered region question saving, repo-frontend-p8-030 the No branch moving on with an empty box, and repo-frontend-p8-042 the default option message for anything that is neither yes nor no.

requirements.statement: The origin page has an optional free-text field labelled 'Your internal reference for this consignment (optional)' (medium label): any characters are accepted, it is trimmed, saved and shown back, and left blank it saves nothing.
requirements.why: The target design and today agree, and the V4 data page makes the internal reference number an optional reference the trader enters for the consignment.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p4-042 and trace-animals-fit-p5-045 show the label and the free-text behaviour, repo-frontend-p8-037 the label in the page's copy and repo-frontend-p8-040 the punctuation saved as typed.

requirements.statement: The internal reference hint reads 'Enter any internal reference you want to use to identify this consignment, or leave blank.'
requirements.why: The target design's hint. The 58-character limit stays enforced by the server, which names it in its error.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-037 and repo-tests-p1-028 show the hint ending at 'or leave blank.' today; the older traces show it carrying the extra sentence 'It can be up to 58 characters.' (trace-e2e-p4-043, trace-animals-fit-p5-028).

requirements.statement: An internal reference over 58 characters is refused with 'Internal reference must be 58 characters or less', keeping the typed value and focusing the field from the summary link.
requirements.why: The length limit is a real validation constraint the prototype cannot express, and the V4 data page gives the internal reference number as at most 58 characters.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p5-069 shows the refusal and repo-frontend-p8-038 holds the message and the focus behaviour today.

requirements.statement: The origin page in the live-animals and germinal products sets ends with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button that saves before going to the overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that reaches the overview even on a notification with no answers.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled (inc-161, rule b) that pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls; the origin page is one of them, so that judgement overrides Design Release 2.1's single button. With nothing missing or invalid, Save and return to overview saves the answers and shows the overview, as the 26 October ruling says.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page ends with Save and continue alone, with no secondary button and no link at all (repo-frontend-p8-043, repo-tests-p1-029); the older end-to-end trace shows all three controls (trace-e2e-p4-046, trace-animals-fit-p5-033, trace-animals-fit-p5-035).
requirements.blockedBy: The EUDPA-774 save and continue work merges to the animals frontend's main, which the 10 November ruling makes the condition for the return links; until then the origin page's exits stay as they are.

requirements.statement: A valid origin page with a country continues to the commodity page 'What are you importing?' in the opening run; opened from the overview it returns to the overview.
requirements.why: The target design and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p4-048 and trace-e2e-p4-054-m1 show both routes, repo-frontend-p8-044 the commodity page after a valid save, and repo-tests-p14-062 the same from a notification started at the type question.

requirements.statement: A refused origin save is not stored: the server answers 400 and re-shows the page with an error summary titled 'There is a problem' (an alert, after the Draft strip and before the heading), inline errors prefixed with a visually hidden 'Error:', and what the user entered.
requirements.why: Not storing answers that fail validation is a real persistence and validation constraint; the prototype stores the country and region answer before validating. The 26 October ruling keeps what the trader entered on the page when an answer is missing or not valid.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-051 and trace-animals-fit-p5-061 show the 400 re-render with nothing saved, and repo-frontend-p8-052 with repo-tests-p1-035 the other answers kept.

requirements.statement: The type and origin pages have an accessible build where the prototype's markup falls short: the browser title gains 'Error: ' in an error state, the country control has a real 'Country of origin' label and is an accessible-autocomplete over a native select that works without JavaScript, and the region code input is linked to its hint and error and takes the error style. Within that build the visible copy follows the design (no hint, the 'Search for a country' placeholder), while opening, matching, the arrow and the announcements are the component's own as the real frontend configures it.
requirements.why: Accessibility and no-JavaScript use are duties a live GOV.UK service must meet and the prototype need not, so they are a real constraint that overrides the prototype only as far as that duty (c-006). The afternoon ruling sets the search box: the real frontend's component, with only how the list reads following the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p4-039 and trace-animals-fit-p6-036 show the 'Error: ' title prefix and the no-JavaScript select, repo-frontend-p8-058 the plain select submitting the code, repo-tests-p1-047 the region code box named by its label and described by its hint, repo-tests-p14-053 and repo-insfrontend-p3-015 the 'Error: ' title on the type question, and repo-insfrontend-p3-043 the type question clear of serious and critical accessibility violations.

requirements.statement: The origin form is a server-validated POST (novalidate) carrying a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token, and a failed save re-shows the page with the entered values and a recoverable-error message (HTTP 500).
requirements.why: Real security, concurrency and persistence constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p4-056 and repo-frontend-p8-054 show the crumb and concurrency token on the form, and repo-frontend-p8-053 the recoverable-error re-render when the save fails.

requirements.statement: The three origin questions (country label, region code legend, internal reference label) are set at the same medium size, and the revealed region code box's own label is one step smaller.
requirements.why: The target design and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p5-030 and trace-animals-fit-p5-031 render the three questions at medium size with the revealed box's label smaller; the prototype sets them with its own medium class (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-072).

requirements.statement: Every English string on the type and origin pages has its Welsh counterpart, with no key missing or extra, in the animals frontend, the germinal products set, the INS front door's type question and the plants frontend.
requirements.why: The real origin pages keep Welsh copy for every English key, and plants reuses the same bundle shape, so each copy change carries its Welsh with it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals origin bundle's Welsh covers every English string (repo-frontend-p8-060), the plants bundles hold the same keys at every leaf (repo-plantsfrontend-p5-067) and the INS type question has Welsh for its title, caption, options, error and button (repo-insfrontend-p3-040), all machine drafts awaiting Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo-frontend-p8-061, repo-plantsfrontend-p5-066, repo-insfrontend-p3-041); no germinal products set exists yet, and the new Germinal products option has no Welsh, so each new or changed string takes its Welsh with it.

requirements.statement: The origin page's full-page visual baseline (origin-of-import.png) matches the page as built, its copy included.
requirements.why: The end-to-end suite holds the origin page to a stored image, which every copy change alters.
requirements.deltaNote: The baseline in the trace is the earlier page, with the country hint and an empty box and no placeholder (trace-e2e-p4-060, trace-e2e-p4-061), and the image itself is not in the trace (trace-e2e-p4-133), so each copy row refreshes it.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: a non-live-animals notification type running through the live-animals origin and commodity pages with a GBN-AG reference.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 every type falls through to the live-animals pages, which render live-animals content and offer nothing to pick for plants; that is a prototype shortcut, not a design for those types. Each type goes to its own set or service from the notification type question: germinal products to its own sibling set (9 October ruling), the plants types to the plants service.

requirements.statement: The reference data service serves GET /countries: a JSON array of code (MDM effectiveAlpha2), name (effectiveAlias) and subDivisions (code and name), sorted by name, with the United Kingdom always removed and, when blocks is given, only countries whose matching MDM block has includeCountry true.
requirements.why: The country list the origin page offers comes from this endpoint; it already does what the journey needs, and the list content stays MDM's.
requirements.deltaNote: The reference data service already serves GET /countries this way (the reference-lists area's working set holds the repo-referencedata claims that prove it, repo-referencedata-p1-073 among them); this area's evidence is the 9 October ruling that countries already come from real MDM through the service.

requirements.statement: The reference data service reads countries from MDM's geography list for the GBNAG system, with the platform subscription key and a client-credentials bearer token reused until it expires.
requirements.why: The MDM integration behind the country list already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: The reference data service already reads MDM's GBNAG geography list this way (repo-referencedata-p1-068, in the reference-lists area's working set); this area's evidence is the 9 October ruling that countries already come from real MDM through the service.

requirements.statement: The reference data service caches MDM countries per blocks value (and ports) in memory for 60 minutes by default, at most 20 entries, and never caches an empty result.
requirements.why: Existing behaviour that limits calls to MDM.
requirements.deltaNote: The reference data service already caches countries this way (repo-referencedata-p1-075 and repo-referencedata-p1-076, in the reference-lists area's working set).

requirements.statement: The reference data service answers an empty MDM countries result with an empty list, and any unexpected failure (including a failed MDM call) with a 500 RFC 7807 problem body carrying the trace id.
requirements.why: Existing error behaviour behind the country list.
requirements.deltaNote: The reference data service already answers this way (repo-referencedata-p1-071 and repo-referencedata-p1-081, in the reference-lists area's working set).

requirements.statement: The reference data service stays the shared home for MDM-sourced reference domains (ADR 0002), serving countries and ports of entry on port 8086 with per-endpoint response-time and external-call metrics.
requirements.why: Existing ruling and operation of the service; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: ADR 0002 already records countries as a managed MDM domain (repo-referencedata-p1-083 and repo-referencedata-p1-084, in the reference-lists area's working set).

requirements.statement: Out of scope: adding commodity, species, commodity identifier, transporter, document type or certification purpose lists to the reference data service, or documenting its endpoints in its README.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for no change to where those lists are served, and nothing in this area needs them in the reference data service.

requirements.statement: The commodity page has the browser title 'What are you importing? - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the caption 'About the consignment' above the heading 'What are you importing?', the Draft tag and notification reference above the caption, and a search field labelled 'Search for a commodity' as a medium label, built from GOV.UK Frontend components in a two-thirds column.
requirements.why: The page's frame already matches Design Release 2.1 and must stay as it is while the rest of the page changes. Where the prototype styles the heading, caption and label with its own classes, the real page's GOV.UK classes give the same look.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-004, -p9-005 and -p9-008 hold the same heading, caption slot and label, repo-tests-p1-111 proves the heading is also the overview task row's name, and trace-animals-fit-p8-003 to -p8-008, -p8-058 and -p8-058-m1 show the title, the Draft strip, the GOV.UK components and the two-thirds column; repo-frontend-p9-006 records that the caption's words come from the journey flow's section copy rather than from this feature.

requirements.statement: The commodity page's inset text, directly under the heading, reads 'You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need a health certificate.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the one-notification-per-certificate rule in terms of the health certificate, having set its earlier ITAHC wording aside, and no DR1 judgement or real constraint covers the inset, so the prototype wins by default. The prototype's 'an health certificate' is a typing slip in the article and is written 'a health certificate'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the inset reads 'You must submit a separate notification for every single ITAHC. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an ITAHC.' (repo-frontend-p9-007, repo-tests-p1-114). trace-animals-fit-p8-007 and trace-e2e-p5-005 captured an earlier health-certificate wording.

requirements.statement: On a live-animals notification the commodity search hint reads 'You can search by common name (for example, cattle), commodity code (0102), or Latin name (Bos taurus).', with no 'Enter at least 3 characters.' sentence.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording wins by default; DR1 left the hint wording unruled, and the reason the frontend departed from it (no common names in the data) no longer holds, since 'cattle' now finds cattle species. The germinal set's own hint ('You can search for semen, ova or embryos, ...') is the germinal-products area's requirement; it is cited here only to show the live-animals hint is the live set's alone.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-009 holds exactly this hint in the copy file and repo-tests-p1-113 proves it end to end; trace-animals-fit-p8-009 and trace-e2e-p5-007 captured the earlier commodity-name wording with 'Enter at least 3 characters.' before it changed (c-374).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the 'What are you importing?' page shows the same title, caption, heading, label, buttons, Cancel link and back link (to the origin page) as the live-animals page, including the inset 'You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an health certificate.'; its search hint reads 'You can search for semen, ova or embryos, or by common name (for example, cattle), Latin name (Bos taurus) or commodity code (05119985).', and continuing with nothing selected shows 'Select a commodity' in the error summary.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a trader importing germinal products what they can search for, and changes nothing else on the page. The 9 October afternoon ruling lets the germinal set's copy of today's commodity page, with this hint, go ahead on today's commodity data; its errors are the live-animal page's, which the germinal specs show as 'Select a commodity'.
requirements.deltaNote: The real animals frontend has no germinal products set today.

requirements.statement: A closed 'Help with commodity codes' details component below the search explains 'Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers.' and 'A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.', and links to the Trade Tariff tool at https://www.gov.uk/trade-tariff in a new tab with rel 'noreferrer noopener'.
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their commodity code need a way to look it up; the service links out to the tool rather than embedding it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-056, -p9-057 and -p9-106 hold both paragraphs and the new-tab Trade Tariff link with its rel, and repo-tests-p1-115 proves them end to end.

requirements.statement: In the commodity code help, '(opens in a new tab)' sits on its own line after the words 'Trade Tariff tool' and is part of the link, so the link's accessible name is 'Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 breaks the line before '(opens in a new tab)'; keeping the words inside the link keeps the link's purpose announced, as GOV.UK guidance and the page's accessibility check require, an accessibility constraint the prototype's layout does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-057 records that the template breaks the line before '(opens in a new tab)' and keeps it inside the link, whose accessible name repo-frontend-p9-106 and repo-tests-p1-115 read as 'Trade Tariff tool (opens in a new tab)'.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, typing in the commodity search lists the matching species in place, with no Search press and no page change, fetched from the commodity search page's own results address, which is guarded exactly as the page is; the results list and the chosen panel are rendered by one shared piece of markup, so a live refresh and a full page load show the same thing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds commodities as the trader types, and the real frontend does the same behind a component that still works without JavaScript. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 'Add a search type-ahead for choosing commodities, reusable across the journey' owns it, with the germinal catalogue it searches owned by EUDPA-569 'Germinal | Commodity search' (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-058, -p9-059 and -p9-100 to -p9-102 show the as-you-type list, its own results address and the shared markup on the page now; trace-animals-fit-p8-059 captured the earlier search-on-button-press behaviour (c-374).

requirements.statement: A visually hidden polite live region announces how many species a typed search lists, counting species rather than commodity headings, reading '3 results available' for three and '1 result available' for one, and 'No results found' when none match, and announces nothing while the typed search is shorter than three characters.
requirements.why: Results that change as the trader types must be announced to screen reader users. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 owns the commodity type-ahead and EUDPA-569 the germinal catalogue it searches (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-060 and -p9-061 hold the species count announcement, its singular form, its no-results form and the silence below three characters; trace-e2e-p5-020 captured the earlier server-written panel with no live region (c-374).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, ticking a species adds it to the chosen panel at once with focus left on the tick box, the typed search text and its results stay on screen so more species can be ticked, and removing one chosen species or clearing them all updates the page in place and puts focus back in the search box with the typed text still there.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader tick several species from one search without losing the search or the selection. Built outside this programme: EUDPA-616 owns the commodity type-ahead and EUDPA-569 the germinal catalogue it searches (ruling 10 November), so the waiting-on-design row inc-014 is dropped.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-064 and -p9-065 show the tick, the kept search text and the in-place update with focus returned to the search box; trace-animals-fit-p8-019 captured the earlier server round trip (c-374).

requirements.statement: Search results list commodities alphabetically by commodity name, and the species under each alphabetically by their label ('common name (Latin name)', or 'commodity name (Latin name)' where a species has no common name), ignoring case and accents.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sorts results so a trader can scan them, for example 'cattle' lists African buffalo first and Yak last. How a list reads, its order included, follows the prototype, and a reference list is never a reason to block a row (ruling 11 November), so the order is not held back by the commodity list's content. The reference service returns groups and species in MDM's own order, so the order is the frontend's to set.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the groups run in ascending commodity-code order and the species inside a group in ascending species-label order (repo-frontend-p9-019, -p9-103, repo-tests-p1-117), over results the reference service returns in MDM's order (repo-referencedata-p2-023).

requirements.statement: In the search results the text that matched the query is shown in bold, in both the commodity header and the species labels (for example 'Domestic **cattle** (Bos taurus)'), with the labels escaped as text before the bold is applied.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the trader why each result matched; escaping the label first means a label always shows as text and can never inject markup.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-023 bolds each matched run in the commodity heading and the species label after escaping them (-p9-111), repo-tests-p1-119 proves it end to end including a match inside the common name, and ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-039 records that the commodities half of the bold-letters row is already on main; trace-animals-fit-p8-022 captured the earlier plain labels (c-374).

requirements.statement: Search results are grouped under a header naming the commodity and its code ('Cattle (0102)'), falling back to the bare code where no name is held for it; the header cannot be ticked, each species under it is a small GOV.UK checkbox, and a query that matches a commodity's code lists every species of that commodity.
requirements.why: Traders pick species, grouped by the commodity they belong to, rather than a whole commodity.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-017 and -p9-018 and repo-tests-p1-118 show grouping under '<name> (<code>)' with the bare-code fallback and a checkbox per species, and repo-referencedata-p2-013 and -p2-067 the whole commodity's species listed for a code search.

requirements.statement: The commodity search matches a species' common name anywhere inside it, its Latin name and a commodity's code, so 'horse' finds the horse species under Horse (0101) and 'ferret' finds both Ferret (Mustela putorius furo) and the weasels whose common name includes ferrets, and a species that sits under two commodity codes is offered once under each as two separate choices.
requirements.why: The hint promises search by common name, commodity code and Latin name, and a species may be importable under more than one commodity.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-021, -p9-022, -p9-104 and -p9-105 show matching on common name, Latin name and commodity code and one species listed under each of two codes, repo-referencedata-p2-019 and -p2-020 the de-duplication by code and Latin name, and repo-tests-p1-117 proves the result set for the queries 0102, cattle, horse, domestic cat and ostrich.

requirements.statement: A search of three or more characters that matches nothing says 'No results found' and lists no checkboxes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not show a no-match state; the real service's message stays so a trader is not left with a blank page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-024 and repo-tests-p1-120 show 'No results found' for a query of three or more characters that matches nothing, and repo-frontend-p9-013 that a shorter query shows no message at all.

requirements.statement: The selected panel lists each chosen commodity, in commodity-code order and each once, as a bold 'Commodity (code):' line followed by one chip per chosen species, the chip reading 'common name (Latin name)' where the species has a common name (for example 'Cattle (0102):' then 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)') and the Latin name alone where it has none.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows what has been chosen as removable chips that name the species the way the trader found it. Where the prototype shows a chip with the Latin name alone, it is because its demo entry carries no common name, which the real list's own entries decide.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each chip carries the Latin name alone, for example 'Bos taurus' (repo-frontend-p9-028, repo-tests-p1-126); the bold commodity line with its colon and the commodity-code order already hold (repo-frontend-p9-113). trace-animals-fit-p8-032 captured an earlier comma-separated 'Common name (Latin name)' text (c-374).

requirements.statement: Each species chip in the selected panel has a remove button with no visible text whose accessible name is 'Remove ' followed by the chip's label (for example 'Remove Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', or 'Remove Sus scrofa domesticus' for a species with no common name), which takes that one species out of the selection and leaves every other choice chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader drop one choice without clearing everything or finding it again in the results, and names the control by the chip it removes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the control's accessible name reads 'Remove <Latin name> from <commodity label>', for example 'Remove Bos taurus from Cattle (0102)' (repo-frontend-p9-029, repo-tests-p1-126); the per-species removal itself already works (repo-frontend-p9-033, repo-tests-p1-127).

requirements.statement: Once something is chosen, the selected panel is headed '<N> selected' and has a 'Clear all' button that empties the selection without saving anything, leaving the current results on screen unticked; with nothing chosen the panel is hidden, with no count, no empty-state sentence and no Clear all.
requirements.why: The trader sees how many species they have chosen and can start again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-027, -p9-030, -p9-031 and repo-tests-p1-122 show the '<N> selected' heading, the Clear all that empties the panel without saving, and no panel at all while nothing is chosen; repo-frontend-p9-032 records that no empty-state wording exists and trace-e2e-p5-023-m1 that the results stay listed, unticked.

requirements.statement: Species from several commodities can be chosen on one notification by searching again: choices made under an earlier search stay in the selection and are all saved together.
requirements.why: A consignment can hold several commodities.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-036 and -p9-038 carry off-screen choices forward and save them together, and repo-tests-p1-121 proves species found under different searches are chosen together and saved.

requirements.statement: Reopening the commodity page shows the species already saved on the notification as chosen in the selected panel, and ticked when a search brings them back (posted once, not also as a hidden choice), while the same Latin name under another commodity code shows unticked.
requirements.why: A trader returning to change their commodities starts from what they saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-042 and -p9-098 show the saved species as the chosen ones with their count, and -p9-025 shows them ticked in results while the same Latin name under another code stays unticked.

requirements.statement: Pressing Save and continue with nothing chosen shows 'Select a commodity' in the error summary and inline on the search field, between its label and hint, as the only error, and the summary link moves focus to the search field, whose description then reads the hint followed by 'Error: Select a commodity', whether or not search results are on screen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 always ties the error to the search field, the control the trader uses to choose, and the specification makes the commodity and species mandatory to proceed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-045 and repo-tests-p1-124 show the error staying on the search box with results on screen and being the only error shown, repo-frontend-p9-044 and repo-tests-p1-123 the summary link moving focus there and the description, and -p9-066 that a save pressed straight after Clear all is refused the same way.

requirements.statement: When the commodity page or the Commodity details page shows an error, the browser title is prefixed 'Error: '.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern announces the error in the title; Design Release 2.1 omits it because the prototype does not model real validation.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p8-047 and trace-e2e-p5-029 show the 'Error: ' title prefix on the commodity page today; the Commodity details page's own evidence sits with that page's area.

requirements.statement: After a valid choice on the commodity page, Save and continue goes to the main import reason page; opened from the overview or check answers it returns there instead.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the reason for import comes between the commodity choice and its details.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-050 lands Save and continue on the import reason page; trace-animals-fit-p8-037 and trace-e2e-p5-030 captured the earlier hop straight to Commodity details (c-374).

requirements.statement: On the commodity page 'Save and return to overview' makes the same checks as 'Save and continue': with no species chosen it shows 'Select a commodity' in the error summary and inline on the search field and keeps the trader on the page with the query they typed still in the box and the selection saved before untouched, and with at least one species chosen it saves the selection and goes to the notification overview.
requirements.why: Ruling 26 October makes the two save buttons behave the same on every page that has both, with no page an exception, and ruling 27 November keeps that default in live animals, the germinal copy and plants, so the commodity page refuses an empty selection whichever button is pressed, a trader never loses what they typed, and a valid selection saves and returns to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-125 proves the empty-selection check already runs on 'Save and return to overview', holding the trader on the page with the earlier selection intact, repo-frontend-p9-097 the valid save returning to the overview, and ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-012 records that both save buttons already make the same checks.

requirements.statement: The commodity page's back link goes to the origin of the import page when the trader reached it from there, for live animals and germinal products, to the page that opened the commodity question when one did, and to the notification overview when the overview sent them.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the commodity page is the step after the origin page, and the prototype's own fallback returns to wherever else the page was opened from.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-095 shows the origin page's Save and continue leading to the commodity page and -p9-054 the back link going to the opener or following the journey trail, so in the journey it returns to the origin page and from the overview to the overview; trace-animals-fit-p8-043 and trace-e2e-p5-034 captured the earlier overview-only back link (c-374).

requirements.statement: The commodity page and the Commodity details page each end with a primary 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification overview, in that order.
requirements.why: Both pages are tasks the overview links to, so under DR1's rule (b) they end with the three return controls, as Design Release 2.1 shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-055 shows all three controls in that order on the commodity page today, and trace-e2e-p5-033 the same three on Commodity details.

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating a template, a valid Save and continue on the commodity page goes to the notification overview.
requirements.why: Out of scope: templates are parked. Ruling 4 November de-prioritises templates and leaves their rows in the parked type-question-and-templates theme, and the interaction designer's 9 November answers record that templates have been dropped for now, so no template behaviour is built on the commodity page in this programme.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search offers only germinal-product commodities, so it never offers a live-animal commodity.
requirements.why: Each set holds one category, so a consignment mixing live animals and germinal products is never written, and the germinal set's own pages and search are not blocked on MDM. Taking today's germinal lines out of the live-animals catalogue is not this programme's work: ruling 10 November puts that in the separate commodity-search ticket's hands, which req-1754 records.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no germinal set today and its search does not exist; the 12 germinal lines it offers are the ones the live-animals commodity catalogue holds (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-026). Taking those lines out of the live-animals catalogue is the separate commodity-search ticket's work (req-1754).

requirements.statement: The germinal products catalogue holds the 12 specified germinal commodities, with embryos and ova as separate items: Cattle, Goat, Horse, Pig and Sheep each as '<Animal>, Embryos' and '<Animal>, Ova' (05119985); and '<Animal>, Semen' for Cattle (05111000), Cat, Dog, Goat, Horse, Pig, Rabbit/Rodent and Sheep (05119985): 18 items, sorted by name, codes shown with their leading zero. Each item offers the species listed under that animal (Cattle: Bison bison, Bos taurus and Bubalus bubalis, plus Bovidae for semen; Horse: Equus asinus and Equus caballus; Goat: Capra hircus; Pig: Sus scrofa domesticus; Sheep: Ovis aries; Cat: Felis catus; Dog: Canis familiaris; Rabbit/Rodent semen: one row labelled Rabbit/Rodent). There are no poultry, fish, bee, amphibian, arachnid or reptile germinal products and no Cat or Dog embryos or ova.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a commodity catalogue's names, codes, species, search terms and tariff codes are reference-list content, which is MDM's and reaches the service through trade-imports-reference-data, never edited in code and never a reason to block a row (ruling:ian-2026-11-11 points 2 and 3). The germinal catalogue's content therefore leaves the backlog as an MDM concern, exactly as the live-animals catalogue's content already has (req-094 to req-101), and c-282 records the clause that had blocked it. What the data page still decides is which germinal commodities the germinal fields apply to, naming the same twelve entries in all five of its applicability lists, and that is carried by req-121, req-123, req-124 and req-251. The 26 November prototype's Cat and Dog embryos and ova and its new Amphibian, Arachnid and Reptile embryos are mock data the 9 October ruling does not copy, and the data page gives them no fields (c-230). The page writes the codes without their leading zero and never says how they map to the codes a notification carries, which c-340 settles in favour of the eight-digit codes the catalogue and MDM use.

requirements.statement: The live-animal catalogue holds the design's 48 live commodities and their 856 species, live crustaceans and molluscs included, plus four extra commodities that split gamebirds and poultry into day-old chicks and adult birds (Gamebirds: day-old chicks and Gamebirds: adult birds under 01063980, Poultry: day-old chicks and Poultry: adult birds under 0105), each with its written names, search terms and tariff codes.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader notify these animals. Out of scope: this is reference-list content rather than service behaviour. Claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 makes a list's content what MDM serves, never a reason to block a row or edit a list in code, so the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November and the content requests sit in deferred.md as MDM concerns; ruling:ian-2026-11-11 makes that a general rule and bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers. The prototype itself calls its generated names draft wording for research rather than agreed content.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's catalogue is what MDM serves through trade-imports-reference-data (repo-referencedata-p2-055, -p2-056): repo-tests-p1-130 and repo-frontend-p9-093 show Bos taurus and Bison bison on 0102, Equus cabalus and Equus asinus on 0101, Felis catus and Nyctereutes procyonoides on 01061900, Struthio spp. on 01063300 and Gallus gallus on 01051111, with Bubalus bubalis, Capra hircus, Ovis aries, Sus scrofa domesticus and Mustela putorius furo among the frontend's own fixtures.

requirements.statement: Commodity code 0102 is named 'Cattle' wherever it shows: result headers, the selected panel, the Selected commodities table and the Commodity details headings.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity Cattle, and the data fields page's own example names code 0102 Cattle. Out of scope: this is reference-list content rather than service behaviour, which claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09 makes MDM's to change rather than something edited in code, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for it.
requirements.deltaNote: The frontend now names 0102 Cattle: repo-tests-p1-118 reads the group heading as 'Cattle (0102)' and -p1-130 its species as Domestic Cattle, from a name the frontend holds itself; MDM's own description of 0102 is 'Live bovine animals' (repo-referencedata-p2-055), which the commodity heading reads once names come from MDM (c-458). trace-e2e-p5-012 and -p5-045 captured the earlier 'Cow' naming (c-374).

requirements.statement: Cattle (0102) offers 11 species: African buffalo (Syncerus spp.), Banteng (Novibos spp), Bison (Bison spp), Bison bison (Bison bison), Buffalo (Bubalus spp (including Anoa)), Cattle (Bos spp), Domestic cattle (Bos taurus), Gaur (Bibos spp.), Musk ox (Ovibos spp), Water buffalo (Bubalus bubalis) and Yak (Poephagus spp.).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists every bovine species a trader may import under 0102. Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers.
requirements.deltaNote: Today MDM's list for 0102 holds 15 species from Bibos spp. to Syncerus (repo-referencedata-p2-059), and the suites drive Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle) and Bison bison (American Bison) among them (repo-tests-p1-130); the specification's own examples spell Bison bison's common name 'Bison' and Bos taurus's 'Cattle' (confluence-6497338582-p1-091).

requirements.statement: Horse (0101) offers three species: Donkey (Equus asinus), Horse (Equus caballus) and Mule (Eq caballus*asinus).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader notify donkeys and mules as well as horses. Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers.
requirements.deltaNote: 0101 now holds two of the three: repo-tests-p1-130 shows Equus cabalus (Horse) and Equus asinus (Donkey), with no mule, where trace-e2e-p5-013 captured Horse alone (c-374).

requirements.statement: Cat (01061900) offers 'Domestic cat (Felis catus)' and Dog (01061900) offers 'Domestic dog (Canis familiaris)', and the Commodity details rows for them read 'Domestic cat' and 'Domestic dog'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives these species their common names; DR1 left the naming unruled. Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers.
requirements.deltaNote: Felis catus now carries the common name 'Domestic Cat' (repo-tests-p1-130), where trace-e2e-p5-014 captured 'Cat (Felis catus)' and 'Dog (Canis lupus familiaris)'; MDM's 'dog' search answers Raccoon Dog and Dog under 01061900 (repo-referencedata-p2-058) (c-374).

requirements.statement: The live-animal catalogue holds Ferret (01061900, Ferret (Mustela putorius furo)) and Other live mammals (01061900) with the design's species, each with its common name; Ferret, like Cat and Dog, is marked as needing a permanent address and Other live mammals is not, and all four offer the same purposes and 01061900 identifiers.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 covers every live mammal under 01061900, not only cats and dogs. Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers or which commodities a rule covers.
requirements.deltaNote: Ferret has since reached the catalogue: repo-frontend-p9-093 and -p9-105 hold Mustela putorius furo (Ferret) among the species the search offers, and repo-tests-p1-130 shows Nyctereutes procyonoides (Raccoon Dog) as a further 01061900 line, where ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-015 recorded that the catalogue then held no ferret.

requirements.statement: The live-animal catalogue holds no finfish: headings 0301 to 0305 and code 0511.91.90 are left out, as are the dried, salted and smoked crustacean codes 0306.91 to 0306.99, while live crustaceans and molluscs are in.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 now leaves finfish out of the commodity list, ornamental fish included. Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p5-015 and trace-animals-fit-p8-026 captured Fish (0301) with Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar); no fish line appears among the commodity lines the suites now drive (repo-tests-p1-130).

requirements.statement: The horse species reads 'Equus caballus' and the mule 'Eq caballus*asinus'; every other species name, common name and code is exactly as the design's species list gives it.
requirements.why: The backend sends a species' display text, with no code beside it, downstream as the GBN-AG scientificName, so a misspelt Latin name would reach the receiving service as a wrong scientific name: a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express (c-014). Out of scope: reference-list content is MDM's to serve under claim 25 of ruling:sam-2026-10-09, the catalogue row inc-012 was dropped on 3 November, and ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers.
requirements.deltaNote: DR2.1 shows 'Equus cabalus' and 'Eq cabalus*asinus' (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p2-031), and the misspelling has since reached the real catalogue: repo-tests-p1-130 and repo-frontend-p9-093 record the horse line's Latin name as 'Equus cabalus' where trace-e2e-p5-013 captured 'Equus caballus'.

requirements.statement: Saving the commodity choice clears any saved answer to the unweaned animals question when no chosen species is one that question applies to.
requirements.why: A trader must not leave a stale answer on the notification for a question the commodity choice has taken away. Which species the unweaned question applies to is the data specification's to decide rather than the prototype's hard-coded commodity code, because ruling:ian-2026-11-11 bars a row resting on the prototype's own files for which commodities a rule covers.

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page's caption names the Description of the goods section, with the section number the service gives it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts Commodity details in its own section, 'Description of the goods', which also holds identification and additional details, and ruling 17 November keeps the section numbers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-006 and -p10-007 and repo-tests-p1-074 show the Description of the goods caption above the heading now, and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-010 records that no test depends on its number; trace-animals-fit-p9-003 captured the earlier 'About the consignment' caption (c-374).

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page has the title 'Commodity details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', the heading 'Commodity details', the notification status strip above the caption, and an error summary titled 'There is a problem' above the caption and heading when it has errors.
requirements.why: The page's frame already matches Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-005 holds the heading and -p10-058 the service's standard error summary title, and trace-animals-fit-p9-002, -p9-004 and -p9-055 show the heading, the title and the summary above the caption today.

requirements.statement: The Selected commodities table on Commodity details has the columns 'Commodity code', 'Commodity' and 'Species', with a visually hidden 'Actions' column holding each row's Remove control. The Commodity cell holds the commodity's name and the Species cell lists the row's chosen species one per line, each but the last followed by a comma (for example '0102 | Cattle | Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'). The table and the 'Add another commodity' link sit above the questions.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows each commodity's name beside its code, and which of its species was chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the table has 'Commodity code', 'Species' and a visually hidden 'Actions' column, with no column naming the commodity (repo-frontend-p10-010, -p10-011, repo-tests-p1-076); the species one per line with a comma, and the table above the groups, already match (repo-frontend-p10-012, -p10-165, repo-tests-p1-085). The commodity's reference-data name is already available to the page (repo-frontend-p10-015). trace-animals-fit-p9-010 and -p9-011 captured an earlier 'Common name' column (c-374).

requirements.statement: The Selected commodities table has one row per commodity, except for a commodity whose species the commodity list offers individually, where each chosen species has its own row, its Commodity cell naming the commodity and its Species cell that one species. Each row's Remove drops that commodity (or that one species) at once, with no confirmation, returns to Commodity details while anything is left, and goes to the commodity page when the last is removed, leaving the counts saved against the commodities that remain exactly as they were.
requirements.why: A trader can correct the selection from the details page without going back to the search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-018 to -p10-023 and -p10-170 show commodity-level and per-species rows chosen from the commodity list, Remove acting at once with no confirmation, the page coming back while anything is left and the last removal going to the commodity page (-p10-025), -p10-163 the surviving counts kept, and repo-tests-p1-085 the shared row for two species of one code. Each row's Commodity cell comes with the column req-105 adds.

requirements.statement: Below the Selected commodities table an 'Add another commodity' link goes to the commodity page, where the existing selection is still chosen, and saving a further species returns the trader to Commodity details with the quantities already entered kept and the new species' fields empty.
requirements.why: A trader can add a commodity without losing what they have.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-030 to -p10-032 and repo-tests-p1-087 show the link, the kept selection and the kept quantities.

requirements.statement: The Commodity details page's back link goes to the commodity page ('What are you importing?'), in the live-animals and the germinal products sets.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 Commodity details follows on from the commodity choice, and its back link goes there rather than to the reason page that precedes it in the step order.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page's back link returns the trader to the overview the hub task came from (repo-frontend-p10-008, trace-animals-fit-p9-007, -p9-008).

requirements.statement: Opening Commodity details with no commodity on the notification sends the trader to the commodity page.
requirements.why: With nothing chosen the page has nothing to ask; the real service must not show an empty details page from Back, a refresh or a bookmark.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-024 redirects to the commodity question when nothing is selected, and -p10-025 shows the same on reopening after the last removal.

requirements.statement: Commodity details groups the questions under an h2 per commodity, '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)' (for example 'Horse (0101)'), and an h3 per chosen species naming it, with the type stepping down from the commodity heading to the species heading to the field labels, a section break between commodity groups and none above the save buttons.
requirements.why: A trader with several commodities sees which commodity and species each question is about, named as Design Release 2.1 names them.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each group's h2 is the bare commodity code with no name beside it (repo-frontend-p10-033); the species sub-heading, the type steps and the one visible section break per group already match (repo-frontend-p10-034, -p10-035, -p10-036). trace-animals-fit-p9-021 and -p9-022 captured an earlier '<common name> (<code>)' heading per species (c-374). How the species is named is the species label requirement's.

requirements.statement: Each live-animal species asks 'Number of animals' in a numeric text field with no hint; it is required ('Enter the number of animals') and must be a whole number of 1 or more ('Enter a whole number greater than 0'), each error shown in the summary and above that species' field and linked to it.
requirements.why: The number of animals is needed for every live-animal species, and Design Release 2.1 and the real service ask it the same way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-037, -p10-038, -p10-041, -p10-043, -p10-044 and -p10-169 hold the label, the empty description, the required rule and both messages, and repo-tests-p1-075 and -p1-083 prove them end to end.

requirements.statement: 'Number of packages (when required)', hinted 'Such as crates, bags or boxes', is asked for a chosen species only where the data fields page's package-count list names its commodity. That list covers bees; birds of prey (owls, falcons and other); cats; cattle; dogs; embryos or ova of cattle, goats, horses, sheep and pigs; ferrets; game birds (adult and day-old partridge and pheasant, and pheasant and partridge hatching eggs); goats; horses and donkeys; insects and other invertebrates, including the Asian hornet; domestic pigs and pig meat under safeguard measure; poultry (adult and day-old chickens, ducks, geese, turkeys and guinea fowl, and chicken, turkey, goose, duck and guinea fowl hatching eggs); psittaciformes, including parrots, parakeets, macaws and cockatoos; domestic European rabbits and other domestic rabbits; reptiles; rodents; semen of cattle, dogs or cats, horses, goats, pigs, rodents or rabbits and sheep; domestic sheep; and SPF eggs. A species whose commodity is not on that list is asked only for the number of animals.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals data fields page is the specification for which commodity codes each conditional rule covers, and ruling 11 November ranks it above Design Release 2.1's demo commodity data on that; Design Release 2.1 still gives the field its label and its hint. A reference list is never a reason to block a row, so the question's coverage is not held back by the commodity list's content.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the question is shown for the commodity codes the frontend's own applicability rules name, read from its commodity service rather than from the specification's list, and a code they do not cover is asked for the number of animals alone (repo-frontend-p10-039, -p10-040, -p10-060, -p10-167: Bos taurus asked, ostrich not). Design Release 2.1 asks it of nine curated commodities only, which c-459 sets aside. Nothing in the end-to-end suite yet asserts the hint or the field's coverage (repo-tests-p1-089).

requirements.statement: For live animals the number of packages is optional, but when given must be a whole number of 1 or more, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number, like 5'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 makes the field optional; the real service still validates what it stores, a constraint the prototype does not model.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-042 takes no required message for the field, and -p10-047 and -p10-168 refuse a non-whole number and anything below one with the same message, which repo-tests-p1-083 proves end to end.

requirements.statement: On the live-animals set the Commodity details error summary lists errors by question, all species for one question before the next: every number of animals error, then every number of packages error.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 orders the error summary by field type. Ruling 2026-10-09 splits this requirement per set and drops the mixed-load ordering, because a set holds one category; the germinal set's order is its own requirement.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-050 and repo-tests-p1-084-m1 list every number of animals error before any number of packages error now; trace-animals-fit-p9-057-m1 captured the earlier page-order listing (c-374).

requirements.statement: A species line that holds animal identifier records cannot be saved with a number of animals lower than the number of records: the error reads 'You have <N> identifier record(s) for <species> but entered <M> animal(s). Remove identifier records or keep the higher count.', singularised for one, shown against that species' number of animals field, its summary link going to that line's identification card, and checked only once every field-level check has passed.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the frontend is right to refuse a lowered count rather than orphan identifier records silently.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-054 to -p10-059 and -p10-058-m1 hold the message, its singular forms, the rule's conditions, the inline error, the link to the species' identification card and the walk that removes a record and carries on.

requirements.statement: Commodity details fills each field with the quantity already saved, and after a validation error re-shows the page with every entered value kept, trimmed of surrounding spaces, each summary link moving focus to its own field.
requirements.why: A trader never retypes what they entered; ruling 26 October keeps what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-062 pre-fills the stored counts, -p10-051, -p10-052 and -p10-053 keep what was typed on a refused save and move focus to the named field, and -p10-061 trims the values before they are checked and stored.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, reached in the journey from the main import reason page, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details goes to Identification details when any chosen species needs identifiers, otherwise to Additional details when that page applies, otherwise to the arrival details; opened from its overview task it returns to the overview.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 Commodity details is a step of the journey that leads on to the next one; ruling 2026-10-09 keeps a page opened from its overview task returning to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-066 sends a saved page to the next page the journey puts after it and -p10-065 shows that next page as Identification details; trace-animals-fit-p9-035 captured the earlier hop to the overview (c-374).

requirements.statement: In the journey, Commodity details comes after the main import reason page and before identification, additional and arrival details, and stays the set's own consignment-details journey page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the reason for import between choosing commodities and giving their details; the page's real path is the service's architecture, which the prototype does not decide.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-066 carries Commodity details on to the next journey page and repo-tests-p1-073 addresses it at the set's consignment-details page; trace-animals-fit-p9-001 captured the earlier hop straight from the commodity page (c-374).

requirements.statement: After changing commodity details from the check your answers page, a valid Save and continue on both the commodity page and Commodity details returns the trader to check your answers; opened from the overview, both return to the overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 states outright that the commodity page returns to the hub or the review depending on where the trader started; Commodity details' walk-on is only inferred from a missing field, so the stated design wins for both pages (c-021). The template review is no part of it, because templates are parked (c-375).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the commodity page returns the trader to where the overview sent them, else to the page that opened the commodity question, else to the next journey page, logging the return (repo-frontend-p9-049, -p9-051), and only Commodity details and animal identification are honoured as openers to return to (-p9-052); no claim records either page returning to check your answers.

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on Commodity details validates the page in full first, making the same checks as 'Save and continue'; once valid it saves and goes to the overview (to check answers when amending). 'Cancel and return to overview' goes to the overview without saving.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not save invalid quantities on a soft save, and rulings 26 October and 27 November make the two save buttons run the same checks. DR1's rule (b) gives a page the overview links to all three return controls.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-063 ends the page with the three controls, -p10-064 and repo-tests-p1-080 show a valid soft save stored and the trader returned to the overview, -p10-053 the refused page served at 400, trace-animals-fit-p9-033 the cancel link to the overview, and ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-012 records that both save buttons already make the same checks.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block on Commodity details asks 'Total gross weight', after Number of packages, in a narrow text input with the suffix 'kg', for every germinal commodity in the catalogue. It is optional: left blank, no error is shown, and the trader enters the figure.
requirements.why: The owner's 27 November ruling keeps the germinal total gross weight per species, as the 9 October ruling has each line's gross weight; V4 makes the total gross weight in kilograms an optional numeric field the trader supplies, with the example 24.50, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. V4's weight row is the one germinal row with no 'Applicable to' list, so it never says which germinal commodity codes the field is asked for; as the germinal set holds only germinal commodities and the other five germinal fields apply to all twelve entries, it is asked on every germinal species block. Design Release 2.1 gives the 'kg' suffix. Design Release 2.1 asks the gross weight after the quantity and the number of packages, so in each species block it follows them.

requirements.statement: The germinal set stores each species line's 'Total gross weight' answer as that line's gross weight in kilograms, held as a decimal, and shows it back in the service; it is not published on GBN-AG, because the current PIMS profile (gbn-ag-pims v0.2.0) has no gross weight.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks, errors and reviews the answer as a total gross weight, the owner keeps it per species, and what the real record stores is persistence, so no prototype storage key decides the quantity. The ruling publishes only what v0.2.0 already carries.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each commodity complement and species line records only whole-number animal and package counts, with no gross weight (repo-backend-p1-039, p1-040, p1-043, p1-044, cited in the backend's own area). The line's quantity stays its number of packages (c-234); only the gross weight is a decimal.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, each species block on Commodity details asks 'Quantity (unit/pieces)' for that species alone, in a text field with no hint, and asks no number of animals; the trader enters the count.
requirements.why: The data fields page makes Quantity (unit/pieces) the germinal commodity line's one mandatory count, held on each line, and Design Release 2.1 asks it with this label and no hint on each germinal species block in place of the number of animals. The owner's 27 November ruling keeps each chosen species' own counts. The data fields page gives the quantity no 'Applicable to' list, and the set holds only germinal commodities, so it is asked on every species block.

requirements.statement: The germinal set's Commodity details page always asks one 'Temperature' radio question, once for the whole page, with the options Ambient, Chilled and Frozen in that order. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown. The answer is stored on every commodity line of the notification.
requirements.why: The option B plan always asks the temperature in the germinal set; V4 captures the temperature on each commodity line as an optional single-select the trader answers, with exactly those three values, the example Frozen, and the same twelve germinal commodities the other germinal fields apply to, and marks it as affecting the germinal journey only. The question's legend, hint and place on the page are Design Release 2.1's, weighed with the Commodity details page.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set the main import reason is one radio choice of five reasons, in this order: Internal market; Transhipment or onward travel; Transit; Re-entry; Temporary admission horses. The germinal-products set's own copy of the page carries its own two-reason list of Internal market and Transit.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service all offer the same five reasons in the same order, as a single-select answer at notification level, and the policy page names which of them the germinals journey offers. The 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set with its own catalogue, so the reduced list belongs to that set's copy of the page, and the 27 November ruling confirms the germinal-products set offers only Internal market and Transit.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-065 and repo-frontend-p8-071 show the five reasons in the service's order today, and repo-tests-p1-059 shows none pre-selected. The policy page marks the reason field block 'At least one' while the field itself is a single-select enumeration and no field records a second reason (confluence-6497338582-p3-006): the single-select reading is what both the prototype and the real service build, so one reason is held.

requirements.statement: Each reason carries its hint: Internal market 'For imports of animals intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'; Transhipment or onward travel 'For animals intended for direct travel to a third country, that will stay only within the same port or airport in Great Britain while moving to another means of transport.'; Transit 'For animals moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'; Re-entry 'For animals authorised for re-entry, or rejected exports re-entering Great Britain.'; Temporary admission horses 'For horses authorised for temporary entry.'
requirements.why: The five hints are word for word the same in the target design and the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-066 to repo-frontend-p8-070 hold the same five hints today, in the page's own copy file.

Without JavaScript every reveal shows open and the page still works, because only the chosen reason's follow-ups are validated and saved.

The policy page names no extra field for Re-entry. The 9 October afternoon ruling requires every page to work fully without JavaScript, which GOV.UK's conditional reveal already gives; the target design's reveals that stay hidden without JavaScript are set aside for that reason.

requirements.statement: Choosing Internal market reveals the radio question 'Purpose in the internal market' (medium legend) with eleven options, in this order: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift; Transfer of ownership - Rescue; Breeding; Research; Racing, competition, show or training; Approved premises or body; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming; Production; Slaughter; Fattening; Restocking. The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, no purpose is pre-selected when the reveal first opens, and in the live-animals set all eleven are offered for every commodity. The germinal-products set's own copy of the reveal offers four: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift, Breeding, Research and Production.

requirements.statement: Each of the eleven internal market purposes carries its own hint beneath its label: Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift describes any movement aimed at sale or transfer of ownership, including gifts; Transfer of ownership - Rescue rehoming, adoption or fostering; Breeding reproduction and breeding programmes; Research 'Animals for use in scientific or medical research.'; Racing, competition, show or training 'Animals to participate in competitive or training events.'; Approved premises or body 'Animals for exhibition, zoos, collections, or conservation programmes where a licence or approval is needed.'; Companion animal not for resale or rehoming privately owned animals that cannot meet the non-commercial rules; Production 'Animals that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'; Slaughter 'Animals to be slaughtered and processed for meat production shortly after arrival into Great Britain.'; Fattening 'Animals to be fattened for meat production.'; Restocking 'To replenish or enhance populations of species, for example, restocking of game or fish.'

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' on the main import reason page makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and continue', and differs only in where it goes when every answer passes: the notification overview rather than the next journey page. A missing or invalid follow-up answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, the chosen reason still checked, its reveal open and the entries shown again. When amending, the 'Save and return' (review) action makes the same checks and goes to the review page.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling makes Save and return to overview run exactly the checks Save and continue runs, with an error for each missing or invalid answer and the trader kept on the page, and says no page is an exception; it replaces the earlier soft save recorded in c-211 and its plants counterpart c-313. The 27 November ruling confirms both save buttons make the same checks, the page's own hard stops together with any answer the data specification marks mandatory to proceed, in live animals and in the germinal-products copy of this page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-117 shows the button making the same checks as Save and continue, so a missing follow-up refuses both the same way, repo-frontend-p8-151 shows it refusing a transit answer with no port of exit while keeping the chosen country, and repo-frontend-p8-116 shows it saving and showing the overview; repo-tests-p1-060 shows the end-to-end suite using it. The 26 October ruling recorded that the button once skipped those checks (ruling-sam-2026-10-26-p1-001), and no fit, E2E or prototype trace in this area exercises it (trace-animals-fit-p7-079, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p3-085).

requirements.statement: When a template is being edited from its review, the main import reason page's Back link goes to that template's review page (the templates list when the template has no id), and saving stores the template and returns to its review page. Template mode walks this same page, not a copy of it, and plants pages have no template mode.
requirements.why: The 9 October templates ruling has template mode walk the same journey pages rather than copies, and the target design sends Back and the save to the template review while a template is edited. The 4 November ruling parks the templates rows and the 9 November rulings drop templates for now, so this is held, not built, until the owner picks templates up again, and the templates area is re-distilled then. Which answers template mode lets the trader leave blank (the target design drops errors for blank follow-ups while a template is created) is left to that re-distil, because the 9 October templates ruling does not say which validation differs.
requirements.deltaNote: The real frontend has no template mode today.
requirements.blockedBy: The owner picks templates up again: the 4 November ruling parks the templates rows in themes/type-question-and-templates and does not say when they are built.

requirements.statement: The main import reason task counts as complete once a reason allowed for the notification is saved with valid follow-ups (Internal market an allowed purpose; Transhipment a listed country; Transit a listed port and country; Temporary admission horses a real exit date and listed port; Re-entry nothing more), whether or not Additional details is answered; with no reason saved it is not complete.

requirements.statement: The additional details page asks 'What are the animals certified for?' The answer belongs to the notification as a whole, nothing is pre-selected on a notification without one, the same sixteen are offered whatever the commodity, and Other reveals nothing.
requirements.why: The policy page, the target design and the real service list the same sixteen values in the same order as a single-select answer the trader gives at notification level; the frontend's own certification-purposes service supplies the list today (repo-frontend-p8-127) and stays the source.

V4 says the same from the other side: every animal identifier field is optional on its own, and the block is satisfied by at least one of them. It holds 'for now' on the footing that it is no change, which today's service confirms.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, pressing a species panel's 'Save and add another' or 'Save and finish' with every identifier of the current animal blank saves nothing, keeps the panel on the same animal and, on a panel that asks for more than one identifier, shows 'Enter at least one identifier' in the error summary and inline, linked to that panel's first identifier field. The check is made per panel, so an empty panel is refused even when another species' form holds data. A partly filled animal saves with no error. The page's 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' never block on missing identifiers: an empty form saves no record and the trader moves on, and the page shows no message about the submit rule.
requirements.why: One identifier is enough (9 October ruling), so DR1's per-identifier errors, which it asked for only if every identifier were ruled required, are not built. An animal with no identifier at all is not a record, and validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so today's at-least-one error stays where DR2.1 silently keeps the trader on the same animal (c-042).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the hub's Identification details row shows Complete on exactly the bar the notification must meet to submit: every animal of every commodity line that is identified holds a saved record with at least one identifier, and a record whose every field is blank does not count.

The policy page asks for an identifier for each animal and is the specification of the data a notification captures, and the frontend now works a line out as short of its identified animals on exactly that bar. Which bar stands rests on the open question c-336.
