requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, to submit, every animal of every commodity line that is identified holds a saved record with at least one identifier. The identification page itself shows no message for this rule.
requirements.why: The policy page asks for at least one animal identifier for each animal, and the frontend now gates on exactly that. The 9 October ruling fixes one identifier per record as enough but expressly leaves unsaid how many records a notification needs, so which gate stands rests on the open question c-336; the review-and-submit area owns the gate and its message. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement; the germinal half is req-261.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-151 and repo-frontend-p10-152 hold the rule today; the traces were captured before the change, when the hub followed the one-record-per-species bar (trace-animals-fit-p10-002, trace-animals-fit-p10-003-m1).

requirements.statement: A germinal product needs one set of identification details per species, whatever its quantity: its panel shows one editable form headed 'Enter details for <species>' (no count, such as 'Enter details for Bos taurus'), prefilled with what was saved, with no panel button and no saved-entries table. The page's own 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' both save the values typed into each germinal species' form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 identifies germinal products once per species, not per package; the real store already holds one line per species. V4 holds the four germinal identifiers at unit level without saying how many unit records a germinal line carries, so the ruling and Design Release 2.1 set the count at one per species.

requirements.statement: Every germinal products commodity asks for 'Donor name/ID' (text), 'Collection date', 'Production date' and 'Identification number/mark' (text), in that order: four unit-level identifiers the trader enters, which apply to every germinal commodity in the catalogue.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields V4 page sets the identifiers a germinal products notification captures, holds all four at unit level, has the trader supply every one of them, marks them as affecting the germinal journey only, and gives each the same twelve germinal commodity entries, so one applicability list covers all of them; Design Release 2.1 asks them in this order.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set's identification page, Collection date and Production date are each a text field asked with the Ministry of Justice date picker's 'Choose date' calendar and the hint 'For example, 27/03/2026'; the field works as a plain text field when JavaScript is unavailable, no range rule applies to either date, and the production date is not checked against the collection date.
requirements.why: The target design asks each germinal date with a calendar. The interaction designer's 9 November answer and Sam's 10 November ruling keep the Ministry of Justice date picker that every other date in both frontends already uses, rather than replacing it with a three-part date input, and fold the calendar into the germinal identification dates row; the picker is a text field a calendar enhances, so the page still works without JavaScript. Neither the target design nor the policy page bounds either date, and the picker shows the field's own hint.

requirements.statement: Each germinal date field has a 'Choose date' calendar toggle, the Ministry of Justice date picker the live animals dates use, opening a month grid with previous and next year and month buttons, 'Select' and 'Close', over the single text input the field already has, so the field still works with the calendar unavailable.
requirements.why: The interaction designer's answer keeps the MOJ date picker on the germinal dates, and Sam's 10 November ruling takes the calendar out of the waiting-on-design theme and builds it with the germinal identification dates, germinal products following live animals rather than being a design question. It enhances the single text input req-2097 builds, because a page works fully without JavaScript and JavaScript only enhances one that already works (c-283).

requirements.statement: A Donor name/ID over 58 characters shows 'Donor name/ID must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline; any characters are accepted up to that length.
requirements.why: V4 limits the donor name or ID to 58 characters and sets no character set, pattern or minimum length for it, its example GB1238765 being an example rather than a format; Design Release 2.1 gives the message.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, an Identification number/mark over 58 characters shows 'Identification number/mark must be 58 characters or less', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: DR2.1's length rule for the identification number. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal date and length checks now, in the germinal set's copy of the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date not in the form day/month/four-digit year, with one or two digits for the day and the month, shows 'Enter a collection date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline; a date such as 1/9/2026 is accepted.
requirements.why: DR2.1's format rule for the collection date. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal date and length checks now, in the germinal set's copy of the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date not in the form day/month/four-digit year, such as 2026-09-01, shows 'Enter a production date in the format DD/MM/YYYY', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: DR2.1's format rule for the production date. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal date and length checks now, in the germinal set's copy of the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Collection date in the right format that is not a real date, such as 99/99/2026, shows 'Collection date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: DR2.1's real-date rule for the collection date. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal date and length checks now, in the germinal set's copy of the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a Production date in the right format that is not a real date shows 'Production date must be a real date', in the error summary and inline.
requirements.why: DR2.1's real-date rule for the production date. The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the germinal date and length checks now, in the germinal set's copy of the page.

requirements.statement: Germinal dates accept one- or two-digit day and month (such as 1/9/2026), any real date past or future, and a production date is not checked against the collection date; they read back as entered.
requirements.why: Neither V4 nor Design Release 2.1 sets a range or ordering rule on these dates; V4 only asks for a valid DD/MM/YYYY date, and its own example 12/12/2026 for both dates is in the future, so a future date is allowed.

requirements.statement: Each germinal identification field is optional on its own, so a partly or wholly blank entry saves without a missing-value error and never blocks 'Save and continue' (only the length and date rules apply to what is entered). But every selected germinal species, a lone species included, counts as identified only once its entry holds at least one of the four identifiers, and that one bar decides both submit and the hub's 'Identification details' Complete status. The identification page shows no message for this rule.
requirements.why: V4 marks all four germinal identifiers Optional and marks no germinal field mandatory to submit, while its own opening rule requires at least one germinal identifier per animal without naming which fields count or how 'per animal' maps to its unit records; the 9 October ruling settles that silence by making one identifier enough for both Complete and submit.

requirements.statement: Arrival details and transit countries each end with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link.

requirements.statement: When arrival details was opened from the notification review, Save and continue saves and returns to the review.

requirements.statement: Save and return to overview on arrival details and on transit countries makes the same checks as Save and continue: a missing means of transport and every other invalid answer is refused with its own error, the trader stays on the page with everything they entered kept, and once every answer is valid the page saves and shows the notification overview (the notification review during an amendment).
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling makes the two save buttons behave the same way on every page that has both, with no page an exception, in live animals and in plants, so a trader is never told different things by two buttons on one page. The same increment gives plants' arrival pages the same checks (req-1935).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-041 shows Save and return to overview making the same checks as Save and continue, with the required error, the other answers shown back and nothing saved, and repo-tests-p2-015 shows the valid path saving and opening the overview. trace-animals-fit-p16-087, trace-animals-fit-p17-059 and trace-e2e-p10-066 record that no trace of the earlier build pressed the button.

requirements.statement: Saved arrival answers are shown again when the trader returns: the date, the chosen port, the means of transport, the transport identification and the document reference.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-045 and trace-e2e-p10-035 show every answer played back on return.

requirements.statement: The overview's 'Arrival details' task shows Complete only when the arrival date is a real date in the window, the port is on the list, a means of transport is chosen, and transport identification and transport document reference are filled in; otherwise it shows To do.
requirements.why: Presence is a completeness rule for the notification, not a page error.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-038 and p11-039 bind the five answers to their obligations, repo-tests-p1-101 and trace-e2e-p10-036 show the row turning Complete once all five are saved, and repo-tests-p1-104 shows it reading To do with only a means of transport saved.

requirements.statement: A saved arrival date that later falls more than 7 days into the past turns the 'Arrival details' task back to To do.
requirements.why: The window is measured from today, so a stale date is no longer complete.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a stale saved date is flagged when the page is reopened (repo-frontend-p11-014); no source shows the overview status reverting.

requirements.statement: When a save fails, arrival details and transit countries come back at HTTP 500 with the trader's entries and the shared recoverable-error message.
requirements.why: A backend failure must not lose what the trader entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-047 shows both pages coming back with a recoverable-error notice at HTTP 500 rather than losing the trader's place.

requirements.statement: Each form on both pages posts back without browser validation and carries a CSRF crumb and a concurrency token that rises with each saved change.
requirements.why: Server-side validation, request forgery protection and optimistic concurrency are real constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-042-m1 shows both forms carrying the tokens and trace-e2e-p10-073 shows the concurrency token rising with each saved change.

requirements.statement: Arrival details (with the calendar open and with an error showing) and transit countries (empty, with a country added, and in an error state) have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.2 AA, and each of the five arrival fields is named to a screen reader by its own question label.
requirements.why: The service must meet the accessibility regulations.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-050 and p11-091 record both pages passing, with the calendar open, with the means-of-transport error showing, with a country added and in the error state, and p11-049 the per-field accessible names.

requirements.statement: The type-aheads on both pages are built from accessible-autocomplete over a native select and the date from the MoJ date picker; the rest of each page uses govuk-frontend components.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's custom search components are prototype builds; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes GOV.UK Frontend the toolbox, with accessible-autocomplete over a native select for long lists and the MoJ date picker the accepted extras, and no custom JavaScript written to copy the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p16-081, trace-animals-fit-p17-058 and trace-e2e-p10-076 show these components in place already.

requirements.statement: The transit country type-ahead filters on what is typed from a list rendered into the page, with no lookup call, and says 'No countries found' when nothing matches.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, choosing a country in the transit search adds it to the list straight away, with no 'Add country' button.
requirements.why: Out of scope: design ruled on 13 November that transit countries keep the 'Add country' button, so a country is added only when the trader presses it and adding on pick is not built. The 9 October afternoon ruling had put the change in the waiting-on-design theme as a design question.
requirements.deltaNote: A country is added only by pressing the secondary 'Add country' button, which submits and re-renders the page (repo-frontend-p11-061, trace-animals-fit-p17-019, trace-e2e-p10-053), and that is what design keeps.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, Remove takes a transit country off the list straight away, without a page load, leaving the others.
requirements.why: Out of scope: design ruled on 13 November that removing a transit country reloads the page, so removing in place is not built. The 9 October afternoon ruling had put the change in the waiting-on-design theme as a design question.
requirements.deltaNote: Remove posts the page's form, naming the country in its action, and the page is rendered again with the row gone (repo-frontend-p11-065, repo-frontend-p11-066), and that is what design keeps.

requirements.statement: Without JavaScript, the transit country search is a native select with an 'Add country' button and a Remove button per row, each submitting the page; the working list rides in hidden fields and is only saved by Save and continue.
requirements.why: Adding and removing transit countries must work for a trader without JavaScript, a real constraint the prototype cannot express. The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps today's native select, Add country button and submitting Remove buttons as what is built now, and every state change is a form post.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-090 shows the native dropdown without JavaScript, repo-frontend-p11-078 the working list carried in the page's own form and saved only on Save, and repo-tests-p2-019 the add working with JavaScript turned off.

requirements.statement: Each transit country's Remove control reads 'Remove' with the country's name in visually hidden text, so its accessible name is 'Remove <country>'.
requirements.why: Screen-reader users can tell the Remove controls apart out of context; this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's bare 'Remove'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-064 and trace-animals-fit-p17-038 show the hidden country name already.

requirements.statement: When arrival details or transit countries shows a validation error, the page title is prefixed with 'Error: '.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-051 and repo-tests-p2-004 show the prefix already.

requirements.statement: Adding a transit country announces 'Added <country>' to screen readers; the country that reaches the 12-country cap is announced with the cap message in the same announcement.
requirements.why: Out of scope: design ruled on 13 November that the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements on the transit countries list are not built, so the announcements keep their present wording.
requirements.deltaNote: It announces '<country> added.' (repo-frontend-p11-062, repo-tests-p2-011), and the twelfth country's announcement carries the limit notice as well (repo-frontend-p11-070).

requirements.statement: Removing a transit country announces 'Removed <country>' to screen readers.
requirements.why: Out of scope: design ruled on 13 November that the 'Added' and 'Removed' announcements on the transit countries list are not built, so the announcement keeps its present wording.
requirements.deltaNote: It announces '<country> removed.' (repo-frontend-p11-062, trace-animals-fit-p17-044).

requirements.statement: Both searches report to screen readers through a visually hidden polite live region (result counts, the port chosen, each country added or removed), nothing is announced on a fresh page load, and neither search carries a results-list label of its own.
requirements.why: Assistive-technology users hear each change as it happens. The announcements are the accessible autocomplete's own plus the page's status region: the 9 October afternoon ruling makes GOV.UK Frontend the toolbox with no custom JavaScript written to copy the prototype, and Sam's 9 November answer drops the prototype's custom search-results label and 'Selected' announcement from the country search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-062 and trace-animals-fit-p17-042 show the polite, atomic status region, trace-animals-fit-p17-053 shows nothing announced on a fresh load, and repo-frontend-p11-057 shows the search as the service's accessible autocomplete with no results-list label of its own.

requirements.statement: Added transit countries are listed in a table with a visually hidden caption 'Countries you have added', one visible column headed 'Country', a second column whose 'Actions' heading is hidden, and one row per country in the order added, each with its own Remove control.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-063 and trace-e2e-p10-055 show the hidden caption, the two columns and the order added.

requirements.statement: Transit countries are optional: Save and continue with none added raises no error and goes to the transporter list, as it does with countries added.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-081 and repo-tests-p2-017 show the empty save accepted, and repo-frontend-p11-087 shows Save and continue opening the transporter list.

requirements.statement: Saved transit countries are listed again, in the order they were added, when the trader returns to the page, with the status announcement cleared.

requirements.statement: The transporter list has a visible sub-heading (h2) 'Select a transporter' above the search box and the transporter table.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the search and the list together with a visible 'Select a transporter' heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-012 puts an h2 'Select a transporter' above both the search box and the table, and repo-tests-p2-066 proves it end to end.

requirements.statement: The fieldset round the transporter table keeps the legend 'Select a transporter', visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the words once as the h2 and keeps the legend for screen readers only.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-012 repeats the same words as the radio fieldset's legend for screen readers only.

requirements.statement: The transporter search box is labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or approval number', and the search button sits joined flush beside it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree, and the list's search uses the same controls as the address pickers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-013 holds the label, the hint and the button, and repo-frontend-p12-014 joins the box flush to it in the left half of the search row.

requirements.statement: The transporter list's search runs when the trader presses the search button or Enter: the server re-renders the list narrowed to the term, with the term kept in the box. Nothing on the list narrows the rows or emboldens matching letters while the trader types.
requirements.why: Design asked for the address searches to be built without live filtering, with the trader typing a term and then pressing Search, and the afternoon ruling of 9 October held the transporter list's in-page filter back so that design's answer to that question would be applied when this area was re-distilled. Every search in the service then behaves the same way, and the page works the same with or without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: Today, with JavaScript on, typing in the search box narrows the rows in the page, keeps focus in the box, loads no new page and emboldens the matching letters, a term already in the box narrows the rows as the page loads, and the search button filters in place without submitting (repo-frontend-p12-036, repo-frontend-p12-037, repo-frontend-p12-037-m1, repo-frontend-p12-099, repo-frontend-p12-100, repo-tests-p2-072). The server-side search behind the button stays as it is (repo-frontend-p12-038, repo-frontend-p12-039).

requirements.statement: A transporter search matches the term against each row's type ('Commercial' or 'Private') and status ('Approved' or 'New') as well as its name, address and approval number.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches all five columns.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-040 matches the term against a transporter's name, one-line address, approval number, type or status.

requirements.statement: Transporter search ignores letter case and accents; an empty term shows the whole list; the term stays in the box; searching saves and validates nothing; and a search that matches nothing shows 'No transporters match your search.' in place of the table.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never shows these states, so today's behaviour stands where it does not contradict the design.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-040 to repo-frontend-p12-043 and repo-frontend-p12-031 hold each of these. What happens to a pick the search hides is req-2637.

requirements.statement: The secondary 'Add a transporter' button sits beside the search, above the transporter table, right-aligned, dropping below the search box on a phone-sized screen, and takes the trader to the 'Choose a transporter type' page; tab order on the list runs search box, search button, 'Add a transporter', then the first transporter's radio.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the way to add a transporter next to the search, where a trader who cannot find theirs is looking.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-015 to repo-frontend-p12-017 put the button in the right half of the search row, before the table, dropping below the box on a phone, with that tab order.

requirements.statement: Transporters are listed in a table inside the 'Select a transporter' fieldset with a visually hidden 'Select' column holding a small radio per row (visually hidden label 'Select <name>'), then Name, Address, Approval number, Type ('Commercial' or 'Private') and Status, and a visually hidden 'Action' column; only one transporter can be chosen, and a 'New' transporter can be chosen like any other.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today share the shape of the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-018 to repo-frontend-p12-020 hold the seven columns, the radio per row and its visually hidden 'Select <name>' name.

requirements.statement: Each transporter row ends with a 'View details' link, followed by the transporter's name in visually hidden text, to that transporter's page in the INS address book, carrying the transporter list's own address back as the return.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader check a transporter's full record before choosing it. Which service holds transporter records, and where their page lives, follow the real services, and the address book now holds them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-026 and repo-frontend-p12-027 end every row with the link and send it to /address-book/transporter/{id} with the list's URL as the return, and repo-tests-p7-113 proves the round trip.

requirements.statement: Each row's Status is a tag reading 'Approved' in green or 'New' in magenta.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree; the prototype's custom 'new' style is the same magenta pairing the GOV.UK magenta tag gives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-024 and repo-frontend-p12-025 give the words and the green and magenta tags; no end-to-end test asserts the tag yet (repo-tests-p2-077), though repo-tests-p7-111 asserts a 'New' one.

requirements.statement: A 'New' transporter's status changes to 'Approved' through an approval step, and the service says what an unapproved transporter means for the notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: approved transporters are parked, so nothing is built for approving one. Neither Design Release 2.1 nor today's service shows any approval of a transporter or any consequence of choosing a New one, and the 6 November ruling names the values without saying what sets them, who may change one or whether an organisation's own transporter starts as New. The gap goes to the report with approved transporters.

requirements.statement: The service's shipped commercial transporters are the design's four, each Commercial and Approved: Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd, Danish Meat Export ApS and Portuguese Livestock Lda, with the addresses and approval numbers the design gives, and García Livestock Transport SL and J & G Campbell LTD are not shipped.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 6 November ruling parks approved transporters and says in terms that the two commercial placeholder records on main are not replaced with Design Release 2.1's four, and the 11 November ruling bars a row from resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers, which is all these seeded records are. The shipped records stay exactly as they are until approved transporters are unparked, when which approved-transporter list they come from is settled with them (req-2172).

requirements.statement: The service's shipped private transporters carry the design's addresses and approval numbers: Aberdeen Livestock Ltd, Romanian Agri Exports SRL, Slovak Farm Export and Finnish Livestock Oy.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 6 November ruling parks approved transporters and says in terms that the shipped private records' addresses and approval numbers are not changed, and the 11 November ruling bars a row from resting on the prototype's app/data files for which values a field offers. The names and statuses already match, so nothing is built for them until approved transporters are unparked.

requirements.statement: A transporter with no approval number shows the service's not-applicable text, 'Not applicable', in the Approval number column.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the cell rather than leaving it blank, so the trader can tell an absent number from a missing one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-022 shows the service-wide not-applicable text instead of an empty cell, and repo-tests-p2-067 proves 'Not applicable' on the journey's list.

requirements.statement: A row's Address cell is the address parts joined with commas, blanks left out, ending with the country.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the country on its added rows and on two seeded rows, and the review shows every transporter's country.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-021 summarises a transporter's address onto one line and trace-animals-fit-p18-068 shows blank optional parts skipped.

requirements.statement: The transporter list shows the organisation's own transporters newest first, ahead of the transporters the service ships.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree. The address book lists an organisation's live records newest first and the list keeps that order rather than imposing one of its own.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-029 reads the organisation's transporters from the address book, repo-frontend-p12-060 adds a new transporter ahead of the others, which ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013 says is the address book's newest-first order, and trace-animals-fit-p18-052 shows added transporters ahead of the shipped records.

requirements.statement: On the transporter list, both 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' refuse a save with no transporter chosen: the trader stays on the list and sees 'Select a transporter from the list' in a 'There is a problem' summary linking to the first radio and repeated inline above the table.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page makes both the commercial and the private transporter mandatory to proceed, and Sam's ruling of 26 October makes 'Save and return to overview' run exactly the checks 'Save and continue' runs, with no page an exception.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-044 makes the pick required with exactly that message, repo-frontend-p12-045 shows it in the summary and against the radio group with the summary link focusing the first option, and repo-tests-p2-071 proves exactly one error on a blank 'Save and continue'.

requirements.statement: A submitted transporter that is not on the organisation's list is refused with 'Select a transporter from the list' (summary linking to the first radio, inline above the table, title prefixed 'Error: ', no radio left checked, linking to the search box when no rows show), and a saved transporter no longer on the list opens the page with 'Select a transporter from the list. The one you chose is no longer available.'
requirements.why: A real validation constraint the prototype cannot express: the server must refuse values it did not offer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-047 holds the no-longer-available message, repo-frontend-p12-046 points the summary link at the search box when nothing matches, and trace-animals-fit-p18-071 to -075 show the out-of-list refusal as rendered.

requirements.statement: Choosing a transporter saves it on the notification with its type, name, address and approval number; picking a private transporter fills the private transporter record, contact details included; nothing is checked on a first visit; and when the trader chooses Change on a saved transporter, the list shows it checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that the choice is saved and shown again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-050 saves the type with the record, repo-frontend-p12-052 shows the saved pick checked when the list is opened again, repo-frontend-p13-105 fills the matching details form, and repo-tests-p2-069 shows nothing checked on a first visit. Today the list is the only view, so it always shows the saved pick checked; the summary shown in its place is req-2634.

requirements.statement: When the transporter list is reached from arrival details in the journey run, 'Save and continue' on it goes on to the documents page ('Upload documents'), which keeps its real path; opened from its overview task, the list returns to the overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 runs the journey straight on from the transporter to the documents, so the trader is not dropped back on the overview mid-journey; the 9 October ruling keeps overview-opened pages returning to the overview and drops the documents page's move to a new path.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is the last page of the transport section and a save lands on the overview rather than on the documents page (repo-frontend-p12-052, trace-animals-fit-p18-059, trace-e2e-p11-022); only the journey-run destination changes.

requirements.statement: The transporter list ends with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to overview', which saves the chosen transporter and shows the overview, and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the three controls, and Sam's ruling of 26 October states the same success path for 'Save and return to overview'. What the button does when the transporter is missing is req-402.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-053 ends the list with 'Save and continue' and the journey's return controls, and repo-tests-p2-070 proves 'Save and return to overview' saving the pick and opening the overview with no error.

requirements.statement: When the notification is being amended, the transporter list shows 'Save and return' (to the review), a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-style 'Save and return to overview'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's amend mode gives the page these controls; they work over the transporter list as it stands.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the transporter list in an amend.

requirements.statement: When the transporter list is edited from a template review, it shows a single 'Save and return' button and a 'Cancel' link back to the template, in the animals sets only, since plants pages have no template mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's template review mode gives the page these controls, and template mode works on pages as they stand.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source shows the transporter list in template mode.

requirements.statement: The transporter list's Back link goes to the notification overview, or to whichever page sent the trader there.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-101 follows the trail the page was opened with, and trace-animals-fit-p18-006 and trace-e2e-p11-021 show the Back link to the overview.

requirements.statement: The old /transport-details path redirects to the transporter list.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the redirect keeps an earlier prototype URL working; the real service never had that path, so no trader can arrive by it.

requirements.statement: The overview's 'Transport details' task links to the transporter list, shows 'To do' until a transporter is saved and 'Complete' once one with a name is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the task's name and completion rule.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-003 opens the trader on the list from the task, and trace-e2e-p11-003 and -023 show the task To do then Complete.

requirements.statement: The transporter list is the journey's one transporter step, reached after arrival details (and transit countries where they are asked) and from the overview; adding a transporter is a detour off it, with no page between the list and 'Choose a transporter type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on where the step sits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-001 and repo-frontend-p12-003 put the list at the transporter step and open the trader on it, and repo-frontend-p12-092 shows nothing between the list and the type question.

requirements.statement: After a transporter is added from the journey, the transporter list shows a one-time GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<name> transporter added', or 'Transporter added' if there is no name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 confirms the add on the list the trader returns to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-056 and repo-frontend-p12-057 hold the banner titled 'Success' reading '<name> transporter added', repo-frontend-p12-058 shows it once, and repo-tests-p2-107 proves it end to end. How the name is cased in it is req-2639.

requirements.statement: Saving a complete private or commercial transporter from the journey returns the trader to the transporter list, with the new transporter as the first row and already chosen, and every transporter that was listed before still listed below it.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 adding a transporter ends back on the list with it selected.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-092 lands the trader on the list and repo-frontend-p13-093 and repo-frontend-p12-059 make the new transporter the first row and already checked, which repo-tests-p2-106 proves end to end.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose a transporter type' page has the caption 'Add a new transporter', the heading 'Choose a transporter type' and the browser title 'Choose a transporter type - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-063 and repo-frontend-p12-064 hold the heading and caption on the journey's page, and repo-tests-p2-079 proves them end to end.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose a transporter type' page's GOV.UK warning text reads 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording, and the service's only guard against a duplicate: nothing stops a trader adding a transporter already on the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-065 holds that wording on the journey's page, and repo-tests-p2-080 proves it end to end.

requirements.statement: The transporter type radios' visually hidden legend reads 'Choose a transporter type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's legend; screen-reader users hear it without it competing with the visible heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-067 repeats the heading as the radio group's legend for screen readers only.

requirements.statement: The type page offers 'Private transporter' (no hint) then 'Commercial' with the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.', no hint on the group, and neither option chosen on a first visit; the hint is tied to its own radio so a screen reader reads it with the option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree, and the Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page gives the field exactly two values (req-2169); how they read is the design's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-066 holds the two options and the hint, repo-frontend-p12-067 leaves neither chosen on a first visit, and repo-tests-p2-082 checks the options. No end-to-end test asserts the hint on the journey's page yet (repo-tests-p2-089), and neither page says what a private transporter is (repo-frontend-p12-091).

requirements.statement: The Commercial option's hint is left unannounced with the option, as in the prototype's markup.
requirements.why: Nothing supports it any more: the 26 November prototype extract records the Commercial hint (prototype-dr2-1-source-p7-055, trace-prototype-dr2-1-p9-041) but no longer records it as unannounced with its option, and a hint tied to its own radio is the GOV.UK pattern (req-418).

requirements.statement: Continuing on 'Choose a transporter type' with no option chosen keeps the trader on the page, answered with HTTP 400, with the error 'Select a transporter type' in a 'There is a problem' summary linking to the first option and inline against the radio group.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the type must be chosen once the trader has set out to add a transporter, and the wording is the design's.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's type question already shows 'Select a transporter type' in the summary and against the radios, answered 400 (repo-frontend-p12-068, repo-frontend-p12-069, repo-tests-p2-084). The address book's own type question, which becomes the one route (req-2264), refuses with 'Select what kind of transporter it is' instead (repo-tests-p2-090), and that wording changes to the design's.

requirements.statement: A submitted transporter type that is neither Private nor Commercial is refused with 'Select a transporter type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives one message for a missing or unknown type, and the server still refuses values it did not offer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-095 refuses a type value that is not one of the offered types with the same 'Select a transporter type' message, its summary link focusing the first option with nothing checked. The 'Select a valid option' trace-animals-fit-p20-014 shows was captured before the page was rebuilt (c-391).

requirements.statement: The 'Choose a transporter type' page's only button reads 'Continue', with no return-to-task-list control.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-072 ends the page with a Continue button alone, which repo-tests-p2-081 drives.

requirements.statement: The type page's Back link returns to the transporter list; every page of the add route keeps a Change link's context (?change=1) on its links, Back links and onward pages.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Back link matches today's; the change context is how the real service returns a trader to the review, which Design Release 2.1 never shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-073 returns the Back link to the list carrying whatever trail it was opened with, and repo-frontend-p12-093 returns a save made from a Change link to the list with the trail still carried.

requirements.statement: The type page remembers the type chosen and checks it on return; 'Private transporter' leads to 'Add a private transporter' and 'Commercial' to 'Add a commercial transporter'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-071 routes each answer to its form, repo-frontend-p13-118 and repo-frontend-p13-119 serve the two forms behind those answers, and repo-frontend-p12-075 shows the last chosen type still selected.

requirements.statement: Opening or posting 'Add a private transporter' or 'Add a commercial transporter' without that type chosen sends the trader to 'Choose a transporter type', saving nothing from the submitted form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 only lets a trader reach each add form through its type.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-080 and repo-frontend-p13-004 to -006 send a trader whose chosen type does not match to the type question, repo-frontend-p13-121 runs the same guard on a post, and repo-frontend-p12-082 saves nothing from that post.

requirements.statement: Changing the transporter type removes the saved transporter of the other type from the notification; a transporter the trader added stays on the list, no longer checked.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint: the notification holds one transporter, of one type, and the obligation model purges the other.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-051 collects the type with the two records, repo-frontend-p13-087 records the type on every save, and trace-e2e-p11-055 and -076 show the other type's record purged while the added row stays listed and unchecked.

requirements.statement: 'Choose a transporter type' and 'Add a private transporter' show no notification status strip, while the transporter list and 'Add a commercial transporter' keep theirs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the status block off these two pages and shows it on the pages either side, and the prototype wins by default (c-053). What the add pages show once the address book serves them is req-2278.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-074 leaves the strip off the type question and repo-frontend-p13-054 off the private form while keeping it on the commercial one, and repo-tests-p2-088 proves all four pages end to end.

requirements.statement: The private transporter page's heading reads 'Add a private transporter' and its browser title 'Add a private transporter - Import notification service - GOV.UK', under the caption 'Add a new transporter'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-009 heads the page 'Add a private transporter' with the new-transporter caption (repo-frontend-p13-012) and the heading-then-service-name title (repo-frontend-p13-013), and repo-tests-p2-091 proves it end to end.

requirements.statement: The private transporter page has no intro paragraph under its heading: the form's first control follows the heading directly.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-018 puts the name field first in a form sitting directly after the heading, and repo-frontend-p13-011 renders the heading with the caption above it and nothing between.

requirements.statement: The private transporter form asks, in order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country', then under the h2 'Enter contact details' 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), with no authorisation number and no other hint on any field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's field order and labels, which the 14 October ruling confirms for the County field between 'Town or city' and the postcode.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-016 asks the fields in that order with those labels, repo-frontend-p13-031 and -032 put the single 'Enter contact details' heading after the country, repo-frontend-p13-030 leaves every other field without a hint and repo-frontend-p13-115 asks for no authorisation number. The labels and section headings the address book's own form uses instead are req-2265 and req-2267.

requirements.statement: The private transporter's Country select stays a plain select (no autocomplete) that opens with United Kingdom chosen when no country is held, with no 'Select a country' placeholder and no divider, and lists its countries sorted by label with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 defaults the country to the UK in a plain select, and the afternoon ruling of 9 October keeps a field the prototype shows as a plain select plain; how the list is presented is not its content, so the MDM judgement on list content does not reach it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-036 offers the country as a plain select sorted by label and repo-frontend-p13-037 and -038 open it on the United Kingdom with no country held and after an earlier save, so the placeholder and divider the traces show are gone.

requirements.statement: The private transporter's Country select lists the United Kingdom plus reference-data's GBNAG_SPS_EX countries, exactly as MDM serves them, and the list is never edited in code.

The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page states no country restriction and no picking list for the private transporter, so it does not narrow the list.

requirements.statement: On the private transporter form, a missing country shows 'Select a country', a country not on the list shows 'Select a country from the list' with the select cleared, a saved country no longer offered opens the form with 'The saved country is no longer available. Select a country from the list.', and the country is stored with its name and ISO code.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-039 to repo-frontend-p13-042 hold the three messages and the tampered-value refusal, and repo-frontend-p13-085 stores the country's code as well as its name.

requirements.statement: Saving a completely blank private transporter form is refused: 'There is a problem' lists 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number', in field order.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 every required field is required outright once the trader has chosen to add a transporter.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-062 lists all six messages for a wholly blank private form, in the order the page asks the questions (repo-frontend-p13-060), which repo-tests-p2-094 proves end to end.

requirements.statement: On the private transporter form, a blank required field shows its own message: 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' or 'Enter a phone number'; Address line 2 and County are never required.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today give the same messages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-064 to repo-frontend-p13-069 hold each message, and repo-frontend-p13-021 and -023 leave Address line 2 and County optional.

requirements.statement: On the private transporter form, over-long values are refused: name, address line 1 and address line 2 over 255 characters, town or city and county over 100, postcode over 12, phone over 20 and email over 254, each with '<field> must be <n> characters or less' using the field's label, and the typed value kept.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-071 to repo-frontend-p13-078 hold each length rule with the field's label in the message.

requirements.statement: On both add forms, an invalid save re-renders the page with HTTP 400, every error listed in field order in a 'There is a problem' summary (announced as an alert, each link focusing its field), each repeated inline with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the browser title prefixed 'Error: ', the Back link kept and every entered value kept.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-058, -060, -061 and -081 hold the summary above the heading, the field order, the 400 with values kept and the focusing summary links.

requirements.statement: The add pages' browser title stays unchanged in the error state, as in the prototype.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a defect in the prototype's markup, not a design decision. The real service keeps the GOV.UK 'Error: ' title prefix, which screen-reader users rely on.

requirements.statement: Both add forms trim surrounding spaces from every value before checking and saving it, and check the email address, phone number, postcode and authorisation number for presence and length only, not format, so an authorisation number is stored exactly as the trader entered it.

requirements.statement: Once the postcode lookup is built on the add-a-transporter pages, and only if design keeps the layout, each page opens on its lookup step with the address and 'Enter contact details' fields not yet shown: 'Add a private transporter' asks the name and the postcode first, and 'Add a commercial transporter' asks only 'Transporter authorisation number', with the 'Important' banner and a 'Continue' button, then the postcode; the details step follows a chosen address or 'Enter address manually', 'Save and continue' shows only on it, and each step's Back link goes to the step before.

requirements.statement: Transporters a trader adds belong to the organisation, not the user or the session: each saved transporter is its own record in the organisation's address book, it appears on every later notification's transporter list without being pre-chosen there, and another organisation's address book holds none of them.

requirements.statement: Transporters a trader adds are held by the address book service, so they survive a restart and every instance of a frontend offers the same list, and reference data serves no transporters list for any page to read.

requirements.statement: A document's Status shows a blue 'Scanning for virus' tag while its virus check runs and a green 'Check completed' tag once clean, each after visually hidden text 'Virus check status for <reference>' that survives a status change.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-062, repo-frontend-p17-063 and repo-frontend-p18-010 give the same tags and hidden text today.

requirements.statement: Every file is really virus scanned. A file the scan rejects shows a red tag naming the reason, 'Virus found', 'Upload failed' or 'Download failed', and the plain 'Rejected' where the upload service gave a reason the page has no wording for; the row has no View file link, and '<filename> cannot be used. Remove it and try again with a different file.' shows in the error summary, linked to the documents table, on every view until the document is removed, with 'The file' standing in where the filename is not known. Save and continue holds while a rejected document is listed. A status the service cannot recognise shows a grey 'Unknown' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 simulates a scan that always passes, so it has no failure state. A real scan can find a virus or fail: a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real failure handling and its own wording stay.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-064, repo-frontend-p18-042 and repo-tests-p5-037 show the reason-named tags and the per-file error today. The trace captured before the wording change reads '<filename> contains a virus. Remove it and try again with a different file.' (trace-animals-fit-p23-021). Only cdp-uploader's scan result sets a file's status, and a later result for the same session overwrites it (repo-backend-p3-060, repo-backend-p3-066). The prototype never shows a settled or rejected state (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p10-053), so the service's own tags stand.

requirements.statement: While a document is scanning, the page updates its status without the trader acting: with JavaScript it polls a JSON status endpoint under the page's own address every 3 seconds up to 10 times, re-reading every document's status each time, updates settled rows in place with their View file link, announces the settled state once in a polite live region, and reopens the page from the server once every scan settles; without JavaScript a 'Refresh virus scan status' link re-reads the status and carries the attempt count; after 10 attempts the hint 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.' shows.
requirements.why: A real scan takes time; the trader needs to see it finish. Design Release 2.1 fakes this with a timed call, which the real scan replaces. The polling is the real service's own enhancement, not script written to copy the prototype, and the refresh link means nothing the trader needs is shown only by script, as Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling requires.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p18-017 to repo-frontend-p18-037 and trace-e2e-p12-048 show the polling, the announcements and the no-JavaScript refresh link today. The announcements read 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use' and, for a rejection, 'Document check failed: the file contains a virus. Remove it and try again.' and its upload and download counterparts (repo-frontend-p18-028 to repo-frontend-p18-032); the trace captured before that wording change reads 'Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.' (trace-animals-fit-p23-031). The prototype never re-reads a status without JavaScript, so its tag stays Scanning for virus (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p10-054); the service keeps its refresh link, since every page must work without JavaScript.

requirements.statement: A document that scanned clean has a 'View file' link (hidden text 'for document N') that downloads the stored file byte for byte through the service, with the file's own content type only when it is an accepted type, otherwise as plain bytes, and with nosniff and the service's other security headers; a pending or rejected file has no link, and another notification's upload is answered 404.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never stores a file, so it cannot show one; storing and serving the real file is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and the trader needs to check what they attached.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-068, repo-frontend-p17-082 and repo-tests-p5-056 offer and serve View file for clean documents today. A download serves the document's first file, answers 403 for another organisation and 404 for a missing file, and is measured as one S3 call (repo-backend-p3-080, repo-backend-p3-082, repo-backend-p3-085).

requirements.statement: Each row has a 'Remove' link, usable while the document is still scanning, that opens a confirmation page for that document; following it leaves the page without saving anything typed in the add form. Rows have no change action: to correct a document the trader removes it and adds it again.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 now sends Remove to a delete confirmation page instead of removing at once, and on look and feel the prototype wins by default (c-473). The design release's goal keeps confirmations as pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Remove is a button styled as a link that posts the page form with the row's position (repo-frontend-p17-133) and removes the document straight away with no confirmation (repo-frontend-p17-074, repo-frontend-p17-119, trace-animals-fit-p22-057, trace-e2e-p12-054). Typed details are already discarded on Remove today (repo-frontend-p17-075). Today a scanning document can already be removed and rows already offer no change action (trace-animals-fit-p22-059, trace-animals-fit-p22-060). The prototype's leftover immediate-remove handler, which no control sends, is not built (prototype-dr2-1-source-p10-087).

requirements.statement: Each Remove link carries visually hidden text naming the document it removes by its document reference.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the document by its reference after the link text, so a screen reader user hears which document it removes; on wording the prototype wins by default (c-474).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Remove's hidden text is 'document N', the row's number in the list (repo-frontend-p17-067, repo-tests-p5-016, trace-e2e-p12-057).

requirements.statement: Uploading a document is optional: with none of the document details entered, Save and continue and Save and return to overview both leave the page with no error. With a document started and a detail missing, the trader is held on the page with an error for each missing detail and everything already entered stays.
requirements.why: The design and the real page agree, and the V4 data fields page makes accompanying documents optional at notification level: a notification can be submitted with none. Which entry makes a part-filled form a document to add is settled by c-351 (req-2178).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-086 leaves an untouched form alone and repo-frontend-p17-087 holds a part-filled form with an error for each missing detail today.

requirements.statement: Save and continue with a complete document in the add form saves it and moves the trader on at once. A document still being scanned does not hold them; only a document the scan rejected does.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves and moves on, and lets the trader continue while a document is still 'Scanning for virus'. Waiting for the scan on this page is a design choice, not a constraint: the backend only publishes documents that scanned clean.
requirements.deltaNote: Either save button now posts the whole form through the upload service, so a complete document is saved by Save and continue as well as by Save and add another (repo-frontend-p17-138), and a pending scan no longer holds the trader while a rejected one does (repo-frontend-p18-073, repo-frontend-p18-075, repo-tests-p5-039). The traces that held the trader until every scan settled, or returned them to the page, were captured before those changes (trace-animals-fit-p23-007, trace-animals-fit-p22-061). The backend claims a document whatever its scan status (repo-backend-p3-050), which is why a scanning document does not hold the trader.

Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue (claim 39), without a ?from=hub marker (c-237).

What remains is that the page returns the trader to the overview, or to the review page, when it was opened from there.

With none of the document details entered it goes straight to the overview.
requirements.why: Sam's 26 October ruling gives the two save buttons one behaviour, withdraws the earlier decision that let Save and return skip a page's checks, and refuses a documents-only exception; his 27 November ruling keeps the same checks on both buttons in live animals and in the germinal products copy.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-036 and trace-animals-fit-p22-034 show the same buttons and link today.

The return context is carried by the service's own mechanisms, the live flow's fallback to the overview and the existing ?change=1 for review; no ?from=hub or ?from=review marker and no hidden 'from' field is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the trader to where they started however often the page reloads, and that is the behaviour kept. How the context travels is architecture: Sam's 9 October ruling says no ?from=hub marker is added and only the live flow's fallback changes (claim 39), and query parameter and form field names are the service's (claim 17).
requirements.deltaNote: The back link already opens the review when the page was opened by changing an answer from there (repo-frontend-p17-009), and the refresh address already carries an open upload session through a reload (repo-frontend-p18-027); nothing shows the return context surviving a Save and add another, a Remove or a validation error.

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating a template, Upload documents is not offered: the one journey's template mode skips the page and its overview has no Documents task to follow. The skip lives in the shared journey flow, not in a copied or forked template journey. No guard on the page's own address is required.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents out of templates, because a document belongs to one consignment, and Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a template never offers documents and that the prototype's template URL guards are not required (c-238). His templates ruling makes template mode a way of walking the same pages, never copied or forked, and animals only. It is built with the templates work, which ruling:sam-2026-11-04 parks and the interaction designer records as dropped for now, so it lands when templates do.

requirements.statement: Each document is saved to the notification as soon as it is added, as its own record in the backend's accompanying_documents collection keyed by the notification reference, with its type code, reference, date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD date, a UUID upload id, scan status and files; it is still listed on a fresh load, and a retried save or removal does not add or remove it twice.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents in the session and only saves the draft on some buttons. Storing them durably is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend keeps each document in accompanying_documents linked by notification reference, with a unique upload id and a YYYY-MM-DD date (repo-backend-p3-016, repo-backend-p3-017, repo-backend-p3-021); a repeated claim never makes a second document (repo-backend-p3-048); repo-tests-p5-079 and trace-e2e-p14-148 show each document still listed after a reload.

requirements.statement: The browser posts the add form and its file straight to cdp-uploader's upload-and-scan address, so the file never passes through the frontend or the backend. Each time the page is drawn the frontend opens a cdp-uploader session limited to 50MB and the eight accepted file types and registers it with the backend against the notification. cdp-uploader scans the file, keeps a clean file in the documents S3 bucket, reports the result to the backend's scan-result callback, matched by correlation id, and returns the browser to the page, which then gives the backend the document's type, reference and date of issue. A document becomes COMPLETE only when no file was rejected (fail closed). A failure to use the uploader shows 'The selected file could not be uploaded. Try again.', and a failure to reach it at all brings the page back as a service failure with the details the trader typed still in the form. In CDP the scan is the real cdp-uploader; on the local stack it is the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan.
requirements.why: This is the real upload handshake behind the page; Design Release 2.1 sends only the filename and cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: The frontend opens and registers a session per render and posts the form straight to cdp-uploader (repo-frontend-p17-134, repo-frontend-p17-139, repo-backend-p3-033, repo-backend-p3-083, repo-perftests-p3-042), then claims the document with an ISO date (repo-frontend-p17-136, repo-backend-p3-046); the scan callback fails closed (repo-backend-p3-058). The earlier traces that show the file posted to the frontend (trace-e2e-p12-073, trace-animals-fit-p22-080) were captured before this direct upload. The backend keeps upload sessions unique by uploadId and correlationId, validates both, refuses a duplicate registration, finds a session only by notification and correlationId together, refuses a scan result with no or an unknown correlationId, records the file details cdp-uploader reports, and holds a scanned document unclaimed with no type, reference or date until the trader claims it (repo-backend-p3-020 to repo-backend-p3-071).

requirements.statement: Documents can be added, listed and removed whatever the notification's status, draft, submitted or in amendment; they are deleted with their notification; and only documents that scanned clean are referenced in the events the backend publishes.
requirements.why: These are the cross-service rules around the document record; the design does not contradict them, and amending a notification reaches the page in Design Release 2.1 too.
requirements.deltaNote: A claim does not check the notification's status (repo-backend-p3-051), documents and sessions are deleted with their notification and share its expiry (repo-backend-p3-087, repo-backend-p3-088), and only claimed COMPLETE documents go on the published event (repo-backend-p3-089), over the four notification statuses repo-tests-p5-062 names. Every document endpoint but the scan callback checks the notification belongs to the calling organisation (repo-backend-p3-039).

requirements.statement: The documents page stays safe and recoverable: text the trader typed is HTML-escaped in table cells; a row with no reference or date of issue reads 'Not provided'; a failed delete of an upload leaves the document in place; and a saved document whose type or attachment type the service no longer lists raises 'One or more of your saved documents are no longer valid. Review the list before you continue.'.
requirements.why: Real-service safeguards with no design counterpart; Design Release 2.1 does not contradict them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-060, repo-frontend-p17-077, repo-frontend-p17-091 and repo-frontend-p18-010 hold these safeguards today.

requirements.statement: Backend document-endpoint defects: the scan callback is unauthenticated; deleting a document leaves its file in S3; the list has no defined order; a notification of another organisation is answered 404 where the API description says 403; the Location header a registration returns points at an address that answers 404 until the document is written; the get, delete and download endpoints check no pattern on the upload id; and a document whose 24-hour upload session has expired can no longer be read, downloaded, deleted or claimed.
