Plants keeps its own sections when a change is mirrored (ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm), and its place of destination sits in the arrival-and-destination section.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-089 shows the animals picker's heading row holding the caption 'Addresses' and the role heading, repo-tests-p7-052 the five headings, and repo-tests-p7-091 to -p7-095 each party's hint repeated straight under the heading row; repo-plantsfrontend-p7-006 shows plants' consignor picker captioned 'Addresses', repo-plantsfrontend-p8-006 its place of destination captioned 'Destination', and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-103 each page title coming from the page's own copy. Before it landed the animals caption read 'Consignment parties' (trace-animals-fit-p14-028, trace-animals-fit-p15-003, trace-e2e-p9-004).

requirements.statement: Each animals party picker's Back link returns to the consignment addresses page, keeping any check-your-answers change context; each plants picker's Back link returns to the page the trader came from.
requirements.why: The animals picker is reached from the consignment addresses page, as in the prototype; plants' pickers are reached from the overview or from the page before them, so Back follows the trail.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p9-046 and trace-animals-fit-p14-036 show the animals picker's Back going to the consignment addresses page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-081, -p7-017 and -p7-018 show plants' pickers following the trail.

requirements.statement: Each of the five animals party pickers offers 'Add a new address' for its role as a secondary button beside its heading; it is left out in stub mode, where there is no address service to add to. The high-risk plants frontend's pickers offer no add-address control.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 presents adding an address as a button beside the heading. It sends the place of origin and consignor to a hand-entered address form and the consignee, importer and place of destination to a UK postcode search; address search waits until the INS address lookup is a real feature, so every add-address page offers manual entry only, and where the button leads is the party-address-add-and-edit area's. Plants has no add-address control to restyle, and ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves plants alone where it has no equivalent; plants traders add a missing consignor in the INS address book first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-090 shows exactly one 'Add a new address' control in the picker's heading row, rendered as a button rather than a link, repo-tests-p7-088 and -p7-089 show it left out in stub mode, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-095-m1 shows no plants picker offering one. Before it landed the animals control was a plain link in a paragraph under the intro (trace-e2e-p9-011).

requirements.statement: Every party picker has a search box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country', in both frontends.
requirements.why: The prototype and both real services already agree on this wording.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-168 shows the animals party pickers' box labelled 'Search' beside a 'Search' button, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-010, -p9-011 and -p9-013 show plants' box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country'.

requirements.statement: The picker's 'Search' label is styled as a medium heading, in both frontends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the search label medium heading weight. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' pickers the same search control in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-101 shows plants' search label rendered as a medium GOV.UK label with the hint under it. No claim in this working set gives the animals label's weight since the pickers were rebuilt; the last rendering of the animals picker showed it small, govuk-label--s (trace-animals-fit-p14-037, trace-animals-fit-p15-008).

requirements.statement: On every party picker the search is run by a search icon button beside the box, with the accessible name 'Search'; the icon button submits the picker's own form, so search still works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses an icon button; DR1 judged that the server-side search must stay as the no-JavaScript fallback, which a non-submitting icon button would lose. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm keeps every search a form with a button that submits it, and the interaction designer confirms the joined search button was built in design snagging with nothing further to change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-012, -p9-014 and -p9-101 show plants' search run by an icon button joined to the box, whose only text is visually hidden, submitting the picker's own form with action=search, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-082 and -p9-083 that the whole picker works without JavaScript; repo-tests-p2-153 and -p7-139 show the animals search loading a fresh page when Search is pressed. ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-015 to -p1-017 record the joined search button as already built in design snagging, with nothing left to change. Before it landed both frontends ran search from a secondary 'Search' text button (trace-animals-fit-p14-038, trace-e2e-p9-018).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, typing in a party picker's search box hides the rows whose name, address lines or country do not contain the text (ignoring case) and updates the results count, with no page reload, on both animals sets' party pickers and on the high-risk plants frontend's pickers. It is its own waiting-on-design increment, built as design answers or dropped if design drops it.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling design-2026-11-13 point 2 decides that address search does not filter as the trader types, the trader pressing Search or Enter as both services already do. Before it, Design Release 2.1 narrowed the list as the trader typed and DR1 judged a live filter worth porting, but ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm held filtering as you type until design answered.
requirements.deltaNote: Neither frontend's picker carries client-side filtering today: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-082 shows the search as a form submit, and repo-tests-p2-153 and -p7-139 show the animals search loading a fresh page.

requirements.statement: Submitting a party picker's search, or opening it with a search in the address, narrows the list on the server to matching addresses and keeps the text in the box; an empty search shows the whole list again, and a submitted search opens the first page of results.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the existing server-side search must stay as the fallback for traders without JavaScript, and the prototype also filters on the server when given a search.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-040 and -p7-045 show the animals picker searching on the server within its own role and keeping the term through paging, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-015 to -p9-019 show plants passing the term to the address book, opening the first page and restoring the whole list on an empty search.

requirements.statement: Each of the five party pickers, place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, in both animals sets, and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, shows eight a page of the addresses it found, its whole list or the matches when a search narrows it, with GOV.UK pagination under the results where more than eight were found and none where eight or fewer were. The page links carry the search term, the page, the address held as chosen and the trail the trader arrived on; a submitted search starts again at the first page; a page past the last page serves the last page and one that is not a page number serves the first, each logged once. A picker offers no sorting, no filter beyond its search box, no tabs and no control over the page size.
requirements.why: Eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses over the same records, and a trader with many addresses for one role needs the list broken up. Ruling ian-2026-11-23 drops the one-page clause this requirement used to carry, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 keeps that drop, so every picker in both journeys pages at one figure. The contact address pages are not party pickers and page at the same figure in their own rows: req-2312 and req-2313 for the animals sets, req-1965 for plants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-044 to -p7-046 show the animals pickers at eight a page with pagination from the ninth match, the search term and the chosen address kept across pages, after EUDPA-827 landed on the animals frontend's main (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-027, -p1-029), and repo-tests-p2-154 that a picker shows at most eight. repo-plantsfrontend-p9-049 to -p9-058 and -p9-089, -p9-090 show the shared plants picker, which its consignor and place of destination pickers use, cutting pages of eight, showing pagination only past one page, carrying the search, the choice and the trail on every link, and logging a page past the last or not a page number once each; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-005 shows the page carried in the form, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-096 no sort, extra filter, tab or page-size control.

requirements.statement: Every party picker, the five in both animals sets and the high-risk plants frontend's consignor and place of destination pickers, shows a 'Selected address: <name>' inset between the search box and the results, naming the address the picker holds as chosen, on every page and after a search; the inset shows only while that address is still a live address-book record the picker offers.
requirements.why: The inset exists because the chosen row can be on another page, which paging at eight makes true again. Without it a trader on page two has nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen. Ruling ian-2026-11-23 restores it in both frontends with the words they already had, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 keeps that restoration. The contact address pages restate the chosen address in their own rows: req-2313 for the animals sets, req-1965 for plants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-042 and -p7-045 show the animals picker naming the chosen address between the Search button and the results heading and keeping it on page two, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-022 and -p9-023 show the same inset in plants, shown only while the held id still resolves to a live record the picker offers.

requirements.statement: Under the search, every party picker shows the heading 'Select an address' above the results count.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list of addresses, and DR1 asked for the same heading. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same heading in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-039 and -p2-113 show the animals picker's second-level 'Select an address' heading above the results, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-031 the same heading in plants; before it landed the results table had no heading and its caption carried the count (trace-animals-fit-p14-039).

requirements.statement: Every party picker's results count reads 'Showing <shown> out of <found> results', in English and Welsh, sits straight under the 'Select an address' heading and outside the table, and counts the rows on the page being shown against every address found.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the count this way, and DR1 asked for the same rewording. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same count in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-039, -p7-040 and -p7-045 show the animals picker's sentence 'Showing <shown> out of <found> results' under the heading and counting matches, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-032 and -p9-056 the same sentence in English and Welsh outside the table; before it landed the table caption read 'Showing <shown> of <total> addresses', plural even for one (trace-e2e-p9-027, trace-e2e-p9-028).

requirements.statement: Every party picker's address table sits inside one fieldset whose legend, visually hidden, reads the results heading, so the radios are announced as one choice; when a selection is refused the form group around the results takes the GOV.UK error state and the fieldset is described by the error message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups the address radios under one legend, so assistive technology announces them as one choice. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same fieldset in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-113 shows the animals picker's radios inside a group under the 'Select an address' heading, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-033 to -p9-036 the fieldset, its visually hidden legend and its error state in plants; before it landed each row's radio sat in its own form group with no fieldset for the whole choice (trace-e2e-p9-022).

requirements.statement: Every party picker lists addresses in a table with a radio column (header 'Select', visually hidden), Name, Address and Country columns, and a last column for the row's action (header 'Actions', visually hidden); each row's radio is a small radio named after the answer the page collects, valued with the address-book record's id, and labelled 'Select <name>' in visually hidden text, so one address at most can be chosen.
requirements.why: The prototype and both real pickers already agree on the table and its radios, which the real pickers build from the GOV.UK table and radios components.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-039 to -p9-043 and -p9-091 show the five columns, their names in both languages and the small radio labelled 'Select <name>', and repo-tests-p7-051 and -p2-113 prove the animals rows the same way.

requirements.statement: Every party picker's Address column shows each street line on its own line, with the town or city, county and postcode together on the line below, and leaves out any part the record does not hold; the country sits in its own column.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 prints one line per address line, which reads more easily in a narrow column. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants the same address lines in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-047, -p7-049 and -p2-117 show the animals rows breaking each street line onto its own line with the town, county and postcode together below, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-044, -p9-045 and -p9-088 the same in plants with empty parts dropped; before it landed the column joined every part with commas on one line (trace-e2e-p9-024).

requirements.statement: Each animals picker row ends with a 'View' link, named 'View <name>' to a screen reader, that opens that address in the INS address book and comes back to the same picker with the search term, the trail and the chosen row as they were. This is the animals pickers' change only: the high-risk plants frontend is not wired to the INS address book, so its pickers keep their 'View details' disclosure.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows an address's details on the address book's own page rather than in an expander; the address book belongs to the INS frontend, so its view page has to honour the return to the animals picker.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-048 shows a row's last cell holding only a 'View <name>' link, and repo-tests-p7-105 to -p7-107 the round trip into the INS address book and back to the same picker with the search term, the trail and the choice kept; before it landed each row held a 'View details' disclosure that expanded in place (trace-e2e-p9-025, trace-e2e-p9-026).

requirements.statement: Reopening a picker for a party that already holds an address picked from the book ticks that address's radio and names it in the inset; a copy whose record has gone from the book, been deleted, or is not offered for the picker's role opens with nothing ticked and the held copy still shown. A selection named in the address wins over the one the notification holds.
requirements.why: The prototype pre-selects the current choice, and both real pickers already do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-043 shows the chosen row ticked once its page is shown and repo-tests-p7-077 a deleted record dropped with nothing ticked; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-060 to -p9-062, -p9-074 and -p9-078 show the same in plants, with a selection in the address winning over the stored one.

requirements.statement: Pressing 'Save and continue' on a party picker with no address chosen shows no error, leaves the party as it was — empty, or holding its earlier address as the trader edited it — and moves the trader on as a valid save would, an animals picker to the consignment addresses page and a plants picker to the next page of its journey or to the overview. The save is logged once as committing nothing.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader leave a picker without choosing; completeness is checked by the task status and the review, not by the picker. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm gives plants' pickers the same lenient blank save, and the owner's 26 October ruling makes plants' 'Save and return to overview' check exactly what its 'Save and continue' checks, so both of its buttons are lenient.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-050 shows an animals picker saved with nothing ticked returning to the consignment addresses page with that party still offering only its add link, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-065, -p9-066, -p7-080, -p7-081 and -p7-099 show plants committing nothing, raising no error, leaving an edited copy untouched and logging the save once. Before it landed both frontends re-rendered the picker with status 400 and 'Select a <party> from the list' (trace-animals-fit-p14-050 to -054).

requirements.statement: Saving a picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, has been deleted since the page loaded, or is not offered for that picker's role saves nothing and re-renders the picker with status 400, an error summary 'There is a problem' and the picker's own error: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list', 'Select a place of destination from the list' or 'Select a contact address from the list' and their Welsh, shown above the results with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the summary link going to the first address radio or, with no rows, to the search box. The ticked row is cleared, the search term and its results stay, and the refusal is logged with the address id and the reason.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: the notification must never hold a party copied from a record the organisation does not have, or does not have for that role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-028 holds the five animals errors; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-067 to -p9-072 show plants refusing such an id at status 400 with its own message, clearing the tick, keeping the search and logging the reason, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-037 shows the summary link going to the first row or to the search box.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each of the five animals party pickers and the CPH number page end with a single primary 'Save and continue' button, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no cancel link. While amending, each ends with the amendment's own save and return controls.
requirements.why: DR1 ruled this same difference (rule (b)): only pages the overview links to end with the three return controls, and a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone; the animals pickers are reached from the consignment addresses page. The amendment's endings are req-1624's, in the journey-flow area.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p9-045 and trace-animals-fit-p15-030 show the animals pickers ending with 'Save and continue' alone today, and document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-057 records the CPH number page built the same way under DR1 rule (b). The permanent address page follows the same rule (req-748).

requirements.statement: Choosing an address on an animals picker and pressing 'Save and continue' saves on the notification a copy of that record — the record it came from, its name, telephone number, email address and address — and returns to the consignment addresses page, or to check your answers under change context. The page names each party from that copy, never from the address book, so renaming, moving or deleting the record afterwards leaves the notification, its review, its submitted view and its amendment as they were.
requirements.why: The prototype and the real service both save the chosen address against the party and return to the page; the copy keeps the notification stable when the book changes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-052 shows every party answer stored as a copy taken when it was chosen rather than a live reference, trace-animals-fit-p14-061 the return to the consignment addresses page, and repo-tests-p7-073, -p7-075, -p7-097 and -p7-100 that a later rename or deletion leaves the draft, the review, the submitted view and the amendment unchanged.

requirements.statement: If saving a picked address fails because the backend is briefly unavailable, the picker re-renders with status 500, the recoverable-error message, the trader's choice still ticked, their search term still in the box and the page of results they were on, and the failure is logged once.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the trader must not lose their choice when the save fails.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-079 shows the picker shown again at status 500 with the recoverable-error banner and the choice still ticked, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-005 the page of results carried in the form, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-080 that a programming failure is raised instead.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, on both animals sets and in the high-risk plants frontend, offers only the organisation's addresses whose roles include that party's role: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination. Its search looks only within that role, and a party filled from another party's record is not offered that record in its own picker.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 filters each picker to its role, so a trader is not offered a GB importer as a place of origin; DR1 found the unfiltered list a live defect on all the pickers, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 keeps address roles because DR1 asked for role-filtered pickers. Ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm builds the role-filtered pickers and gives plants the same change in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-029 binds each animals party to its address-book role so only records offered for that role can be chosen, and repo-tests-p7-038, -p7-040 and -p7-085 prove the role-filtered list, the role-scoped search and the source record not being offered after a same-as fill; repo-plantsfrontend-p7-007, -p8-023 and -p9-073 show plants' consignor and place of destination pickers asking for their own role. Before it landed all five animals pickers searched one undifferentiated book (trace-animals-fit-p14-045).

requirements.statement: The consignor picker offers addresses saved for the consignor role, including any a trader thinks of as the exporter; there is no separate exporter party and no exporter role. How the address book records those roles is the address book's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's consignor section covers the exporter too. Ruling ian-2026-11-16 decides that no EXPORTER role is added anywhere, because the prototype's consignor-or-exporter vocabulary is its own internal type rather than a domain role, and ruling sam-2026-10-09 leaves the field shape of address roles to the address book service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-131, -p7-132 and -p2-144 show the address book holding five roles an address can play, place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee and importer, with no exporter among them.

requirements.statement: An address saved with several roles appears on the picker of every party whose role it carries.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets one saved address be reused across parties, such as the same company as consignee and importer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-038 shows a record saved for two roles listed on both roles' pickers.

requirements.statement: The address book holds one or more roles on each address record and lets a frontend list an organisation's live addresses for one or more roles, newest first and a page at a time, excluding deleted records, with the role filter running in the service before the page is cut. The animals frontend and the high-risk plants frontend each ask for their picker's role. The record's field shape for roles is the address book service's own design, not the prototype's.
requirements.why: DR1 found role filtering needs a typed address record, which no frontend can fake, and the address book is one of this programme's repos. Ruling paul-2026-11-05 point 8 keeps pagination on the list even though the prototype has none, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, and ruling ian-2026-11-25 drops this requirement's earlier 'unpaginated' clause and confirms Paul's point 8 stands in full.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-012 to -p1-018 record the service as it stands on main: a list request filters on searchTerm, countryCodes, roles and searchRoles, lists the caller's live addresses newest first one page at a time with a 1-based page and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, and cuts the page after the role filter has run. repo-tests-p7-131 and -p2-144 show the roles held against each record, repo-tests-p2-145 that a transporter carries none, and repo-frontend-p14-029, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073 and -p9-019 show each frontend asking for its picker's role. Collecting the roles when an address is saved is the address-book and party-address-add-and-edit areas' work. The list API's own parameters, limits and filter order are req-2352 and req-2353 in the address book list area; this row holds the roles on the record, the role-scoped list a picker reads and each frontend asking for its picker's role.

requirements.statement: An address-book record that carries no role yet is offered on every party picker, in the animals frontend and in the high-risk plants frontend, until it is given a role, in the compose stack and in CDP alike.
requirements.why: Records saved before roles existed are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and DR1's judgement rules out filtering them on a guess, which would hide addresses the trader legitimately wants.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-073, -p7-008 and -p7-009 show plants' pickers offering the records that carry their own role together with those carrying no role, and no others. repo-tests-p2-155 and -p7-137 show the end-to-end suite expecting an animals picker to offer the records held for its role and those held for no role, but no test yet creates a record with no role and looks for it on a picker.

requirements.statement: In stub mode, each canned address-book record carries one or more roles, in the animals frontend's stub and in the high-risk plants frontend's stub book, so the stub-mode pickers filter by role as the real ones do.
requirements.why: The stub mirrors the tests repo's address-book fixture record for record and is what local development and each frontend's own suite run against; without roles it cannot show role filtering.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants' stub book now holds roles: nine of its records are offered on the consignor picker and nine hold the destination role, while eighteen are offered on the role-free contact picker (repo-plantsfrontend-p7-009, -p8-042, -p7-073). No claim in this working set shows the animals frontend's own stub records carrying roles.

requirements.statement: Each party picker lists its addresses newest first, so an address just added through the address book appears at the top.
requirements.why: The prototype lists newly added addresses first, and the address book already serves its list newest first.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-013 records the address book listing the caller's live addresses newest first, one page at a time, and trace-e2e-p9-030 and -p9-031 show the newest record filling the top of page one of the picker.

requirements.statement: When a party picker has no rows to list, because a search matched nothing or because the organisation's book holds no address it offers, it shows 'No addresses match your search.' where the results count would go, renders neither the fieldset nor the table, and still offers 'Save and continue'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not draw an empty result; the real message tells the trader why the list is empty, and nothing in the prototype contradicts it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-054, -p7-136 and -p2-115 show the animals message today, keeping the term in the box, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-021 and -p9-102 the same wording in plants, with the 'Select an address' heading still shown above it.

requirements.statement: Every address-book read a journey makes is made on the server, for the signed-in session's organisation only, and a record belonging to another organisation is never offered or resolved; with no organisation on the session no read is made.
requirements.why: A real authorisation constraint: the address book trusts the organisation the caller names, so the frontend's scoping is what keeps one organisation's addresses from another.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-094 scopes the read to the organisation on the trader's signed-in session so another organisation's record is never returned, repo-plantsfrontend-p9-084 scopes both the addresses offered and the record a save resolves, and trace-e2e-p9-101 shows the calls made server-side.

requirements.statement: A deleted address-book record is never offered on a picker and can never be saved, and a stored answer picked from one shows no ticked row; an address book that cannot be reached is an error, never read as a deletion.
requirements.why: Deleted addresses must not be chosen again, and an outage must not look like a deletion.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-071 and -p9-074 keep a deleted record off the picker and show no ticked row, and repo-tests-p7-076 and -p7-077 prove the soft delete and the dropped row end to end. repo-plantsfrontend-p7-102 shows plants handling no failure at all when the address book cannot be reached while listing addresses: only a failed save of the notification is handled.

requirements.statement: A journey reads the address book and never writes to it: adding a record goes through the INS frontend, and neither journey serves a create-address page of its own.
requirements.why: The INS frontend is the address book's only writer; how Design Release 2.1's in-journey add page is met belongs to the party-address-add-and-edit area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p7-096 shows the live-animals addresses/create path answering 404, repo-frontend-p14-075 the hand-off out to the INS address book's add page, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-095-m1 that no plants picker offers a way to add an address the book does not hold.

requirements.statement: Every string on the consignment addresses page and on every party picker, in both frontends, has a Welsh counterpart, still marked as a machine draft awaiting translator sign-off and not to be shown to users before Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual, and DR1 asked for each copy change in both languages; the prototype has no Welsh.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page and every party picker, in both frontends, have no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 A and AA and 2.2 AA, on first render and in their error states, and a stored address name or address line holding markup characters is shown as text rather than rendered as markup.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page's Change links drop the visually hidden party name, as the prototype's do.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page served inside the live-animals journey at /<role path>/add-address that saves into the address book without the trader leaving the animals service.
requirements.why: Where the add page is served and which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the single-app prototype cannot express, so the INS frontend stays the address book's only writer, reached through the journey handshake; the animals frontend serves no /<role>/add-address page and its address-book service stays read-only (c-106).
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Add a new address' sends the trader to the INS address book's add page (repo-frontend-p15-159), whose page sits in the INS layout (trace-e2e-p9-055-m1); the journey's own create page was retired and answers 404 (trace-e2e-p9-080, trace-e2e-p9-081).

requirements.statement: Every party picker (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination) has an 'Add a new address' control to the INS address book's add page, carrying journey-type 'gbn-ag', the notification reference, the role's fulfilment id and a fresh handshake token, which the INS add page keeps as hidden fields and sends back unchanged; the pickers show no add control while the frontend runs in stub mode.
requirements.why: The handshake is how the INS address book knows which notification and role to return the new address to; it stays because the INS frontend remains the address book's only writer (c-106). DR1 asked for a route to add an address from every address-selection page (inc-053), and it now exists on every party picker.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker offers 'Add a new address' beside its heading and links to the INS add page through the link the hand-off issues for the party (repo-frontend-p15-056, repo-frontend-p15-159), all five pickers are proven to open the page (repo-tests-p7-002), the handshake carries the four parameters and comes back unchanged (trace-e2e-p9-013, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1), and stub mode offers no add control on any of the five pickers (repo-frontend-p15-036, repo-frontend-p15-158).

requirements.statement: The journey's address-return route accepts a return only when its fulfilment id names a role and its handshake token matches the single-use token the picker issued for that role, a missing, reused or mismatched token included, and looks the returned address id up in the signed-in organisation's own address book.
requirements.why: Stops a forged or replayed return from writing another organisation's address, or any address, into a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The return route is built and carries the fulfilment id and token back unchanged, with a fresh token on every render of the picker (trace-e2e-p9-016, trace-e2e-p9-070, trace-e2e-p9-070-m1); what no source in this area shows is a missing, expired, reused or mismatched token being refused (trace-e2e-p9-078), so the refusals are what is left to prove.

requirements.statement: When a return cannot be completed, the trader goes back to the role's picker: an address that is not found or is deleted shows 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.', and an address book that cannot be reached, or a save that fails, shows 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: A failed return must leave the trader somewhere they can carry on, with a reason they can act on.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the picker opens with the not-found message (repo-frontend-p15-059) or the unreachable message, marked as a recoverable error (repo-frontend-p15-060).

requirements.statement: A trader with no INS session who follows 'Add a new address' signs in through Defra ID first and then lands on the INS add page with the handshake intact.

requirements.deltaNote: Seen today end to end (trace-e2e-p9-052).

requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern tells assistive technology the page holds errors; today's address forms already do it.
