requirements.statement: The add-address page's fields carry browser autocomplete hints: organization for the name, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2 for town or city, postal-code, email and tel.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask personal-data inputs to identify their purpose.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every field but the name carries its hint: the name field has none, while address line 1, address line 2, town or city, postcode, email and phone carry theirs (repo-tests-p7-028). The journey's edit page already sets organization on the name (repo-frontend-p15-105).

requirements.statement: The add-address page's primary button reads 'Save and select'.
requirements.why: The design's copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The page reached from a party picker offers 'Save and select' (repo-tests-p7-003); the traces still show 'Save and continue' (trace-e2e-p9-067, c-396).

requirements.statement: 'Save and select' saves the new address to the address book, puts a copy of it on the notification for the role it was added for, and returns the trader to the Consignment addresses page, where the role shows the address with a 'Change' link; after a consignee is saved this way, the unset importer and place of destination rows offer the 'Same as consignee' shortcut that page already carries.
requirements.why: The design finishes the role in one step.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven: Save and select lands on the Consignment addresses page with the role filled and a Change link (repo-tests-p7-004), reached from the Overview task 'Consignment addresses' (repo-tests-p7-011, repo-tests-p7-006). The same-as shortcut rows are req-577 and req-578 and are already on the page (repo-frontend-p15-091). The traces still show the older return to the picker with the address merely preselected (trace-e2e-p9-071, trace-e2e-p9-073, c-396).

requirements.statement: A secondary 'Save and return to address page' button saves the new address to the address book without selecting it, and returns the trader to the role's picker, where the new address is listed first and nothing is selected.
requirements.why: The design lets the trader add an address and still choose among the book. Its checks are the primary save's, because the owner's decisions make both save buttons on a page check alike.
requirements.deltaNote: The button is on the page and lands on the picker with the banner and nothing selected, the new address listed first (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-007, repo-tests-p7-008). The picker it lands on shows eight addresses a page and restates the chosen address above the results (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-022, ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-025); the traces still show only 'Cancel and return to address page' (trace-e2e-p9-067, c-396).

requirements.statement: After either save, the page the trader lands on shows a GOV.UK notification banner titled 'Success' reading '<Name> address added to your address book', which stays on screen until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: The design, like DR1, confirms the address went into the address book; a message that leaves on a timer fails WCAG 2.2.1, so the banner stays and the INS frontend's script that hides it is removed (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: The banner is shown on the Consignment addresses page and on the picker, is still there ten seconds later and goes on reload (repo-tests-p7-004, repo-tests-p7-021, repo-frontend-p15-058).

requirements.statement: The add-address page offers a 'Cancel and return to hub' link to the notification's hub, which saves nothing.
requirements.why: The design's copy and destination.
requirements.deltaNote: The link is on the page and lands on the Overview saving nothing, leaving the role with only its named add link (repo-tests-p7-003, repo-tests-p7-009, repo-tests-p7-010, repo-tests-p7-012); the traces still show a 'Cancel and return to address page' button (trace-e2e-p9-075, c-396).

requirements.statement: An address added from the journey is saved into the signed-in organisation's address book with its email and phone, and is then listed in the address book and in every picker of a role it holds.
requirements.why: The design and today agree that a journey-added address joins the shared book.
requirements.deltaNote: A newly added address is listed in the picker (repo-tests-p7-008), created through the organisation-scoped address book API (trace-e2e-p8-011), and the picker already shows its town and postcode joined on one line as the design does (repo-frontend-p15-027).

requirements.statement: The add-address page and the postcode lookup pages are built from GOV.UK Frontend components only (input, select, checkboxes, hint, error summary, notification banner, buttons, back link and width classes).
requirements.why: The prototype's app-* field and heading classes are its own implementation, not a difference a trader sees, and its lookup pages already use GOV.UK Frontend alone.
requirements.deltaNote: The add page uses only GOV.UK Frontend components (trace-e2e-p9-068); the lookup pages are new and blocked with the rest of the lookup (req-647).

requirements.statement: The add-address round trip (both saves and cancel) is proven end to end from every party picker.
requirements.why: Each picker issues its own fulfilment id, so a return that works from one proves nothing about the rest.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add control is proven to open the page from all five pickers (repo-tests-p7-002), but each of the two saves and the cancel is proven once only (repo-tests-p7-004, repo-tests-p7-007, repo-tests-p7-009), the traces drove the round trip from the consignor picker alone (trace-e2e-p9-077), and the hand-off is skipped in stub mode so no fit spec covers it (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-146).

requirements.statement: A picked or added address is copied onto the notification, not linked: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record later leaves the draft's copy as it was, with no error, and the picker then neither preselects nor offers a deleted record.
requirements.why: A notification must hold the address it was made with; the design also stores a copy on the section.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today: a chosen address is copied rather than referenced (repo-frontend-p15-063), a deleted or role-less record counts as no selection (repo-frontend-p15-055, repo-frontend-p14-095), and the copy survives renaming and deletion of the record (trace-e2e-p8-001, trace-e2e-p8-006, repo-tests-p7-061).

requirements.statement: On the review page each consignment party reads back as the name followed by the address lines and country (GB shown as 'United Kingdom'), each on its own line, without the telephone number or email address, under a card titled 'Consignment addresses'. The plants frontend's check-answers place of destination, consignor and contact cards read back the same way, in the same increment: the name, then one line per address line, then the country, with no telephone number and no email address row.
requirements.why: The trader checks the copy the notification holds before submitting, and the owner's 17 November decision gives the addresses the same wording on check your answers, the overview task list and the addresses page. Plants has the same party cards, so it takes the same change at the same time (ruling 2026-10-09 pm), which withdraws plants' own d-013 addition of telephone and email to the contact card (c-293). The address-book record still carries both.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review shows each copied address as a block, name in bold then each non-empty field on its own line, telephone and email included (trace-e2e-p8-004, trace-e2e-p8-018), and the review already carries a 'Consignment addresses' card (repo-tests-p7-067). Plants' party cards today carry Name, Address, Telephone number and Email address rows with the address joined by commas, and lose telephone and email and read line by line in the same increment (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-045); the plants repo claims that show today's cards sit in the party-cards area's working set, not this one. The overview-and-review area writes the same card title, so the cross-area pass merges the two.

requirements.statement: Each party a notification holds has its own page for editing the copy the notification holds: in live animals one each for the place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination at /notifications/<journeyId>/<party>/edit, reached from the party's 'Edit details' link on the Consignment addresses page and from the review page's error for a broken copy; in the high-risk plants frontend the same page serves the consignor, the place of destination and the consignment contact, reached from the picker's current-address card and from check your answers.
requirements.why: The address book accepts records that break the notification's address rules, so a notification needs a way to correct its own copy without touching the book: a real validation and cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today in both frontends: five edit pages in live animals, which holds no consignment contact party (repo-frontend-p15-151, repo-frontend-p15-152), and three in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-052), reached from the 'Edit details' links (repo-tests-p7-055, repo-tests-p7-056, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-116, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-117). The older traces still show a live animals contact edit page (trace-e2e-p8-031). The design shows no such page; it is kept because rule-breaking copies need it (req-694).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is headed 'Edit address details', captioned with the party's own title (in live animals 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer' or 'Place of destination'; in plants 'Consignor', 'Place of destination' or 'Contact address'), titled 'Edit address details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', below the notification's journey strip.
requirements.why: The merged consignor-and-exporter party is the single Consignor, as the design's own section heading reads and the service's role vocabulary already holds, so the caption names the party once.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, the title and the strip are built (repo-frontend-p15-098, repo-frontend-p15-169, trace-e2e-p8-032-m1, trace-e2e-p8-090), and the caption is the party's title, the consignor's reading 'Consignor' (repo-frontend-p15-098, repo-frontend-p15-008, repo-tests-p7-056); the older traces still show 'Consignor or exporter' (trace-animals-fit-p15-045, trace-e2e-p8-032, c-482). Plants already captions the same page with the party's own title (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-053).

requirements.statement: The party edit page explains 'Changes apply to this notification only. Your address book is not changed.'
requirements.why: The trader must know the edit does not reach the book.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-099, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-054, repo-tests-p7-057).

requirements.statement: The party edit page asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code' (width 10), 'Country' (a plain select, 'Select a country' then the address book's country list by name, saving the code), 'Phone number' (a telephone input with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code') and 'Email address' (an email input with spellcheck off), in that order; only address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The page sets every field the address book record carries, so a corrected copy loses nothing. Its Country stays a plain select in this programme: the animals party address country's autocomplete is a follow-on ticket recorded in deferred.md (ruling 2026-10-09 pm).
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with these nine fields in this order in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-100, repo-frontend-p15-101, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-056, repo-tests-p7-059, trace-e2e-p8-035 to trace-e2e-p8-044). The live animals fit spec does not yet prove the country select or the phone hint (repo-frontend-p15-147); the tests repo proves the labels (repo-tests-p7-059).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's buttons are 'Save changes' and a secondary 'Cancel', with no save-and-return-to-overview control and no task-list caption, progress or hub link of its own.
requirements.why: The page is an aside from a picker, the addresses page or the review, not a step of the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-072, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-130, trace-e2e-p8-045).

requirements.statement: The party edit page opens pre-filled with every field of the notification's copy, the country select set to its code; before any address is picked for that party, opening or posting it sends the trader to the party's picker and saves nothing, and in plants a party the notification's commodity does not owe, such as a potato notification's consignor, is sent to the picker too.
requirements.why: There is nothing to edit until a copy exists, and nothing to edit for a party the notification does not hold.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-121, repo-frontend-p15-131, repo-frontend-p15-106-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-080, repo-tests-p7-058, trace-e2e-p8-034).

requirements.statement: The party edit page applies the address book's rules and messages: 'Enter a name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode', 'Enter a country' for a blank country, 'Enter a telephone number', 'Enter an email address', plus the length caps and the email-format check, with address line 2 and county never required and no rule on the shape of a phone number.
requirements.why: The copy must meet the same rules the address book sets, so a corrected copy is valid.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-110 to repo-frontend-p15-119, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-048, trace-e2e-p8-051), and plants copies the same rules and sentences from the address book (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-093, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-115). Both frontends label the postcode 'Postcode or Zip code' while its messages name only a postcode (repo-frontend-p15-115, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-104), which stays the address book's own wording.

requirements.statement: A refused edit answers 400, re-renders 'Edit address details' with the error summary and an error on each field, each summary link moving focus to its field, keeps what was typed (the country select resets to 'Select a country' for an unlisted value) and saves nothing; browser validation is off, every field is validated on every save, and a trader's own entry error is not logged as a refusal.
requirements.why: A refused edit must leave the notification's copy as it was, and the owner's 26 October decision is that a save with a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one and what they entered kept.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-130, repo-frontend-p15-133, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-136, repo-tests-p7-064, trace-e2e-p8-047, trace-e2e-p8-053).

requirements.statement: A valid edit replaces only this notification's copy of the party: the address book record and any other notification holding a copy of it are unchanged, nothing is sent to the address book, the party's picker opens with no address preselected, and no banner is shown.
requirements.why: The copy belongs to the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-122 to repo-frontend-p15-124, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-083, repo-tests-p7-060, repo-tests-p7-061, repo-tests-p7-062, trace-e2e-p8-028).

requirements.statement: Save changes, Cancel and Back on the party edit page return to where the edit was started, named by its return marker from a closed list, carrying the trail: in live animals the Consignment addresses page or the review page, falling back to the Consignment addresses page; in plants check your answers or one of its three party pickers, falling back to the party's own picker, never an outside address. Cancel is acted on before anything is checked and discards what was typed.
requirements.why: The trader comes back to the page they left, and a return value from the request is never followed off the service.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-153, repo-frontend-p15-154, repo-frontend-p15-129, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-135, repo-tests-p7-065, trace-e2e-p8-057). The older traces still show a live animals return to the consignment contact picker (trace-e2e-p8-046-m1, trace-e2e-p8-058), which the journey no longer has (repo-frontend-p15-152).

requirements.statement: If saving an edit fails with a recoverable backend error, the party edit page re-renders with status 500 and the recoverable-error message, and the held copy is unchanged.
requirements.why: A failed save must not lose or corrupt the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Built in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-132, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-090, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-136).

requirements.statement: The party edit page has Welsh copy for every piece of wording it shows, the character-limit sentences included, marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Today's Welsh copy, which needs Welsh Language Standards sign-off before it ships to users.
requirements.deltaNote: Present in both frontends and marked as a machine draft (repo-frontend-p15-142, repo-frontend-p15-172, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-127, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-128).

requirements.statement: The party edit page is built only from GOV.UK Frontend components and has no serious or critical accessibility violations against WCAG 2.2 AA.
requirements.why: Accessibility.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-140, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-124, trace-animals-fit-p15-067).

requirements.statement: A copy is checked against the notification's address rules: the address book accepts a record the rules refuse (such as a country name rather than a listed code), the picker lets the trader pick it, and its edit form then opens with no country selected.
requirements.why: The address book only checks a country is present, so the notification must catch a copy that breaks its rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Built and proven today (repo-frontend-p15-109, repo-frontend-p15-134-m1, trace-e2e-p8-013, trace-e2e-p8-022), and plants can check a held copy the same way (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-126).

requirements.statement: On the review page an answered party whose copied address breaks the address-book rules is named in a 'There is a problem' error summary ('Correct the address details for the <role>'), linked to that party's edit page with return=notification-view and repeated inside the party's row; a stored answer that has become invalid is named on its card; these entries come before the unfinished-card entries, and either stops Continue. A party not yet chosen is not flagged.
requirements.why: The trader must see which copy to correct and get straight to it. The single-app prototype holds no copy that can break a rule, so it cannot express these errors (c-139).
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today end to end (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-016, trace-e2e-p8-017, trace-e2e-p8-019), and plants links its own check-answers refusal straight to the party's edit page (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-118).

requirements.statement: While a copy breaks the rules, Continue on the review page is refused (400, same error summary) and a direct declaration submit is refused and sent back to the review page.
requirements.why: A notification with an invalid party address must not be submitted, and the review page is where submission is refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-020, trace-e2e-p8-020-m1, trace-e2e-p8-021).

requirements.statement: Correcting the copy on its edit page and saving returns to the review page with the error gone, after which the trader can continue to the Declaration and submit to 'Import notification submitted'.
requirements.why: Correction must unblock submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-023, trace-e2e-p8-024).

requirements.statement: Once a notification is submitted its copied addresses are frozen: renaming, moving or deleting the address book record changes neither the submitted view, whose status tag reads 'Submitted' and which offers no Change or Edit details links, nor an amendment, neither shows an error, and cancelling the amendment restores the submitted copy.
requirements.why: A submitted notification is a record of what was declared, and a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED like any other, no separate status being introduced.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (trace-e2e-p8-081, trace-e2e-p8-084, trace-e2e-p8-085), with one gap: no source edits a copy during an amendment and then cancels it (trace-e2e-p8-097).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the CPH number question applies when the consignment holds a commodity line for cattle (0102), pigs (0103), sheep (010410), goats (010420) or poultry, whether day-old chicks (01051111, 01051200, 01051300, 01051400, 01051500), adult birds (01059400, 01059910, 01059920, 01059930, 01059950) or hatching eggs (04071100, 04071911, 04071919). The rule is held as a list of the commodities that need a CPH number, in whatever shape the animals frontend chooses, and covers the rest of that list once the MDM catalogue holds them, with no further change. Where it does not apply, the CPH page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The plants frontend has no CPH number and gets nothing from this rule.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the commodities that need a CPH number, and the 11 November ruling makes it the source of truth for which commodities a conditional rule covers and has its allow-list replace the frontend's exempt list, so a commodity MDM adds no longer defaults to needing one. The page stays out of reach for a consignment whose commodities have no holding. This is the live half of the CPH rule: the 2026-10-09 ruling splits req-699 per set, and the germinal set has no CPH page at all (req-1832). The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling blocks the new catalogue on MDM but lets the CPH page go ahead on today's commodities, and never mirrors CPH into plants.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the rule is an exempt list, so every code MDM adds defaults to needing a CPH number, rabbits, reptiles, parrots, bees and insects among them (ruling-ian-2026-11-11-p1-033). The skip itself is built: a consignment with no CPH commodity cannot open the page and is sent to the consignment addresses page, with the skip logged (repo-frontend-p16-030, repo-frontend-p16-031). The germinal codes 05111000 and 05119985 leave the live-animals catalogue, so the live rule no longer names them.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page the CPH section is headed 'County parish holding (CPH) number', described 'The county parish holding (CPH) number identifies the holding where the animals will be kept.', sits after the place of destination, and before a number is saved offers the link 'Add a CPH number'.
requirements.why: The link text is Design Release 2.1's; a bare 'Add' action reads as nothing on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: The heading, description and position already match, and the CPH page is reached from an add control in the section (repo-frontend-p16-002, repo-tests-p1-166, repo-tests-p1-163). No current claim gives that control's text; the e2e trace, an earlier recording of the service, shows an 'Add' link with the hidden suffix ' county parish holding (cph) number' (trace-e2e-p6-073).

requirements.statement: A saved CPH number is shown on the consignment addresses page and on the review page as county/parish/holding with slashes, such as '12/345/6789', with a 'Change' link back to the CPH page.
requirements.why: The slashed form is how traders read and check a CPH number, and it is how Design Release 2.1 shows it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: The consignment addresses page already shows the slashed form (repo-frontend-p16-027, repo-tests-p1-162, repo-tests-p1-165) and already offers the Change link (trace-e2e-p6-076). No current claim shows the review page's CPH row; the e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows nine bare digits there (trace-e2e-p6-075).

requirements.statement: A valid CPH number is stored as nine bare digits, the three parts joined with no separators, and is split back 2/3/4 into its boxes when the page is shown again.
requirements.why: The stored shape is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: the record, and every stored notification, holds nine digits, so only the display gains slashes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026: saving stores the nine digits as one value and reopening shows them split back into county, parish and holding.

requirements.statement: The CPH page has the caption 'Addresses', the single h1 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH)', and the browser title 'Add the county parish holding number (CPH) - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: The heading and title are Design Release 2.1's and the service's alike, and the caption names the section the page belongs to, which the 17 November ruling words 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-003 shows the caption 'Addresses' directly above the H1 and repo-frontend-p16-004 that the H1 is the only level-1 heading; repo-tests-p1-157 proves the heading end to end. The fit and e2e traces, earlier recordings, show the caption 'Consignment parties', which the caption conflict sets aside.

requirements.statement: The CPH number and permanent address pages show the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the content.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-023 and trace-e2e-p6-108: the journey strip with the Draft tag and reference is on the CPH page, and the permanent address page shares the same strip.

requirements.statement: A collapsed 'What is a CPH number?' details component sits above the CPH inputs and, when opened, says 'A county parish holding (CPH) number is a unique 9-digit number used to identify land and buildings where livestock are kept, moved or handled.'
requirements.why: Traders who do not know their CPH number need to know what it is before they look for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-005 and repo-tests-p1-160 show the same summary and definition.

requirements.statement: The CPH help's second paragraph reads 'You can find your CPH number on documents from the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA) or by checking your holding details on GOV.UK.', in English and Welsh, with 'checking your holding details on GOV.UK' as a link to the GOV.UK 'Get a county parish holding (CPH) number' guidance (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/get-a-county-parish-holding-cph-number).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds a second place to find the number and the prototype wins; its href is only a placeholder, so the link opens the GOV.UK page its text names (c-117).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-006 and repo-tests-p1-160: the paragraph carries the GOV.UK clause and the link to that guidance, opening in the same tab. An earlier recording of the page, the claim c-117 sets aside, showed the second paragraph ending after '(APHA)'.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is asked as one fieldset with the small legend 'CPH number', not as a heading.
requirements.why: One question, one legend, so the page keeps a single h1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-frontend-p16-004: one fieldset group legended 'CPH number', and the legend is not a heading.

requirements.statement: The CPH question's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789', with no comma and no full stop, and describes the whole group.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's wording of the hint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-007 and repo-tests-p1-159: the group's hint reads 'For example 12/345/6789' with no full stop. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows 'For example, 12/345/6789.' (trace-animals-fit-p13-007).

requirements.statement: The CPH number is entered in three boxes in one row, laid out with the GOV.UK date-input pattern, with visible labels 'County' (2 wide), 'Parish' (3 wide) and 'Holding number' (4 wide), each asking for a numeric keypad. The boxes do not cut typing short.
requirements.why: A CPH number is three parts of 2, 3 and 4 digits; boxes sized to the parts make each part easy to enter and check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-008 and repo-tests-p1-158: three boxes labelled County, Parish and Holding number, two, three and four characters wide, in the GOV.UK date input's item classes; repo-frontend-p16-011 shows a whole number typed into County is kept rather than cut short.

requirements.statement: Each CPH box has autocomplete turned off and the pattern [0-9]* as well as the numeric input mode.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sets both so browsers do not offer unrelated saved values and phones show the digit keypad.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-009: each box carries inputmode numeric, pattern [0-9]*, autocomplete off and spellcheck off. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows plain text inputs with neither the pattern nor autocomplete off (trace-animals-fit-p13-014).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, each CPH box drops any non-digit as the trader types and stops at its maximum length.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the county parish holding boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and drops the type-behaviour row, and the boxes are built that way; the server's checks catch a non-digit instead (req-715).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010: the CPH page uses no JavaScript and takes and saves the number with JavaScript disabled.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, pasting into a CPH box keeps only the digits and spreads them across that box and the ones after it (2, 3 then 4 digits), so pasting 123456789 or 12/345/6789 into County fills all three boxes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer has the boxes follow the GOV.UK date input with no JavaScript on top and no paste spreading, and drops the type-behaviour row. A whole number pasted into County is kept and split by the server instead (req-2122).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-frontend-p16-011: nothing spreads a paste in the browser, and the server splits a whole number on save.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, focus moves to the next CPH box once a box is full, and Backspace in an empty box moves focus back to the previous box and deletes its last digit.
requirements.why: Out of scope: moving focus while the trader types is a change of context accessibility guidance warns against, and the interaction designer's 9 November answer has focus stay where the trader put it, with no JavaScript on the boxes at all.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-010 and repo-tests-p1-164: nothing moves focus between the boxes.

requirements.statement: Saving the CPH page with all three boxes empty raises no error: it saves no CPH number (clearing any saved before), the trader moves on to the consignment addresses page, and the CPH section stays incomplete, so the notification cannot be submitted until a number is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader move on and holds the gap at submission instead; required-to-proceed is a design choice the prototype can express, not a constraint it cannot. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page agrees: the CPH number is mandatory to submit, not mandatory to proceed. The 26 October ruling makes every save button on a page check the same thing as the others, which leaves this unchanged because there is nothing the page requires before the trader moves on (c-361).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-021 and repo-tests-p1-163: a blank save is allowed, nothing is saved and the trader lands back on the consignment addresses page, which still offers the add link; repo-frontend-p16-093 keeps the CPH number as one of the notification's obligations. The fit and e2e traces, earlier recordings, show the page refusing an empty save (trace-animals-fit-p13-032, trace-e2e-p6-090).

requirements.statement: A partly filled or wrongly formed CPH number is refused with one error per wrong part, in county, parish, holding order: 'Enter the county', 'Enter the parish' or 'Enter the holding number' for a missing part; 'County must be 2 digits', 'Parish must be 3 digits' or 'Holding number must be 4 digits' for a wrong length; 'County must only contain numbers', 'Parish must only contain numbers' or 'Holding number must only contain numbers' for a non-digit. Each box shows one message at a time, checked in that order, so a box of the wrong length that also holds a non-digit gets the length message. What is in County is read as a whole number only when Parish and Holding number are both empty and County holds nine digits once spaces and slashes are taken out.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 silently drops a part-entered number, which loses what the trader typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-012 to repo-frontend-p16-020 hold these nine messages, repo-frontend-p16-020-m1 shows one message per box in the order required, length, digits, and repo-frontend-p16-104 and repo-frontend-p16-105 when County is read as the whole number. repo-tests-p1-168 records that the end-to-end suite asserts none of them, so the coverage is the fit specs' alone.

requirements.statement: CPH errors re-render the page with every typed value kept: an error summary titled 'There is a problem' links each error to its box and moves focus there, one inline message on the whole question lists every error with a hidden 'Error:' prefix between the hint and the boxes, the group's accessible description includes the error, and only the boxes whose own part is wrong take the error border, none carrying a message of its own.
requirements.why: A three-part question needs one message on the question, so the trader reads every part to fix in one place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-023: every wrong part is named at once, each summary link moves focus to its box and typed values are kept; repo-frontend-p16-022-m1: only the boxes whose own part is wrong take the error border; trace-animals-fit-p13-042 and trace-animals-fit-p13-043: one message on the whole question, described by hint and error.

requirements.statement: A stored CPH number that is not nine digits is flagged on the page with 'The saved CPH number is no longer valid. Re-enter the county, parish and holding numbers.', linked to the County box, with all three boxes shown empty.
requirements.why: Stored data can predate today's rules; the trader is told to re-enter it rather than shown stray digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-025 holds the message against the county box. repo-frontend-p16-035 records that no fit spec exercises it, so the message has no test behind it.

requirements.statement: The CPH page opens with three empty boxes when nothing is saved, and with the saved parts filled back in (County 12, Parish 345, Holding number 6789) when a number is saved, however the page is reached.
requirements.why: The trader can check and change what they entered.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-161 shows the three boxes empty on opening and repo-frontend-p16-026 the saved parts split back into them.

requirements.statement: The CPH page's back link always goes to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH page is a step of the consignment addresses section, opened from it and returning to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-029: the Back link returns to the consignment addresses page, carrying the trail when the trader arrived with one and going to the plain addresses URL when the page was opened by its own address. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows it going to the notification overview (trace-e2e-p6-079).

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the CPH page always returns to the consignment addresses page, never on to the next step of the journey or the notification overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns every consignment-addresses step to the addresses page, from where 'Save and continue' moves on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026 and repo-tests-p1-162: saving a valid number returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, which shows it as 12/345/6789. The fit trace, an earlier recording, shows the opening run continuing to the contact page (trace-animals-fit-p13-026).

requirements.statement: The CPH page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, with no return-to-hub button and no cancel link.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): only pages the task-list overview links to end with the three return controls, and the CPH page is reached from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-028: the page offers 'Save and continue' alone, with no 'Save and return to overview' button and no 'Cancel and return to overview' link.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on the consignment addresses page never goes on to the CPH number page or the permanent address page, whether or not they apply: each is reached only from its own link in its section on that page, and returns to that page when saved.
requirements.why: In Design Release 2.1 the CPH number and the permanent address are sections of the consignment addresses page, each with its own add link, not steps after it. The 2026-10-09 ruling has a page opened from its overview task return to the overview, and removes the rule that the addresses page opened from the overview runs on to the CPH page. Where the addresses page's own 'Save and continue' goes next depends on the contact address question.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-066 marks the CPH number and permanent address pages as sub-pages, so 'Save and continue' never lands on either, and repo-frontend-p16-002 reaches the CPH page from an add link on the addresses page. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the addresses page going on to the CPH page when a CPH-triggering line exists, which c-116 sets aside.

requirements.statement: The CPH number and permanent address forms, and the plants consignment contact form, post back to their own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and a failed save re-renders the page with status 500, the recoverable-error banner and the trader's values kept. On the plants contact page an unavailable address book raises the error rather than treating the contact as deleted or unselected.
requirements.why: Real persistence and concurrency constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-108: the CPH and permanent address forms each post a hidden crumb and concurrency token; repo-frontend-p16-032 and repo-frontend-p16-068 answer a refused submit with 400 and a save that cannot complete with 500 and the page again in its recoverable-error state, values kept. The plants half is already built; this area's working set carries no plants frontend extract, so its evidence is the rulings' plants clauses alone.

requirements.statement: The CPH number and permanent address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in their error states, and the CPH question's group description names its hint and, on error, its error.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-033 and repo-frontend-p16-069: axe passes on the CPH page clean, with the whole number in County and in error, and on the permanent address page clean, with a reveal open and in error; trace-animals-fit-p13-043 shows the CPH group described by hint and error. The plants half is already built; this area's working set carries no plants frontend extract.

requirements.statement: Every English string changed or added on the CPH number and permanent address pages gets a Welsh version in the same change, marked as a machine draft that must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: These pages carry a Welsh version of every string, so a changed English string without its Welsh would leave the Welsh page wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-100 and repo-frontend-p16-101: each page's Welsh copy carries exactly the same key tree as its English twin; repo-frontend-p16-102 and repo-frontend-p16-103 mark both as machine drafts no translator has reviewed.

requirements.statement: Cats, dogs and ferrets need a permanent address; 'Other live mammals', which shares their commodity code 01061900, does not. It is asked for cats and dogs now, and the same rule takes in ferrets once the commodity catalogue holds them.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for a permanent address only for pets that APHA must be able to check, and the Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page names the same three commodities, all under the one code 01061900, so the rule needs the commodity name as well as the code. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling builds the permanent address page for cats and dogs now, and ferrets once the commodity catalogue, which waits on MDM, holds them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-047: the Permanent address section is shown for a domestic cat and absent for cattle, and repo-frontend-p16-063 keeps the page out of reach for a consignment that needs none. Ferrets are not in today's commodity catalogue, so the rule reaches them with no further change once MDM's catalogue holds them.

requirements.statement: The permanent address is its own page in the live-animals set's addresses section, opened from the consignment addresses page at a slug of its own (not the prototype's /permanent-address/select path): caption 'Addresses', heading 'Permanent address', browser title 'Permanent address - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and a back link to the consignment addresses page. It applies only when the consignment holds commodity 01061900 with at least one species that needs a permanent address; otherwise the page cannot be opened and sends the user to the consignment addresses page. The address fields are not asked on the animal identification form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 (and DR1 before it) asks for the permanent address as its own step, so a trader can answer it, leave it and come back, instead of reopening animal identification. The 2026-10-09 ruling gives the page a real slug in the addresses section, because the prototype never decides URL paths, and the 17 November ruling words that section 'Addresses' wherever it appears.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-036 serves the page at /notifications/{journeyId}/permanent-address as a sub-page of the consignment addresses hub, repo-frontend-p16-037 shows the caption 'Addresses', the H1 and the title, repo-frontend-p16-067 the back link and repo-frontend-p16-063 the redirect when no line needs one; repo-tests-p2-045, repo-tests-p2-048 and repo-tests-p2-059 prove the address, the redirect and the Back link end to end. The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the fields inside the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-028).

requirements.statement: When the permanent address applies, the consignment addresses page has a 'Permanent address' section explaining 'A permanent address is where an animal:' with the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', and the link 'Add a permanent address' to the permanent address page; for cats it has no CPH section.
requirements.why: The section is how the trader reaches the permanent address step in Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: The section and its 'Add a permanent address' link are built, shown only while a permanent address is still owed and only for a commodity that needs one (repo-tests-p2-046, repo-tests-p2-047, repo-frontend-p16-059, repo-frontend-p16-063). No current claim quotes the section's explanation or its two bullets.

requirements.statement: Once at least one animal has a saved permanent address, the consignment addresses page's Permanent address section lists every animal that needs one by its card heading, each with its saved address, and one 'Change' link that goes straight to the permanent address page. Each address reads as the name, then address line 1, then the town, postcode and country separated by commas, with the country named in words.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lists each animal's permanent address on the addresses page, so the trader can check every animal's answer without opening the page again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the section counts the animals that have one, such as 'added for 2 animals', and shows one shared address once with a single Change link when several animals use the place of destination (repo-frontend-p16-059); repo-frontend-p16-060 already offers each saved address with its animal's label and the country name resolved, and repo-tests-p2-052 and repo-tests-p2-053 prove the read-back and the Change link end to end.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows the GOV.UK warning 'Providing a false address is an act of fraud', with no full stop.
requirements.why: Traders must know a false address is fraud before they give one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-038: the warning sits below the heading on the permanent address page, with no full stop.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page explains 'A permanent address is where an animal:' followed by the bullets 'will permanently reside' and 'can be checked by the Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA)', then asks 'Where will their permanent address be?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's explanation and question for the page.
requirements.deltaNote: No current claim shows the explanation or the question on the permanent address page, whose claimed content runs from the caption and heading to the warning and then straight to the animal cards (repo-frontend-p16-037, repo-frontend-p16-038, repo-frontend-p16-039). The e2e trace, an earlier recording, shows the same copy on the animal identification form (trace-e2e-p6-030, trace-e2e-p6-031).

requirements.statement: The permanent address page shows one card for each animal that needs a permanent address, as many as the number of animals entered for that species, each headed with the species' common name, its scientific name in brackets and a running number, such as 'Domestic cat (Felis catus) 1'; species that do not need one get no cards. The same heading names the animal in every error summary message on the page and in the consignment addresses page's Permanent address section.
requirements.why: Each animal can live at a different address, and the page asks for all of them in one place; Design Release 2.1 names each animal by its common and scientific names so the trader can tell which animal each card and each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card is a GOV.UK summary card titled with the species' Latin name and the animal's number, such as 'Felis catus 1' (repo-frontend-p16-039, repo-tests-p2-049), and the error summary names the animal the same way (repo-tests-p2-056); the common names are already there, labelling each animal on the other pages that list saved permanent addresses (repo-frontend-p16-107).

requirements.statement: Each animal card shows, in inset text, the identifiers already entered for that animal as 'label: value' (such as 'Microchip: MICROCHIP-1'), leaving out blank ones, and no inset when none are entered.
requirements.why: The trader can tell which animal each card is for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-040: each card shows the animal's identifiers in an inset, one line per identifier it has, reading '<identifier label>: <value>'.

requirements.statement: Each animal card has a radio group with the legend 'Select an address' and two options, 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' and 'Enter a new address', with neither chosen when the page first opens.
requirements.why: Most pets live at the place of destination; reusing it saves the trader typing the same address again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-041: each card asks one question legended 'Select an address' with exactly those two options, neither pre-selected until the trader has answered; repo-tests-p2-050 proves both options end to end.

requirements.statement: Once a place of destination is given, the 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' option shows that address on one line as its hint, the party name then its address lines, such as 'Tech Imports Ltd, 18 Dockside Road, London, E14 9GE, United Kingdom', and carries no hint while the notification has no place of destination.
requirements.why: The trader sees which address they are reusing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-042: the option is hinted with that address on one line, the party name then its address lines joined by commas, and carries no hint while there is no place of destination.

requirements.statement: The 'Enter a new address' option has the hint 'This is where they will stay after spending 48 hours at the place of destination.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader what the permanent address means for a pet that moves on from the place of destination.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-043 carries the 48-hour hint verbatim on that option.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals that animal's own address fields inside its card, as a GOV.UK conditional reveal.
requirements.why: The fields are only needed when the place of destination is not reused.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044: choosing 'Enter a new address' reveals the address boxes inside that card alone.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address asks for 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', 'County (optional)', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Email address' and 'Phone number' (hint 'For international numbers include the country code'), has no country field, and is stored with the country code GB.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws these eight fields and no country, and a permanent address is a Great Britain holding, so the country is saved rather than asked (c-360).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 holds the eight boxes in that order, repo-frontend-p16-045 the phone hint and the email and phone input types, and repo-frontend-p16-046 that no country is asked and the address is stored with country code GB; repo-tests-p2-051 proves the eight labels end to end.

requirements.statement: In a new permanent address, 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number'.
requirements.why: This is Design Release 2.1's field order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-044 lists 'Email address' then 'Phone number' as the last two of the eight boxes. The e2e trace, an earlier recording of the identification form, shows phone before email (trace-e2e-p6-032).

requirements.statement: When 'Enter a new address' is chosen for an animal, its name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, email address and phone number are required, showing 'Enter a name or organisation name', 'Enter address line 1', 'Enter a town or city', 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', 'Enter an email address' and 'Enter a phone number' on the blank fields; address line 2 and county are optional.
requirements.why: The choice decides whether an address is needed, so the fields are required exactly when the trader says they will enter one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-047 holds these six messages with address line 2 and county optional, and repo-tests-p2-054 proves a blank new address is refused with HTTP 400. repo-tests-p2-062 records that only the name's message is proven end to end, so the other five rest on the fit specs.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page, each address error in the error summary names its animal by that animal's card heading, such as 'Enter a name or organisation name for Domestic cat (Felis catus) 1' and 'Enter address line 1 for Domestic cat (Felis catus) 1', and links to the field; the inline message on the field leaves the animal out. The summary lists the refusals in card order and then each card's own field order, and a place-of-destination refusal is not animal-named.
requirements.why: With several animals' forms on one page, the summary must say which animal each error is about.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-051 names the animal in the summary and keeps the field's own message plain, repo-frontend-p16-052 orders the summary by card and field and moves focus to the control each link names, and repo-tests-p2-056 and repo-tests-p2-057 prove both forms of the message end to end. The animal is named today as 'Felis catus 1'; the heading it names changes with the card heading.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal before a place of destination is given shows 'Add a place of destination before you can continue' on that animal's radios and in an error summary titled 'There is a problem', linked to the radios.
requirements.why: There is nothing to reuse until the place of destination exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-050 refuses that card's question with the message verbatim and logs the refusal at warn level.

requirements.statement: An animal left with no option chosen raises no error: the page saves the other animals and moves on, and the permanent address section stays incomplete until every identified animal that needs one has an address, which a notification cannot be submitted without.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader save what they know and come back; completeness is checked at the section and at submission. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page agrees: a permanent address is mandatory to submit, and only for an animal whose commodity is cats, dogs or ferrets (c-363).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-054 saves an unanswered animal as unanswered rather than refusing it and keeps the other animals' answers, repo-frontend-p16-094 completes the task only when every identified animal that needs one holds an address, and repo-tests-p2-060 submits a cat consignment once its permanent address is answered.

requirements.statement: When the permanent address page shows errors, each animal's chosen option stays selected and a chosen 'Enter a new address' keeps its fields open with what was typed, nothing is written to the notification until every card passes its checks, and the page works the same with JavaScript and without; when the page is opened again, each animal's saved choice is selected and its saved address filled back in, the optional county included.
requirements.why: The trader never has to re-enter what they already gave, and a part-refused save never leaves half the page stored.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-053 keeps every other card's option checked and values on the page with JavaScript and without, repo-frontend-p16-053-m1 writes nothing until every card passes, repo-frontend-p16-057 fills each saved choice and address back in, and repo-tests-p2-053 and repo-tests-p2-058 prove both end to end.

requirements.statement: When a line needs a permanent address but none of those lines has a number of animals yet, the permanent address page shows 'Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.', with 'consignment details' linking to that page, instead of the animal cards; when such a line has a number of animals but no animal identified yet, it shows 'Identify an animal on identification details before you can continue.', with 'identification details' linking to the animal identification page. Saving from either state saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: The cards depend on the animals counted and identified for the line, which are given on the consignment details and identification pages; in the service a card is an identified animal, so a counted but unidentified line has its own message.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-097 and repo-frontend-p16-098 show both messages with their links, repo-frontend-p16-065 saves nothing and returns to the consignment addresses page from either state, and repo-frontend-p16-099 logs both.

requirements.statement: Saving 'Same as the place of destination (POD)' for an animal gives that animal the place of destination's address as its permanent address; saving 'Enter a new address' gives it the animal's own name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode, country United Kingdom, email and phone. The answer is written onto the animal's own record on its commodity line, one commit per line that holds an answered animal.
requirements.why: Each animal's permanent address must be held with the notification, whichever way it was given. The 2026-10-09 ruling keeps this behaviour and leaves its storage shape to the real service's model (c-239).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-055 writes the choice and the address onto the animal's record on its line, one commit per line, and repo-frontend-p16-056 stores a copy of the place of destination rather than a pointer to it, which is the shape the plan chose.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address keeps every field in its own place: the county is saved, and a saved address with no address line 2 opens with the town in 'Town or city' and the postcode in 'Postcode or Zip code'.
requirements.why: Persistence is a real constraint the prototype cannot express: Design Release 2.1 loses the county and shifts fields on return, which the real service must not copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-057 fills a hand-entered address back into its own boxes, the optional county included, and repo-frontend-p16-044 keeps each box its own named field.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page ends with the primary 'Save and continue' button alone, which saves and returns to the consignment addresses page.
requirements.why: DR1's inc-161 judgement (rule b): a page reached from another page, not from the task-list overview, ends with the primary button alone, like the CPH page and the party pickers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-066: the page offers 'Save and continue' alone, with no return-to-overview button and no cancel link, and saving returns the trader to the consignment addresses page.

requirements.statement: The review page shows the permanent address as one row per animal, labelled with the species' common name and number (such as 'Domestic dog 1'), whose value is that animal's saved address; with no animals identified it shows a single row 'Address'.
requirements.why: The trader checks each animal's permanent address before submitting.
requirements.deltaNote: No current claim shows the permanent address on the review page; repo-frontend-p16-060 offers each saved address to the pages that list it, with the animal's label and the country name resolved, which is what the review row needs.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own permanent-address routing and storage are not reproduced: /permanent-address resetting the answer and redirecting to /permanent-address/select, the unused 'Are all the animals going to the place of destination?' page, the retired /permanent-address/enter-address redirect, the notification-level permanent address and 'Permanent addresses added for N animals' summary it stores alongside each animal's address, a posted choice other than the two options being ignored, errors kept in the session after a failed save, and the failure when only a later animal is given an address.
requirements.why: Out of scope: these are prototype internals and faults with no behaviour a trader should see beyond landing on the per-animal page, the real service has none of these routes to retire, and it holds each permanent address on the animal's own record.

requirements.statement: The prototype's custom heading, card, width and layout classes on the contact and permanent address pages, its own permanent-address script, its 'action' button values and its /design-release-2.1 mount paths are not reproduced.
requirements.why: Out of scope: they are how the prototype is built, not behaviour a trader sees, and the real pages use GOV.UK Frontend components.

requirements.statement: The contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets has the h1 'Contact address for consignment', no section caption, and the browser title 'Contact address for consignment - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and the service agree on the page's identity, and the plants contact page shares it.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: Directly under the contact page's heading, body text reads 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'
requirements.why: It tells the trader whose address this is; DR1 inc-046 judged the copy sentence it replaces loses nothing the trader can act on. The 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling has plants' contact picker take the new intro in the same increment, because plants has the same page with the same hint.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: Each live-animals notification has its own hub page in the live-animals set, addressed by the notification at the set's own notification path (/live-animals/notifications/{reference}).

requirements.statement: Above the 'Overview' heading the hub shows the notification's status as a tag ('Draft' until it is submitted) and the notification reference, which the notification already has before any task is answered, in the form 'GBN-AG-', a two-digit year, a hyphen and six upper-case letters or digits (for example GBN-AG-26-DGWJ47).

requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-044-m1 shows every saved page committing to the stored notification (the concurrency token rises per save), so the draft is already saved whenever the hub shows.

requirements.statement: Transit countries are optional for submission: the review never marks them unfinished on their own account and an empty transit-countries answer does not stop Continue, reading back as 'Not applicable'.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, a notification is complete enough to submit when origin, commodity selection, consignment details, import reason, additional details, arrival, transport and consignment addresses are complete, and, when more than one species is selected, every species has at least one identified animal record, a record counting as identified once one identifier is filled; no contact address is asked for, and the review's 'nothing unfinished' verdict uses exactly this test.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-115 and p6-139 make readiness one test that refuses Continue, and p6-105 sets the identifier bar per species.

requirements.statement: The trader reaches the review from the overview's 'Review and submit' and a submitted notification's view from the notification list's View link; Continue on an unfinished notification re-shows the review with its errors and a 400 status, and Continue on a complete one goes to the declaration page.
requirements.why: Both sources behave this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-117 keeps the trader on the review after a refusal, p6-124 posts Continue on to the declaration, and repo-tests-p3-064, p3-054 and p3-056 drive both paths.

requirements.statement: The review names a rejected document on every visit and a document still being scanned once Continue is refused, and either message stops Continue and the declaration submit.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-112 marks a rejected document's card as soon as the review opens, p6-113 holds the still-scanning message until Continue is refused and p7-041 refuses the declaration for a document still being scanned.

requirements.statement: An unanswered consignment role makes the Consignment addresses card unfinished, so the review's error summary carries the single 'Complete consignment addresses' entry linking to that card and names no party separately; a role the trader has not answered is never reported as an address error.

requirements.statement: The review's error summary takes focus only after a refused Continue, not on a plain visit, and every card and section heading can take focus from a summary link.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-121 takes focus only after a refusal and repo-tests-p3-065 proves focus moving to the summary on a second refused Continue.

requirements.statement: A draft review ends with 'Continue' alone, with nothing after it, its Delete being the warning control in the view header.
requirements.why: A draft's review carries the view header (c-246), whose Actions menu gives the trader the Delete that Design Release 2.1 draws beside Continue on its header-less journey review.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-122 ends a draft review with Continue alone, p6-016 and p6-021 put 'Delete notification' in the header, and repo-tests-p3-053 and p3-040 assert both.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the review ends with three actions in order: 'Continue' (submits), a secondary 'Cancel amend' button that opens the cancel-amendment confirmation, and a red 'Delete' control leading to the delete confirmation.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-123 ends an amendment review with Continue, Cancel amend and Delete notification, and repo-tests-p3-057 asserts that order.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the review is headed and titled 'Review your notification' when first opened, and 'Review before re-submitting' once any answer differs from the submitted version; putting a changed answer back returns the heading to 'Review your notification', and a fresh amendment raised after a cancelled one opens with that heading too.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-005 and p6-006 switch the heading and title on whether the amendment's answers differ from the submitted version.

requirements.statement: An amendment's review opens with no error summary and no card errors; if the trader presses Continue on an amendment that is not complete, it is refused and the re-shown review names the card that is missing an answer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides errors on an amendment's review, but real validation must still refuse an incomplete resubmission and say why.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-119 holds every answer error silently on an amendment until Continue is refused, and p6-120 then reveals the summary.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view shows the review page header in place of the journey heading: the notification reference as the h1, with the status tag 'Submitted' beside it and no caption above. The header is keyed on the real route and the stored status, and is drawn in the set's own review template with the shared status strip switched off; the shared layout is not changed.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-003, p6-011 and p6-012 head a submitted notification by its reference with a 'Submitted' tag and no journey strip, and repo-tests-p3-033 and p3-062 assert it.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view has the page title '<reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', a draft's unfinished view is titled 'Error: <reference> - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and the journey review of an amendment keeps 'Review your notification - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: A page title names the page before the service, a GOV.UK accessibility duty that overrides Design Release 2.1's title with no page name (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p3-037 and p3-036 assert both titles, and repo-frontend-p6-003 makes the reference the browser title for a draft and a submitted notification.

requirements.statement: Under its header, a submitted notification's view shows 'Date submitted: <d Month yyyy>' from the notification's stored submission instant, naming the day in the service's own time zone with the month in full, and shows no date line at all when the notification holds no submission instant.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view header offers 'Amend this notification' as the first item of its Actions menu, and a draft's offers none.

requirements.statement: A notification's view header ends its Actions menu with 'Delete', leading to the notification's delete confirmation, on a draft and on a submitted notification alike. It reuses the shared notification actions wording 'Delete'.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification's view is read-only and shows that notification's own submitted answers: no Change links, no row actions, no errors, no submit form and no buttons below the cards.

requirements.statement: An action-required notification missing only animal identifiers shows the header warning 'You need to complete animal identifiers'.

requirements.statement: Submitting records the date the notification was declared and submitted, which the view's 'Date submitted' line and the confirmation page read, and the notification record holds no list of outstanding items.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows a green 'Past' status tag in its view header, and its Actions menu offers no 'Amend this notification'. It is held as a status of its own, never replacing an existing one.

requirements.statement: Opening the view of a notification reference that does not exist answers 404 and shows the service's standard 'Page not found' page, in live animals and in high-risk plants.

requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when.

requirements.statement: Signing in to the INS front door lands the trader on the home, which only a signed-in trader can open.
requirements.why: The home is the signed-in landing page in Design Release 2.1 and today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p4-001: sign-in redirects straight to the service root.

requirements.statement: The INS aggregated read model holds one document per notification, created when the notification is created and updated as it is edited and submitted, and can lag the journey a little. The home's table, the home's counts and the drill-downs all read it.
requirements.why: The read model is the cross-journey source the home was handed off to; its eventual consistency means a list or count can briefly trail a change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-027 and repo-tests-p14-036: one aggregated document per notification, written as soon as its answers are saved and updated on submit rather than duplicated; repo-tests-p14-018 and trace-e2e-p15-094: a submitted notification reaches the INS home only after a wait, so the store is eventually consistent.

requirements.statement: The INS front door reads the home's counts and the drill-down lists from ins-backend, carrying the request's trace id, and from its built-in stub when stub mode is on (never in production).
requirements.why: The front door already reads the read model this way for its table; the home and drill-downs need new reads (counts by category, filtered lists) on the same terms.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the front door makes one read, GET /notifications with the page, and the sort and reference when set (repo-insfrontend-p2-054).
requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when.

requirements.statement: If the read model cannot be loaded, the home and drill-downs still render their heading, flag a recoverable error, respond with HTTP 500 and log the failure; an error already shaped for the framework is passed on.
requirements.why: A failure in another service is a constraint the prototype cannot express; the front door already handles it this way for its table.
requirements.deltaNote: Today this handling covers only the table on / (repo-insfrontend-p2-048-m1); the home's counts and the three drill-downs need it too.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when.

requirements.statement: The home's 'Create new' button carries Welsh copy with the same key as the English, marked as a machine draft not to ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The front door keeps Welsh copy beside every English copy file; Design Release 2.1 shows only English. The button goes ahead now under Sam's 9 October rulings, so its Welsh goes with it. Templates are parked, so no 'Use template' key is added (c-416).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p2-067 and repo-insfrontend-p2-066: the Welsh copy already reads 'Creu newydd' for the button, in the machine-draft file marked not to ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

requirements.statement: The home and each drill-down have no serious or critical axe violations against the WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA tags, proven by a fit test.
requirements.why: The front door proves its dashboard accessible today and the new pages must hold the same bar.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the axe fit test covers the table page at / (repo-insfrontend-p2-075); the drill-downs have none.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when.

requirements.statement: The home and drill-downs keep the standard GOV.UK header (logo to gov.uk, service name to the service root), the 'Skip to main content' link and the standard GOV.UK footer.
requirements.why: The shared layout already provides them on every INS page.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p4-006-m1: every INS page has the GOV.UK header, the skip link and the GOV.UK footer.

requirements.statement: Following a link from the home into the animals or plants frontend lands the trader there signed in, without a second sign-in, and the notification is found there by its reference number alone.
requirements.why: The home links across service origins, so the cross-service sign-in must hold for the links to work, and the reference number is the only value that travels with the trader.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-107: opening a submitted notification from the INS home lands on the animals frontend signed in without another sign-in; repo-tests-p14-019 and repo-tests-p14-100: the link opens the notification in the service that owns it, carrying only its reference number.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the category dashboards' own content — the animals and plants dashboards' intro text, filters, sort options and empty states.
requirements.why: The home stops at a category's notification list; those pages belong to the notification list's own requirements.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the submission confirmation page, the read-only notification view and the declaration step.
requirements.why: They belong to the live-animals journey's own requirements; here they only show how a notification reaches the read model.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the address book pages reached from the home's navigation, their titles and the journey into them.
requirements.why: The address book has its own requirements.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an 'At a glance' band of Alerts, Errors and Messages cards with 'View alerts', 'View errors' and 'View messages' links, and a 'Create a new notification' button label on the home.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements; the per-category glance cards and 'Create new' of the current design replace that earlier design.

requirements.statement: The live animals notification list is the page at the live-animals set root in the animals frontend, and it reads the animals backend's notification list.
requirements.why: The afternoon rulings of 9 October keep each notification list in its own frontend and reframe it in place, built on the animals frontend and animals backend; this replaces, for this programme, the move to the INS frontend that the morning ruling had kept from Rhys's DR1 judgement (c-159).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-001 (proven by trace-e2e-p3-001 and repo-tests-p3-067): the list is already the animals frontend's page at the live-animals set root, and it reads the animals backend's list (repo-frontend-p4-024, repo-perftests-p2-042); what the page shows changes under the requirements that follow.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's browser title is 'Dashboard - Import notification service - GOV.UK', with the caption 'Dashboard' above an h1 naming the category, 'Live animals'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every list 'Dashboard' and heads it with the category, so a trader can tell which category's notifications they are looking at; the 9 October afternoon ruling names this frame for the reframed list. Plants' own list takes the same title in the same increment (req-2028).
