requirements.deltaNote: Today the page title and the h1 are both 'Import notification service' (repo-frontend-p4-004), so the browser title reads 'Import notification service - Import notification service - GOV.UK'; the 'Dashboard' caption already exists (repo-frontend-p4-003).

requirements.statement: On the live animals, germinal products and plants lists the heading is followed straight away by the 'Create new' button, with no introductory paragraph, no guidance sentence and no Messages link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list goes straight from its heading to its actions; plants takes the same frame in the same increment (9 October afternoon ruling, claim 55).
requirements.deltaNote: Today one paragraph about telling the authorities about imported live animals sits under the animals heading, and plants' list has its own intro paragraph about high-risk plants (its guidance-link sentence renders only when a guidance address is supplied, and none is). The 'Use template' button Design Release 2.1 puts beside 'Create new' is not built while templates are parked (req-1038).

requirements.statement: The list page has a 'Back' link to the overall home.
requirements.why: Not built: the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every page Design Release 2.1 points at the overall dashboard to the set's own list, and has the INS front door reached through the service navigation as today, so the list, now the set's own landing page, carries no Back link (c-298).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has a primary 'Create new' button, which starts a live animals notification and carries the list's category into the create journey. Where it points and how the category is carried are the services' to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 starts a notification from 'Create new', carrying the category the trader was looking at; the 9 October rulings keep the destination and the category, not the prototype's create-notification?category= address (c-251), and name 'Create new' starting a notification as part of the reframed list's frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a GOV.UK start button 'Start a new notification' posts to the set's notifications path, which creates a draft and its reference on every press and redirects straight to its origin page (repo-frontend-p4-007, p4-008).

requirements.statement: The live animals and germinal products lists have a secondary 'Use template' button beside 'Create new' that goes to the templates page.
requirements.why: Not built: Design Release 2.1 offers starting from a saved template on every category list, but templates are parked and dropped for now, so the lists offer no way into them (c-420), and the button is built only when templates are planned again. Plants was never in scope for templates.

requirements.statement: The list page has an h2 'Summary' section with two glance cards: 'Action needed' with 'Tasks requiring your attention' and a 'View tasks' link to the action-needed page filtered to the category, and 'Status updated' with 'Changes in the past 24 hours' and a 'View updates' link to the changes page filtered to the category.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts what needs the trader's attention at the top of each category list; the 9 October afternoon ruling counts the list's Summary cards (inc-139) as the INS dashboard's summary information, blocked until its requirements firm up.
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October): the counts, glance cards and drill-downs are summary information, re-distilled once those requirements exist.

requirements.statement: The list's 'Action needed' glance card shows a live count for the category of the notifications that need something from the trader, matching the Action needed list its link opens.
requirements.why: The count is only useful if it agrees with the drill-down page. It is summary information, blocked with the Summary cards, and what counts as needing action now waits on the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce (16 November ruling).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS dashboard's requirements firm up (Sam, 9 October) and the outstanding-actions banner the dashboard designs under test introduce is agreed (Sam, 16 November), because nothing action-required is shown until then.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the notifications sit under an h2 'Notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 heads the list section 'Notifications'; DR1's 'My notifications' row was only deferred, never judged; plants takes the same frame. DR1's inc-021 also left open whether the breadcrumb label that shares these words on the delete and cancel-amendment pages follows the heading, which those pages' own area settles.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use the medium h2 'Your notifications' (Welsh 'Eich hysbysiadau'), which the animals frontend also uses as the breadcrumb label on the delete and cancel-amendment pages.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list the search and sort sit in one column above the cards inside the 'Notifications' section, with no 'Filter notifications' heading and no separate one-third filter aside beside the results; on the live animals list the 'Additional filters' disclosure follows them, above the tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lays the list out as one column: search and sort, then the filters disclosure, then the tabs and cards. Plants takes the same frame in the same increment, its filters aside (9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists are two columns inside the full-width content column: a one-third aside headed 'Filter notifications' (h3) holding the search, and a two-thirds column holding the results count, sort and cards (repo-frontend-p4-013, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-054).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field is labelled 'Search by'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label; today's 'Keyword or reference' promises a keyword search the service does not give.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field is labelled 'Keyword or reference' (small bold label) and named referenceNumber.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search field has the hint 'Keyword, notification number, commodity, consignee or consignor'.
requirements.why: The hint tells the trader what the search matches.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's search is submitted by a real submit button that shows only a magnifying-glass icon and whose accessible name is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search control; the 9 October afternoon ruling lets the icon-only button stand as long as it is a real submit button of the GET form (c-299).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button is a standard primary GOV.UK button with the visible text 'Search'.

requirements.statement: A search on the live animals list lists the notifications whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains the searched text, ignoring case.
requirements.why: The hint promises a keyword search over those facts, and DR1's own inc-019 row read the same three things as searchable. The prototype cannot persist or query, so its search is inert; a real search box that does nothing would mislead the trader, so the real service applies it (c-162).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the term is passed to the listing only as referenceNumber, an exact match on a complete reference, so a commodity or a party name finds nothing (repo-frontend-p4-016, repo-tests-p3-089).

requirements.statement: After a search the field keeps the searched text, and searching with an empty or whitespace-only field clears the search and lists everything again.
requirements.why: The trader can see and change what they searched for; both Design Release 2.1 and today keep the text.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-017, p4-022 and p4-023: the field is filled with the current term, and a blank or whitespace-only term means no filter.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list, search, sort and every additional filter are one GET form to the list's own path, submitted by the search button or by the 'Apply filters' button; it carries the current tab (unless it is the default tab) and the current page (when above 1) as hidden fields, so the result stays on that tab. Changing a select or a radio submits nothing by itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts sort and filters inside the search form, and both its search button and its 'Apply filters' button submit that one form; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it one GET form whose submit buttons search, sort and filter on the server, so the page works without JavaScript. Today search and sort are two forms and a search always restarts at page 1.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the search form carries only the sort as a hidden field (no page, no tab), and the sort is a separate GET form (repo-frontend-p4-018, p4-036).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select is labelled 'Sort by:'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the sort control.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the select is labelled 'Sort by' with no colon (small bold label).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's sort select offers exactly 'Newest first', 'Oldest first' and 'Arrival date', in that order, with no unselected 'Select one' option.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the sort three orderings; DR1 already rejected an unsorted 'Select one' state, so the list is always sorted, and its own sort-label row was deferred while the list was thought temporary, never judged (c-167).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the options are 'Arrival (newest to oldest)', 'Arrival (oldest to newest)', 'Date created (newest to oldest)' and 'Date created (oldest to newest)'.

requirements.statement: The live animals list is always sorted and the sort is applied for real: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by when the notification was created, 'Arrival date' orders by arrival date newest first, and with no sort chosen the list is ordered by arrival date newest first with 'Arrival date' selected.
requirements.why: DR1 judged the list always sorted; the prototype never orders its list, so the real service applies the orderings, keeping today's default order (which the prototype's completed tab also shows).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the default is 'Arrival (newest to oldest)' and any unknown value falls back to it; no end-to-end test proves the order of the cards (repo-tests-p3-098).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no 'Update sort' button: the chosen sort is applied by the search button, or by 'Apply filters', with the rest of the form, and the chosen option stays selected after the page reloads.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's sort has no button of its own; DR1 only deferred this difference, and the 9 October afternoon ruling has one submit button for the whole form, with no select submitting on change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a separate GET sort form with a secondary 'Update sort' button applies the sort, carrying the page and the search as hidden fields (repo-frontend-p4-029, p4-034).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has an 'Additional filters' disclosure built from the GOV.UK details component inside the search form, closed on load and open whenever an arrival-date, date-range or status filter is set, so after applying a filter the trader sees the filters they chose.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the extra filters out of the way until the trader needs them; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the disclosure from GOV.UK details rather than the prototype's custom chevron markup (c-299).

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By arrival date' column of small GOV.UK radios 'Today', 'Tomorrow' and 'Next 7 days' (legend visually hidden, the same words shown as its heading); choosing one and searching lists only notifications arriving in that range, and the choice stays checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader find what is arriving soon; the prototype's filter is inert, so the real service applies it.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'By date range' column with the hint 'For example, 27/3/2026' and two MoJ date pickers, 'Start date' and 'End date' (a 'Choose date' calendar opening on the current month, weeks starting Monday, each a plain text field without JavaScript); the list shows only notifications arriving between the two dates, and the entered dates are kept.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's date range. DR1's own row records that the design never says which date a date filter narrows, so three things settle it on the arrival date: the radios beside it name the arrival date in their legend and heading, DR1's row has those radios built on this same range rather than on parameters of their own, and the arrival date is the only date Design Release 2.1's card shows at all. The 9 October afternoon ruling accepts the MoJ date picker here, because the range is a search filter, not a date read from a document, and the interaction designer keeps that picker as the one every other date in both frontends uses.

requirements.statement: When the start or end date cannot be read as a date, or the end date is before the start date, the list shows a GOV.UK error summary and an inline error on the date field ('Enter a real start date', 'Enter a real end date' or 'End date must be the same as or after the start date'), opens 'Additional filters', keeps the entered text in the 'Start date' and 'End date' pickers, and lists notifications without the date-range filter.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so a date the filter cannot use is answered with an error rather than silently ignored; the prototype still sets the labels and keeps the entered dates, and the GOV.UK date-input error pattern supplies the messages (c-166, which the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps). The 26 October ruling sets the same shape for any answer that is missing or not valid: an error message for each one, the trader kept on the page, and what they typed never dropped.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Status' select offering 'All statuses' (the default, meaning no status filter), 'Draft', 'Amend', 'Submitted' and 'Past'; choosing one and applying the filters lists only drafts not being amended, notifications being amended, submitted notifications or completed notifications respectively, and the choice stays selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's status filter offers each stage a notification can be at, using the same words as its tabs and status tags. 'Past' matches nothing until a real source of completion exists (16 November ruling), and the select still offers it because the design names it. Which words the tabs and this filter use is the tab vocabulary question (c-497).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has three tabs, 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past', built as MoJ sub navigation, each a link that loads the page with that tab chosen; 'Submitted' is the list with no tab chosen, an unknown or missing tab shows 'Submitted', and following a tab drops the search, sort and filters. The tab parameter's name and values are the animals frontend's.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 separates submitted notifications, unfinished work and finished notifications, and drafts keep a home on the list, which DR1 said must not be lost; the 9 October afternoon ruling builds the tabs as MoJ sub navigation on the animals frontend's own list, and the prototype never names query parameters (c-251). The 9 October afternoon ruling named the then prototype's tabs 'In progress', 'Draft' and 'Completed', while the 26 November prototype names them 'Submitted', 'Draft and Amend' and 'Past'; which words are built is an open question whose default is the 26 November prototype's (c-497).

requirements.statement: The 'Submitted' tab lists submitted notifications, the 'Draft and Amend' tab lists drafts and notifications being amended, and the 'Past' tab lists completed notifications.
requirements.why: Each tab holds the notifications at that stage, as Design Release 2.1 sets them out; a notification submitted with something outstanding is submitted like any other (16 November ruling), and a notification being amended sits with the drafts, as the design groups them (c-165).

requirements.statement: A notification being amended is listed in the 'Draft and Amend' tab with a yellow 'Amend' tag and its status-driven actions (Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives a notification being amended its own yellow 'Amend' tag and groups it with the drafts under 'Draft and Amend'; listing it there is how the page reads, which the backend's AMEND lifecycle does not stop (c-165). DR1's judgement keeps its status-driven actions (c-160).
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amending notification is listed with every other notification and there are no tabs; its tag already reads 'Amend' in yellow from the shared status kit (repo-frontend-p4-085).

requirements.statement: The 'Submitted' and 'Draft and Amend' tabs each show their count in bold brackets, such as 'Submitted (2)' and 'Draft and Amend (3)'; 'Past' shows none, even when selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 counts the notifications still in play; the counts belong to the tabs, which the 9 October afternoon ruling builds now, not to the blocked Summary cards.

requirements.statement: Under the tabs the cards sit under an h3 naming the tab: 'Submitted notifications', 'Draft notifications' or 'Past notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's subheading for each tab panel.

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows 8 notifications a page.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling pages the reframed list 8 at a time, which is also Design Release 2.1's page size for every list and the figure the rest of the estate pages at; how many rows a page holds over a dataset that grows is not the prototype's to set (23 November ruling), so the ruling is the authority and the prototype agrees with it.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page size comes from the listing: 25 from the animals backend (end to end) and 20 from the frontend stub (fit), and the page reports the size it is given (repo-frontend-p4-070).

requirements.statement: A list of more than one page shows GOV.UK pagination with numbered page links, a 'Previous' link from page 2 and a 'Next' link before the last page; a list of one page, or no results, shows no pagination. This holds on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses numbered pagination; today both lists have only Previous and Next. Pagination is kept and wanted wherever a list is paged (25 November ruling), and plants takes the same paging in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both lists use block-style pagination with only Previous and Next links and no page numbers, reading 'Next' and 'Previous' rather than the 'Next page' and 'Previous page' the suite's other lists use (repo-tests-p3-082).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and a page past the last shows the last page, on the live animals list as on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 clamps the page, so a stale or hand-typed page never shows an empty list; plants' list already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-075, p4-076 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-033: both lists already ignore a page that is not a whole number of at least one and clamp a page past the last to the last page.

requirements.statement: The live animals list's page links keep the tab (unless 'In progress'), the sort (unless the default), the search text and every additional filter.
requirements.why: Because the real search and filters apply, a page link that dropped them would show a different, unfiltered list on page 2 (c-163).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Previous and Next keep the sort (unless the default) and the reference search, and the list's address carries only what differs from the default view; there are no tabs or filters to keep (repo-frontend-p4-035, p4-074).

requirements.statement: Neither the live animals list nor plants' list shows a 'Showing ... results' count above the cards, on any tab or page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category list works out a results count but never shows one; DR1 only deferred its rewrite of the count; plants takes the same frame. The only count line the live animals list shows is the filtered results line when a status filter is set.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a small bold line above both lists' cards reads 'No Results', 'Showing 1 Result', 'Showing N of T Results' or 'Showing S to E of T Results' (Welsh twins on plants), worked out from the page, the size and the total, so it can disagree with the cards shown when deleted rows are dropped after the page is cut (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-057).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a search that matches nothing, with no status filter set, shows an empty list with no message about it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message on its lists outside the filtered results line, which a status filter brings up; plants takes the same frame.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a search with no match on either list replaces the results line with 'No notifications found' and shows no cards.

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a tab or list holding no notifications shows no cards and no message about the empty list; on the live animals list the tab keeps its subheading and description.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no empty-state message: an empty tab shows its subheading and description only. Today's sentence also wrongly says the animals list is session-scoped. Plants' own copy quoted the same sentence, but the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same frame (c-300).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a user with no notifications who is not searching sees 'You have not started any notifications in this session.' on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-068; on plants the same English sentence and the Welsh 'Nid ydych wedi dechrau unrhyw hysbysiadau yn y sesiwn hon.'), and the animals list shows 'No Results' beside it.

requirements.statement: Each notification card on the live animals list and on plants' list is labelled for screen readers 'Notification <reference>' and has the reference as its h3.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card names itself to assistive technology, and the 9 October afternoon ruling names the cards for screen readers in the reframed frame; the reference heading already exists on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each card on both lists is a GOV.UK summary card with the reference (or the notification's own id before a reference is issued) as its level-3 title, but no 'Notification <reference>' accessible name.

requirements.statement: A live animals card shows its facts in two rows: 'Commodity', 'Arrival date', 'Consignee' and 'Notification status', then the quantity, 'Origin' and 'Consignor'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card leads with what is coming, when, to whom and its status, and shows no inspection fact.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows eight facts in three rows: Commodity, Origin, 'Arrival at destination'; Consignee, Consignor, Status; 'Date created', 'Date submitted' (repo-frontend-p4-039).

requirements.statement: The card labels the arrival date 'Arrival date', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the card, and DR1's own rename row was deferred rather than judged. The 17 November ruling words the arrival date 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the question page, check your answers and the overview task list, and the 27 November ruling keeps the card's own 'Arrival date' (c-421).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Arrival at destination' on the animals card and 'Arrival' on plants' card.

requirements.statement: The card labels the status 'Notification status', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label for the status fact; plants takes the same card layout.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label is 'Status' on both cards.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's card shows its quantity as 'Number of animals', from the notification's own count in the animals backend's record.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows how much is coming on every card; today no card shows a quantity, and the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card's facts from the animals backend's record.

requirements.statement: The card shows no 'Date created' and no 'Date submitted', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card has no dates other than arrival; today's 'Date submitted' is also blank on every card, submitted ones included, on both lists.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards show 'Date created' and 'Date submitted', each the day the event happened in the service's own time zone; 'Date submitted' is blank in every end-to-end trace, and blank on a plants draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-077, trace-e2e-p3-033).

requirements.statement: The card writes the arrival date as the day, the full month name and the year, such as '21 June 2026', on the live animals list and on plants' list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's card writes the arrival date with the full month name, in its code and its render alike, and nothing overrides the prototype here (c-164).
requirements.deltaNote: Today both cards write the arrival date as day, short month name and year, such as '7 Nov 2026' and '5 Mar 2026' (trace-animals-fit-p2-031, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-058); the tests repo already reads the animals card's date as 'd Month yyyy' (repo-tests-p3-073).

requirements.statement: On the live animals list and on plants' list, a card whose notification has no commodity, no arrival date or no quantity yet shows 'Not applicable' for that fact.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows 'Not applicable' for a fact the notification does not hold yet, so an empty value is never mistaken for a missing card row.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a fact with no answer yet is shown with an empty value and no placeholder on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-045, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-061).

requirements.statement: The live animals card's commodity is the notification's commodity name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the commodity as the trader chose it; germinal products need the product type as well as the species (req-1738).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card shows the commodity's name, falling back to its commodity code and then to nothing (repo-frontend-p4-041, p4-047); a commodity chosen as Bos taurus shows 'Cow'.

requirements.statement: A draft's status is a 'Draft' tag in a colour set apart from the blue 'Submitted' tag, a submitted notification's status is a default blue GOV.UK 'Submitted' tag, and a notification being amended shows a yellow 'Amend' tag; plants' card follows the same styles for Draft, Submitted and Amend and keeps its red 'Late' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tags every status on the list: the default GOV.UK tag for 'Submitted', a draft style for 'Draft' and yellow for 'Amend'; a notification submitted with something outstanding is shown as 'Submitted' like any other (16 November ruling, c-418). The draft colour is built from a GOV.UK tag colour modifier rather than the prototype's custom class. Plants mirrors the component (c-301).
requirements.deltaNote: Today every status on both lists is a tag: Draft blue, Submitted green, Amend yellow, Deleted grey and never shown (repo-frontend-p4-085, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-025). The completed style is req-1739.

requirements.statement: A delayed notification shows a 'Delayed' tag on an error card, with the reason for the delay as its message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows delays on the list; its own message there is placeholder copy, so the reason the record carries is shown instead.
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; no delay status or reason reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification the authorities have finished with shows the status 'Past' and is listed in the 'Past' tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 files finished notifications under 'Past' by their completed status. 'Completed' stays out as a status until a real source of completion exists (16 November ruling), so nothing reaches this tab yet. The words follow the tab vocabulary question's default (c-497).
requirements.blockedBy: A real source of completion exists (Sam, 16 November): the authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes back to the notification record, and no completed status reaches the service today.

requirements.statement: A notification chosen for inspection shows an extra 'Inspection' fact with a 'Required' tag at the end of the card's second row.
requirements.why: Not built: the Design Release 2.1 card no longer shows an 'Inspection' fact, so nothing on a card marks a notification for inspection; the inspection page that lists them is summary information, blocked with the INS dashboard.

requirements.statement: A live animals card keeps its status-driven actions, each named for screen readers with ' notification <reference>': a draft offers Resume, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a submitted notification offers View, Amend, 'Copy as new' and Delete; a notification being amended offers Resume, 'Copy as new', 'Cancel amendment' and Delete. Amend and 'Copy as new' stay link-styled buttons that post, each in its own form and in the same typeface as the links, while View, Resume, 'Cancel amendment' and Delete are links.
requirements.why: DR1 judged that the card keeps its status-driven links rather than DR1's flat 'Copy as new' and 'View', and that judgement wins over Design Release 2.1's same flat pair. Without it a trader could not resume a draft from the list. The 19 November ruling's one-form-each rule for posting buttons is what the card already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-051, p4-052 and p4-053 (proven by trace-animals-fit-p2-037, p2-042 and p2-044 and by repo-tests-p3-075 and p3-076): the card already offers these sets in this order, each posting action in its own form with the CSRF crumb and visually hidden ' notification <reference>' text.

requirements.statement: A card whose notification is delayed or completed offers a single 'View' link, opening the notification's review page.
requirements.why: DR1's judgement keeps the status-driven actions only for the cards the service builds today (draft, submitted, being amended); for the statuses the real service does not yet have, Design Release 2.1's card gives a single 'View' link (c-160).
requirements.deltaNote: Today a notification in any status other than Draft, Submitted or Amend has no actions on its card (repo-frontend-p4-054).
requirements.blockedBy: The authorities' case system (PIMS Dynamics) sends post-submission outcomes (inspection required, delayed, completed) back to the notification record; until it does, no card is in these statuses.

requirements.statement: After an action that sends the trader back to the list with that action's flag on the redirect (such as a delete), the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner with role alert, titled 'Success', carrying that action's message; plants' deletion banner carries the same 'Success' title. Each list feature holds this wording in its own copy, and the shared notificationActions wording that other pages use stays as it is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one success banner titled 'Success'; the message itself is set by the action. The 9 October ruling keeps the flag on the redirect (such as ?deleted=1) rather than a message held for the trader (c-252), and the afternoon ruling gives plants' banner the same title in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners are titled for the action: 'Notification deleted' with 'The notification has been deleted.' on both lists (repo-frontend-p4-066, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034), and each banner shows only when its own flag is on the address.

requirements.statement: The list's success message is held for the trader, shown once and then cleared.
requirements.why: The 2026-10-09 ruling drops moving the success banner to a message held for the trader and shown once (inc-140 criteria 2 and 3): the flag on the redirect, such as ?deleted=1, stays, so the banner shows whenever the list is opened with it (c-252).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banners show whenever the list is opened with the action's flag on the address, and that stays (repo-frontend-p4-066, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034).

requirements.statement: The notification list's success banner, the deletion message included, does not dismiss itself on the live animals list or on plants' list: it stays until the trader leaves or reloads the page.
requirements.why: A message that disappears on a timer can vanish before a screen reader or a slow reader reaches it (WCAG 2.2.1); this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's 5-second auto-dismiss, and the 9 October afternoon ruling confirms it (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-066 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-034: today's deletion banners are GOV.UK success banners announced to assistive technology, with no timer that dismisses them.

requirements.statement: The live animals list keeps its stale-action banner and its 'There is a problem' banner when an action started from a card fails.
requirements.why: Concurrency and failure handling are real constraints the prototype cannot express, so they stay although Design Release 2.1 shows neither.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-067: when an action on a notification fails for a reason worth retrying, the list is shown again with the service's recoverable-error banner above it.

requirements.statement: Every list string has a Welsh version, on the animals lists and on plants' list, marked as a machine draft that ships only after a translator signs it off under the Welsh Language Standards, and no label is left blank in either language.
requirements.why: Both real services are bilingual and their list Welsh is an unreviewed machine draft; Design Release 2.1's new strings need Welsh twins too.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every English list key on both lists has a machine-drafted Welsh twin, not yet reviewed by a translator, and the sort options are paired with their wording by position rather than by name (repo-frontend-p4-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-063).

requirements.statement: The live animals list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, empty or with cards, and does not scroll sideways at 1280px or at 769px wide; plants' list has no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, with or without its amend-refused banner.
requirements.why: Both real lists meet this today and the reframed lists must keep meeting it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-079 and p4-080, and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-084 and p1-085: fit tests prove no serious or critical axe violations on either list and no sideways scroll on the animals list.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's root in the animals frontend renders its own copy of the reframed list: the caption 'Dashboard', the h1 'Germinal products', the same search, sort, additional filters and tabs pointed at its own address, and a 'Create new' button that starts a germinal products notification in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal products the same list as live animals under its own heading. The 27 November ruling ships the germinal list now as a copy of today's live animals list, and the animals dashboard rows that reframe the live animals list carry the germinal copy with them in the same increments (c-496).

requirements.statement: The live animals list shows only live animals notifications: a germinal products notification never appears on it, and a notification whose record holds no category counts as live animals.
requirements.why: A trader looking at one category must not see another's notifications; the animals backend stores each notification's category on its record, an absent category meaning live animals, and the reframed list reads that record.

requirements.statement: Deleted notifications never appear on any list or in a search.
requirements.why: A deleted notification is gone for the trader; both Design Release 2.1 and the real services leave it out.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-050 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-030: both frontends drop a deleted row even when the service returns it, and the INS read model leaves DELETED notifications out of its own list (repo-insbackend-p2-039).

requirements.statement: A newly started notification appears on the list straight away.
requirements.why: A trader must find their new draft on the list as soon as they have started it; the list reads the animals backend's own record, not an event-populated read model that lags writes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p3-069 and trace-e2e-p3-049: a newly started notification is found on the list by its reference, though the suite still reopens the list and searches again for up to 15 seconds before the card shows (repo-tests-p3-070, req-2351).

requirements.statement: A list shows only the notifications of the signed-in trader's organisation, and the animals backend's list API refuses a caller that does not say which organisation it acts for.
requirements.why: Authentication and data separation are real constraints the prototype cannot express; today the animals backend's list serves every trader's notifications to every caller, while both frontends show only what the trader's own session knows about.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each frontend narrows the list to the notifications its own session knows about (repo-frontend-p4-069, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-029), so a trader signing in afresh sees none of their earlier notifications, although the journey's backend calls already carry the trader's organisation in their headers (repo-perftests-p2-044).

requirements.statement: The INS backend's notification read model and its GET /notifications list API keep their record fields, event handling, paging, sorts, reference search and scoping as they stand, and no notification list reads them.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling builds the reframed lists on the animals frontend and animals backend and drops the INS read model's part of the list rows; the INS dashboard that does read it is blocked until its requirements firm up, and its category gap (germinal notifications listed without their category) is a known gap until then.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list returns, for each notification, every fact the card shows: the reference number, status, commodity name, arrival date, origin, consignee name, consignor name, the notification's category, and its number of animals or, for germinal products, its total quantity (units or pieces) with each line's species and product type. A fact the notification does not hold is returned as empty.
requirements.why: The card cannot show facts its list API does not return; the 9 October afternoon ruling takes the card facts from the animals backend's record, and that list item carries no category or quantity today.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the card reads the reference, status, commodity, origin, arrival date, consignee, consignor and the created and submitted dates from each row (repo-frontend-p4-039, p4-041, p4-046, repo-plantsfrontend-p1-091), and no row carries a category or a quantity; the card reads the arrival date only from the top level of the row, while a helper that reads it from the transport answers goes unused (repo-frontend-p4-087).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by category (live animals or germinal products, absent meaning live animals) and by tab (submitted notifications, drafts together with notifications being amended, or completed notifications), and reports how many notifications the 'Submitted' and 'Draft and Amend' tabs each hold.
requirements.why: Each set's list and each tab shows only its own notifications, and the 'In progress' tab shows its count; with both lists built on the animals backend, the category filter belongs to its list (c-159).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API takes a search text and returns every notification whose reference number, commodity, consignee or consignor contains it, ignoring case and surrounding spaces, paged like any other list.
requirements.why: The list's search matches a keyword across those facts; today the list API matches only one exact, case-sensitive, whole reference and returns at most one notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend sends the search to the service as referenceNumber (repo-frontend-p4-024), which matches only a whole reference: a complete reference returns exactly that notification and any other text finds nothing (repo-tests-p3-085, repo-tests-p3-089).

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API filters by status (drafts not being amended, notifications being amended, submitted or completed) and by an arrival-date range (from and to dates, either optional).
requirements.why: The status select and both arrival-date filters need the API to narrow the list; today the list API has no filter beyond an exact reference.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API sorts by creation date (newest or oldest first) and by arrival date, defaults to arrival date newest first, and breaks ties on a second key so no notification repeats or goes missing between pages.
requirements.why: 'Newest first' and 'Oldest first' order by creation date and 'Arrival date' by arrival; a single-key sort with ties (such as drafts with no arrival date) is unstable across pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend sends an arrival-date or created-date sort to the service (repo-frontend-p4-033, repo-tests-p3-091), defaulting to arrival date newest first (repo-frontend-p4-031), and nothing shows a second key that breaks ties.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's list API serves 8 notifications a page, numbered from 1, and reports the page, size, number of elements, total elements and total pages.
requirements.why: The list shows 8 a page and builds numbered pagination from the totals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals backend serves 25 a page end to end (repo-tests-p3-081) and the frontend reports the size it is given (repo-frontend-p4-070); the 1-based page and the page totals already reach the frontend.

requirements.statement: The INS backend's list API answers a bad request, such as a page below 1, with a 400 validation problem response naming the field, and an unexpected failure with a 500 problem response that hides the underlying error.
requirements.why: This is the INS list API's behaviour today; the notification lists no longer call that API in this programme (req-1097), so nothing here is built or changed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insbackend-p1-029 and p1-104: a page below 1 answers 400 'Validation Error' with an errors map keyed 'page', proven by repo-insbackend-p1-118.

requirements.statement: The INS read model's own defects and operational details stay as they stand: a non-numeric page likely answering 500, a shared reference likely answering 500, failed events never retried and so lost, no dead-letter queue shown, untested lastUpdated sorts and deletion end to end, the metrics, logging, port, switched-off OpenAPI, template README, empty seed, missing rulings ledger and the absence of a get-one endpoint.
requirements.why: None of these is a difference from Design Release 2.1; the programme does not fix them, so they are reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the INS backend as it is today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's demo data is not built: its seeded notifications and their fixed references, the arrival, created and submitted dates it works out from today for them, the states it fakes by a notification's position (action required, status changes, delays, inspection, Plants), the fixed glance counts on its overall home, its placeholder number of animals, its demo consignee and consignor names, its fixed commodity-code look-up, its category guess for unlabelled notifications, its session ordering of drafts, submissions and seeds, and its design-release version switch.
requirements.why: These are demonstration mechanics of the prototype, not rules for the real service, which holds real notifications with their own facts and statuses.

requirements.statement: The prototype's list with no category is not built: its fallback heading 'Live animals and germinal products', its use of the live animals path for an uncategorised list, its 'By type' select (shown only without a category, hiding Plants) and its uncategorised 'View tasks' and 'View updates' links; no list combines categories, and plants' list stays plants only.
requirements.why: The rulings keep each notification list in its own frontend for its own set, and the afternoon ruling says this programme no longer builds the INS notification lists the overall home linked to, so a list combining categories has no place; plants' list has no set or type filter of its own.

requirements.statement: The address book lives in the INS frontend at /address-book, reached from an 'Address book' item in the service navigation, and that item is marked active (aria-current) on the list, view and delete pages. The navigation also has a 'Log out' link.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts the address book behind the service navigation; DR1's inc-062 ruling already placed the real book in the INS front door rather than the animals frontend.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend serves the list at /address-book (repo-insfrontend-p4-001, repo-tests-p12-001), its navigation links to it and marks it active on the list, view and delete pages (trace-ins-fit-p2-004, trace-ins-fit-p2-007, trace-ins-fit-p3-069), the fit suite proves the links (repo-insfrontend-p4-101), the INS dashboard links across to it (repo-tests-p12-039), and the list is the service's signed-in landing page (repo-tests-p12-129). The navigation's Templates item belongs to the shared layout area.

requirements.statement: A signed-out user opening any address book page is sent to sign in and returned to the page they asked for; a user whose identity holds more than one organisation chooses one first, and a session with no organisation is refused.
requirements.why: The book belongs to an organisation, so every page needs a signed-in user and their organisation: an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: Signed-out requests redirect to sign-in with the requested path (trace-e2e-p15-010, trace-e2e-p15-011) and sign-in returns there (repo-tests-p12-128); a multi-organisation identity picks one (repo-tests-p12-130, repo-tests-p15-124); the list needs the session's organisation (repo-insfrontend-p4-003).

requirements.statement: Address book page titles read '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK': 'Address book - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the list, '<address name> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the view page and 'Delete this address? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' on the delete page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 titles every page with the GOV.UK suffix and a hyphen separator.
requirements.deltaNote: The pages set their titles to 'Address book', the address's name and 'Delete this address?' (repo-insfrontend-p4-004, repo-insfrontend-p6-004, repo-insfrontend-p6-070), and the last captured rendering appends ' | Import notification service' with a pipe separator and no GOV.UK suffix (trace-ins-fit-p2-008, trace-ins-fit-p2-037). No claim records the suffix changing.

requirements.statement: The list page's heading is 'Address book'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading; today agrees.
requirements.deltaNote: The list's h1 is 'Address book' (repo-insfrontend-p4-004, repo-tests-p12-002, trace-ins-fit-p2-009).

requirements.statement: Under the heading the list page shows, in large body text, 'Manage your addresses for use across all your import notifications'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's intro copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS list's lead paragraph reads this (repo-insfrontend-p4-005, repo-tests-p12-003). The older captures that show 'Manage addresses used across import and export services.' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The list page has an 'Add a new address' button (a link styled as a button) that starts the add-an-address flow, shown whatever the list holds, on every tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers adding from the list; the add flow's own path is the INS service's.
requirements.deltaNote: The button shows always, whichever tab is selected (repo-insfrontend-p4-006), and opens the address type step (repo-insfrontend-p4-007, repo-insfrontend-p4-103, repo-tests-p12-217), including on an empty book (repo-insfrontend-p4-133).

requirements.statement: On the list page the 'Add a new address' button comes directly under the intro, above the 'Filter addresses' panel and the category tabs.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's order of the page's controls.
requirements.deltaNote: The list template renders the button before the filter disclosure and the tabs (repo-insfrontend-p4-006, repo-insfrontend-p4-009).

requirements.statement: Search and the Type filter sit inside a collapsible 'Filter addresses' disclosure with a chevron, collapsed when the list loads with no search or Type filter applied, so the search field is hidden until the user opens it. It is the GOV.UK details component, styled to match the design, so it opens and closes without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 hides the filter behind a disclosure; the 9 October afternoon ruling makes it the GOV.UK details component so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: The filter is a GOV.UK details disclosure, 'Filter addresses', closed on load (repo-insfrontend-p4-009), and the fit and end-to-end suites prove it opens and closes with and without JavaScript (repo-insfrontend-p4-116, repo-tests-p12-010).

requirements.statement: The search field is labelled 'Search'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label.
requirements.deltaNote: The search input is labelled 'Search' (repo-insfrontend-p4-010, repo-tests-p12-007). The older captures labelled 'Search addresses' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The search field's placeholder is 'Search by name, address or country', and it has no hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts this text in the field as a placeholder.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the same words are the field's hint, read as its accessible description, with no placeholder (repo-insfrontend-p4-011, repo-insfrontend-p4-117).

requirements.statement: The search field has an icon-only search button whose accessible name is 'Search'. It is a real submit button of the filter form, so pressing it, or pressing Enter in the search field, submits the form with or without JavaScript.
requirements.why: The design's icon button, made a real submit control so the page works without JavaScript (the 9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: The button shows a magnifying-glass icon with the visually hidden text 'Search' (repo-insfrontend-p4-012), and a search submitted with it or with Enter works with JavaScript on or off (repo-insfrontend-p4-118, repo-tests-p12-011).

requirements.statement: Search matches the trimmed text, case-insensitively and anywhere inside a field, against an address's name, every address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode), the names of the countries containing the text and the Type column labels of the roles it holds; a multi-word search is matched as one phrase, taken literally, and a blank search is no search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 searches 'by name, address or country' and over the type labels; the address book holds role codes and country codes, so the INS frontend widens the search with the matching roles and countries.
requirements.deltaNote: The address book matches q over the name and address lines as a literal phrase (repo-addressbook-p3-021 to repo-addressbook-p3-025), and the INS frontend adds the codes of matching countries and the roles whose labels match (repo-insfrontend-p4-018, repo-insfrontend-p4-019), proven by name, line, county, country and role label (repo-insfrontend-p4-121, repo-insfrontend-p4-130, repo-tests-p12-029 to repo-tests-p12-031).

requirements.statement: The address book's country filter takes one or more ISO alpha-2 codes, each trimmed and blank ones dropped, matched exactly against the stored code, organisation-scoped, leaving out deleted addresses, and combined with the search term and search roles by OR; an unrecognised code simply matches nothing.
requirements.why: The address book stores a country code, so a search 'by country' reaches it as the codes of the countries whose names match.
requirements.deltaNote: countryCode is repeatable, trimmed, exact and unvalidated, and ORs with q and searchRole (repo-addressbook-p3-027 to repo-addressbook-p3-030, repo-addressbook-p3-040).

requirements.statement: The address book filter is a GET form to the address book list carrying the selected tab, the search and the chosen Type, and the address book API filters the whole tab by the search and the Type and returns 8 a page. The parameters that carry the tab, the search and the Type, and the values the tab parameter takes, are the INS service's to name. Pressing the search button, or pressing Enter in the search field or on the Type select, submits the form; typing or changing the Type select submits nothing by itself. The page works fully without JavaScript, and no script re-requests the list as the user types. The same holds locally, in the stub, on the compose stack and in CDP.
requirements.why: The real book is paged on the server, so filtering must run there; the 9 October rulings keep the server-side filters and the GET form, and design dropped filtering as the user types.
requirements.deltaNote: The filter is a GET form carrying the tab in a hidden field (repo-insfrontend-p4-014), the list request sends the tab's roles, the term and the matched countries and roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-071), typing or choosing a Type without submitting changes nothing (repo-insfrontend-p4-122, repo-insfrontend-p4-128, repo-tests-p12-073), and it works with JavaScript off (repo-tests-p12-079).

requirements.statement: While a search or Type filter is active, the submitted list's results line counts the matches (for example 'Showing 1-2 of 2'), and pagination shows only when the matches run past one page of 8.
requirements.why: The count and the pages describe what the user is looking at, which after a search is the matches.
requirements.deltaNote: A search with two matches reads 'Showing 1-2 of 2' with no pagination, and eleven matches page at 8 (repo-insfrontend-p4-119, repo-insfrontend-p4-120, repo-tests-p12-076).

requirements.statement: The list is split into category tabs, in this order: 'Origin and Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer' and 'Transporter'. The tabs are the Ministry of Justice sub navigation component, labelled 'Address types', each a link that loads the address book list on that tab, with the selected one marked as the current page. The query parameter that carries the tab, and its values, are the INS service's to name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups the book by category; the 9 October afternoon ruling draws the tabs as MoJ sub navigation so they work by link without JavaScript, and EUDPA-776 left three categories on main (c-499).
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows the three tabs in this order as an MoJ sub navigation of links labelled 'Address types', selected by the addressType parameter and working without JavaScript (repo-insfrontend-p4-024 to repo-insfrontend-p4-026, repo-insfrontend-p4-115, repo-tests-p12-148, repo-tests-p12-154).

requirements.statement: Each tab panel has its own heading: 'Origin and Consignor addresses', 'Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses' or 'Transporter addresses'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's panel headings.
requirements.deltaNote: Each panel has its h2 (repo-insfrontend-p4-029, repo-tests-p12-152).

requirements.statement: An address is listed on the one tab whose category holds the roles it has: Origin and Consignor holds place of origin and consignor; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer and place of destination. Because an address's roles all come from one group, it is never listed on more than one tab, and the list API can be asked for one category's addresses. How the address record holds its roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's category membership; the 5 November ruling keeps an address's roles in one group, so one record sits on one tab.
requirements.deltaNote: Each role belongs to one address type and each tab lists exactly its roles' addresses (repo-insfrontend-p4-088, repo-insfrontend-p4-111, repo-tests-p12-059), and roles of two groups are refused (repo-tests-p12-162).

requirements.statement: With no tab chosen in the request, or an unknown one, the list opens on the Origin and Consignor tab.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's default tab.
requirements.deltaNote: A missing or unknown addressType selects Origin and Consignor (repo-insfrontend-p4-027, repo-insfrontend-p4-110, repo-tests-p12-150).

requirements.statement: Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the Type filter; the filter form carries the selected tab as a hidden field so filtering stays on the current tab, and the chosen Type stays selected after a search.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's tab and filter behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: Following a tab keeps the term, goes to page 1 and resets the Type (repo-insfrontend-p4-028, repo-insfrontend-p4-129, repo-tests-p12-068); the form carries the tab hidden (repo-insfrontend-p4-014) and the Type stays chosen (repo-insfrontend-p4-016).

requirements.statement: The legacy category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are not accepted as aliases.
requirements.why: They exist only so the prototype's older design releases keep working; the real service never used those values, so there are no links to keep alive.

requirements.statement: The filter has a select labelled 'Type' whose first option is 'Select one' (empty value), then options for the current tab only: 'Place of Origin' and 'Consignor' on Origin and Consignor; 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of Destination' on Destination, Consignee and Importer. A Type value the tab does not offer is ignored.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type filter options.
requirements.deltaNote: The Type select starts 'Select one' and offers each tab's own roles in this order (repo-insfrontend-p4-013, repo-insfrontend-p4-034, repo-insfrontend-p4-035, repo-tests-p12-072), and an option the tab does not offer is ignored (repo-insfrontend-p4-038).

requirements.statement: The Type filter keeps an address when one of the roles it holds equals the choice, and narrows within the search; the list API takes the roles and the tab so the filter runs over the whole category on the server, still organisation-scoped and without deleted addresses. How the record and the API carry roles is the address book service's design.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type filter, run on the server because the real list is paged.
requirements.deltaNote: Choosing a Type lists only addresses holding that role, AND with the search, across the whole tab (repo-insfrontend-p4-021, repo-insfrontend-p4-039, repo-insfrontend-p4-127, repo-tests-p12-075).

requirements.statement: Above the table a results line reads 'Showing <start>-<end> of <total>'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's results line.
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows 'Showing {from}-{to} of {total}' (repo-insfrontend-p4-057, repo-tests-p12-012).

requirements.statement: When nothing matches, or the book or tab is empty, the list shows 'Showing 0 of 0' and the table's headings with no rows, with no empty-state or no-match message.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws no empty-state message.
requirements.deltaNote: An empty book and a search with no matches both show 'Showing 0 of 0' and an empty table, with no message (repo-insfrontend-p4-058, repo-insfrontend-p4-059, repo-tests-p12-014). The older captures of 'You have no addresses yet.' predate the change (c-171).

requirements.statement: The list's filter holds the search field, the Type select and the search button and nothing else: a user clears a search by emptying the search field and submitting it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 has no Clear search link; nothing that overrides the prototype applies.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a 'Clear search' link shows above the table while a term is in force and returns to the tab's first page with no term, keeping the Type (repo-insfrontend-p4-022, repo-insfrontend-p4-023, repo-tests-p12-017); its Welsh is 'Clirio'r chwiliad' (repo-insfrontend-p4-092).

requirements.statement: On the Origin and Consignor and the Destination, Consignee and Importer tabs the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, then an action column whose header 'Action' is visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's table.
requirements.deltaNote: The address tabs' table has these columns (repo-insfrontend-p4-041, repo-tests-p12-018). The older captures with no Type column predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, then the hidden Action column, with no Country column. The Address cell ends with the transporter's country as its last line, 'Northern Ireland' for a commercial transporter; Approval number reads 'Not applicable' when there is none; and Type reads 'Commercial' or 'Private'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's transporter table; the 6 November ruling fixes a commercial transporter's country to Northern Ireland.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter table has these columns and cells (repo-insfrontend-p4-042, repo-insfrontend-p4-051 to repo-insfrontend-p4-054, repo-insfrontend-p4-131, repo-tests-p12-019).

requirements.statement: In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest; a one-word name stays on one line.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's rendering of a listed name.
requirements.deltaNote: The Name cell breaks after the first word (repo-insfrontend-p4-043, repo-insfrontend-p4-109, repo-tests-p12-032).

requirements.statement: In the Address column every stored address line (line 1, line 2, town or city, county, postcode) is shown on its own line, each but the last ending in a comma; blank lines are left out.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's address cell.
requirements.deltaNote: The Address cell shows each filled-in line on its own line (repo-insfrontend-p4-046, repo-tests-p12-033). The older captures that joined three lines into one predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The Country column shows the country's name, not its code, from the countries reference data, which always includes United Kingdom.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows country names; the address book stores codes.
requirements.deltaNote: The Country cell shows the name, or the stored code when the code is not in the reference data (repo-insfrontend-p4-047, repo-tests-p12-034).

requirements.statement: The Type column shows the labels of the roles the address holds, joined by ', ', in the order the address holds them, using the list's labels: 'Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer' and 'Place of destination'. These differ in case from the Type filter's options.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Type column labels.
requirements.deltaNote: The Type cell joins the five roles' column labels (repo-insfrontend-p4-044, repo-insfrontend-p4-045, repo-insfrontend-p4-113, repo-tests-p12-170).

requirements.statement: Each address row ends with a 'View' link to /address-book/{id}; its accessible name adds the address's name in visually hidden text ('View <name>'). Each transporter row's 'View' link opens that transporter's own page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's row action, with a distinct link purpose for screen reader users.
requirements.deltaNote: Address rows link to /address-book/{id} with the name hidden (repo-insfrontend-p4-049, repo-tests-p12-036), and transporter rows to the transporter's page (repo-insfrontend-p4-050).

requirements.statement: The address book list shows 8 addresses a page, asked for through the list API's page-size parameter, which runs from 1 to 100 and defaults to 25.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's 8 a page; the 5 and 25 November rulings keep the API's own bounds and default.
requirements.deltaNote: The list pages at 8 and sends pageSize (repo-insfrontend-p4-060, repo-insfrontend-p4-071, repo-insfrontend-p4-105, repo-tests-p12-020); the API takes 1 to 100, default 25 (repo-addressbook-p3-004).

requirements.statement: When there is more than one page, GOV.UK pagination shows below the table, with the current page marked, 'Previous' except on the first page and 'Next' except on the last; page links are the first page, the pages either side of the current one, the current page and the last page, with an ellipsis where pages are skipped. With one page there is no pagination.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 pages the list with the GOV.UK pagination component; a real book can run to many pages, which the prototype's three-page book never shows (c-500).
requirements.deltaNote: Pagination shows only past one page, with Previous, Next and the first, neighbouring, current and last page numbers with ellipses (repo-insfrontend-p4-061, repo-insfrontend-p4-062, repo-tests-p12-022).

requirements.statement: Pagination links keep the category, search and Type filter, and add page only for pages after the first.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's pagination links.
requirements.deltaNote: Every pagination link keeps the tab, term and Type, and page only above 1 (repo-insfrontend-p4-063, repo-insfrontend-p4-064, repo-tests-p12-026).

requirements.statement: A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page's addresses.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's page handling.
requirements.deltaNote: Page 0 and 'abc' show page 1 and page 99 shows the last page (repo-insfrontend-p4-065, repo-insfrontend-p4-066, repo-insfrontend-p4-106, repo-insfrontend-p4-107).

requirements.statement: The list shows the newest address first, with a stable order from page to page.
requirements.why: A newly added address is the one a user looks for next.
requirements.deltaNote: The API orders newest first with ties by id, pages disjoint, no sort parameter (repo-addressbook-p3-013 to repo-addressbook-p3-015, repo-insfrontend-p4-080), proven end to end (repo-tests-p12-035).

requirements.statement: After an add, edit or delete the list shows a GOV.UK success notification banner titled 'Success' above the heading, once: it is cleared when read, and it still shows when the list itself fails to load.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation of a change.
requirements.deltaNote: The list shows a waiting success message once in a 'Success' banner, also on its load-failure view (repo-insfrontend-p4-008, repo-insfrontend-p4-067-m1, repo-tests-p12-047).

requirements.statement: The success banner stays on the page until the user leaves or reloads it, and no script hides it on a timer.
requirements.why: WCAG 2.2.1 rules out a message that leaves on a timer (the 9 October afternoon ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: The banner is still showing ten seconds later and gone after a reload (repo-tests-p12-043).

requirements.statement: After a delete the list's success banner reads '<name> address deleted', with the address's name as the user entered it, or 'Address deleted' when the name is blank.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording; how the name is cased is c-367.
requirements.deltaNote: The banner reads '<name> address deleted', or 'Address deleted' with no name, set only when the delete lands on the list (repo-insfrontend-p6-081 to repo-insfrontend-p6-083, repo-tests-p12-044). The older captures reading '<name> deleted from your address book' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The address book is stored by the address book service and belongs to the organisation: every user signed in to the same organisation sees the same addresses, and one user's additions and deletions show for the others.
requirements.why: Persistence and sharing are real constraints the prototype's session store cannot express (c-172).
requirements.deltaNote: The address book keeps each organisation's records and another user of the same organisation sees additions and deletions (repo-tests-p12-124, trace-e2e-p15-077, trace-e2e-p15-078).

requirements.statement: Address book additions, edits and deletions held only in the user's session, with no address book API behind them, and a list that shows the session's own additions ahead of seeded addresses.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-172: the real book is persisted and organisation-wide.

requirements.statement: No caller can list, read or delete another organisation's addresses: the path organisation must match the caller's organisation header exactly, and any miss, whether unknown or another organisation's, is the same 404, never 403; in the INS frontend another organisation's view link returns the user to their own address book without showing the name.
requirements.why: Tenant isolation, a real constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: A mismatched path organisation is a 404 before any handler runs, with the same body as an unknown id (repo-addressbook-p3-053, repo-addressbook-p3-065), and the INS view redirects home without the name (repo-insfrontend-p6-022, repo-tests-p12-125).

requirements.statement: Every address book API call must carry a well-formed Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header (1 to 64 letters, digits, underscores or hyphens); a missing, blank or malformed one is refused with a 400 problem response with no errors map, before any handler runs, and a new address is stamped with that organisation. Requests outside /organisation/, such as /health, are not checked.
requirements.why: The header is the address book's sole tenant key.
requirements.deltaNote: IdentityHeaderFilter refuses a missing, blank or malformed header with a 400 problem (repo-addressbook-p3-050 to repo-addressbook-p3-052) and stamps the organisation on create (repo-addressbook-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend calls the address book server-side under /organisation/{orgId}/addresses with the signed-in session's organisation in the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, a JSON content type and the trace id, and refuses to call it without an organisation; a list answer that is not OK is raised as a failure.
requirements.why: The frontend is the trusted hop that sets the organisation.
requirements.deltaNote: The client builds the org-scoped URL and headers and refuses without an organisation (repo-insfrontend-p4-070, repo-insfrontend-p4-073, repo-insfrontend-p4-073-m1).

requirements.statement: The address book's trust boundary outside the service: stripping a client-sent organisation header, setting it from the verified session, CDP network policy, and the service's own resource-server authentication.
requirements.why: Platform and deployment controls the Design Release 2.1 programme does not change; it goes to the report as a standing risk nothing in the repo proves.

requirements.statement: The address book service logs each request with the caller's organisation id and no address personal data, logs list requests with their filters but never the search term itself, and logs each header refusal and cross-organisation miss once at warn or info; the INS frontend logs list, view and delete failures with the organisation and ids.
requirements.why: Operability without leaking personal data.
requirements.deltaNote: The list logs only whether q was present (repo-addressbook-p3-048), the organisation id sits in the logging context with no field values (repo-addressbook-p3-058), and the INS frontend logs its failures (repo-insfrontend-p4-068, repo-insfrontend-p6-024).

requirements.statement: The list API (GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses) returns a camelCase page object with items, page, pageSize, totalItems and totalPages, holds only live addresses, answers a page beyond the last with no items and the real totals, lists every live address when given no filter, and answers errors as application/problem+json.
requirements.why: The contract the INS frontend's list, results line and pagination read.
requirements.deltaNote: AddressPageResponse carries these fields over live addresses only (repo-addressbook-p3-009 to repo-addressbook-p3-012, repo-addressbook-p3-017), and the frontend reads them (repo-insfrontend-p4-072).

requirements.statement: Reading one address by id returns it with every stored field, including a deleted one with deleted true; only that tells a caller the address was deleted, and a 404 means unknown or not this organisation's.
requirements.why: Notifications hold address copies, and a tombstone must still resolve by id.
requirements.deltaNote: get-address fetches tombstones too and answers 404 for unknown or out-of-scope ids (repo-addressbook-p5-023, trace-e2e-p15-081).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address removes it from the list and search for everyone in the organisation but keeps it as a tombstone (deleted, name intact, readable by id); delete answers 204, is idempotent, cannot be undone, and is reached in the interface only through the delete confirmation page.
requirements.why: A notification that references a deleted address must not dangle.
requirements.deltaNote: DELETE soft-deletes, answers 204 idempotently and keeps the record readable (repo-addressbook-p5-008, repo-addressbook-p5-025, trace-e2e-p15-075); search skips tombstones (repo-addressbook-p3-018, repo-tests-p12-046).

requirements.statement: The address view page is at /address-book/{id}, headed with the address's name, and can be opened directly by its URL.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page.
requirements.deltaNote: GET /address-book/{id} renders the name as its h1 (repo-insfrontend-p6-001, repo-insfrontend-p6-003) and opens directly (trace-ins-fit-p2-050).

requirements.statement: The view page's summary list always shows, in this order, 'Name or organisation name', 'Address line 1', 'Town or city', 'Postcode or Zip code', 'Country' (as a name), 'Email address' and 'Phone number', each value trimmed.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page rows.
requirements.deltaNote: The rows and their order are already right, but the first row's label is the form field's 'Name or organisation' (repo-insfrontend-p6-006), where the design reads 'Name or organisation name'; the last capture still showed 'Name or organisation name' (trace-ins-fit-p2-039).

requirements.statement: The view page shows 'Address line 2 (optional)' after Address line 1, and the county row after Town or city, only when they have a value.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves empty optional rows out.
requirements.deltaNote: An optional field with no value has no row (repo-insfrontend-p6-007, repo-insfrontend-p6-009). The older capture with blank optional rows predates the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The view page's county row is labelled 'County (optional)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label, and the 14 October ruling keeps County on every address page.
requirements.deltaNote: The row is labelled 'County (optional)' (repo-insfrontend-p6-006, repo-insfrontend-p6-009). The older capture with a bare 'County' predates the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The view page's last summary row, 'Address can be used for', lists each role the address holds, one per line, worded as the roles question words them ('Place of origin', 'Consignor', 'Consignee', 'Importer', 'Place of destination'). The summary rows have no Change links: the whole address is changed through the Edit button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows on the view page what an address can be used for.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page shows no row for the address's roles (repo-insfrontend-p6-030); it already has no Change links (repo-insfrontend-p6-029, trace-ins-fit-p2-043).

requirements.statement: The view page's 'Edit' button, to /address-book/{id}/edit, is a secondary button, beside the Delete button in a button group.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page actions.
requirements.deltaNote: The Edit button is styled secondary (repo-insfrontend-p6-012) and sits with Delete in a GOV.UK button group (trace-ins-fit-p2-046).

requirements.statement: The view page has a red warning 'Delete' button to /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's view page actions.
requirements.deltaNote: The Delete button is a warning button to the delete page (repo-insfrontend-p6-013).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the view page's Back link goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Back link.
requirements.deltaNote: Back goes to the list when there is no return (repo-insfrontend-p6-014).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages honour a return query: the view page's Back link goes to it, its Edit and Delete links carry it on, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it to the view page, and after a delete the user goes to it unless it is one of the deleted address's own pages, when they go to the list. A return is honoured when it starts with a single / (an INS page), or when it is an absolute URL whose origin exactly equals the configured animals frontend origin, so a user who opened the address from a journey page of either animals set (live-animals or germinal-products, both in the animals frontend) goes back to it; anything else falls back to the list (view page) or the view page (delete page). A return that is the address book list itself is not carried onto the links. The return parameter's name is the INS service's to choose. Locally, on the compose stack and in CDP the allowed origin is each environment's animals frontend base URL, taken from the INS frontend's own configuration; in the INS stub mode only same-origin paths are honoured.
