requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the user back to where they opened the address from; the animals frontend is on another origin, a cross-service constraint that extends the prototype's single-/ rule to that one origin and never to any origin (c-170).
requirements.deltaNote: An INS return is already honoured throughout: Back follows it, Edit and Delete carry it, the delete page's Back and 'No, cancel' carry it, a delete lands on it and one naming the address's own pages falls back to the list (repo-insfrontend-p6-015, repo-insfrontend-p6-016, repo-insfrontend-p6-079, repo-insfrontend-p6-084, repo-insfrontend-p6-085); the stub ignores an animals return (repo-insfrontend-p6-018). A return on another origin is ignored everywhere (c-170), so nothing yet honours an absolute animals frontend return.

requirements.statement: Opening the view page for an id that is not a live address in the organisation's book (unknown, malformed, another organisation's or deleted) sends the user to the view page's back link (the return path or the list) rather than a 404 page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 redirects to the back link when no address has the id.
requirements.deltaNote: Unknown, malformed, other-organisation and deleted ids redirect to the list or the honoured return (repo-insfrontend-p6-019 to repo-insfrontend-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Opening the delete page for an id that is not a live address in the book redirects to the return path or the list; posting a delete for such an id, or for one already deleted, changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page guards.
requirements.deltaNote: Unknown and malformed ids redirect, a stale delete deletes nothing and shows no banner, and a not-found during delete redirects quietly (repo-insfrontend-p6-087 to repo-insfrontend-p6-091).

requirements.statement: The address view page showing addresses found outside the book (a notification's consignment, contact or transporter addresses), without Edit or Delete.
requirements.why: Set aside by c-173: those addresses are copies held by the notification service, not the address book, so the INS view page reads the book only.

requirements.statement: When the address book service fails unexpectedly, the list answers 500 with the shared recoverable error banner and no tabs, results line, table or pagination, while its heading, intro, add button and filter still show; the view and delete pages respond with the service error page; when the countries reference data is unavailable the list hands the failure to the service's generic error handling; each failure is logged.
requirements.why: A real cross-service failure the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The list's load-failure view and the view and delete pages' error responses are built (repo-insfrontend-p4-067, repo-insfrontend-p6-025, repo-insfrontend-p6-092).

requirements.statement: The view and delete pages render in the two-thirds column with a large heading; every address book page keeps the skip link, the GOV.UK header and the standard GOV.UK footer, and is built from GOV.UK Frontend components.
requirements.why: Today's layout; Design Release 2.1's custom page classes are styling of GOV.UK components, not a different layout.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-ins-fit-p2-038 and trace-ins-fit-p3-070 show the two-thirds column, trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m1 and trace-ins-fit-p2-002-m2 the skip link and footer.

requirements.statement: The list, view and delete pages have no serious or critical axe violations against WCAG 2.0 A/AA, 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA after the changes, on every tab, with the filter open and with a Type chosen.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint the service must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: Fit tests prove each page free of serious or critical axe violations (repo-insfrontend-p4-104, repo-insfrontend-p6-026, repo-insfrontend-p6-093).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation is served by GET and POST at /address-book/{id}/delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page; a confirmation stays a page.
requirements.deltaNote: GET and POST /address-book/{id}/delete are served (repo-insfrontend-p6-069).

requirements.statement: The delete page's heading is 'Delete this address?'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: The h1 is 'Delete this address?' (repo-insfrontend-p6-070, repo-tests-p15-118). The older captures headed 'Delete address' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows a summary list with one row, 'Address', holding the name, each address line and the country name on separate lines, blank lines left out, and never the email or phone; with none of those it shows 'Not applicable'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete summary.
requirements.deltaNote: The one-row 'Address' summary and its 'Not applicable' fallback are built (repo-insfrontend-p6-071, repo-insfrontend-p6-072).

requirements.statement: Below the Address summary the delete page's only text is its warning line; it has no separate sentence asking the user to confirm the delete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete page has the inset, the summary and the warning, and nothing else.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page also says 'Confirm that you want to delete this address.' (repo-insfrontend-p6-073, repo-tests-p15-118).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it warns 'Deletions are permanent and you cannot undo this.' (repo-insfrontend-p6-074, repo-tests-p15-118).

requirements.statement: The delete page's confirm button is a red warning button reading 'Yes, delete'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button.
requirements.deltaNote: A warning 'Yes, delete' submits the form (repo-insfrontend-p6-075). The older captures of 'Yes, delete this address' predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: Beside the confirm button the delete page has a 'No, cancel' link to the address's view page, deleting nothing and showing no banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel.
requirements.deltaNote: 'No, cancel' is a link to the view page that deletes nothing (repo-insfrontend-p6-076, repo-insfrontend-p6-077, repo-tests-p12-045). The older captures of a secondary Cancel submit button predate the change (c-501).

requirements.statement: With no return path, the delete page's Back link goes to the address's view page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's Back link.
requirements.deltaNote: Back goes to the view page (repo-insfrontend-p6-078).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete deletes the address through the address book service and, with no return path, lands on the list, which shows no row for that address and counts one fewer.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's delete outcome.
requirements.deltaNote: Confirming deletes through the service and lands on the list without the address (repo-insfrontend-p6-080, repo-insfrontend-p6-081).

requirements.statement: The delete form is protected by a CSRF token, posts nothing else, posts to its own URL and turns off browser validation.
requirements.why: Every state change is a protected form post.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete form posts only the CSRF crumb with novalidate (repo-insfrontend-p6-067, repo-insfrontend-p6-068, trace-ins-fit-p3-068).

requirements.statement: Deleting an address makes no check on whether a notification uses it and shows no in-use warning.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds no such check, and notifications hold their own copies of addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: No delete path checks for use on a notification (trace-ins-fit-p3-067).

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's in-memory address book stub behaves like the real list: 8 a page, filtering by search, tab and role, newest first, refusing an address with no roles or roles from two groups, and soft-deleting so a deleted address leaves the list and its view page redirects.
requirements.why: The fit suite runs against the stub, so it must exercise the list the design asks for rather than an unfiltered one.
requirements.deltaNote: The stub matches the term, countries and roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-020, repo-insfrontend-p4-078), lists the newest first (repo-insfrontend-p4-079), leaves deleted addresses out (repo-insfrontend-p4-077), refuses bad roles (repo-insfrontend-p4-084), and the fit suite proves 8 a page and a deleted address's redirect against it (repo-insfrontend-p4-105, repo-insfrontend-p6-023).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed English string on the list, view and delete pages has a Welsh counterpart, kept marked as an unreviewed machine draft until it has Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The INS frontend carries Welsh copy for every address book string; leaving the old Welsh would show users a different page in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: Welsh exists for today's strings, tabs and types included, marked as a machine draft (repo-insfrontend-p4-091 to repo-insfrontend-p4-099, repo-insfrontend-p6-094 to repo-insfrontend-p6-099), but it renders the hint as 'Chwilio yn ôl enw, cyfeiriad neu wlad', keeps 'Clirio'r chwiliad', and has the old delete wording 'Cadarnhewch eich bod am ddileu'r cyfeiriad hwn.' and 'Mae dileadau'n barhaol ac ni allwch ddadwneud hyn.'; there is no Welsh for the delete inset, the view page's inset or its 'Address can be used for' row, and no fit test covers the view or delete pages in Welsh (repo-insfrontend-p6-100).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's shared address book fixtures each carry one role the add flow offers, so they land on the right category tab and the journey parties still find them; the pre-run reconcile treats a missing or drifted role as drift, keeps exactly one live record per fixture name, and the tidy-up deletes only the suite's own run records, never fixtures or performance-test records, and never in production.
requirements.why: The suites read the tabbed list against a shared organisation's book.
requirements.deltaNote: Twelve fixtures each hold a single role (repo-tests-p12-164, repo-tests-p12-165) and seeding rewrites a drifted role (repo-tests-p12-115, repo-tests-p12-116); the tidy-up is scoped to run records (repo-tests-p12-119, repo-tests-p12-120).

requirements.statement: End-to-end specs reach the address book's view and delete pages through its own links (list, category tab, search, View, Delete, 'No, cancel', 'Yes, delete'), and cover the empty and no-match state.
requirements.why: The behaviour is proven the way a user meets it.
requirements.deltaNote: The suite reaches a tab, searches, follows View and the delete and cancel controls (repo-tests-p12-036, repo-tests-p12-045, repo-tests-p12-141) and proves the no-match state (repo-tests-p12-014).

requirements.statement: The prototype's seeded demonstration addresses (its farms, transporters, three Defra branches, multi-type entries and padding copies), their slug ids, and its transporter country read off the end of a free-text address.
requirements.why: Demonstration data: the real book holds each organisation's own records, with generated ids and a stored country code.

requirements.statement: DR1's own address book screens and the animals frontend's navigation into them.
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements (the ruling), and inc-062 struck DR1's address book screens; Design Release 2.1 governs the INS book's design.

requirements.statement: Closing the test gaps today's suites leave on the address book: no fit test proves the list's load-failure view, the banner, the View links, the 'Not applicable' approval number, the Previous link or the ellipses; no end-to-end test proves the Previous link, a transporter row's action, the Private filter, the roles refusal's wording, a status code for another organisation's address, or the Consignee and Place of destination filters through the list; no fit test covers the view or delete pages in Welsh.
requirements.why: Coverage gaps in behaviour this programme does not change; they go to the report. Each requirement that changes one of these behaviours carries its own proof.

requirements.statement: Adding and editing an address happen in the INS front door for a signed-in user, saved to the address-book service and scoped to the user's organisation: every single-address call carries the organisation id in the path and the Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header, a new address is owned by the caller's organisation, and an address is only ever found inside that organisation.
requirements.why: The address book moved out of the animals frontend to the INS front door, and organisation scoping is the only guard on whose addresses a user sees.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-091 saves for the signed-in organisation, repo-addressbook-p2-005, p2-024 and p2-049 own and scope every record by the organisation header, and repo-tests-p13-061 and p13-115 prove the scoping end to end against a record another organisation owns.

requirements.statement: Adding an address starts on a 'Choose an address type' page, before any address fields, with a 'Back' link to the address book list. The type step takes a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape; the address form stays at /address-book/add.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added first, because that decides the form and the roles offered next. URL paths are the real service's architecture.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-001, p5-003 and p5-010 and repo-tests-p13-001 and p13-008: the step is served at /address-book/add/address-type, opened with start=true from 'Add a new address', with a Back link to the address book list (marked at maturity 'exploring', p5-002). trace-e2e-p15-041 and trace-ins-fit-p1-006 describe the build before it, which served only the one-page add form (c-428).

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page shows the caption 'Add a new address' above its heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-005 and repo-tests-p13-001 show the caption 'Add a new address' above the heading.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page's heading and page title are 'Choose an address type', and the radio group's legend repeats the heading, visually hidden.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; the hidden legend names the radio group for screen readers.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-006 and p5-007: the heading and page title read 'Choose an address type' and the radios' legend repeats it, visually hidden.

requirements.statement: The first address type option is the radio 'Origin or Consignor' with the hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups place of origin and consignor addresses under one type, worded with 'or'.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-008 and repo-tests-p13-003: the first radio reads 'Origin or Consignor', hinted 'Place of origin, Consignor'.

requirements.statement: The second address type option is the radio 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' with the hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-008 and repo-tests-p13-004: the second radio reads 'Destination, Consignee or Importer', hinted 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'.

requirements.statement: The address type options include the radio 'Transporter' with the hint 'Private, Commercial', listed third, before 'Branch'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy and order. Ian's ruling of 6 November decides that the address book manages transporters, so the option leads somewhere.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-008 and repo-tests-p13-005: 'Transporter' is the third radio, hinted 'Private, Commercial'. It is also the last today, because 'Branch' is not offered (repo-tests-p13-125); req-1199 puts 'Branch' after it.

requirements.statement: The last address type option is the radio 'Branch' with the hint 'Branch address', after 'Transporter'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers a Branch address type, and Paul's ruling of 5 November keeps branch address among the six roles an address can play, in a group of its own (c-502).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the step offers three radios, Origin or Consignor, Destination, Consignee or Importer and Transporter, and no Branch (repo-insfrontend-p5-008, repo-tests-p13-125).

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page submits with a 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-009: the page has one button, 'Continue'.

requirements.statement: Continuing with no address type chosen shows 'Select an address type' inline on the radios and in a 'There is a problem' error summary whose link goes to the first option.
requirements.why: An address type is needed to know which form and roles to show.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-011 and repo-tests-p13-009 and p13-010: the message shows in the summary and against the radio group with status 400, and its link moves focus to the first option.

requirements.statement: The add remembers the chosen address type between its steps, so coming back to 'Choose an address type' pre-selects it; opening the add afresh, and saving, clear the type, the entered address and the ticked roles, so the next add starts empty.
requirements.why: A two-step add needs the first answer kept while it is in progress and cleared when it ends.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-004 and p5-014, and repo-tests-p13-012, p13-015 and p13-016: Back pre-selects the chosen type, and both an abandoned add and a saved one leave the next add with no type, empty fields and no role ticked.

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Transporter' and continuing leaves the address book add and opens the add-a-transporter pages; reached this way, their 'Back' link returns to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 adds transporters through their own pages, not the address form; a transporter is its own record with no roles (ruling of 6 November). Where the pages live follows the services as built.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-013 and repo-tests-p13-013: 'Transporter' goes to the transporter type page at /address-book/add/transporter with start=true and carries no roles. No today claim shows that page's Back link.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page reached from the address book has the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and page title 'Choose a transporter type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy on the hand-over target.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter option already opens a transporter type question (repo-tests-p13-013, repo-insfrontend-p5-013); no today source in this area shows that question's caption or heading.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page shows the warning 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy on the hand-over target.

requirements.statement: The add-a-transporter page offers the radios 'Private transporter' and 'Commercial' (hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.') and a 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; a transporter stores a private-or-commercial type, and a commercial transporter's country is Northern Ireland (ruling of 6 November).

requirements.statement: Choosing 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' or 'Branch' and continuing goes to the add-details step, the address form at /address-book/add, which posts back to itself.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 flow: these three types use one add-details page whose content depends on the type. The form keeps today's path; the prototype's /address-book/add/lookup path is not copied (ruling of 9 October, claim 21).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-012 and p5-016 and repo-tests-p13-126: 'Origin or Consignor' and 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' open the add page at /address-book/add. 'Branch' is not offered today; req-1199 adds it and it opens the same page.

requirements.statement: Opening the add-details step directly with no address type chosen redirects to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: The add-details step cannot be shown without knowing the type.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-019 and repo-tests-p13-017: opening /address-book/add with no type the form serves lands on 'Choose an address type'.

requirements.statement: The add-details step reached from the address book shows no caption above its heading, and no notification status banner.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; the page is the address book's, not a notification's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add page shows the caption 'Add new address' (repo-insfrontend-p5-020, repo-tests-p13-126); it already shows no status banner in the address-book mode (p5-024).

requirements.statement: The add-details step reached from the address book has the heading and page title 'Add an address'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the heading and page title read 'Add address and contact details' (repo-insfrontend-p5-021, repo-tests-p13-126); the build before it read 'Add address details' (trace-ins-fit-p1-004, trace-e2e-p15-041, c-428).

requirements.statement: The add-details step has a 'Back' link to 'Choose an address type'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the user go back and change the type. While no address search is built, no find-an-address page stands between the two steps, so every type's Back goes to the type step.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-022 and repo-tests-p13-012: Back from the add page returns to 'Choose an address type' with the chosen type still selected. Once address search is built, req-1214 sends the Destination and Branch Back link to the find-an-address pages instead.

requirements.statement: The 'Choose an address type' page, the add-details step and the edit page have browser titles reading '<page heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 title format.
requirements.deltaNote: The add page already reads '<heading> - Import notification service - GOV.UK' (repo-insfrontend-p5-021). The latest evidence of the edit page's title shows '<heading> | Import notification service' (trace-ins-fit-p3-003), and no today claim shows the type page's title format, so both are checked and brought into this format where they differ.

requirements.statement: For 'Origin or Consignor' the add-details step shows the address and contact fields straight away with no address search, and a section break separates them from the roles question.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1: origin and consignor addresses are often outside the UK, so they are entered by hand.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-070 and p5-144 and repo-tests-p13-023: the form opens with its fields and one section break above the roles question, and the only way to enter an address is by hand (p13-120).

requirements.statement: Once address search is built, 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' go from 'Choose an address type' to the find-an-address pages before the add-details step: the add-details step then opens with its fields filled from the picked address, or empty with the country United Kingdom after 'Enter address manually', and its 'Back' link returns to the find-an-address page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 finds these UK addresses by postcode before the address form. The find-an-address pages themselves are the address lookup area's.
requirements.deltaNote: No address book page offers an address search today: the add form is manual entry only (repo-insfrontend-p5-171), and repo-tests-p13-120 finds no search or lookup step between the type step and the add-details form.
requirements.blockedBy: Parked by ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2: address search is concept work, not needed for the deadline. When it is planned, the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in), and the address search area is re-distilled once it lands (ruling 9 October, claim 34).

requirements.statement: No free-text type-ahead address search is built on the add-details step: no matches appear below a field as the user types, and no 'Address search results' list or results-count announcement is shown.
requirements.why: The 26 November prototype no longer has the type-ahead: it finds Destination and Branch addresses by postcode on pages of their own (req-1214), and design's answer of 13 November builds address searching without live filtering. Nothing supports the type-ahead any more.

requirements.statement: Once address search is built, an address picked on the find-an-address pages fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city and postcode on the add-details step, with country United Kingdom; name, email address and phone number stay blank for the user, and any field the user types over wins.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fills the address from the pick and leaves the name and contact details to the user. The lookup returns no organisation name.
requirements.deltaNote: The add form offers manual entry only today (repo-insfrontend-p5-171).
requirements.blockedBy: The address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in); once it lands, the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 9 October, claim 34).

requirements.statement: Once the address lookup is a real feature, the address searches find real UK addresses from the address lookup the INS backend serves, and a failed lookup leaves the user able to enter the address manually.
requirements.why: The prototype's addresses are made-up data; the real service must search real addresses, which only the address lookup holds (c-178). Sam ruled the search waits for the lookup to become a real feature (c-217).
requirements.deltaNote: The add form has no address search or lookup today (repo-insfrontend-p5-171); the lookup is still only the EUDPA-390 spike (ruling-ian-2026-11-06-p1-067).
requirements.blockedBy: The address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend (today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in); once it lands, the address search area is re-distilled (ruling 9 October, claim 34).

requirements.statement: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the country is fixed: the Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', pre-selected, and the save stores United Kingdom (GB) whatever is posted.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 fixes these UK-only types to the United Kingdom, and Paul's ruling of 5 November refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Destination form offers every country with United Kingdom selected (repo-insfrontend-p5-054, p5-144), and the address book restricts no role by country (repo-addressbook-p1-029).

requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-026 and repo-tests-p13-022 and p13-043: both forms group their fields under the level-2 headings 'Address' and 'Contact details'. trace-ins-fit-p1-008 and trace-e2e-p15-042 show the earlier 'Enter address details' (c-428).

requirements.statement: Email address and phone number on the add and edit forms sit under the section heading 'Contact details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy, the same on both forms.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-026 and repo-tests-p13-022 and p13-043: Email address and Phone number sit under 'Contact details' on both forms. trace-ins-fit-p1-018 shows the earlier 'Enter contact details' (c-428).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy; its specs and traces show the add and edit labels differ.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-028 and repo-tests-p13-019: the add form's name field reads 'Name or organisation'.

requirements.statement: On the edit page the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation name'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the edit page labels the field 'Name or organisation', the same as the add form (repo-tests-p13-044); the earlier build read 'Name or organisation name' (trace-ins-fit-p3-005).

requirements.statement: The add-details step has no County field.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 14 October keeps County on the add-details step, because the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose it on a round trip, so Design Release 2.1 leaving the field out is a prototype mistake (c-432). req-2363 carries what the step asks instead.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the add form asks 'County (optional)' (repo-insfrontend-p5-039, repo-tests-p13-020).

requirements.statement: The edit page keeps the 'County (optional)' field between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code', prefilled from the stored address.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's edit form keeps county.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p13-019 and p13-047-m1: the field sits between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' and opens prefilled from the stored address.

requirements.statement: The add and edit forms ask 'Address line 1', 'Address line 2 (optional)', 'Town or city', a postcode field, 'Country' (a select), 'Email address' and 'Phone number' with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code', and no other field has a hint. The postcode field reads 'Postcode or Zip code', except on the add-details step for 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch'.
requirements.why: These labels and the phone hint already match Design Release 2.1.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-027 to p5-063 and repo-tests-p13-018, p13-019 and p13-021 show these labels in page order, Country as the one select among them, and the one phone hint. The UK-only postcode label is req-2796.

requirements.statement: On the edit page 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number', as on the add form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 uses one field order for both forms.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p13-045: the edit page lists Email address above Phone number. trace-ins-fit-p3-005 and trace-e2e-p15-061 show the earlier phone-first order (c-428).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step 'Name or organisation', both address lines and 'Email address' are full width, 'Town or city' and the postcode field are half width, and 'Phone number' is two-thirds width.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 field widths.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-028 to p5-059: name, both address lines and email are full width, town or city and postcode one-half, and phone two-thirds. trace-ins-fit-p1-020 shows the earlier half-width phone (c-428).

requirements.statement: The edit page lays its fields out like the add form: the same section headings, order and field widths.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds both forms from the same Address and Contact details sections.
requirements.deltaNote: The section headings and field order already match the add form (repo-tests-p13-043, p13-111). The only evidence of the edit form's input widths shows two-thirds text inputs, a width-10 postcode and a default-width country select (trace-e2e-p15-062, trace-ins-fit-p3-007-m1), so its widths are checked and made the add form's.

requirements.statement: For 'Origin or Consignor' the Country select opens with United Kingdom selected.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 defaults the country to the United Kingdom.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-054 and p5-130: in the address-book mode the add form opens with United Kingdom selected. trace-ins-fit-p1-015 shows the earlier build starting on the placeholder (c-428).

requirements.statement: On the add-details step the Country select's blank first option reads 'Select one'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the placeholder reads 'Select a country' (repo-insfrontend-p5-047, p5-130).

requirements.statement: On the edit page the Country select offers no blank option and opens with the stored country selected; where the stored country code is not one the list offers it opens on a blank option, so no country is changed without the user choosing one, and saving with no country chosen shows 'Select a country'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's edit form offers only real countries, and validation and persistence are real constraints it cannot express: a stored code the reference list no longer offers must not be replaced silently, and the blank state is what the 'Select a country' refusal rests on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-102: the edit form's select leaves out the placeholder when the saved country is in the list and shows it when not; repo-tests-p13-064 and p13-065 prove the blank option and the refusal. trace-ins-fit-p3-013 shows the earlier build keeping the placeholder above the stored country (c-428).

requirements.statement: The countries offered come from the reference data service's unfiltered country list, which is MDM's content (each option shows the name and submits its ISO alpha-2 code, stored as given), not from a list held in the address book pages; no country is added, removed or renamed in code.
requirements.why: Country lists are master reference data that the service takes from MDM, and DR1 judged that their content is not edited page by page; Sam ruled that no reference list waits on MDM, so what MDM serves is the list. The germinal data fields call the address block's country an enumeration from the MDM country list, mandatory, with United Kingdom as its example.
requirements.deltaNote: The list already comes from reference data's countries endpoint with no blocks asked, each option submitting its code, and the chosen code is stored as given (repo-insfrontend-p5-048, p5-053, repo-addressbook-p1-027, repo-tests-p13-036). Today the frontend drops any GB entry reference data returns and adds its own 'United Kingdom' entry (repo-insfrontend-p5-049, c-177), and in stub mode it reads a captured fixture (p5-052).

requirements.statement: Add and edit keep today's length limits and email format check, in the frontend and the address book API: name and both address lines 255 characters, town or city and county 100, postcode 12, phone 20 and email 254, each with the frontend's '<field> must be N characters or fewer' message, and 'Enter an email address in the correct format' for a malformed email; postcode and phone stay free text.

requirements.statement: The address-book record and its create, read-one and update API carry the roles the address can play on a notification, every one ticked when it was added, out of place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer and branch address; at least one role is required, a repeated role collapses to one, an unknown role is refused with 'Select valid roles', and no address type is stored, the address type being the front door's grouping of those roles. The field names and shape are the address-book service's own design.
requirements.why: A kept question must persist, and DR1 asked for role-filtered address pickers that wait on exactly this record (ruling of 9 October, claim 22). Paul's ruling of 5 November settles the vocabulary and the shape: role rather than use, six roles, roles stored and nothing else, and the address type worked out from them by the INS front door. The prototype decides what is asked, not how the record stores it.
requirements.deltaNote: The record already stores the ticked roles and requires at least one, collapses repeats, refuses unknown names, refuses a type or role field and ignores an addressType (repo-addressbook-p1-002, p1-038 to p1-043, p1-051, p1-052, p2-076, repo-tests-p13-036). requirements.statement: Creating an address persists its full record in the address-book service: POST /organisation/{orgId}/addresses answers 201 with the address and a Location header ending in the new id, the address starts ACTIVE (deleted false) with server-set id, organisation and timestamps, and server-owned or unknown fields in the body are ignored.
requirements.why: The prototype keeps addresses only in the session; the real service must persist them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-001 to p2-009 and repo-tests-p13-095 to p13-097 show a created address persisted with its full record, and a refused create storing nothing.

requirements.statement: Saving an edit fully replaces the address's editable fields and roles through PUT /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}: a cleared optional field is cleared, id, organisation, status, createdAt and expiry are kept, modifiedAt moves on, and the record stays live.
requirements.why: An edit must change the stored address in place, not add a new one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-027 to p2-031 and repo-tests-p13-047 show an edit replacing the record in place, clearing an optional field left blank and leaving the record undeleted.

requirements.statement: An update is refused without change when the body is invalid (400 with per-field errors), the id is unknown, another organisation's or deleted (404 'Address not found'), or another write changed the address first (409 conflict); a stale write can never bring a deleted address back.
requirements.why: Persistence and authorisation constraints the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-033 to p2-037 and p2-045 prove these refusals, and repo-tests-p13-061 to p13-063 prove that another organisation's, a deleted and a concurrently deleted address are all refused without saving.

requirements.statement: The address-book API answers errors as RFC 9457 problems (application/problem+json, CDP problem types, traceId when one is set, no instance field): a validation error carries a camelCase per-field errors map, every other 400 is the bad-request problem with none, a not-found reads 'Address not found', a conflict 'The resource was modified by another request', and a 500 never leaks the underlying message.
requirements.why: The frontend maps these shapes to the form, and the shapes are a cross-service contract.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-052 to p2-070 define these problem shapes, and repo-tests-p13-095 and p13-096 prove the validation problem's type and its camelCase per-field errors end to end. A path organisation that disagrees with the header is refused by the header filter with the detail 'Resource not found' (repo-addressbook-p2-067-m1); it stays, because it answers the caller's own mismatch and discloses nothing about another organisation's address.

requirements.statement: When the address-book service rejects a save the form is shown again with the service's errors against the fields and the values kept; any other save failure shows the recoverable error with the values kept; reference data being unavailable or empty gives a 503.
requirements.why: Cross-service failures the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-051, p5-094 and p5-095 already handle these failures; p5-170 records that no fit test proves the refused or failed save.

requirements.statement: Outside prod, when a TTL in days is configured, a new address is given an expiry that many days after it is created, after which it may be removed; an update keeps the expiry set at creation and never adds one; prod sets no expiry and keeps addresses and their tombstones indefinitely.
requirements.why: Test data must not build up outside prod while prod data is never expired.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p2-010 to p2-012, p2-026 and p2-048 implement and test the non-prod expiry and prod's indefinite keeping.

requirements.statement: The address-book service keeps its API surface and storage as built: the stored record and its response fields (with deleted derived from status, and status, version and expireAt never returned), camelCase wire names and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, the request-to-record mapping checked at build, the org_status_created index, logging that never records a request body or rejected values, the address.change counter and the per-operation timers.
requirements.why: This is the system of record other services depend on; none of it differs from Design Release 2.1 visibly.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-001 to p1-070 and p2-013 to p2-016 and p2-068 to p2-074 describe the service as built, and repo-tests-p13-112 lists the record a client sees. The code marks a response's roles required while the generated API document does not (repo-addressbook-p2-019-m1); the field is always sent, so nothing visible differs.

requirements.statement: A notification journey's 'Add a new address' hands over to the INS address book add through today's handshake (journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token; only a registered journey type, today gbn-ag and gbn-ag-germinal-products; the return URL built on the server; the new address id handed back; cancel returns without one; no address book banner), and an unregistered journey type is refused with the INS 'Page not found'. In journey mode the INS add page opens the add-details step for the type the hand-off's party implies, skipping 'Choose an address type', shows the draft journey strip, opens the Country select on United Kingdom for a receiving party and on the placeholder otherwise, keeps nothing between visits, and saves the new address with that party's role. It returns through the journey's own /address-return on the animals frontend, carrying the fulfilment id, the token, the new address id and a landing, to the page each button names: 'Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, and 'Cancel and return to hub' is a link that saves nothing. INS and each journey service take the other's address from their own configuration, with no hard-coded host or port, and the end-to-end suite proves the hand-over in the local and CI Docker stacks.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's journeys add addresses on their own pages, but which service writes the address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express, so the real address book stays a separate service reached through this handshake while everything the prototype can express about the page follows Design Release 2.1 (c-106). Sam's ruling of 4 November has every link between services work from each service's own configuration, and his ruling of 27 November keeps the default that the hand-over is proved in the local and CI Docker stacks with no new CDP check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-018 to p5-025, p5-055, p5-088 to p5-097 and p5-148 to p5-158, and repo-tests-p13-100 to p13-109, show the hand-off values, the refusal of an unrecognised journey type, the germinal products journey type, the journey strip, the Back link and 'Cancel and return to hub' link, both save buttons and the return path with its landing and address id. repo-tests-p13-101 records that the hand-off specs run only against the local compose stack, and p13-134 that a stale token is unproven.

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a submitted notification's view page, and the Amend action on its card in the set's notification list, open an amend confirmation page at the notification's own amend route, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants): its title and level-1 heading are 'Amend this notification?', and nothing changes until the trader confirms.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 now draws the amend confirmation as a page of its own, titled 'Amend this notification?', and the 27 November ruling sends the design's changes since 5 October to this work to catch up, which outranks the wording the 9 October afternoon ruling borrowed from the earlier pop-up (c-512). The interaction designer's 9 November answer makes amend a page in every set, plants included (c-190, c-310), and the 25 November ruling makes the view header's Amend a link to this page (c-438).
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no amend confirmation: the card's Amend is a form button that starts the amendment and opens the review page straight away (trace-animals-fit-p3-027, repo-tests-p6-001), as plants' card Amend does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-108), and the view header's 'Amend this notification' posts and starts the amendment at once (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-008, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-010).

requirements.statement: On the amend confirmation page, 'Yes, amend' is a primary button that submits the page's form (with the CSRF crumb) and starts the amendment, and 'No, cancel' is a link beside it in the button group that returns to the notification's view page without changing anything, leaving the notification Submitted; the page's Back link goes to the view page too.
requirements.why: The trader confirms or backs out of amending without losing their place; a state change is a form post (c-189). The wording is the design's page (c-512).

requirements.statement: With JavaScript, 'Cancel amend' opens the cancel-amendment confirmation as a dialog over the current page rather than sending the trader to the confirmation page, in live animals, germinal products and plants: hidden until opened, role dialog labelled by its heading, with a Close (X) button labelled 'Close' for screen readers and an overlay; Close, the overlay and the dialog's 'Go back' dismiss it without acting and leave the trader where they were.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the interaction designer's 9 November answer is that amend and cancel amendment are their own pages, not dialogs, so the dialog increment is dropped rather than waiting on design. The design itself now draws amend as a page and keeps only cancel amendment as a dialog. GOV.UK Frontend has no modal, MoJ's modal dialog is not accepted and has no fallback without JavaScript, and no custom JavaScript is written to copy the prototype (c-190).

requirements.deltaNote: Today a page opened from the overview while amending ends with two buttons, 'Save and continue' then 'Save and return to overview', with a 'Cancel and return to overview' link below them that discards what was typed (repo-tests-p6-012, repo-tests-p6-013, repo-tests-p6-016); there is no 'Save and return' to the review, and a Change link's page returns to the review only by walking on with Save and continue (repo-tests-p6-017, repo-tests-p6-018, repo-tests-p6-019, trace-e2e-p14-047). The origin, CPH number and permanent address pages end with 'Save and continue' alone (repo-tests-p6-020, repo-tests-p6-021, repo-tests-p6-023). The pickers, CPH number and permanent address pages keep to two buttons because of DR1 rule (b) (document-dr1-parity-notes-p1-055, c-210), and the prototype's action field is set aside by c-267.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages keep the journey's usual Back links (the origin of the import back to the notification type page, arrival details back to the overview hub), not a link to the amend review.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 does not change Back links for an amendment.

requirements.statement: During an amendment, question pages are prefilled with the notification's saved answers and keep their usual copy, and they are the same pages a draft uses, reached at the same addresses.
requirements.why: The trader changes only what needs changing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Change link during an amendment opens the question with the saved answers (repo-tests-p6-017, trace-e2e-p14-046), and an amendment is walked through the same journey pages as a draft with the Amend state carried in the shared strip (repo-tests-p6-100, repo-frontend-p7-132).

requirements.statement: The amend review opens with no error summary on it. Pressing Continue while any answer is missing or invalid keeps the trader on the amend review, still tagged Amend, with a 'There is a problem' error summary whose links name each task left to finish, and does not open the Declaration. Plants' amend review refuses Continue the same way.
requirements.why: A resubmitted amendment must be complete and valid, and the trader must be told in words why Continue was refused: accessibility is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and both frontends already identify the unfinished task (c-201).
requirements.deltaNote: A refused Continue already holds the trader on the review at ?refused=1 with the 'There is a problem' summary naming the unfinished task and the Amend tag kept (repo-frontend-p7-131, repo-tests-p6-026, repo-tests-p6-027, repo-tests-p6-028), and the review opens clean (repo-tests-p6-010); plants does the same (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-102).

requirements.statement: Continue on a valid amend review goes to the Declaration page; ticking the declaration and pressing Continue resubmits the amendment.
requirements.why: An amendment is resubmitted through the same declaration as a first submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Continue on the amending review already leads to the Declaration, and ticking it resubmits (repo-tests-p6-058, repo-tests-p6-060, trace-e2e-p14-056).

requirements.statement: Resubmitting an amendment shows the ordinary 'Import notification submitted' confirmation with the notification's existing reference and no wording about an amendment; the same record becomes Submitted again, read only, with the edited answers, the set's notification list shows the amended answers, and it can be amended again.
requirements.why: An amendment replaces the submitted notification rather than creating a second one.
requirements.deltaNote: Resubmission already lands on the submitted confirmation and the notification is Submitted, read only and amendable again with the edited value (repo-tests-p6-060, repo-tests-p6-062, repo-tests-p6-063, trace-e2e-p14-057, trace-e2e-p14-057-m1). The dashboard cards' empty 'Date submitted' (trace-e2e-p14-062) is the notification list's, which drops that fact (req-1075).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's title and level-1 heading are 'Are you sure you want to cancel this amendment?', with no caption, in every set that amends (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for cancelling an amendment, carried onto the page by the 9 October afternoon ruling; on a page the heading is the level-1 heading, where the pop-up drew a level-2.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the cancel-amend page's title and level-1 heading are 'Cancel this amendment?' (repo-frontend-p7-107, repo-tests-p6-033, trace-e2e-p14-035, trace-animals-fit-p3-036-m1), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-086); plants' page shows no caption already (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-114).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page shows no body paragraph between its heading and its buttons, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's cancel-amendment confirmation has no description line, and the 9 October afternoon ruling carries that onto the page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page says 'Your changes since you started amending will be discarded and the submitted version restored.' (repo-frontend-p7-108, repo-tests-p6-034, trace-e2e-p14-036), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-087).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirm button reads 'Yes, cancel amendment' and is a standard (not warning) primary button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on this button.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's cancel-amend page already has a standard 'Yes, cancel amendment' button (repo-frontend-p7-109, repo-tests-p6-035, trace-animals-fit-p3-038), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-088).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation page's way back is a link-styled 'Go back' that returns to the notification's view (the amend review while amending; plants' check answers view) and leaves the amendment in progress, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not cancelling; as a page at today's route, it goes back where today's way back goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to notification' to the notification view, which keeps the amendment and the changed value (repo-frontend-p7-110, repo-frontend-p7-111, repo-tests-p6-037, trace-e2e-p14-039), and the same in plants (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-088, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-097-m1).

requirements.statement: 'Cancel amend' (in the Amend status bar and beside Continue on the amend review) and the card's 'Cancel amendment' go to the cancel-amendment confirmation page at the notification's own cancel-amend route in each set, which carries only the confirmation's heading and buttons: no journey strip and no Back link.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the cancel confirmation as a separate page at today's route carrying the pop-up's wording, so the page holds what the pop-up held.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page at /notifications/{id}/cancel-amend still shows the Amend journey strip (without its own Cancel amend link) and a Back link to the notification view (repo-frontend-p7-106, repo-frontend-p7-112, repo-frontend-p7-123, repo-tests-p6-036, trace-e2e-p14-034, trace-e2e-p14-037); plants has the same page with the strip and a Back link, reached from the card, the strip and its view (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-084, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-091, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-107).

requirements.statement: Confirming the cancellation discards every edit made during the amendment, restores the submitted answers, returns the notification to SUBMITTED with its original submitted and created times, and takes the trader to that notification's view page, read only and showing Submitted, whose Back link goes to the set's own notification list.
requirements.why: Cancelling must leave the notification exactly as it was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancel-amend already restores the submitted answers and returns to the read-only Submitted view (repo-frontend-p7-117, repo-frontend-p7-118, repo-tests-p6-040, repo-tests-p6-043, trace-e2e-p14-045), keeping the original times (trace-e2e-p14-072-m1), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-094, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-095-m1), and Back from the restored view already opens the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-119, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-106).

requirements.statement: After an amendment is cancelled, the view page shows no success banner, and the redirect to it carries ?cancelled=1 in its address, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns to the view page without a message; the 9 October ruling keeps ?cancelled=1, because the prototype never decides URL shapes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the view opens at ?cancelled=1 with a 'Success' banner reading 'The amendment has been cancelled and the submitted version restored.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-044, trace-animals-fit-p3-045, repo-tests-p6-040, repo-tests-p6-041): the address stays, the banner goes. Plants already redirects with a cancelled marker and shows the restored Submitted notification (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-094).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting cancel amendment for a notification that is not being amended changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends every 'overall dashboard' destination, this one included, to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a Submitted notification is redirected to its view page, and any other status, or a notification the session does not hold, to the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-114, repo-frontend-p7-115, repo-frontend-p7-120, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-092, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-093).

requirements.statement: When copy as new, cancel amendment or delete fails to save, the page the trader came from is shown again with HTTP 500 and the recoverable-error banner, in every set that has the action; a copy started on the notification view returns there and one started on the list returns to the list.
requirements.why: A real save can fail; the prototype cannot express that.
requirements.deltaNote: Each controller already re-renders with 500 and the recoverable-error banner (repo-frontend-p5-069, repo-frontend-p7-100, repo-frontend-p7-121, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-080, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-116), and the copy remembers where it started (repo-frontend-p5-068). Plants' copy takes the same handling with its Copy as new (req-2055).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets (live animals and germinal products), Copy as new goes straight, with no confirmation, to the new draft's overview hub titled 'Overview', which has no Back link and no banner announcing the copy; it is started by a 'Copy as new' button that also names the notification's reference for a screen reader.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree that copying is immediate and quiet.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already posts to the notification's copy address and redirects straight to the new notification's overview with no page or banner of its own (repo-frontend-p5-064, repo-frontend-p5-066, trace-e2e-p3-073, trace-e2e-p3-077, trace-animals-fit-p2-075), from a button naming the reference (repo-frontend-p5-073, repo-tests-p6-065).

requirements.statement: A copy is a new notification saved at once as a Draft, with its own new reference (same GBN-AG prefix, fresh suffix); the source is unchanged, the copy is independent of it, every copy is distinct, and the copy is one of the trader's own notifications, listed beside its source under its own reference.
requirements.why: Copying must never alter or merge with the notification it came from.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy already makes a fresh DRAFT with a new reference and leaves the source alone (repo-backend-p2-039, trace-e2e-p14-073, trace-e2e-p14-074, trace-e2e-p14-075), and both notifications stay listed under their own references (repo-frontend-p5-074, repo-frontend-p5-076, repo-tests-p6-064).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the origin of the import: country of origin, whether a region of origin code is required, and the region of origin code with its suffix.
requirements.why: These describe the trade, not the shipment, so they usually repeat.
requirements.deltaNote: The copy keeps the origin's country code, subdivision, region flag and region code (repo-backend-p2-031), and the copy's origin task comes back Complete with the same country of origin (repo-frontend-p5-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the internal reference number, in the notification record as well as on the page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 carries it over with the import details.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy clears the origin's internal reference in the notification record (repo-backend-p2-031-m1), though the copy's origin page shows it from the copied fulfilments (trace-animals-fit-p2-078).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over what is being imported: the commodity (id, code and name), the commodity selections, the selected species and the notification type (worked out from the copied answers when missing).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks What are you importing? Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps each commodity's name, code and description only and clears its species (repo-backend-p2-032); the fulfilments payload travels as it is (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the number of animals, the number of packages or the net weight: the copy's commodity details show To do, its Animals total reads 0 and its Packages/boxes total shows no figure.
requirements.why: Counts are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's overview carries the totals (1 animal, 5 packages) and marks Commodity details Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-animals-fit-p2-077): the record clears commodity details beyond name, code and description (repo-backend-p2-032), but the fulfilments payload carries them across (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over animal identifiers (ear tags, passports and the like): the copy's Identification details show To do.
requirements.why: Identifiers belong to the animals in one shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Identification details show Complete (trace-e2e-p13-109, trace-e2e-p3-075), because the fulfilments payload is copied as it is (repo-backend-p2-037).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, the transit port of exit, transit destination country, and the temporary admission exit date and port of exit.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Main import reason Complete on the copy; the 17 November ruling names the exit port 'Port of exit' everywhere, so the transit follow-up is the transit port of exit.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps the reason, purpose, destination country and port of exit (repo-backend-p2-033, repo-backend-p2-036) but clears the exit date (repo-backend-p2-038). The field the design calls the transit exit border control post takes the ruled name (ruling-sam-2026-11-17-p1-005).

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the additional animal details: what the animals are certified for, whether unweaned animals are included, and the storage temperature.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 marks Additional details Complete on the copy.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps only the certified-for answer of the additional details, clearing the unweaned animals answer and the storage temperature (repo-backend-p2-034).

requirements.statement: When copying a live-animals notification, a certified-for value the set does not offer is mapped to one it does: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value the set does not offer becomes 'Further keeping'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: which values the certified-for question offers is data, which the data dictionary specifies and reference lists supply, so a mapping drawn from the prototype's own retired option values rests on neither data owner and is not a row (c-440). A copy carries certified-for over as stored.

requirements.statement: A copy carries over the roles and addresses (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination, each in full as stored), the CPH number and the permanent address details.
requirements.why: Trading partners usually repeat between shipments.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend copy keeps the CPH number and the whole fulfilments payload (repo-backend-p2-036, repo-backend-p2-037), but keeps each party with only its name, email, phone and address (repo-backend-p2-035), so anything else stored on a party is not carried; the copy's overview shows Roles and addresses Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the arrival details (port of entry, arrival date, means of transport, transport identification and transport document reference): the copy's Arrival details show To do.
requirements.why: Arrival is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Arrival details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109), though the backend copy clears the transport details in the record (repo-backend-p2-038).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transit countries.
requirements.why: The route is specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transit countries show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the transporter: the copy's Transport details show To do.
requirements.why: The transporter is chosen per shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Transport details show Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over the contact address: the copy's Contact address shows To do.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks for the contact address again on each notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the copy's Contact address shows Complete (trace-e2e-p3-075, trace-animals-fit-p2-077).

requirements.statement: A copy does not carry over uploaded documents: the copy's Upload documents shows To do.
requirements.why: Documents are specific to each shipment.
requirements.deltaNote: Upload documents already shows To do on a copy (trace-e2e-p3-076, trace-e2e-p13-109).

requirements.statement: Copying a notification that is being amended copies its submitted version, not the edits in progress.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copies the saved notification; an unfinished amendment is not yet the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Today copying an AMEND notification copies its current, in-progress answers rather than the amendment snapshot (repo-backend-p2-039-m1).

requirements.statement: Copy as new for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, a notification with no content, or a status that cannot be copied such as deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that copies.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Copy already returns a refused copy to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p5-067); the backend refuses a source with no content (repo-backend-p2-040), and plants' backend refuses an uncopyable status (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-023).

requirements.statement: Copy as new is checked against the version the trader was looking at: when the notification has changed since, nothing is copied and the trader returns to where they started, the set's notification list or the notification's view page, with the 'The notification has been updated' banner, in live animals, germinal products and plants.
requirements.why: A trader must never copy content different from what they saw; the prototype cannot express concurrent edits. The 25 November ruling gives plants the same stale-copy return now that its header offers Copy as new.
requirements.deltaNote: The token check and banner exist (repo-frontend-p5-070, repo-frontend-p5-072, trace-e2e-p14-073, repo-tests-p6-054, repo-tests-p6-055), but a stale copy started from the view page redirects to /notifications/{id}/check-answers?staleAction=1, which no route serves, so the trader lands on a page that does not exist (repo-frontend-p5-071). Plants' persistence already posts the token with its copy (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-024).

requirements.statement: The amend review ends with a button group of 'Continue', a secondary 'Cancel amend' and a warning-styled 'Delete' that opens the notification's delete confirmation page, in every set that amends, and a notification being amended is deleted as any other notification is.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 offers Delete during an amendment at the foot of the amend review.
requirements.deltaNote: Both frontends already delete a notification being amended (repo-frontend-p7-094, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-075), and the amending card offers Delete (trace-e2e-p14-060), but the live animals amending view offers no Delete (trace-e2e-p14-032-m1), plants' amending view ends with Continue, Cancel amend and Save and return to overview and no Delete (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-100), and nothing proves deleting an amending notification (repo-frontend-p5-078, trace-animals-fit-p3-057).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page identifies the notification in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin), in every set (live animals, germinal products and plants).
requirements.why: The trader confirms they are deleting the right notification; the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants the same layout in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete page has only a heading, one sentence and two buttons (repo-frontend-p7-086, repo-frontend-p7-089), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-069, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070), where the reference and status come from the journey strip instead (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-074).

requirements.statement: In the animals sets, the Commodity row on the delete and amend confirmation pages lists each commodity's common name with its species' Latin names in brackets, the commodity lines comma-separated (for example 'Sheep (Ovis aries), Goat (Capra hircus)'); for other live mammals each species' common name is used.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's format for naming what was notified, the same on both confirmation pages. Whether the Latin names are re-cased is its own question (c-510).

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, the Number row on the delete and amend confirmation pages shows the notification's total number of animals across all its commodity lines.
requirements.why: Animals are counted by head. The 9 October ruling splits this requirement by set; the germinal set's packages count is its own requirement.

requirements.statement: A summary row on the delete or amend confirmation page that has no value from the notification shows 'Not applicable', in every set.
requirements.why: Every row shows something, even for an early draft. The design's fall-back to its own list's seeded details exists for its demo data, which the real service, whose list reads the same record, does not have.

requirements.statement: Below the summary the delete page says 'Confirm that you want to delete this notification.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page has no such sentence (repo-frontend-p7-089, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070).

requirements.statement: The delete page warns 'This action cannot be undone.', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's warning wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'This cannot be undone.' (repo-frontend-p7-089, trace-e2e-p3-060), in plants too, in a plain paragraph (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-070).

requirements.statement: The delete page's red warning button reads 'Yes, delete', in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's button wording.
requirements.deltaNote: Today it reads 'Yes, delete notification' (repo-frontend-p7-090, repo-tests-p6-047, trace-animals-fit-p3-008), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071).

requirements.statement: Beside 'Yes, delete' the delete page has a plain link 'No, cancel' in the button group, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording and pattern for not deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the way back is a secondary button-styled link 'No, return to dashboard' that leaves the notification in place (repo-frontend-p7-091, repo-frontend-p7-092, trace-animals-fit-p3-009), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-079).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Back link and 'No, cancel' both return to the notification's view page, in every set (plants' check answers view).
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sends the trader back to the notification they were deleting.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both go to the set's list (repo-frontend-p7-093, trace-animals-fit-p3-010, trace-e2e-p3-063), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-071, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-072).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page shows no journey strip (status tag and reference) above its heading and offers no Cancel amend control, in every set; the summary list identifies the notification instead.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 builds the page from GOV.UK components only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page shows the journey strip with the status tag and reference (trace-animals-fit-p3-011, trace-animals-fit-p3-012, trace-e2e-p3-064), as plants' does (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-074).

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation page is titled 'Delete this notification? - Import notification service - GOV.UK' with the level-1 heading 'Delete this notification?', is reached from the Delete action on the notification's card in the set's list and from the notification's view, serves every deletable status, and can be opened directly by its address, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 and today agree on the heading.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's delete page already has this title and heading for drafts and submitted notifications (repo-frontend-p7-088, repo-tests-p6-046, trace-animals-fit-p3-006-m1, trace-animals-fit-p3-013), reached from each card's Delete (repo-frontend-p7-087, repo-tests-p6-050) and the view's Delete (repo-tests-p6-053, trace-e2e-p13-110) at /notifications/{id}/delete (repo-frontend-p7-086, trace-e2e-p3-065), and plants' delete page is the same (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-066, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-069).

requirements.statement: Confirming the delete (a POST with the CSRF crumb) soft-deletes the notification: its status becomes DELETED and the record is kept; a repeat is a harmless no-op; deleting a submitted notification records a NotificationSubmissionDeleted event carrying the acting user's organisation id; a notification the trader's session does not hold is not deleted. Plants soft-deletes through its own backend the same way.
requirements.why: The real store keeps deleted records for other services and audit; the prototype's outright removal cannot express persistence (c-193).
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already soft-deletes, idempotently (repo-frontend-p7-097, repo-tests-p6-051, trace-e2e-p14-077, trace-e2e-p14-078), for a submitted notification carrying address-book parties as for a draft, with the organisation id forwarded for the event (repo-frontend-p7-099, trace-animals-fit-p3-024), refuses a notification the session does not hold (repo-frontend-p7-098, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-076), and plants keeps the record and marks it deleted (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077).

requirements.statement: After 'Yes, delete' the trader lands on the set's own notification list (the live-animals set root, the germinal products set root, plants' own list), and the redirect keeps ?deleted=1 in its address.
requirements.why: The 9 October afternoon ruling sends every Design Release 2.1 'overall dashboard' destination, the delete landing included, to the set's own list, replacing the INS landing; the 9 October ruling keeps ?deleted=1 on the redirect (c-198, c-269).
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals delete already lands on /live-animals?deleted=1 (repo-frontend-p7-096, repo-tests-p6-051, trace-e2e-p3-066), and plants' on its own list with a deleted marker (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077); the germinal set gets it with its copy of the feature.

requirements.statement: The deletion success message reads 'Notification has been deleted.' in the live animals and plants lists.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for a list that does not know the deleted notification's reference: its '<reference> has been deleted.' form needs the reference, and the 9 October ruling keeps the redirect's address as ?deleted=1, which does not carry it (c-513). The germinal products list's message is its own question (c-511).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner is titled 'Notification deleted' and reads 'The notification has been deleted.' (trace-animals-fit-p3-017, trace-animals-fit-p3-018, repo-tests-p6-048, trace-e2e-p3-068), in plants too (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-078). The banner's 'Success' title is req-1086's.

requirements.statement: A deleted notification does not appear in the set's notification list, and searching the list for its reference finds nothing.
requirements.why: Deleted notifications are gone from the trader's view.
requirements.deltaNote: The deleted notification already disappears from the dashboard and its search (trace-animals-fit-p3-020, repo-tests-p6-049, trace-e2e-p3-072), and from plants' list (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-077).

requirements.statement: Opening or posting delete for a notification the trader cannot reach (unknown reference, another session's notification, or a status that cannot be deleted) changes nothing and returns to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the route; the real service must also check the record exists, which the prototype's POST does not; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends the guard to the set's own list.
requirements.deltaNote: Delete already refuses an unknown or non-deletable notification and returns to the set's list with no banner (repo-frontend-p7-095, repo-frontend-p7-098), as plants' does on both opening and confirming (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-076).

requirements.statement: The view page shows the notification's answers in the same numbered sections and cards as the review page; the sections and the card contents follow the review page's requirements.
requirements.why: One rendering of a notification's answers serves review and view.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's notification view already renders the review page's numbered sections (trace-animals-fit-p3-051); differences in the sections and inside the cards are carried by the review page's requirements.

requirements.statement: The backend notification API supports the lifecycle: create gives DRAFT with a minted reference; save keeps DRAFT or AMEND; submit takes DRAFT or AMEND to SUBMITTED and stamps submittedAt; amend takes SUBMITTED to AMEND; cancel-amend takes AMEND back to SUBMITTED; copy reads the source at the caller's concurrency token and makes a new DRAFT; soft-delete makes DELETED. Each write advances the concurrency token, and callers from outside carry the API key.
requirements.why: Every action in this area rests on these transitions.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend already implements this lifecycle, proven through the API (trace-e2e-p14-064, trace-e2e-p14-067, trace-e2e-p14-070, trace-e2e-p14-072, trace-e2e-p14-073, trace-e2e-p14-077, trace-e2e-p14-067-m1) and modelled as four statuses by the suite (repo-tests-p6-052).

requirements.statement: A notification is saved as a draft as the trader goes: one record per reference, keeping its created date, without errors or transient page state.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 autosaves drafts; the real service persists each save.
requirements.deltaNote: Each journey page's save already persists the whole record under its reference (trace-e2e-p14-083).
