requirements.statement: The delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the restored submitted view and a copied notification's overview have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA axe violations, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: The service must meet accessibility standards.
requirements.deltaNote: The fit specs already assert this (repo-frontend-p5-077, repo-frontend-p7-103, repo-frontend-p7-128, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-081, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-096).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's animals specs and page objects for amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete assert the copy, the confirmation pages (the amend confirmation page included), the landing pages and the banners these requirements give, assert ?cancelled=1 on the cancel redirect and ?deleted=1 on the delete redirect, keep the smoke-tagged cancel and delete cases, and cover the delete page's body copy and its way back, the cancel page's way-back wording, deleting a notification that is being amended, the guard redirects, a stale amend review, what cancelling does to a document added during the amendment, and what a deleted notification's own view shows.
requirements.why: End-to-end proof must follow the changed behaviour, and the gaps the suite leaves today are the cases these requirements change.
requirements.deltaNote: Today's specs assert the current copy ('Yes, delete notification', 'Cancel this amendment?', its body paragraph, the cancel alert, ?deleted=1, ?cancelled=1) (repo-tests-p6-033, repo-tests-p6-034, repo-tests-p6-047, repo-tests-p6-048), expect Amend to open the review straight away (repo-tests-p6-001), name no delete-page body copy or way back (repo-tests-p6-107), do not pin the cancel page's way-back wording (repo-tests-p6-108), and prove nothing about a stale amend review, a document added during an amendment or a deleted notification's own view (repo-tests-p6-109, repo-tests-p6-110, repo-tests-p6-111).

requirements.statement: Every new or changed string on the delete and cancel-amendment confirmations, the amend confirmation page and the view page has a Welsh entry of the same shape, and the copy tests that pin those strings verbatim are updated with them, in the animals frontend and in plants.
requirements.why: Today's action pages carry Welsh copy, and the frontend's standing rule (req-1659) is that every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version of the same shape; Design Release 2.1 is silent on Welsh, so nothing it shows overrides that rule.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the delete and cancel-amend pages have machine-drafted Welsh copy carrying exactly the English keys (repo-frontend-p7-105, repo-frontend-p7-130), and plants' copies of them too, with its delete strings pinned verbatim by their own test (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-082, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-083, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-110).

requirements.statement: Delete and cancel amendment are checked against the version the trader opened, and the dashboard Amend carries a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: delete and cancel-amend post a token nobody reads, and Amend posts none. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for a fix, so the programme does not make one.

requirements.statement: Soft delete checks that the caller owns the notification or is an admin.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as an access-control weakness in the backend: its lifecycle calls carry only the API key and no caller identity. Design Release 2.1 does not cover it, so it needs its own ticket.

requirements.statement: Create, save, copy, submit, amend and cancel-amend write audit records attributed to a user.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: the backend's lifecycle calls take no body and no user id, so nothing attributes them. Design Release 2.1 does not ask for audit.

requirements.statement: Backend edge cases answer with a client error rather than a server error: copy of a source with no content, and submit of an empty notification.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report as backend defects no user journey reaches; Design Release 2.1 does not cover them.

requirements.statement: The place of destination picker's search does not fail with HTTP 500, and the 500 page offers a way back.
requirements.why: Recorded for the report: seen on the copy test's first attempt, it belongs to the address pickers and the error page, not to copying.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics are reproduced: its session keys and journey resets, the ?resume=1 shortcut into an amendment, ?reference addressing, a default reference, deleted-reference lists, seeded review snapshots and their fixed sample data, the confirmation summary's fall-back to the list's seeded details, and its seed-format arrival answers.
requirements.why: Prototype internals with nothing a user sees; the real service persists notifications in the backend, holds one record per notification and has its own test data.

requirements.statement: Amend for a notification the trader cannot amend (unknown reference, a notification since deleted, or any status but Submitted, such as Draft or one already being amended) changes nothing and returns the trader to the set's own notification list with no message, in every set that amends, both on opening the amend confirmation page and on confirming it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 guards the amend route silently; the 9 October afternoon ruling sends its 'overall dashboard' to the set's own list, plants' included.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an amend pressed on a card for a notification since deleted lands on the set's list with an Important banner reading 'This notification could not be amended.' (repo-tests-p6-005, repo-tests-p6-006): the landing stays, the banner goes.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's stored notification record, the validation it applies at its API, its lifecycle writes and what it publishes carry only the additions other requirements in this area name: the facts, filters and sorts each set's own notification list needs, the templates store, the authorities' outcomes once they arrive, and the germinal products set's category held on the record only with its details and its trade-line codes. Everything else about the record, its API validation, its writes and its events is as the backend already has it, the submitted date and the flag saying whether a submitted notification's answers have since changed included.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows no persistence, API, event or PIMS behaviour, so the backend changes only where another area's requirement needs it to.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by the backend behaviour the requirements below record from repo:backend, repo:tests and trace:e2e. The backend already records the submitted date (repo-backend-p1-011, req-1499) and the answers-differ flag (repo-backend-p1-015, this area's own requirement for it). Each addition named is its own requirement: the templates store req-1310 (repo-backend-p2-123: no templates today), the authorities' outcomes req-1082, and the germinal products set's category, details and trade-line codes req-1884 to req-1895. The repo holds no rulings ledger of its own (repo-backend-p1-093). The outstanding items list this statement used to name is withdrawn by the 19 November ruling, and the status it used to name beside the four is withdrawn by the 16 November ruling; both withdrawals are recorded as this area's conflicts.

requirements.statement: A notification is stored as one document in the MongoDB collection 'notification', with a database id, its identity and metadata (reference number, status, timestamps, fulfilments) at the document root and its answers nested under a notification sub-object, which holds no section beyond origin, commodities, reason for import, additional details, the five parties, CPH number, transport, purpose in the internal market, destination country, port of exit and exit date.
requirements.why: Every page reads and writes this one record, and the tests and the INS read model rely on its shape.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-001 to p1-003 (the notification collection, content sub-object and database id), repo-tests-p9-002 (the collection), p9-003 (one document per reference), p9-132 (the root fields) and p9-153 (the fifteen content sections the stored content may hold) show the shape today.

requirements.statement: A notification carries exactly one reference number, a string held at notification level rather than per commodity line, and it is unique across all notifications through a sparse unique index that lets records without a reference number coexist.
requirements.why: The reference number is how traders, PIMS and every endpoint find a notification, and one notification never carries two.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-004: the sparse unique index on the reference number. The V4 data fields page's Reference Number row says the same: a string that applies at notification level, one per notification and not driven by commodity selection (confluence-6497338582-p1-021, p1-026).

requirements.statement: The service, never the trader or any other caller, gives a new notification its reference number in the form GBN-AG-{YY}-{XXXXXX}: GBN for Great Britain Notification, AG for Animals and Germinals, YY the last two digits of the year the reference is allocated in, then a six-character Crockford base32 body (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O and U) drawn from a cryptographically secure source, for example GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P. A germinal products notification takes a GBN-AG reference like a live-animals one, so no GBN-GP reference exists.
requirements.why: References must be unguessable, readable aloud and unique per notification, and the AG in the prefix stands for Animals and Germinals, so one shape serves both sets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-023 and p2-024 (ReferenceNumberGenerator's format and secure random source), p2-020 (create assigns the number) and p2-025 (one fixed GBN-AG prefix whatever the commodities) already meet it. The V4 data fields page's Reference Number row gives the same four parts, the same example and the same six-character Crockford base32 body, marks the field N/A for mandatory so no trader is asked for it (confluence-6497338582-p1-028-m1), and records that it impacts both the animals and the germinals journeys (p1-030). The page names no source for the value (p1-027), so the backend's own generation stands.

requirements.statement: When a generated reference number collides with an existing one, create tries a fresh number up to three times in all, then fails with a 500.
requirements.why: The generator does not guarantee a new number; the caller handles the clash.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-022: createNotification retries up to three times in all, then throws an IllegalStateException that the generic handler answers as 500.

requirements.statement: Every endpoint that takes a reference number in its path refuses one that does not match ^GBN-AG-\d{2}-[0-9A-HJ-KM-NP-TV-Z]{6}$ with a 400 Validation Error before any lookup, its errors map keyed by referenceNumber.
requirements.why: A malformed reference is turned away before it reaches the store.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-008: the pattern on every path reference number in NotificationController, a violation answered as 400; p1-077: a method-parameter violation's errors map is keyed by the last segment of the property path.

requirements.statement: Every notification carries a concurrency token, returned in each response, that is its optimistic-lock version: it advances on each write, and a content save is checked against the token the caller sends, not the stored one, so a save without a token is refused with 400.
requirements.why: Two people or tabs editing one notification must not silently overwrite each other.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-006 (the concurrencyToken version field), p2-004 (every write returns the whole record), p2-010 (no token, 400) and p2-011 (the save is made at the caller's token).

requirements.statement: A save sent with a stale concurrency token changes nothing and answers 409 with title 'Stale Concurrency Token', code STALE_CONCURRENCY_TOKEN and detail 'The record was modified by another request; refresh and try again.'; the first writer's change stands.
requirements.why: The second of two concurrent writers is told to refresh rather than losing the first writer's work.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-084 (GlobalExceptionHandler's stale-token answer) and p2-011 (a save at a stale token is refused as a conflict).

requirements.statement: Amend and cancel-amend take no concurrency token from the caller, so they act on the version stored when the call arrives; content saves, submit and copy each require the token the caller last read.
requirements.why: Records today's behaviour: the actions that change or send the content are checked against the version the user last saw.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-051: amend and cancel amend take no token; p2-042-m1: copy and submit refuse a request without the concurrencyToken query parameter; p2-010: a content save needs one.

requirements.statement: A notification has exactly one of four lifecycle statuses, DRAFT, SUBMITTED, AMEND or DELETED, in the notification API and its fulfilments view alike, with no cancelled, rejected, in-progress or template status among them; any further status sits beside these four rather than replacing one of them.
requirements.why: Every lifecycle rule and every published event keys off these four values.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-008 (NotificationStatus) and repo-tests-p9-006 hold the four values today, p2-125 shows the service only ever moves a notification between them, and repo-tests-p9-004 and p9-042 show a draft and a two-commodity notification taking DRAFT and SUBMITTED. The one status this programme would have added beside them is withdrawn by the 16 November ruling, and 'Completed' waits for a real source of completion (req-1082).

requirements.statement: The server stamps created on creation and updated on every save and lifecycle change, as instants; a client cannot set the database id, created, updated, submittedAt or expireAt through a save request.
requirements.why: Audit times and expiry must not be forgeable by a caller.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-009 and p1-010: server-stamped created and updated that the inbound shape cannot carry; p1-053: the inbound notification carries only a reference number, a status, a concurrency token and the fulfilments beside its content; p2-018: updated is stamped on every write.

requirements.statement: submittedAt records the most recent submission: set to now on the first submit from DRAFT and on each re-submit from AMEND, left unchanged by starting or cancelling an amendment, and set by no other action.
requirements.why: PIMS and the dashboard show when the notification was last submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-011 and p1-011-m1 (the submittedAt field and what a submission records), p2-045 (stamped on a first submission and each resubmission) and p2-059 (cancelling an amendment keeps the original date).

requirements.statement: In a non-prod environment with NOTIFICATION_TTL_DAYS set, each new notification (copies included) gets an expireAt that many days after its created time, whatever its status later becomes; nothing (save, submit, amend) extends it; no expiry is stamped in prod (ENVIRONMENT 'prod' in any letter case, 'local' when unset) or when the setting is unset, and a value that is not positive is refused.
requirements.why: Test environments clear out old notifications without any risk to production data.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-112 and p2-113 (expiry stamped once, at creation, from created plus the configured days), p2-030 (a copy gets its own expiry), p2-115 to p2-117 (never in prod, prod matched in any case, days must be positive and are unset by default) and p2-119 (no days value set in the repo for any environment).

requirements.statement: Removal of expired notifications is switched on only where NOTIFICATION_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED is true (false by default): the backend then creates expiry indexes at start-up and the database removes each notification at its expiry time, and the backend refuses to create those indexes in prod even when removal is switched on.
requirements.why: Expiry must never run in prod, so production is protected twice: by no expiry being stamped and by no expiry index being made.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114 (NotificationExpiryIndex creates expiry indexes at start-up when expiry is enabled), p2-115 (refused in prod) and p2-116 (NOTIFICATION_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED, false by default). The scheduled sweeper an earlier extraction recorded is gone from main.

requirements.statement: A notification of any status whose expiry time has passed is removed together with its accompanying documents; a notification with no expireAt is never removed by expiry.
requirements.why: Expired test data and its uploads are removed together.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114: expired notifications and accompanying documents are removed by the database through expiry indexes; p2-113: the expiry applies whatever the status; p1-012: a record may carry no expireAt.

requirements.statement: Expiry writes no audit record and no outbox event, so other services are not told when a test notification expires.
requirements.why: Records today's behaviour: removal is done by the database, not by the service's lifecycle code.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-114: the database removes expired records through expiry indexes, so no service code runs; p2-104: only admin hard deletes and replays write an audit record.

requirements.statement: At start-up the backend logs whether new notifications get an expiry and, when they do not, why: prod, or no days set.
requirements.why: Operators can see whether expiry is in force in an environment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-118: NotificationExpiryStampingLog. The per-sweep log lines this used to record went with the sweeper, which main no longer has.

requirements.statement: expireAt and the pre-amend notification and fulfilment snapshots are never shown in any API response.
requirements.why: They are server-only state.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-012 and p1-014 (never returned in an API response) and p1-069 (the fulfilments view returns none of the server-only fields).

requirements.statement: The fulfilments payload (each obligation holding a single value or a list of records with their own fulfilment id and value) is stored exactly as sent and never interpreted by the backend, and date-shaped strings inside it, in plain text fields and in outbox data stay strings.
requirements.why: The frontend journey engine owns the fulfilment model and rehydrates the journey from it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-017 (opaque fulfilments), p1-061 (date-shaped strings stay strings) and repo-tests-p9-123 (the stored fulfilment entries).

requirements.statement: Starting an amendment stores independent deep copies of the notification content (inline parties as they stood included) and of the fulfilments payload; cancelling restores both, submitting the amendment clears both while keeping the edited content; a notification never amended, or submitted, holds no snapshot.
requirements.why: Cancel-amend must be able to restore exactly what was submitted.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-014 and p1-014-m1 (the two deep-copied snapshots), p1-072 (the content deep copy), p2-052 (opening an amendment stores them), p2-046 and p2-058 (submit and cancel clear them); repo-tests-p9-029 and trace-e2e-p14-130 show no snapshot after submit.

requirements.statement: Wherever the backend needs a notification's content, a record with no content sub-object fails at once, which the catch-all handler answers as a 500.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The claim it rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted, and the new extraction records only the record's shape (repo-backend-p1-002). The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.

requirements.statement: A save body (POST /notifications and PUT /notifications/{referenceNumber}) is a wrapper holding a required, validated notification object (content fields plus referenceNumber, status, concurrencyToken and fulfilments) and an optional actor; a body without notification is refused with 400 Validation Error naming notification.
requirements.why: The frontend sends this one shape for every save.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-052 and p2-003 (SaveNotificationDto with a required, validated notification and an optional actor), p1-053 (what the inbound notification carries) and p1-074 (the validation error shape).

requirements.statement: The backend enforces no rule on the notification's content: no required field, length or format on any section or free-text field (CPH number, email, phone, postcode, country code), and submit checks only the status and the concurrency token, not completeness. Every check a trader sees is the frontend journey's, which decides what a page must hold before it saves and what the notification must hold before it submits.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's validation is built in the frontend journey, the owner's rulings keep every page check there and apply it to both save buttons alike, and the backend accepts drafts at any depth.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-054 (no validation rule on any content field), p1-039 (nothing validates the country code's format) and p2-048 (no completeness check on submit) meet it. The owner's 26 October ruling and the 27 November ruling's answer on the save buttons put the same checks on both save buttons, the page's own hard stops plus whatever the data specification marks mandatory to proceed; those checks are the frontend's, so the backend's own validation does not change.

requirements.statement: The record's origin section holds the country of origin code, whether a region code is required (as the text 'yes' or 'no'), the region of origin code with its country prefix (for example FR-75), the country subdivision code and the trader's internal reference.
requirements.why: The origin page saves here and the GBN-AG payload reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-020 and p1-021 (Origin's five text values) and repo-tests-p9-007 to p9-010 / trace-e2e-p14-123 (stored FR, yes, FR-75, Imports456GB).

requirements.statement: The record holds a list of commodities, one per commodity the trader chose and empty by default, each with a name (the commodity's display name, such as 'Cattle' for 0102), a commodity code, a description, whole-number totals of animals and packages, and a list of species lines; each species line holds a species value, its display text and its common name, with its own whole-number number of animals and number of packages. Counts the frontend sends as strings are stored as numbers.
requirements.why: One notification can carry several commodity lines and species, each chosen species keeps its own counts, and PIMS receives a trade line per species.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-022 to p1-027 (the commodities list, Commodity and Species) and repo-tests-p9-011 to p9-016, p9-040 and p9-121 meet it; p2-013 stores an empty list when commodities are missing. The 27 November ruling keeps each species' own number of animals and packages, which the record already holds. The older commodity-complement shape a trace and the tests repo's API model still show is settled by c-514.

requirements.statement: Each species line holds a list of animal identifier units, one per animal (every unit kept), each with a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, free-text identification details, a description and a permanent address as a full party; an identifier the journey did not ask for is stored as an empty string or left out, and the two are treated alike. The line also keeps single ear tag, passport and microchip fields carrying its first unit.
requirements.why: PIMS needs each animal's identifiers, and records saved before per-animal identifiers still map.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-028 to p1-032 (Species and AnimalIdentifier) and repo-tests-p9-017, p9-018, p9-019 and p9-041; trace-e2e-p14-136 shows a missing and an empty passport stored the same way.

requirements.statement: The record holds the reason for import (for example internalMarket) and the purpose in the internal market (for example breeding) as text codes.
requirements.why: The import reason page saves here and the GBN-AG clauses read it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-033 and p1-049 (reasonForImport and purposeInInternalMarket as text) and repo-tests-p9-020, p9-021 (each stored as the answer's code).

requirements.statement: The record's additional details hold what the animals are certified for (a text code, for example slaughter) and whether there are unweaned animals (as the text 'yes' or 'no').
requirements.why: The additional details page saves here and the GBN-AG payload reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-034 (AdditionalDetails) and repo-tests-p9-022, p9-023 / trace-e2e-p14-126.

requirements.statement: The record holds five parties, each with an optional name, email, phone and address: placeOfOrigin, consignor, consignee, importer and destination; an unanswered role stores none of them, and the record holds no consignment contact.
requirements.why: The party pickers save here and the GBN-AG payload maps each role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-035 and p1-036 (the five parties and ConsignmentParty) and repo-tests-p9-025, p9-152 and p9-154 (five parties stored, no consignment contact) meet it. The consignment contact an older trace still shows stored is settled by c-515.

requirements.statement: Each party is stored as a literal copy of the address-book record picked for it, with no address id linking back, so later address-book edits or deletions never change the notification.
requirements.why: A submitted notification must keep what the trader declared.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-037 (a party is a literal copy); repo-tests-p9-024 and trace-e2e-p14-127-m1 prove no addressId is stored, and p9-028 reads each stored party back against the live address-book record.

requirements.statement: An address is a Standard Address Block named as the address book names it: address line 1, optional address line 2, town or city, optional county, postcode and an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (any country, not only the UK); there is no address line 3, city or free-text country.
requirements.why: Addresses copy across from the address book without translation and PIMS gets a country code.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-038 and p1-039 (Address) and repo-tests-p9-026 / trace-e2e-p14-128.

requirements.statement: The CPH number is stored as one text string, the county, parish and holding parts joined with no separator (12, 345, 6789 stored as '123456789').
requirements.why: The CPH page saves here and the GBN-AG final destination reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-040 (CPH number as text) and repo-tests-p9-030 / trace-e2e-p14-131 (stored unbroken).

requirements.statement: The record's transport section holds the port of entry (as the port's code), the arrival date, the means of transport, the transport identification, the transport document reference and the transited countries as country codes in the order added.
requirements.why: The arrival and transit pages save here and the GBN-AG transport movement reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-041 to p1-047 (Transport) and repo-tests-p9-031 to p9-034; trace-e2e-p14-132 stores FR then BE.

requirements.statement: The means of transport is one of AIRPLANE, RAILWAY, ROAD_VEHICLE or VESSEL; any other value is refused as a 400 Malformed Request.
requirements.why: PIMS needs a mode code for each value.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-045 (MeansOfTransport).

requirements.statement: The transport section holds one transporter with a name, an address, an approval number and a free-text type (for example 'Commercial') and no email or phone; it is not an address-book party.
requirements.why: The transporter page saves here and the GBN-AG carrier reads it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-048 (Transporter, its type free text) and repo-tests-p9-035, p9-036, p9-037.

requirements.statement: The record holds a destination country, a port of exit and an exit date (the calendar day chosen, sent as YYYY-MM-DD, with no time or zone).
requirements.why: The exit pages save here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-050 and p1-051 and repo-tests-p9-133, which also records that no spec in that slice asserts the three fields. The 27 November ruling keeps the exit date question in live animals and asks none in germinal products, so a germinal record leaves the field empty.

requirements.statement: Every date-only field (arrival date, exit date, a document's date of issue and any added later) accepts only a plain date such as 2026-07-21; a value carrying a time or an offset is a 400 Malformed Request, never a 500 or a silently dropped time, and how moments are read does not change.
requirements.why: A calendar date must never shift by a day between the user's choice and PIMS.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-057 and p1-058 (StrictLocalDateModule) and p1-075 (the malformed-request answer).

requirements.statement: Calendar dates are stored as YYYY-MM-DD strings ('2026-07-21'), so they read back as the chosen date in any server time zone and sort in date order; moments (created, updated, submittedAt, expireAt and audit timestamps) are stored without a zone, to millisecond precision.
requirements.why: Fixes EUDPA-282, where UK summer time stored the previous day.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-059, p1-060 and p1-062 (LocalDateStringConverters and the design notes) and repo-tests-p9-038 / trace-e2e-p14-133.

requirements.statement: The API sends dates and moments as ISO-8601 strings, never epoch numbers or arrays, and its OpenAPI schema marks each calendar-date field as format date and each moment as format date-time.
requirements.why: Callers can parse every date the same way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-063 and p1-064 (the design notes on the API date contract).

requirements.statement: Every error the backend's exception handler answers is an RFC 7807 problem detail sent as application/problem+json, carrying the request's traceId when there is one.
requirements.why: Callers get one error shape and support can follow a request.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073 (GlobalExceptionHandler and ProblemDetailsFactory).

requirements.statement: A body or parameter that fails validation gets 400 with type validation-error, title 'Validation Error', detail 'Validation failed for one or more fields' and an errors map from each failing field to its messages: a method-parameter violation keyed by the last segment of its property path, a missing required parameter mapped to 'Required request parameter is missing', and a parameter of the wrong type mapped to 'Request parameter has an invalid value'.
requirements.why: The caller can tell which fields failed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-074, p1-077, p1-078 and p1-079 (GlobalExceptionHandler's validation answers).

requirements.statement: A body that cannot be read gets 400 with type malformed-request, title 'Malformed Request' and detail 'Request body could not be read. Check the JSON is well-formed, that each date-only field is a date, for example 2026-12-12, and that each timestamp is an RFC 3339 instant, for example 2026-12-12T00:00:00Z'; the parser's own message is only logged.
requirements.why: The caller learns what to fix without the response echoing submitted values or internal types.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-075 and p1-076.

requirements.statement: A payload that binds but the application rejects, such as a callback missing required metadata, gets 400 with type bad-request, title 'Bad Request' and the refusal's own message as detail.
requirements.why: Lifecycle refusals reach the caller with their reason.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-080 (BadRequestException handling).

requirements.statement: A missing resource gets 404 with type not-found, title 'Resource Not Found' and the refusal's message as detail; a missing notification's message is 'Cannot find notification with reference number: ' followed by the reference.
requirements.why: One not-found shape for every endpoint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-082 (the 404 handler) and p2-084 (the not-found message).

requirements.statement: An upstream failure (unreachable, timed out or non-2xx) gets 502 with title 'Upstream Service Error' and the exception's message as detail.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The backend's exception handler on main has no upstream-error answer, and the claim this rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted; today the handler's answers are those repo-backend-p1-073 to p1-086 record. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073: today's handler and its problem-detail answers, none of them a 502.

requirements.statement: A resource conflict such as a duplicate key gets 409 with type conflict, title 'Resource Conflict' and the refusal's message as detail.
requirements.why: One conflict shape for duplicate writes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-083 (ConflictException handling).

requirements.statement: An oversized upload gets 413 with title 'Payload Too Large' and detail 'Uploaded file exceeds the maximum permitted size'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The backend's exception handler on main has no payload-too-large answer, and the claim this rested on left the working set when the backend was re-extracted. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-073: today's handler and its problem-detail answers, none of them a 413.

requirements.statement: A failure to write the outbox event, or to get a notification's write lock after two retries 50 milliseconds apart, gets 500 with title 'Internal Server Error' and detail 'An error occurred during submission. Please try again.', whichever lifecycle action failed.
requirements.why: The user is asked to retry without internal detail leaking.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-085 (the outbox-write answer), p2-019 (the lock gives up after two retries with 500) and p2-120 (50 milliseconds between tries).

requirements.statement: Any other unexpected runtime failure gets 500 with title 'Internal Server Error' and detail 'An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.'; Spring's own framework errors, such as an unknown path, keep Spring's default answers (for example 404).
requirements.why: Unexpected faults never leak internals and unknown paths are not turned into 500s.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-086 and p1-087.

requirements.statement: The backend listens on port 8085, writes a notification and its outbox event in one MongoDB transaction, so MongoDB runs as a replica set, and serves Swagger UI in the local profile only.
requirements.why: Records the runtime the record depends on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-088 (README: port and replica set) and p2-132 (Swagger UI off in deployed environments, on locally). The Floci provisioning and start-up settings an earlier extraction recorded are no longer in this area's working set.

requirements.statement: The backend README describes its tests accurately.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a documentation inaccuracy the DR2.1 goal does not cover, which goes to the report. The claim that the README calls the tests mock-free while a test uses Mockito left the working set when the backend was re-extracted; repo-backend-p1-093 is what the new extraction says of the README. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-093: the README, AGENTS.md and design notes give reasons, not rulings.

requirements.statement: POST /notifications with no reference number creates a notification: its created time stamped, its organisation set from the organisation header, a new reference number, status DRAFT, every sent field stored and returned, and a NotificationCreated outbox event at aggregate version 1; in the live-animals frontend a post to the set's notifications path redirects to the new notification's origin page.
requirements.why: Starting a notification creates the record the journey then fills.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-001, p2-002, p2-020 and p2-021 (create), p4-004 and p4-019 (the NotificationCreated event, versions starting at 1) and repo-tests-p9-064, p9-131.

requirements.statement: Every save and lifecycle endpoint answers 200 with the whole stored notification record, and no endpoint returns the inbound notification shape.
requirements.why: The frontend picks up the new concurrency token and state from each write.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-004 and p1-070.

requirements.statement: A content save replaces the whole notification content (origin, commodities, reason for import, additional details, the five parties, CPH number, transport, purpose in internal market, destination country, port of exit, exit date and the fulfilments payload), so a field left out of the body is saved as empty rather than merged, keeps the status, creates no second notification and writes a NotificationEdited event.
requirements.why: Each page save sends the whole record built from the journey.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-012 and p2-013 (the save replaces every field), p2-017 and p4-005 (status kept, NotificationEdited written) and repo-tests-p9-125 (replace whole).

requirements.statement: POST /notifications with a reference number updates that notification under the same rules as PUT: 404 for an unknown reference, 400 unless the notification is DRAFT or AMEND, 400 without a concurrency token, and a NotificationEdited event on success.
requirements.why: Only an editable notification the caller has the current version of can be saved.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-002 and p2-131 (POST with a reference updates under PUT's rules) and p2-084 (the not-found message).

requirements.statement: PUT /notifications/{referenceNumber} replaces the content and fulfilments of the notification named in the path, keeps its DRAFT or AMEND status and writes a NotificationEdited event on every save; it answers 404 for an unknown reference, 400 unless the notification is DRAFT or AMEND, so a SUBMITTED notification is saved only once moved to AMEND, and 400 without a concurrency token.
requirements.why: The frontend engine's save path.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-007, p2-009, p2-010, p2-017 and p2-127 (replace).

requirements.statement: Each event's metadata carries the correlation id of the request that caused it, and the published message carries it again as its correlationId attribute.
requirements.why: An event can be traced back to the request that caused it, through to PIMS.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-023 (the metadata correlation id) and p4-039 (the message attributes).

requirements.statement: POST /notifications/{referenceNumber}/submit, with the concurrency token the caller last read and an optional actor as its body, moves a DRAFT or AMEND notification to SUBMITTED, so the submitted content is exactly what the caller last read; it answers 400 for any other status or a missing token, 409 for a stale token, and 404 for an unknown reference. After submission the stored status is SUBMITTED and the notification view reloads read-only as Submitted.
requirements.why: Submission is the one action that sends the notification to PIMS.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-041 to p2-044, p2-042-m1 and p2-129 (submit); repo-tests-p9-005, p9-039 and trace-e2e-p14-134.

requirements.statement: Declaring a notification in the live-animals frontend takes two posts to the declaration page, each carrying a concurrency token read from the page before it, and the second redirects to the confirmation page; declaring a draft that is not finished is refused back to the notification view with a refused marker.
requirements.why: The trader reaches their reference once the notification is sent, and an unfinished draft cannot be sent.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-066 (the two declaration posts and the redirect to confirmation), p9-067 (an unfinished draft's declaration is refused) and p9-156 (addresses, view, declaration, confirmation in the browser).

requirements.statement: A first submission (from DRAFT) writes a NotificationSubmitted event and a re-submission (from AMEND) writes NotificationSubmissionAmended; only these two count as submissions.
requirements.why: PIMS tells a first submission from an amendment by the event type.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-047, p4-006, p4-007 and p4-033.

requirements.statement: Submit stores the notification as it stands and its event carries the GBN-AG body built from the notification at that moment, identified by the reference number, with the consignor published as stored.
requirements.why: PIMS gets what the trader declared.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-041 (submit), p4-031 (the event's data is a snapshot of the notification), p4-064 (the identifier) and p4-125 (the consignor).

requirements.statement: Every event's payload lists only the notification's accompanying documents that are claimed and scanned clean, read as the event is written; a document still uploading, unclaimed or not clean is left out without refusing the submit, and with none the referenceDocument key is left out rather than sent empty.
requirements.why: PIMS is never sent a document that has not passed the scan.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-069 and p4-070 and repo-tests-p9-162 (no referenceDocument on a notification with no document).

requirements.statement: An actor sent with a write (inside the save body for POST and PUT, as the optional body of copy, submit, amend, cancel-amend and soft delete) is recorded on that event and its status change: id, source, userType, displayName, organisationId and onBehalfOfOrganisationId, with the organisation always the one the request was made for, not one the caller supplies, and missing fields left out of the published JSON; without one no actor is recorded. The admin hard delete and replay name the person by a User-Id header instead.
requirements.why: PIMS records who submitted or changed the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-055, p2-006, p2-129, p2-130, p4-026 and p4-027, and repo-tests-p9-108.

requirements.statement: A submission event's versionId is the count of earlier submission events plus one (1, then 2 on the next); amendment-requested, amendment-cancelled and submission-deleted events carry the latest submission's versionId; created, edited and deleted events carry no versionId.
requirements.why: PIMS orders the versions of one notification by versionId.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-032 to p4-034 (OutboxService versionId rules).

requirements.statement: Each event for a notification takes the next aggregateVersion, starting at 1 on creation; two events can never share one ('Duplicate aggregateVersion on outbox insert').
requirements.why: Consumers apply one notification's events in order.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-019 and p4-020.

requirements.statement: Every save and lifecycle change to one notification writes the record and its outbox event together under a lock for that notification, held at most 10 seconds and tried again up to twice, 50 milliseconds apart.
requirements.why: Concurrent writes cannot interleave their events.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-019, p2-019-m1, p2-120 and p4-013 (the per-notification outbox lock).

requirements.statement: For PUT, copy, submit, amend, cancel-amend and soft delete, saving the notification and writing its outbox event happen in one transaction: both land or neither does.
requirements.why: A change and its event are never out of step.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-013 (the transactional outbox in @Transactional service methods) and p1-088 (one MongoDB transaction).

requirements.statement: Creating or saving a notification through POST /notifications saves the notification and its outbox event in one transaction, as PUT and submit do.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a reliability defect in the backend that the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-131: POST's save path is not marked @Transactional where PUT's is; the outbox lock still couples the record and event writes.

requirements.statement: The backend checks that a caller belongs to the organisation it names, guards every admin route, and answers a request for another organisation's notification the way it answers one for a notification that does not exist.
requirements.why: Out of scope: access-control weaknesses in the backend that the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix (authentication is a real constraint, not a design difference); they go to the report, named in general terms only.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-087: the organisation header is taken on trust; p2-093: two admin read routes are protected by neither the header nor the admin secret; p2-094: the admin secret has a built-in fallback in the shared configuration; p2-098: the hard delete is not scoped to an organisation; p2-081: the fulfilments read answers 403 for another organisation's notification where other endpoints answer 404. repo-tests-p9-126 shows every call names the organisation in its header.

requirements.statement: GET /notifications/{referenceNumber}/fulfilments, taking only the organisation header, returns the reference number, concurrency token, status, created and submittedAt, the fulfilments payload and whether an open amendment's answers differ from the submitted version, for a notification in any status, soft-deleted included; it backs the frontend's rehydrate. An unknown reference answers 404, and a reference held by another organisation answers 403 with type forbidden, title 'Forbidden' and detail 'Cannot read fulfilments for notification with reference number: ' followed by the reference and the caller's organisation id.
requirements.why: The frontend journey engine rebuilds every page from this view.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-069, p2-080 to p2-082, p2-081-m1, p1-081-m1 and p2-005-m1, and repo-tests-p9-124; req-1886 adds the category to it.

requirements.statement: The backend offers no read of one notification's whole content by reference other than the fulfilments view and the notification list searched by that reference, whose row carries the reference number, concurrency token, status, created moment, origin, commodities, consignor, consignee and transport; the notification API echoes unreached sections as null beside status, created, updated, submittedAt, fulfilments and the concurrency token.
requirements.why: Pages that show stored answers read them from the fulfilments payload or the list row.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-079 (no whole-notification read), p2-075 (the exact reference search) and p1-065 (the list row's fields); repo-tests-p9-119 and p9-122.

requirements.statement: GET /notifications/reference-numbers returns reference numbers only, 50 per page, newest created first, across every organisation and every status (soft-deleted included), with a 0-based page parameter (default 0, at least 0) and a response of content, page, size, numberOfElements, totalElements and totalPages.
requirements.why: Admin and test tooling enumerate every reference without loading content.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-068 and p2-105 to p2-107.

requirements.statement: DELETE /notifications permanently removes the notifications named in a JSON array of references, in any organisation, with their accompanying documents, and answers 204, all or nothing: an empty list or a missing trace id or User-Id header is 400 with nothing deleted, and any unknown reference is 404 'Cannot find notifications with reference numbers: ' followed by the missing ones, comma-separated, with nothing deleted.
requirements.why: Admins and the test suite clear notifications without leaving orphaned documents.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-095 to p2-098 and p1-056 (the trace id and User-Id headers).

requirements.statement: Every DELETE /notifications request writes a DELETE_NOTIFICATIONS audit record to the audit collection with its result (SUCCESS, or FAILURE kept even when the request fails on a missing reference), the references, their count, the trace id, the user id and the time; it writes no outbox event, so other services are not told. Trader lifecycle changes write no audit record.
requirements.why: Hard deletes are audited; the lack of an event is today's behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-099 to p2-104 (the hard delete's audit and the audit collection).

requirements.statement: DELETE /notifications and POST /notifications/{reference}/replay require the Trade-Imports-Animals-Admin-Secret header to match the TRADE_IMPORTS_ANIMALS_ADMIN_SECRET setting, compared in constant time; a missing or wrong secret gets 401, and with no secret configured every check fails, so the routes are closed. The four admin routes need no organisation header.
requirements.why: Destructive and replay operations are kept to holders of the admin secret.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-089 to p2-092 and p2-094 (AdminSecretFilter and AdminNotificationRoutes).

requirements.statement: The backend's soft-delete tests pin only the answers the service gives, a repeat soft delete returning the notification unchanged with 200.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a misleading test in the backend that the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report. The claim about the mocked controller test left the working set when the backend was re-extracted; repo-backend-p2-062 is today's behaviour the test should pin. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-062: a repeat soft delete changes nothing and answers 200.

requirements.statement: The trader notification list (GET /notifications: its paging, sort, reference search, status filter, row shape and indexes) is specified and proven by the notification-list area, not this one.
requirements.why: Out of scope for this area: the list API is notification-list's, which owns its fields, filters and sorts.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-018, p1-019, p1-066, p1-067 and p2-066 to p2-078 record the list as it is today.

requirements.statement: The backend defines eight notification lifecycle event types, each with the wire value uk.gov.defra.imports.notification.<Type> and a schema in DEFRA/trade-imports-schemas under schemas/profiles/imports/gb/events/: NotificationCreated, NotificationEdited, NotificationSubmitted, NotificationSubmissionAmended, NotificationAmendmentRequested, NotificationAmendmentCancelled, NotificationDeleted and NotificationSubmissionDeleted (gbn-ag-event-notification-<kebab type>-v1.schema.json).
requirements.why: Consumers discover and validate every event against its governing schema.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-001 to p4-003 (OutboxEventType) and repo-tests-p9-159 (the suite finds the submission event by its wire type).

requirements.statement: Each lifecycle action writes its event: amend NotificationAmendmentRequested, cancel-amend NotificationAmendmentCancelled, soft delete of a DRAFT NotificationDeleted and of a SUBMITTED or AMEND notification NotificationSubmissionDeleted, a repeat soft delete none; a copy appears only as the new draft's NotificationCreated, and the source gets no event.
requirements.why: Downstream services follow every change of state.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-008 to p4-012 (which event each step writes), p2-030 (the copy's NotificationCreated), p2-054, p2-060 and p2-064. The backend has no templates (repo-backend-p2-123), so no template use writes an event today.

requirements.statement: Outbox events are stored in the MongoDB collection outbox, each with eventId (a new random UUID), aggregateId 'Imports.Notification.GBN-AG.<reference>', aggregateType Notification, subType GBN-AG, aggregateVersion, eventType, timestamp (write time to the millisecond), the notification's organisationId at the top level, data (the GBN-AG body built from the notification as it stands when the event is written, for every event type), metadata (correlationId, schemaVersion 1, schemaUrl), actor and statusChanges.
requirements.why: Every consumer reads this envelope.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-014 to p4-025 and p4-031 (OutboxEvent and OutboxService), repo-tests-p9-106, p9-109 and p9-159; the envelope does not change in this programme, and the notification's category stays off it (c-272).

requirements.statement: Each event carries the notification's full status history so far, each entry a status, the date it changed and the actor who changed it, adding a status change only when the status differs from the last recorded.
requirements.why: PIMS sees who moved the notification between statuses and when.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-028 and p4-029.

requirements.statement: An event's publish time is stored with it but left out of the published event.
requirements.why: Records today's behaviour: consumers are not told when the outbox published an event.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-030 (publishedAt not published) and p4-047 (the publish time recorded).

requirements.statement: A poller (on unless outbox.poller.enabled is false) publishes waiting events, running again 2,000 milliseconds after each run ends, one instance at a time under the lock outbox-poller (held 1 to 30 seconds), reading 10 at a time up to 500 per run (OUTBOX_POLLER_MAX_EVENTS_PER_RUN; zero or less falls back to 10 and 500, and an interval that is not positive stops start-up), oldest written first then by aggregateVersion, marking each published event with its publish time so it is never published again, and logging each published event's eventId, aggregateId and version.
requirements.why: Events reach consumers in order, once, from one publisher.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-040 to p4-047 and p4-051 (OutboxPoller, OutboxConfig and OutboxPublishService) and p2-121.

requirements.statement: Events are published to the one SNS FIFO topic set by OUTBOX_SNS_TOPIC_ARN, a setting the configuration marks required, and nothing is published while no topic is configured; each message is the whole event as JSON, with group id the aggregateId, deduplication id the eventId, and string attributes eventType, correlationId, schemaVersion and schemaUrl (empty string when missing). Locally the topic is trade_imports_animals_eu_notifications.
requirements.why: One notification's events stay ordered while different notifications flow independently.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-035 to p4-039 and p4-035-m1 (OutboxConfig and OutboxPublishService) and p2-122 (the local topic).

requirements.statement: An event with no data is skipped with an error log and never published; an event SNS refuses, or whose payload cannot be turned into JSON, stays unpublished, stops the run and is tried again on the next poll, so no later event overtakes it (a JSON failure is logged as needing manual investigation).
requirements.why: No event is lost on a failed publish.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-048 to p4-050.

requirements.statement: A poison event never blocks later events: an event that always fails, or a run of payload-less events at the head of the queue, is set aside with an alert rather than stopping publication for every notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: an operability defect in the backend publisher that the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-049 and p4-050: a refused or unserialisable event stops the run and stays at the head of the queue; p4-048-m1: skipped payload-less events still count towards the run's 500-event limit and are re-read each page.

requirements.statement: Integration tests prove publication: create then submit publishes each event once, in aggregate version order, with its envelope, metadata, payload and attributes.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set records the backend's publication tests any more; the claims about them left the working set when the backend was re-extracted. What is published is recorded from the code in req-1567 and req-1571 (repo-backend-p4-038). The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.

requirements.statement: Backend tests prove that amend, cancel-amend, copy and soft-delete events reach SNS, and call the outbox-events read through the API.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a test gap in the backend the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report. The claims that recorded the gap left the working set when the backend was re-extracted.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-052: the outbox-events read exists; no claim in this area's working set records a test of it.

requirements.statement: GET /notifications/{referenceNumber}/outbox-events returns every outbox event for a notification in the order written, aggregate version ascending.
requirements.why: Support can see what was sent for a notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-108 and p4-052.

requirements.statement: POST /notifications/{referenceNumber}/replay, with the admin secret and a User-Id header, re-publishes every event for the notification to the SNS FIFO topic in aggregateVersion order with the original group and deduplication ids, changes nothing in the outbox, answers 200 with the number of events replayed, answers 404 'No outbox events found for: <reference number>' with no audit record when there are none, logs the replay with its event count, reference and user id, and writes a REPLAY_EVENTS audit record (result, reference, event count, trace id, user id, time); an event replayed inside SNS FIFO's deduplication window may be dropped.
requirements.why: Support can resend a notification to PIMS.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-109 to p2-111, p2-111-m1, p1-071 and p4-053 to p4-057, p4-060-m1 (OutboxReplayService).

requirements.statement: Replay reports failures truthfully: a replay that stops early reports only the events it sent, and an SNS rejection is audited as a failure.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a defect in the backend's admin replay that the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-058 and p4-060: a JSON failure stops the replay and audits FAILURE yet reports every event found; p4-059: an SNS refusal ends the replay with an error and no audit record.

requirements.statement: A submitted notification reaches PIMS Dynamics by way of the backend's outbox and its SNS topic, the dynamics gateway and Azure Service Bus, arriving as one row of PIMS's importer notifications table named with its reference number.
requirements.why: Records the cross-service route a submission takes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-035 (the SNS topic), repo-tests-p9-072 (one PIMS row per reference) and p9-095 (the dynamics gateway's allow-list stands between the backend's events and PIMS).

requirements.statement: A submitted notification appears in PIMS Dynamics as exactly one importer-notification row named with its reference number, at status Submitted and version 1, with a submission date within about ten seconds of the backend's submit time, the submitting user's display name, the country of origin and each party's country by PIMS's own full country names, whether the consignment includes unweaned animals as a true or false flag, the arrival date, the port of entry as its code, the means of transport in PIMS's own words, the consignor, place of destination, place of origin, consignee and importer each as a company name with an address line 1, a city and a country lookup, the transporter's company name, and the trader's internal reference as the trader reference.
requirements.why: The end-to-end proof that submission reaches the case-working system.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-072 to p9-087 (the animals Dynamics specs) prove all of it today; p9-085 proves only that the rest of the transporter is filled in, because it comes from the transporter's reference record rather than the trader's answers, and p9-086 records that four answers the journey leaves out arrive empty.

requirements.statement: The PIMS Dynamics tests run only against a CDP environment (the compose stack has no PIMS Dynamics), set up their Dynamics client before the journey so a missing setting fails at once, run with Playwright tracing off so no credential is recorded, report a failed sign-in and any error without the secret or the request's call log, allow two minutes for a notification to reach PIMS and ten for an amendment or deletion, and attach the row they read to the report; the Mongo persistence and submission-event tests run only on the compose stack, where Mongo can be read.
requirements.why: Each end-to-end proof runs where its dependency exists, without leaking credentials.

requirements.statement: The rest of the PIMS Dynamics importer-notification record (its second consignor, harvest, compliance, weight, exit, departure and journey-time columns) is proven to carry the submitted data.
requirements.why: Out of scope: widening the PIMS data test is not a DR2.1 difference; the gap goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-103 to p9-105: the record is typed from the Dataverse table metadata, so it describes what PIMS can hold rather than what the service sends, and only the primary key, the reference, the state code and the owner are always filled in.

requirements.statement: A submitted-notification outbox event can be placed straight onto the dead-letter FIFO queue, where the admin UI shows the event id as the message Id.
requirements.why: Out of scope: nothing in this area's working set supports it any more. The tests-repo claim it rested on now records the REST client's retry backoff instead, and no claim here names the dead-letter queue. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve; repo-tests-p9-106 is the event shape such a check would use.

requirements.statement: Tests-repo specs prove the whole submission event: its specified consignment, actor, status changes and metadata as well as its exchanged document, and the party, country, location and transport fields the suite's event model types.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a test gap the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-164: only the field names of the submission event's exchanged document are checked; p9-114 and p9-115: the event model types party, country, location and transport fields no spec reads.

requirements.statement: The GBN-AG event data always carries $model 'defra/certificate-internal/1' and $type 'gbn-ag', and two sections, exchangedDocument about the notification and specifiedConsignment about the consignment, built from the notification as it stands when the event is written.
requirements.why: PIMS reads the GBN-AG certificate model.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-061 to p4-063 (GbnAgEventData), p4-031 and repo-tests-p9-109.

requirements.statement: exchangedDocument carries identifier (the reference number), traderAssignedId (the internal reference), notificationStatusCode (the status name), versionId (left out when the event has none), issueDateTime (when the notification was last updated, as an ISO-8601 UTC instant), the signed clauses and, when there are any, the referenced documents; for a notification with only the mandatory answers it carries exactly the first six.
requirements.why: PIMS identifies and versions the notification from this block.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-064 to p4-068 (ExchangedDocument) and repo-tests-p9-160, p9-161 (the six fields the mandatory-answers submission event carries).

requirements.statement: exchangedDocument.issuer carries the person responsible for the notification.
requirements.why: Out of scope: an open GBN-AG mapping gap that no DR2.1 or DR1 source settles and the parity goal does not fix; it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-160: the exchanged document carries no issuer; neither the model nor the test names one.

requirements.statement: Each published accompanying document is one referenceDocument entry with a typeCode from its document type, urlId https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/gbn-ag-document-types, its document reference as identifier and its date of issue as a date-only issueDateTime.
requirements.why: PIMS receives each scanned supporting document.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-071 (ReferencedDocument).

requirements.statement: Each accompanying-document type is published with its typeCode: veterinary health certificate 853, air waybill 740, sea waybill 710, rail waybill 720, bill of lading 705, commercial invoice 380, ITAHC 856, import permit 911, journey log GBN3, self-declaration GBN1, CITES permit or certificate GBN2, packing or species list GBN4, and Other 916, used only for Other and never as a default; the mapping covers every type with no default, so a new type cannot be added without choosing its code.
requirements.why: PIMS classifies documents by these codes.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-072 to p4-085 (the document type code switch, thirteen types today).

requirements.statement: exchangedDocument.firstSignatoryAuthentication.includedClause holds, in order, a PURPOSE clause from the reason for import naming the list https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/gbn-ag-purposes, then, only when the reason is internal market, an INTERNAL_MARKET_PURPOSE clause from the purpose in the internal market naming https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/gbn-ag-internal-market-purposes, then a GOODS_CERTIFIED_AS clause from the certified-for answer naming https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/gbn-ag-goods-certified-as. A clause whose answer is not given is still published, with its identifier and no content or list; an answer with no code in its list is published unchanged as the content, with the list named, and a warning naming the reference number is logged.
requirements.why: PIMS receives the trader's declaration in coded form.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-086 to p4-092 (Authentication and Clause).

requirements.statement: The GBN-AG payload carries the record's purpose in the internal market in the INTERNAL_MARKET_PURPOSE clause.
requirements.why: Out of scope as its own requirement: the backend now publishes the purpose in the internal market in that clause, and req-1590 carries it with the rest of the declaration clauses. The id is kept so earlier citations still resolve.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-087 and p4-089: the clause comes from the purpose in the internal market.

requirements.statement: specifiedConsignment maps the consignor to consignorParty, the consignee to consigneeParty, the place of origin to despatchParty, the place of destination to deliveryParty, the importer to importer and the transporter to carrier. Each consignment party, and an animal's permanent address, is published with its name and postal address, its email and phone as one definedContact with no person name only when at least one is given, and no identifier, partyRoleCode or partyTypeCode.
requirements.why: PIMS receives every party the trader named.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-125 to p4-130, p4-139, p4-140 and p4-175 (SpecifiedConsignment and TradeParty) and repo-tests-p9-111.

requirements.statement: The carrier is published with the transporter's approval number as identifier (urlId https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/uk_transporter_authorisation when one is given), its name and postal address, a partyTypeCode holding the transporter type coded against https://traces-codelists.ec.europa.eu/operator_activity_type (none when no type is given), no contact details and no partyRoleCode; with no transporter the carrier is left out.
requirements.why: PIMS identifies the authorised transporter.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-141 to p4-143 and p4-142-m1 (TradeParty's carrier).

requirements.statement: The stored transporter types are confirmed to match the TRACES operator_activity_type codelist the carrier's partyTypeCode names.
requirements.why: Out of scope: an open GBN-AG codelist gap (EUDPA-274) no DR2.1 or DR1 source settles; it waits on the PIMS mapping work and goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-142: the transporter type is published against the TRACES list as stored; repo-tests-p9-036: the journey's default transporter stores the type 'Commercial'. The commodity classCode half of this gap closed: the trade line now carries the commodity code (repo-backend-p4-162).

requirements.statement: A postal address is published as lineOne (address line 1), lineTwo (address line 2), cityName (town or city), postcodeCode (postcode), countryId (the ISO country code) and countrySubDivisionName (county), never with a countryName.
requirements.why: PIMS derives the country name from the code.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-144 and p4-145 (TradeAddress).

requirements.statement: originCountry is published with code.value the country of origin code (left out when no country is given), the country subdivision as one subordinateTradeCountrySubDivision entry (the MDM subdivision code as identifier, urlId https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/country_subdivisions and functionTypeCode 106, left out when none is given), and the regionOfOriginCode, a disease zone from the health certificate, only when the trader answered yes to needing a region code and gave one.
requirements.why: PIMS receives where the animals come from, with the subdivision and the disease zone held apart.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-131 and p4-146 to p4-150 (TradeCountry and TradeCountrySubDivision) and p1-021 (the origin values it reads).

requirements.statement: unloadingBaseportLocation.identifier is the port of entry with no other location details, left out when there are no transport answers or no port; finalDestinationLocation is the CPH number with urlId https://refdata.tbc.defra.gov.uk/cph_number, left out when no CPH number is given.
requirements.why: PIMS receives where the animals arrive and the destination holding.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-132, p4-132-m1 and p4-133 (LogisticsLocation).

requirements.statement: The transport movement is published as one mainCarriageLogisticsTransportMovement whenever there are transport answers, with no identifier or urlId: modeCode from the means of transport (vessel 1, railway 2, road vehicle 3, airplane 4; left out when none), usedLogisticsTransportMeans.name the transport identification (left out when none), a transportContractRelatedReferencedDocument holding the transport document reference with a typeCode inferred from the means (vessel 705, railway 720, road vehicle 730, airplane 740; none when the means is not given; left out when no reference), and an arrivalEvent whose scheduledOccurrenceDateTime is the start of the arrival date in UTC (left out with no date) and which carries no actual time or location; the transited countries go as transitTradeCountry codes, left out when none.
requirements.why: PIMS receives how and when the animals travel.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-135, p4-136 and p4-151 to p4-159 with p4-154-m1 and p4-155-m1 (LogisticsTransportMovement, ReferencedDocument and TransportEvent).

requirements.statement: isOrHasUnweanedAnimals is published as true when the unweaned animals answer is yes (in any letter case), false for any other answer, and left out when it is not answered.
requirements.why: PIMS receives the unweaned-animals answer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-137 (SpecifiedConsignment).

requirements.statement: includedConsignmentItem holds one consignment item whose trade lines are one per species of every commodity, with that species' counts, and is left out when there are no commodities; a commodity with no species gives one line from the commodity's own totals, with the commodity name as commonName and no scientific name or animals, and a commodity with species publishes no totals of its own. Each line carries a CN applicableClassification of the commodity code (systemId CN, left out with no code), the commodity description as a one-item description (left out when blank), scientificName the species' text, commonName the species' common name or else the commodity name, specifiedLineTradeDelivery.productUnitQuantity.content the number of animals (left out when not given) and physicalReferencedLogisticsPackage.itemQuantity the number of packages (left out when not given), with no unit, level or type codes.
requirements.why: PIMS receives what is being imported, line by line.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-138, p4-160 to p4-167 with p4-166-m1, p4-167-m1 and p4-173-m1 (ConsignmentItem, TradeLineItem, LineTradeDelivery and LogisticsPackage) and repo-tests-p9-112, p9-113 meet every part of it. The trade line's typeCode is the one change, made by req-1894 for live-animal lines and req-1800 for germinal ones (c-273).

requirements.statement: Each identified animal on a species is published as an individualTradeProductInstance: the horse name as name, its identifiers in the order ear tag, passport, microchip, tattoo with typeCodes EAR_TAG, PASSPORT, MICROCHIP and TATTOO and urlId https://codelists.tbc.defra.gov.uk/animal_identifier_types (a blank identifier left out, and no list when there are none), and its permanent address as permanentLocation. A species with no identified animals is published as one instance holding the species' own ear tag, passport and microchip, with no name, tattoo or permanent location.
requirements.why: PIMS receives each animal's identity.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-168 to p4-170 (TradeProductInstance).

requirements.statement: The GBN-AG payload carries what the record holds and PIMS needs: the destination country, port of exit and exit date, each identified animal's identification details and description, the species code, and a postal address on the final destination location as the schema requires.
requirements.why: Out of scope: GBN-AG payload gaps no DR2.1 or DR1 source asks to close and the parity goal does not fix; they go to the report for the PIMS mapping work. The created, submitted and expiry times, the fulfilments, the pre-amend snapshot and the answers-differ flag stay off the payload by design.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-171 to p4-173: the destination country, port of exit, exit date, identification details, description and species code are not published; p4-134: the final destination carries no postal address although the schema requires one; p4-174: the record's times, fulfilments, snapshot and answers-differ flag are not published.

requirements.statement: GBN-AG mapping edge cases are safe: every section leaves out a field with no value, and a missing port of entry or an empty commodity list sends no empty element.
requirements.why: Out of scope: latent mapping defects the DR2.1 parity goal does not fix; they go to the report. The claims that recorded the defects left the working set when the backend was re-extracted, and today's extraction shows the port of entry and the consignment item left out when absent (repo-backend-p4-132-m1, p4-138).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-132-m1 and p4-138: the base port and the consignment item are left out when there is nothing to publish.

requirements.statement: A notification seeded through the animals frontend's own save-and-continue forms, as a user signed in through the Defra ID stub, stores the same status, notification content and fulfilments as the same journey walked in the browser; seeding never writes to the backend directly, names each party the answers name, and first makes sure the shared journey addresses exist in the address book.
requirements.why: Test set-up builds records exactly as a user would.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-058 to p9-061 and trace-e2e-p14-135 (the seed parity spec); p9-028 reads each party back from the live address book by name, p9-069 seeds a draft, submitted or amend notification from the command line, p9-148-m1 signs in through the Defra ID stub and p9-168 makes sure the shared addresses exist.

requirements.statement: The live-animals journey's save-and-continue pages, in order, are origin, a commodity search per line then the species choice, consignment details, commodity identification, import reason, additional details, the five party selections, the permanent address where a species needs one, the addresses page, the CPH number, the port of entry, the transit countries where given, the transporter, then the accompanying documents and addresses pages, reaching check your answers; '/' is a server-wide redirect to the default set.
requirements.why: Records the route map today's record is filled through; the journey areas own any change to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-155 (the seeded journey's page order) and p9-070 (no set at the root).

requirements.statement: The record is fed by the live-animals pages' own forms: a species is chosen by a checkbox whose value is the commodity code and the Latin name joined by a pipe, each party is picked by its address-book id, the permanent address is asked once per animal, and the declaration is two posts each carrying a concurrency token.
requirements.why: Records how each page feeds the record; the journey areas own any change to the pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-066, p9-140, p9-143, p9-144 and p9-147 (the tests repo's form builders) post these fields.

requirements.statement: A page that rejects its submission re-renders with an error summary rather than redirecting; a successful save, and a refused state change (amend, cancel, delete), redirect, the outcome shown by where they land; every form post carries a CSRF crumb minted by loading the set's own dashboard.
requirements.why: Records today's save contract the record's writes go through.

requirements.statement: A seeded draft can be left unlocked (origin and commodity answered, which opens the other tasks), partial (on through arrival) or ready (every section answered, so it can be declared), and can leave the import reason, the certification answer or the unweaned-animals question unanswered; an answer set that gives a region of origin code exactly when the origin does not require one is refused before any post.
requirements.why: Records the depths tests seed the record to.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-065 names the three stages; p9-146 shows a seeded draft can leave a named question unanswered, and p9-145 shows the answer-set guard.

requirements.statement: The persistence traces record the Mongo document reads, so the stored shapes rest on captured documents as well as the spec assertions.
