requirements.why: Out of scope: an evidence limitation, not a behaviour the programme changes.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p14-150: the Mongo reads behind every persistence test are not recorded in the traces.

requirements.statement: In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'What are you importing?' goes to 'Main import reason', and 'Main import reason' goes on to 'Commodity details': the reason for import is asked before the numbers of animals and packages.
requirements.why: The target design asks origin, what you are importing, the reason for import and then commodity details, in that order, and the owner's 9 October ruling counts question order as look and feel the prototype decides.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-019, repo-frontend-p3-020 and repo-tests-p8-007: the animals frontend and the tests repo now walk origin, 'What are you importing?', 'Main import reason', 'Commodity details'. The older captures of the same journey still show commodity details before the reason (trace-animals-fit-p1-055, trace-e2e-p14-118), so those traces are behind the repos.

requirements.statement: In the opening run, 'Save and continue' on 'Consignment addresses' goes to the review page: the journey has no contact address step. The CPH number page and the permanent address page are not steps of the journey: each is reached only from its row on 'Consignment addresses', and saving it returns there.
requirements.why: The target design's step order has no CPH step: roles and addresses is followed by the contact address, and the CPH number and permanent address are reached from inside roles and addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-189 and repo-tests-p4-176: Continue on the consignment addresses page reaches check your answers, with no contact address page between; repo-tests-p4-177: Back on the CPH number page returns to the consignment addresses page; repo-frontend-p1-241: the set asks for no contact address at all. The older captures still walk the addresses page on to the CPH page (trace-animals-fit-p1-061, trace-e2e-p14-108).

requirements.statement: When every section on the overview is already complete, 'Save and continue' on 'Consignment addresses' returns to the overview.
requirements.why: The target design skips the rest of the linear run once nothing is left to answer, so a trader who finishes the addresses last lands on the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and continue' on the addresses page goes to check your answers whatever the rest of the notification holds (repo-tests-p1-189, repo-frontend-p1-064), not to the overview when every section is complete.

requirements.statement: A new notification's opening run takes 'Save and continue' from page to page through every question that applies, in the journey's order, without stopping at the overview; the overview is reached by 'Save and return to overview', by 'Cancel and return to overview' or by the notification's own root address.
requirements.why: The target design sends each saved step to the next step in a fixed order. The real journey already does this for a new notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-074 and repo-tests-p8-013: the opening run carries a new notification from the origin page through every question to its review page in one pass; repo-frontend-p3-108: the overview is reached by 'Save and return to overview' or by the notification's root address.

requirements.statement: 'Save and continue' on 'Consignment addresses' at the end of the opening run always goes to the review page, even when the notification is incomplete; the review page then names what is outstanding.
requirements.why: In the target design the review is an ordinary step after the contact address, and completeness is enforced only by the overview's statuses and the review page's submit.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-189 and repo-tests-p4-176: Continue on the consignment addresses page reaches check your answers, which shows the notification's reference. The review section's own readiness gate is still in the set's flow (repo-frontend-p1-053) and is set aside for the run in c-205.

requirements.statement: A page opened from a task on the overview returns to the overview when it is saved rather than carrying the trader on through the rest of the journey. The service tells such a page apart by where it already records the trader as having come from.
requirements.why: Every overview task in the target design returns to the overview when saved, and the owner's 9 October ruling confirms it. Each page the real journey chains on to has its own row on the overview, so nothing becomes unreachable.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and continue' always offers the next page in journey order, whatever the page was opened from: a task opened from its overview row carries only the overview as where it came from and still walks on (repo-tests-p8-044, repo-tests-p8-045, repo-frontend-p1-064, repo-frontend-p3-076). 'Save and return to overview' already returns to the overview (repo-tests-p8-147), and the older captures show the earlier behaviour of chaining through a section before returning (trace-animals-fit-p1-059 to trace-animals-fit-p1-062).

requirements.statement: A journey page's Back link goes to the page the trader pressed 'Save and continue' on, to the overview when the page was opened from the overview, to the review page when it was opened from a Change link there whether or not the notification is being amended, and to the overview when nothing says where the trader came from or when it names a place the journey does not have. A page shown again after a refused save still goes back to the page 'Save and continue' was pressed on.
requirements.why: The target design builds every journey page's Back link from the context it was opened in, and the real journey now does the same.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-226 and repo-tests-p8-057: Back now goes to one of five places — the page 'Save and continue' was pressed on, the overview when the trader came from the overview, the review when they came from a Change link (amending or not), and the overview as the fallback; repo-frontend-p1-227: a refused save keeps Back on the page it was pressed on. The older capture still shows Back going to the overview in change mode (trace-animals-fit-p1-083).

requirements.statement: 'Save and return to overview' saves the page and takes the trader to the notification's overview rather than to the next page of the journey. The button submits the service's own exit=hub form field.
requirements.why: The target design treats it as a save that leaves the linear flow. The real journey already does this; form field names are architecture, which the prototype does not decide.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-136 and repo-frontend-p3-108: 'Save and return to overview' commits what the trader typed and lands on the overview rather than the next page; trace-animals-fit-p1-050: the button submits exit=hub.

requirements.statement: 'Cancel and return to overview' is a link to the overview that leaves the page without saving what was typed, and it is always available, whatever the page still has unanswered.
requirements.why: The target design's cancel control is a plain link to the overview, and the data specification makes cancel always allowed whatever is unfilled. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-135: 'Cancel and return to overview' discards what the trader typed and lands on the overview, and repo-frontend-p3-060: it is a link that follows the two save buttons with no checks of its own.

requirements.statement: Every page the overview links to ends with a primary 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link, in that order, with the two buttons in one button group above the link.
requirements.why: This is the target design's default page ending, and the DR1 rule (b) judgement gives exactly the overview-linked pages these three controls. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-060, repo-tests-p4-134 and repo-tests-p8-061: a page offering all three controls shows 'Save and continue', then 'Save and return to overview' as the form's last button, then the 'Cancel and return to overview' link below the group.

requirements.statement: No contact address page is built, so no page carries the hub-worded return controls 'Save and return to hub' and 'Cancel and return to hub'.
requirements.why: The target design words the contact address page's return controls with 'hub'. The prototype wins over the frontend's own rule that 'hub' never appears to users, which is not a DR1 judgement.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-241: the set has no contact address obligation, section, task row or route; repo-tests-p4-167: the suite's shared page object still names a hub-worded pair that no animals flow uses. Design Release 2.1 drops the page too (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p10-122, prototype-dr2-1-specs-p10-156).

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, the party pickers, the CPH number page and the permanent address page show a primary 'Save and return' button that goes to the review page and a secondary 'Save and continue' button, and no link-styled 'Save and return to overview'. The buttons submit the service's own form fields.
requirements.why: DR1 rule (b) judged where return-to-overview controls go and keeps the hub control off these pages, while the amend-only 'Save and return' and 'Save and continue', which DR1 never judged, follow the target design's amend ending.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page outside the task-row journey ends with its primary button alone and offers no 'Save and return to overview' (repo-frontend-p3-061, trace-animals-fit-p1-051, trace-animals-fit-p1-052), and an amendment ends every page with exactly the controls it shows on a draft (repo-plantsfrontend-p12-088).

requirements.statement: On every page that offers both, 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make exactly the same checks, with no page an exception, in live animals, in the germinal products copy and on plants' pages. A page whose answers all pass saves them, and 'Save and return to overview' then shows the notification's overview. A page with an answer that is missing or does not pass its own rule keeps the trader on the page, shows an error for each such answer, and shows back everything they entered. The answers checked are the page's own hard stops together with any the data specification marks mandatory to proceed; an answer that is only mandatory to submit can still be left blank on either button.
requirements.why: The owner's 26 October ruling adopts the business analyst's expected behaviour: both save buttons behave the same way, upload documents included, and what the trader typed is kept. The data specification says the same.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-125 to repo-tests-p4-131: 'Save and return to overview' makes the same checks as 'Save and continue' on the main import reason, arrival details, commodity details, transporter list and commodity selection pages, refusing each with the page's own errors and leaving its row 'To do'; repo-tests-p4-132: a page with only mandatory-to-submit answers outstanding, such as additional details, is accepted on either button. The 27 November ruling keeps this reach (ruling-sam-2026-11-27-p1-011 to ruling-sam-2026-11-27-p1-013).

requirements.statement: Pages inside a notification (the overview, the question pages and the review page) show a status strip above the caption: a blue 'Draft' tag, or the notification's own status, followed by the notification reference in bold, a GBN-AG-<two-digit year>-<six characters> reference minted by the backend when the notification is created. The strip shows from the first request on the origin page and never on the dashboard. The shared strip is not changed in place: a page that needs a different header switches the shared strip off and draws its own header in the set's template.
requirements.why: The target design shows the status and reference on every journey page, with 'Draft' when the notification has no other status. The real journey already does this, and the 9 October afternoon ruling keeps the shared strip as it is.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-138 and repo-tests-p4-141: the strip shows a blue 'Draft' tag and the notification's reference from the first request and stays on the overview and every task page; repo-frontend-p1-152: the reference is GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX in Crockford base32; repo-tests-p4-137: the dashboard carries none. Today the declaration also carries the strip (trace-e2e-p13-010).

requirements.statement: Starting a new notification creates a fresh, empty notification with its own reference and opens its origin page; the trader's other drafts, submitted notifications, templates and address book are kept.
requirements.why: The target design clears the journey's answers when a notification is started but keeps everything else. The real service already creates a new record for each start.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-011 and trace-e2e-p13-003: 'Start a new notification' creates a notification with its own reference and redirects to its origin page.

requirements.statement: Opening any page of a notification directly sends the trader to its origin page when the notification holds no answer the trader entered; the origin page itself, the create path and the amend, cancel-amend, copy and delete actions are exempt, and the redirect is logged once with the notification's id and the path that was asked for.
requirements.why: Real notifications are server records anyone signed in can reach by URL, which the prototype (one notification per browser session) cannot express: the entry guard is a real persistence constraint that overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-094 and repo-frontend-p1-094-m1: every path under a notification is guarded except the create path, the four action slugs and the origin page, the overview among the guarded ones; repo-frontend-p1-095 and repo-tests-p8-050: a notification with no answer the trader entered is sent to its origin page.

requirements.statement: Every page needs a signed-in session: a signed-out trader who opens any page is sent to the service's /auth/sign-in with the page they asked for kept in a 'redirect' parameter, and after signing in returns to that page with its saved answers intact, or to the dashboard when none was asked for. A redirect is followed only when it is a relative path on the same service, and it is used once.
requirements.why: Authentication is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so it overrides the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-042: a signed-out request to a notification page goes to /auth/sign-in with the path in a redirect parameter and returns to it after signing in; repo-tests-p4-166 and repo-frontend-p3-005: the overview, a question page and check your answers each need a signed-in trader and authorisation is enforced even in stub mode.

requirements.statement: A page opened from the review page returns to the review page when it is saved, and keeps that context through its own in-page actions (add, remove, upload) until it does; 'Save and return to overview' still goes to the overview first.
requirements.why: The target design returns a page reached from the review to the review, with the overview taking precedence over the review, and the prototype wins by default on where a saved page goes.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a page opened from a Change link walks on through the rest of the journey instead of returning to the review: origin reaches the commodity selection page and additional details reaches arrival details (repo-tests-p4-116), and the review is reached only once every later page has been saved (repo-tests-p4-118, repo-tests-p4-121, repo-frontend-p3-084). The context already survives the page's own add, remove and upload round trips (repo-tests-p4-123, repo-frontend-p3-081).

requirements.statement: Every journey page is a server-rendered form: a successful save is a full-page POST answered by a redirect to the next page, each save stores the notification as a draft, and every option list arrives in the page rather than from a browser call to another service.
requirements.why: The target design posts each page and redirects, persisting a draft each time, with every list rendered by the server. The real journey already works this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-054: a save is a POST to the page answered by a 302 to the next page; repo-frontend-p3-058: each page's answers are posted by one POST form; trace-e2e-p14-121: a notification walked to the declaration is stored as DRAFT; trace-e2e-p13-111: the browser talks only to the frontend.

requirements.statement: A page refuses a save only for its own hard stops; every other answer can be left blank to proceed, and completeness is enforced by the overview's statuses and the review page's submit. For example, a blank transporter and an empty transit countries list are allowed, a reason's follow-up question is required once that reason is chosen, the number of animals is required, and documents are optional unless the trader has started one.
requirements.why: The target design separates what blocks a page from what blocks submission, and the data specification does the same by marking an answer optional, mandatory to proceed or mandatory to submit. The real journey already keeps that separation.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-136, repo-frontend-p1-172 and repo-frontend-p1-175: the transporter, transit countries and documents answers do not hold back a save; repo-tests-p4-132: additional details is accepted with both questions blank and its row stays 'To do'.

requirements.statement: On 'Arrival details', in the live-animals and germinal products sets, a save is refused only when the means of transport is missing; the arrival date, port of entry, transport identification and transport document reference can be left blank to proceed. Plants' arrival details keeps its own rules.
requirements.why: The target design makes the means of transport the arrival page's only hard stop, because it decides whether transit countries apply. The 9 October afternoon ruling makes arrival details' own rules animals only.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the arrival details page refuses a date that names no real day as well as a missing means of transport, on either save button (repo-tests-p4-126, repo-tests-p4-127, repo-tests-p8-079), and the obligation model marks the arrival date, the port of entry, the means of transport, the transport identification and the transport document reference all mandatory (repo-frontend-p1-127, repo-frontend-p1-128, repo-frontend-p1-133).

requirements.statement: On commodity details, a save is refused when a line that asks for a number of packages has none.
requirements.why: The target design makes the number of packages a hard stop on that page alongside the number of animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a line's number of packages is asked only when its commodity code is on the package-count list and is optional there (repo-frontend-p1-158, repo-tests-p4-027); the number of animals is already refused when blank (repo-tests-p4-129).

requirements.statement: The transit countries step, and its row on the overview, apply only when the means of transport is rail or road; choosing any other means skips the step, takes the row off the overview and deletes any saved transit countries. Transit countries are optional to proceed.
requirements.why: The target design adds the transit countries step only for rail or road. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-005, repo-tests-p4-006 and repo-frontend-p3-033: the transit countries step and its overview row appear only for rail or road; repo-tests-p4-008 and repo-tests-p4-009: changing the means to one that does not ask for them takes the row off the overview and wipes the saved countries; repo-frontend-p1-136: they are never compulsory.

requirements.statement: The animal identification step follows commodity details only when at least one chosen species has identifiers of its own; a consignment with none never reaches the identification page, and a commodity with none gets no panel on it.
requirements.why: The target design adds the identification step only when a selected species has identifier fields. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-054: opening the identification details page for a notification with no commodity line that asks for it shows the commodity selection page instead; repo-frontend-p1-179 and repo-frontend-p1-191: a per-animal gate decides line by line, so a line whose code is outside the identified list is asked for free text rather than a named identifier.

requirements.statement: The additional details step applies to every live-animals consignment because it always asks what the animals are certified for; its unweaned animals question appears only when a commodity line is one that triggers it, such as cattle.
requirements.why: The target design adds the additional details page whenever it would ask the certification purpose or the unweaned question, and live animals are always asked the purpose. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-014 and repo-frontend-p1-150: the certified-for question is always asked; repo-tests-p4-015 and repo-frontend-p1-160: the unweaned question shows only once a triggering commodity line exists.

requirements.statement: The CPH number applies when any commodity line's commodity code is one the data specification requires it for, and is out of scope otherwise; for cats, dogs and ferrets each animal's permanent address is asked in place of a CPH number.
requirements.why: The data specification decides which commodities a conditional rule covers, and the owner's 11 November ruling makes its allow-list the shape the service holds, with how the list is held in code the frontend's own call. The target design brings the CPH number in by commodity code and asks a cat's permanent address in its place.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-159 and repo-frontend-p1-194: the CPH number is asked when any commodity line's code is on a seventeen-code allow-list and is out of scope otherwise, which is the shape the 11 November ruling called for; repo-frontend-p1-170 and repo-frontend-p1-196: the three species under 01061900 are asked for a permanent address instead; repo-tests-p4-018 and repo-tests-p8-068: a cats-only consignment shows no CPH row.

requirements.statement: Each reason for import brings in only its own follow-up questions, revealed on the same page: the purpose for internal market; the exit port and destination country for transit; the destination country for transhipment or onward travel; the exit date and port of exit for temporary admission of horses. Changing the reason deletes the follow-up answers that are out of scope for the new reason.
requirements.why: The target design requires a reason's follow-ups once that reason is chosen and walks each branch this way. The real journey already scopes them like this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-144 to repo-frontend-p1-147: the purpose, destination country, port of exit and exit date are each in scope only for their own reason and are purged when the reason changes; repo-tests-p4-030 to repo-tests-p4-032 prove the reveals and the wipe.

requirements.statement: Only the transporter details that match the chosen transporter type are kept: switching between commercial and private deletes the other type's details.
requirements.why: Keeping one consistent transporter record is a real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express. The real journey already does this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-130 and repo-tests-p4-038: switching the transporter type drops the other type's stored record.

requirements.statement: An answer to a question that is out of scope is not shown, checked or saved, and any stored value is cleared in the same save; when one field of a collection entry leaves scope only that field is cleared.
requirements.why: The real service must not store answers the notification no longer needs: a real persistence and validation constraint that holds whatever the prototype shows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-178: a gate that swaps an answer's scope drops the stored answer when the gate answer flips; repo-tests-p4-016 and repo-tests-p4-009 prove it for the unweaned question and the transited countries, and repo-plantsfrontend-p12-055 for plants' arrival status.

requirements.statement: A notification's arrival date counts as complete only when it falls between 7 days in the past and 6 months ahead.
requirements.why: The target design holds the arrival details task back outside that window. The real journey already applies the same window.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-062, repo-tests-p4-063 and repo-tests-p8-074: the arrival date must fall between seven days in the past and six months ahead, and a saved date that falls out of the window puts the row back to 'To do'.

requirements.statement: Each journey page carries the caption of the part of the notification it belongs to, immediately above its heading: 'About the consignment' (origin, what are you importing, animal identification, main import reason), 'Description of the goods' (commodity details), 'Commodity details' (additional details), 'Transport and arrival' (arrival details, transporter), 'Movement' (transit countries), 'Add a new transporter' (the add-a-transporter pages), 'Documents' (accompanying documents), 'Addresses' (consignment addresses, CPH number, permanent address) and 'Dashboard' (the set's dashboard). The overview, the review page, the declaration and the confirmation carry none, and nor do the delete-notification and cancel-amend pages, which interrupt the journey rather than belong to a section.
requirements.why: The target design's pages carry these captions, and the owner's 17 November ruling words the addresses section 'Addresses'. The real journey already captions them this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-105 to repo-frontend-p1-113: the nine caption sections and the pages in each; repo-frontend-p1-116-m1: the review page, the declaration, the confirmation and the contact address page carry none, and repo-frontend-p3-089: the overview is exempt. The addresses, CPH number and permanent address pages now read 'Addresses' (repo-frontend-p1-109), which the older capture shows as 'Consignment parties' (trace-animals-fit-p1-069).

requirements.statement: The tests repo walks a cattle-by-air notification (identification details, the unweaned question and a CPH number) from create to submitted in the journey's step order, checks every overview task reads Complete before the review, and checks the review shows the answers given.
requirements.why: The target design proves this journey end to end, and the real suite now proves it too, so the step-order changes have a walk to keep green.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-006 and repo-tests-p8-007: the suite walks a cattle-by-air notification from create to submitted in the journey's order, through identification details, the unweaned question and a CPH number; repo-tests-p8-017: every overview row reads 'Complete' before the review, and repo-tests-p8-023 and repo-tests-p8-036 check the review shows the answers given.

requirements.statement: A poultry-by-rail notification (Chicken 01051111 Gallus gallus, Transit with an exit port and destination country, transit countries and a CPH number, no identifier given) can be walked from create to submitted, and the tests repo proves it.
requirements.why: The target design proves this journey end to end. The real suite already walks it as far as the review, and the 9 October afternoon ruling makes the rest wait with the MDM commodity catalogue.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the suite walks a poultry-by-rail notification in transit from create to the review, through the identification details page, with every overview row complete (repo-tests-p8-080, repo-tests-p8-081), and stops there: the MDM stub serves no species page for that commodity, so Continue from the review is refused (repo-tests-p8-086).
requirements.blockedBy: Commodities must come from MDM: the chicken commodity's species page is only in the MDM commodity catalogue, which waits on MDM supplying commodities.

requirements.statement: Whether a pet-cats-by-air notification can be walked from create to submitted is weighed with the other whole journeys, not here.
requirements.why: The target design proves this journey end to end, and the real suite now proves it with the permanent address answered on its own page.

requirements.statement: Whether a horse-by-sea notification can be walked from create to submitted is weighed with the other whole journeys, not here.
requirements.why: The target design proves this journey end to end, and the real suite now proves it too.

requirements.statement: Every new or changed piece of user-facing text has a Welsh version, the English and Welsh copy keep the same shape, and a machine-drafted Welsh string does not reach users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The real service is bilingual, a real constraint the English-only prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-114: the Welsh caption file carries exactly the same keys as the English one, none missing and none extra; repo-frontend-p1-115 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-115: the Welsh drafts are machine-made and must not ship without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's journey structure holds: the obligation model decides what applies and whether it is mandatory, the journey flow decides the page order and the sections, task rows decide grouping on the overview, each answer is claimed by exactly one page, and the obligation model holds no display copy.
requirements.why: These are the real frontend's recorded rules on how scope, order and grouping are kept apart; every flow change in this area lands through them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-023 and repo-frontend-p1-072: the journey flow decides the sections, the page order and the twelve task rows; repo-frontend-p1-025 and repo-frontend-p1-028: each answer is claimed by exactly one page; repo-frontend-p1-058: a page applies when at least one obligation it collects is in scope; repo-frontend-p1-015 and repo-frontend-p1-015-m1: boot refuses an obligation carrying display wording.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend refuses to start when the journey is not fully configured — a seam left unwired, a journey cookie unregistered, an obligation collected by no page or by two, an obligation carrying display wording, or an obligation id holding a path metacharacter — and the platform's limits hold: scope rules are code, asking the journey flow anything before it is configured raises rather than answering, a page's gate opens when one of its answers is in scope, and a collection entry's position is not a durable identifier.
requirements.why: These are real constraints of the platform every flow change runs on.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-013, repo-frontend-p1-014 and repo-frontend-p1-022: the set refuses to mount on an unwired seam or an unregistered cookie and refuses to answer before the journey flow is configured; repo-frontend-p1-016 to repo-frontend-p1-019: the boot checks on obligation ownership, display keys and ids; repo-frontend-p1-177: a document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value.

requirements.statement: Every page this programme touches passes an accessibility check with no serious or critical violation of WCAG 2.0 A and AA, WCAG 2.1 A and AA or WCAG 2.2 AA, on first render and in its error state, and no page overflows sideways at a 360 by 740 phone viewport or a 1280 by 720 desktop viewport.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint of a GOV.UK service that the prototype does not check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-069 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-058: a page a fit spec checks must have no serious or critical violation against those rule sets, and the failure names every violation found; repo-plantsfrontend-p14-063: a picker is checked empty, after a search that matched and after one that did not; repo-frontend-p3-068: pages are checked at both viewports.

requirements.statement: A page with validation errors shows a GOV.UK error summary titled 'There is a problem' ('Mae problem' in Welsh) at the top of the content, above the caption and heading, listing one entry per field in field order with the first failing rule's message, each linking to its field. The summary is exposed as an alert and takes focus when the trader has just been refused, each field shows the same message beside it, and the browser title gains an 'Error: ' prefix. A page with no errors shows no summary.
requirements.why: The target design shows every error this way. The real journey already does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-012 and repo-tests-p4-168: a refused page shows a 'There is a problem' summary whose links name each problem, with a message beside each field; repo-frontend-p3-063: the summary is announced as an alert and a summary link puts focus in its field; repo-tests-p1-013 and repo-frontend-p3-093: the browser title gains an 'Error: ' prefix.

requirements.statement: Date fields take a date as d/m/yyyy with single-digit days and months allowed, through a Ministry of Justice date picker the trader can also type into, whose 'Choose date' button opens a calendar that ends above the next question on the page and names each day by its weekday, day, month and year.
requirements.why: The target design's date pickers work this way, the interaction designer's 9 November answer keeps the Ministry of Justice picker, and the real journey already uses it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-154: the arrival date is one box in d/m/yyyy backed by a date picker; repo-frontend-p3-065 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-065: the 'Choose date' button opens a calendar beside the box that ends above the next question.

requirements.statement: The prototype's version mount and session mechanics are not built: the /design-release-2.1 base path, the per-version session nest and its shared keys, path prefixing, override-view fallback, the redirect-only and retired routes it keeps for its own pages (such as /dashboard, /permanent-address and /address-book/add/usage), and the route and coverage tables that describe them.
requirements.why: They are how the prototype kit hosts several design releases side by side, not behaviour of the real services, which serve live animals under /live-animals and keep notifications and the address book in their own services.

requirements.statement: The prototype's seed shortcuts and fixtures are not built: the /prototype/reason-for-import seed route, the legacy /transport-details redirect, the design release index page, its reference format and random reference generator, the fixed GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P reference and the seeded dashboard reference mapping, the seeded GBN-GP germinal references, and the submitted view's fixed sample answers.
requirements.why: They exist to demo and test the prototype, not as service behaviour; the real service's references are minted by the animals backend, and the owner's 9 October ruling calls GBN-GP references demonstration data only.

requirements.statement: The prototype's mount leaks are not copied: the template Cancel link, the transporter 'View details' links and the document virus check that leave /design-release-2.1 for the root paths.
requirements.why: They are defects of the prototype's version mount, with no counterpart in a service that has one set of paths.

requirements.statement: The plants for planting, potatoes and wood products journeys are not built in the animals frontend.
requirements.why: Those types belong to the high-risk plants journey in its own frontend, and in the target design they reach a commodity search that offers nothing. Germinal products is not excluded: the owner's 9 October ruling makes it a sibling set of live animals in the animals frontend, and its journey is carried by req-1898 and req-1899.

requirements.statement: What the target design's traces and specs do not exercise is recorded, not built: the importer and place of destination postcode lookups' address lists, making a template, the permanent address and contact address override pages, the documents virus-check endpoint, the address book's usage page, dashboard pagination, the date-range filter, Needs action through the filter form, signing in under the intro pages, and what each snag asks to change.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the target evidence; nothing in them says what to build differently.

requirements.statement: What today's traces, suites and repos do not show is recorded, not built: backend calls behind the browser, real identity-provider sign-in, 404 and error pages, no-JavaScript country and port selects in the end-to-end traces, copy as new, cancelling an amendment from the dashboard, where the overview and cancel controls lead from a page opened in change mode, which commodity codes make the CPH number, package-count and unweaned questions appear, how far ahead an arrival date may be, the port-of-entry search's wording and announcements, the no-results wording of either search box, the means-of-transport prompt, a transporter being added inside a whole-journey walk, the look of any journey page other than the origin page, what the Address book, Manage account and Log out navigation items lead to, what a journey page does when the stub address book or reference data cannot be reached, which caption each plants journey page shows under a cross-page test, amending or copying a plants notification, and any heading, copy or validation error on the pages the k6 performance suite drives.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the evidence of today's behaviour; each is weighed where its page is built.

requirements.statement: The suites' fixture data and driving mechanics are test scaffolding, not requirements: the stub sign-in routes and organisation ids, the fresh-organisation trick, the seeded notification stages and the pages a seeded draft posts to, the canned transporters, document files and address-book records, the named parties and country, species and port constants, the field names a seeder posts, the k6 blank-field answers, select defaults, skipped search boxes, sample draft id and endpoint tags, and the Playwright projects, timeouts, retries and video settings each suite runs with.
requirements.why: They describe how the suites drive the service, not what a trader sees; they change only as the journeys they drive change.

requirements.statement: The last navigation item, 'Log out', links to /auth/sign-out on every frontend (animals, INS and plants) and is never marked as the current item. Log out ends the user's session with the service and sends them to Defra ID's sign-out page, headed 'You have signed out'. Opening the dashboard again afterwards asks them to sign in again with their user ID and password.
requirements.why: Ending a real session properly is an authentication behaviour the prototype cannot show. It already works and is proven end to end.
requirements.deltaNote: The item links to /auth/sign-out on all three frontends (repo-frontend-p2-010, repo-insfrontend-p1-015, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-007, trace-e2e-p9-082, p9-086, p15-002) and only Dashboard and Address book can be current (repo-insfrontend-p1-013-m1). trace-e2e-p1-041 to p1-046 and repo-tests-p6-073 and p6-075 show Log out reaching the signed-out page and the dashboard asking for sign-in again. The INS sign-out callback checks the state value only when Defra ID sends one (repo-insfrontend-p1-168-m2).

requirements.statement: The Manage account navigation item is a placeholder on every frontend (animals, INS and plants): it links to '#', leads nowhere, and is never marked as the current item.
requirements.why: The target design shows Manage account as a placeholder with no destination, which is what all three frontends do today, and the earlier parity programme recorded that the item has no owner or destination to point at.
requirements.deltaNote: All three frontends link Manage account to '#' (repo-frontend-p2-011, repo-insfrontend-p1-014, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-008, trace-e2e-p15-003, p9-087) and never mark it current (repo-insfrontend-p1-013-m1), as the prototype does (prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-023, p1-024).

requirements.statement: The first navigation item, Dashboard, links to the dashboard home of the set or frontend the page belongs to and is marked as the current item there. On the animals frontend it links to the set's own root (/live-animals for live-animals), which renders that set's own notification list, and stays current on every page inside a notification, because the list, the create action and everything under them count as one section. On the plants frontend it links to the plants set's own root and stays current on the list and on every page of a notification. On the INS frontend it links to / and is current on the dashboard and on the notification type page. A Back, 'View dashboard' or 'Return to your dashboard' link that the target design sends to the overall dashboard goes to the set's own notification list.
requirements.why: In the target design the dashboard is the home: it is the Dashboard item's target and where the back link to the dashboard goes. The owner's 9 October afternoon and templates rulings keep each notification list in its own frontend at the set root, so the item and every return to the dashboard stay on the set root, which all three frontends already link to.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals Dashboard item goes to the page's home URL and stays current while the dashboard section is active (repo-frontend-p2-009, p2-013, p2-130, p1-005, p1-006, trace-e2e-p9-083); the plants item goes to the set's own base URL and every path under the set's /notifications counts as the dashboard section (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-007, p13-010, p13-069-m1); the INS item goes to / and is current on the dashboard and the notification type page only (repo-insfrontend-p1-010, p1-011, p1-013). The prototype makes the dashboard its home and Dashboard target (prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-083). Each set root keeps rendering its own list (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-089, p3-103), so nothing moves. Where each return link points is built by the areas that own those pages (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-101).

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend (both sets) and the INS frontend, the Address book navigation item takes the user to the INS frontend's address book at /address-book, and is marked as the current item on the address book and every page under it, the transporter pages and the add page reached from a journey hand-off included. From the animals frontend this is a link to the INS frontend's origin, and a user with no INS session goes through INS sign-in first.
requirements.why: The target design treats the address book as part of one service. In the deployed services it is a shared capability in the INS frontend, a cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals item already goes to the INS address book (repo-frontend-p2-158, trace-animals-fit-p1-020, trace-e2e-p9-084, p9-085); the INS item goes to /address-book and is current under it, transporter pages included (repo-insfrontend-p1-010, p1-012, trace-e2e-p9-086, p9-083-m1), and the INS smoke test reaches the list through it (repo-insfrontend-p1-132). The afternoon ruling keeps the INS front door reached through the service navigation, as today (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-102).

requirements.statement: On every frontend, the service navigation items appear only to a signed-in user; a signed-out page shows the service name with no items and no Log out link.
requirements.why: The navigation leads to pages that need a signed-in user. This is a real authentication constraint, and it already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-007, repo-insfrontend-p1-008 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-009 hide the items when signed out.

requirements.statement: Every page on every frontend uses the GOV.UK service navigation component, which shows the service name 'Import notification service' in the navigation bar rather than in the header. On narrow screens the items collapse behind a 'Menu' button, and the navigation landmark is named 'Menu'.
requirements.why: The target design names the service 'Import notification service' and uses GOV.UK service navigation with the name in the bar. All three frontends already do this, from GOV.UK Frontend components.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-016 and trace-e2e-p15-001 show the service navigation component carrying the name on the animals and INS frontends, repo-insfrontend-p1-001 and p1-016 the INS name and Menu button, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-002 and p13-011 the same on plants, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-095 that every shared chrome component but the date picker is a GOV.UK Frontend one.

requirements.statement: The GOV.UK header logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on every frontend, and the service name in the service navigation links to that page's dashboard home: the live-animals set's own root on live-animals pages of the animals frontend, the plants set's own root on the plants frontend and / on the INS frontend. A page outside every set links the service name to the site root, which sends the user on to the default set.
requirements.why: The target design sends both links to its index of design releases, prototype tooling with no counterpart in a deployed service, so it names no real destination; with no earlier parity judgement on the header links, the deployed frontends' targets are the only buildable ones and stand.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the logo links to https://www.gov.uk/ on all three frontends (repo-frontend-p2-005, repo-insfrontend-p1-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-005), and the service name links to the page's home URL on the animals frontend (repo-frontend-p2-013, trace-e2e-p9-082), to the plants set's base URL (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-007) and to / on the INS frontend (repo-insfrontend-p1-007, trace-e2e-p9-086). The prototype also links the service name to its dashboard (prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-103). A page outside every set takes the site root as its home link (repo-frontend-p2-156, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-057, p13-109).

requirements.statement: The prototype's service index at /index is not built: its title and 'Prototypes' caption, its introduction, its header that shows the service name in place of service navigation, and its 'Latest designs' and 'Testing prototypes' groups of version cards (Design release 1, Design release 2, Round 1 (Live animals), Round 1 (Germinals) and Round 2 (Live animals)) with their tags, subheadings, descriptions, 'What this version includes' details and start buttons.
requirements.why: The index is prototype tooling for choosing between design versions and research rounds. A deployed service has one version, so the page has no counterpart and nothing in the goal asks for it.

requirements.statement: The prototype kit's own tooling is not built: the kit's absence of custom Nunjucks filters and default session data.
requirements.why: This is how the prototype kit is set up to run demonstrations, not anything a user of the deployed service sees.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, every page's browser title reads the page name, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - '.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, every page's browser title reads the page's title, then 'Import notification service', then 'GOV.UK', joined by ' - ', as on the animals frontend.
requirements.why: The target design uses one title pattern on every page; the INS frontend's pipe pattern is today's build, not a constraint the prototype cannot express. The 9 October afternoon ruling says this row is not the blocked summary information and goes ahead.

requirements.statement: When a page shows an error summary, its browser title starts with 'Error: ' ('Gwall: ' in Welsh) in front of the whole title, on every frontend.
requirements.why: This is the GOV.UK pattern for telling screen-reader users there are errors, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-004, repo-insfrontend-p1-004 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-004 add the prefix, trace-animals-fit-p1-002 shows it rendered, repo-insfrontend-p1-129 and p1-130 prove it on two INS forms, and repo-insfrontend-p1-005 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-089 give the Welsh 'Gwall: '.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, page content sits in a two-thirds-width column by default, and a page that shows a table or other display content can use the full container width. These are the only two layouts: a page asking for any other width is refused rather than rendered at a default width.
requirements.why: The target design lays journey pages out in a two-thirds column. All three frontends already default to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-018, repo-insfrontend-p1-025 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-031 default to two-thirds, repo-frontend-p2-019, repo-insfrontend-p1-026 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-031 give display pages the full width, and repo-frontend-p2-020 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-032 refuse any other width.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, a page shows a GOV.UK back link labelled 'Back' ('Yn ôl' in Welsh), above the page content, only when it supplies somewhere for it to go. No page shows breadcrumbs, even when breadcrumbs are passed to the layout. On the animals and plants frontends Back goes to the place the trader actually came from, carried between pages in a 'from' query parameter listing those places newest last and holding at most 40 of them. The places a trail may name are the notification's overview, the set's notification list, the INS type question and any page of the journey by its slug; a trail naming anywhere else, an empty trail or one given twice is ignored in full and Back falls back to the notification's overview, or to the place the page names instead. Saving a page adds it to the trail the next page carries, going Back carries the rest of the trail beneath it, and a link with no trail gets no empty 'from' parameter. A page opened from another page returns to it when the request carries a 'return' marker naming a page allowed to open it, and a marker naming anything else is ignored. The trail and the return marker are percent-encoded into the address and join a query string the address already has.
requirements.why: Each page gets one route back (the back link) and one route up (the service navigation), and the trail is what makes the back link lead where the trader came from rather than to a fixed page. This already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-017, repo-insfrontend-p1-023 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-016 render the back link only when one is set, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-017 shows breadcrumbs are never rendered. repo-frontend-p2-047-m1 and p2-054 to p2-059 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-073 to p13-077, p13-111 to p13-113, p13-120 and p13-078-m1 give the trail, its places, its 40-place cap, how it grows and unwinds, and the return marker.

requirements.statement: A journey page on the animals frontend names its section in a caption directly above its heading, such as 'About the consignment' above 'Main reason for import', in the large GOV.UK caption size, and shows nothing where the journey leaves the page uncaptioned. Where the question legend is visually hidden, the caption still sits directly above the page heading. The dashboard has an extra-large 'Dashboard' caption above its heading, and the overview has no caption. The plants frontend shows its journey pages' section caption the same way and may ask for another caption size.
requirements.why: Section captions already exist on both journey frontends, derived from where the page sits in the journey. No source in this area's working set from the target design says otherwise.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p1-007 to p1-012 show the captions as rendered, repo-frontend-p2-032 and p2-033 how they are derived, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-059, p13-060 and p13-118 the plants captions and their sizes. Each page's own caption wording against the target design belongs to that page's area.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, where a field's own copy gives no message, the shared default validation messages apply: 'Select a valid option', 'Enter a valid postcode', 'Enter a valid registration number', 'Enter a valid UK telephone number', 'Enter a valid date', 'Enter a real time, like 14:30', 'Enter a whole number', 'Enter N characters or fewer' and 'Enter a number between MIN and MAX'. Each has a Welsh twin, a page's own message wins over them, and only the first failing message is reported for each field.
requirements.why: These are the fallbacks every page shares. Each page's own messages against the target design belong to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: The same defaults exist in all three frontends' shared copy (repo-frontend-p2-065, p2-066, repo-insfrontend-p1-054 to p1-062, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-093), each with a Welsh twin (repo-insfrontend-p1-063, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-104), a page's own message wins over them (repo-insfrontend-p1-064, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-107) and only the first message per field is reported (repo-insfrontend-p1-065).

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, a save that hits a recoverable backend failure re-renders the page with an alert banner titled 'There is a problem' that reads 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.' The banner sits at the top of the content column, and the page carries on working.
requirements.why: Real persistence can fail, which the prototype cannot express. The banner tells the user their answers are safe.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-021 and p2-154 render the banner and the fallback on animals, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-019 and p13-064 on plants, where it is announced as an alert and sits first in the content column (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-101).

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a page whose service call fails logs the failure once and is shown again with status 500 and a GOV.UK notification banner with role 'alert', above the page content, titled 'There is a problem' and reading 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Try again in a few minutes.' The Welsh banner reads 'Mae problem' and 'Mae’n ddrwg gennym, mae problem gyda’r gwasanaeth. Rhowch gynnig arall arni ymhen ychydig funudau.'
requirements.why: Real upstream services can fail, which the prototype cannot express, and the user is kept on the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-027 and p1-149 render the banner and the 500 status, and p1-028 gives its Welsh twin.

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, a form post refused because the notification changed after the page was opened sends the user back to the same page, with a staleAction marker added to any query string the address already carried. There an alert banner titled 'The notification has been updated' reads 'This notification was updated since you opened it. Review the details and try again.' Every page of a notification carries the token that says which version of it the trader is looking at, even a page that leaves its status strip off, and a stale refusal is passed on as a stale refusal rather than shown as a brief backend failure.
requirements.why: Concurrent edits to a stored notification are a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and the user must be told rather than shown a generic failure.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-022, p2-052 and p2-053 implement the refusal, the marker and the banner on animals, and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-020, p13-061, p13-062, p13-099, p13-100 and p13-110 on plants.

requirements.statement: A page inside a notification can show a shared strip above its content with the notification's status tag and its reference in bold, the reference being the notification's own journey id: blue 'Draft', green 'Submitted', yellow for an amendment or grey 'Deleted'. While the notification is being amended the strip also offers a 'Cancel amend' link to that notification's cancel-amend page, and a page can switch that link off while keeping the strip, or leave the strip off altogether and draw its own header in the set's template. The strip is shared by every set on the animals and plants frontends and is not reworded in place except by the Amend bar. The INS layout has its own journey strip, a blue 'Draft' tag ('Drafft' in Welsh) and the notification's id in bold, shown only on a page that passes one.
requirements.why: This is shared page chrome that already exists. The afternoon ruling keeps it as it is for every set: a page that needs another header switches it off, and only the Amend bar changes it in place. Each page's use of it belongs to that page's area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-023 to p2-025 and p4-049 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-021 to p13-026 render the strip, its tag and its Cancel amend link, and a page can leave it out (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-025, ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p2-061). The INS layout's strip shows only when a page passes one (repo-insfrontend-p1-029 to p1-031).

requirements.statement: No page shows a cookie banner.

The Welsh chrome names the service 'Gwasanaeth hysbysu mewnforio', labels Back 'Yn ôl', tags the phase 'Alffa', labels the navigation Dewislen, Dangosfwrdd, Llyfr cyfeiriadau, Rheoli cyfrif and Allgofnodi and the footer Preifatrwydd, Cwcis and Datganiad hygyrchedd, and carries the error summary, banner, error page, save control and status strip wording. requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends, when sign-in fails the user sees a page titled 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in' and headed 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.', asking them to 'Please try again', where 'try again' links to sign-in. In Welsh the heading reads 'Mae'n ddrwg gennym, ni allwn eich mewngofnodi.', with 'Rhowch' before the link 'gynnig arall arni'. The page shows when the sign-in callback receives an invalid code and state.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-031 gives the animals page and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-056, p13-102 and p13-103 the plants page, its full-stop-free title and its Welsh twin; repo-tests-p6-079, p6-079-m1 and p14-084 show when it appears and the suite trying again once.

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend, a sign-in callback that cannot be authenticated shows the unable-to-sign-in page: browser title 'Unable to sign in', heading 'Sorry, we are unable to sign you in.' and body 'Please try again.', where 'try again' links back to the sign-in it came from, /auth/sign-in from the service's own sign-in. The page uses the larger main wrapper spacing and shows the Exploring maturity banner. In Welsh it reads 'Methu mewngofnodi', 'Mae'n ddrwg gennym, ni allwn eich mewngofnodi.' and 'Rhowch gynnig arall arni.'
requirements.why: These are authentication failures the prototype cannot express, and the page already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-080 to p1-086 give the page, its link, its spacing, its Welsh twin and when it shows, and p1-079 its maturity level.

requirements.statement: An error response on every frontend is shown as the shared error page with the error's own HTTP status. The page's large heading is the status number, and a paragraph below it, which is also the browser title, reads 'Page not found' (404), 'Forbidden' (403), 'You need to sign in to view this page' (401), 'There is a problem with your request' (400) or 'Something went wrong' (any other), each with a Welsh twin. Its content holds only that heading and message: no back link and no error summary, with the service navigation still there for a signed-in user. A notification that cannot be found shows that standard page not found, like every other page in the service. An error on a path inside a journey set, routed or not, uses that set's chrome; a path under no set, such as /health or /auth/sign-out, uses set-free chrome whose home link is the site root and which shows no status strip, no success banner and no recoverable-error banner, at the form width.
requirements.why: Real errors are a constraint the prototype cannot express, and every frontend already shares this page; the owner's 19 November ruling makes a missing notification take it too.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-029 and p2-030, repo-insfrontend-p1-045 to p1-052 and p1-131 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-053, p13-054 and p13-103 render the page and its Welsh messages; repo-plantsfrontend-p13-057, p13-058, p13-109 and p13-114 and repo-frontend-p2-156 decide which set's chrome an error takes. The ruling's missing-notification clause is the only part not yet proven for the review page (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-030).

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, the service root / sends a signed-in user to the default set's dashboard, /live-animals, which starts a notification from 'Start a new notification'. A new live-animals notification is created by posting to /live-animals/notifications, its overview is at /live-animals/notifications/<journeyId>, each of its pages at /live-animals/notifications/<journeyId>/<page slug>, its review page at the slug notification-view and its cancel-amend page at the slug cancel-amend, and a journey can also be entered at /start.
requirements.why: This is how the animals frontend reaches its home today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-047 and repo-tests-p6-072 record the redirect, repo-tests-p6-069 and p6-078 the landing dashboard and its start button, repo-frontend-p1-002 to p1-005, p1-103 and p2-049 the addresses under the set, and repo-frontend-p2-129 the /start entry.

requirements.statement: The shared notification actions read 'Copy as new' and 'Delete' on the animals and plants frontends. After a copy, a success message titled 'Notification copied' reads 'A new draft notification has been created.' After a delete, one titled 'Notification deleted' reads 'The notification has been deleted.' Each has a Welsh twin. This shared copy is never reworded in place: a page whose wording differs adds keys in its feature's own copy.
requirements.why: This is shared copy the lists and notification pages already use, and the afternoon ruling forbids rewording it in place because the notification list uses it too. Comparing it with the target design belongs to the dashboard and notification-actions areas.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-062 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-092 give the copy, with the Welsh twins in repo-plantsfrontend-p13-090 and p13-103.

requirements.statement: Address pickers offer a shared 'Add a new address' link, and a success banner titled 'Success' says the named address was added to your address book. When a chosen address is not in the user's address book, the error reads 'The address could not be found in your address book. Select another address or try adding it again.' When the address book cannot be reached, it reads 'The address book could not be reached. Your answers on this page have been saved. Try again in a few minutes.'
requirements.why: This is shared copy the journey's address pickers already use. Comparing the pickers with the target design belongs to the addresses area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-063 and p2-064 give the copy.

requirements.statement: Sign-in hands off to Defra ID with an OpenID Connect authorisation-code request (scope openid offline_access, query response mode, policy b2c_1a_cui_cpdev_signupsigninsfi), naming each frontend's own serviceId and its own /auth/sign-in-oidc callback. On success the organisation the user signed in for comes back through the callback and the user is held in a server-side session. For a user signed in with Rural Payments credentials, the INS sign-in callback looks up the user's permissions from the Rural Payments and Siti Agri APIs with the Defra ID token, because the token carries the role name rather than its permissions.
requirements.why: Real sign-in through Defra ID is an authentication constraint the prototype's sign-in page cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-002 to p1-004, p1-028, p15-012, p15-020 and p15-112 record the hand-off on each frontend, and repo-insfrontend-p1-168-m1 the INS permissions lookup.

requirements.statement: After signing in, a user who belongs to more than one organisation is asked to 'Choose your organisation' from radios labelled with each organisation's name and SBI, with a Continue button. A user with one organisation never sees that choice. The chosen organisation reaches the service through the sign-in callback, and the user lands on the page they asked for. A page that needs an organisation refuses with 'Forbidden' when the session has none.
requirements.why: Organisation choice is part of real Defra ID authentication, which the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p15-016 to p15-020 record the single-organisation and multi-organisation paths on the INS frontend, repo-tests-p6-080, p14-083 and p14-083-m1 the picker's heading and options, repo-tests-p6-081 the two identities the suite signs in as, one of them in two organisations, and repo-insfrontend-p1-097 the refusal without an organisation.

requirements.statement: Signing in to one frontend signs the user in to the others without asking for credentials again, because Defra ID answers their requests straight away. Each frontend keeps its own session cookie on the shared host (sid for animals, ins-sid for INS, plants-sid for plants, unless a run names one), so all three sessions are kept side by side, and the three homes sit at different paths. Each service has its own landing page after sign-in, the INS frontend's checked landing page being the address book.
requirements.why: Moving between the animals journey and the INS dashboard and address book is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express. It already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-078 to p14-081 and trace-e2e-p15-111, p15-113 and p15-114 prove single sign-on and kept sessions across the three frontends from a browser with no cookies, and repo-tests-p14-086 that the INS landing page the suite checks is the address book.

requirements.statement: The session cookie lasts 4 hours and is HttpOnly. Every page route needs a signed-in user, on the request that shows a page and on the request that saves it alike; only health, static assets and the sign-in routes opt out.
requirements.why: Real sessions are an authentication constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already work this way.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-031, p1-031-m1 and p1-032 record the cookies, and repo-insfrontend-p1-096 and p1-170 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-033-m1 which routes need a session. What a user sees when a session lapses is not recorded (trace-e2e-p1-062).

requirements.statement: One switch, STUB_MODE, makes the INS frontend serve stub data and sign users in with its own stub session, and the switch is refused in production.
requirements.why: This is how the INS frontend runs locally and in its own browser tests. It is part of today's real authentication set-up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-155 gives the switch and its production refusal, and p1-156 that nothing loaded at boot can stop the service starting.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, every form post must carry a valid CSRF token. Every page carries the token in a csrf-token meta tag in its head, every form has a hidden 'crumb' input, and the CSRF cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite Strict.
requirements.why: Protection against cross-site request forgery is a real security constraint, and it already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-027, trace-e2e-p1-033-m1 and p1-032, repo-insfrontend-p1-034 and p1-140 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-029 show the token in the head, the form and the cookie.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend sends a Content-Security-Policy on its pages, redirects and sign-in callback. It limits scripts, styles, fonts, images and the base URL to its own origin (plus one hashed inline script), lets forms post to itself and the address book origin, and forbids framing and plugins. It also sends Strict-Transport-Security for a year, X-Frame-Options DENY, X-Content-Type-Options nosniff, X-Download-Options noopen, X-XSS-Protection and Cache-Control no-cache.
requirements.why: Security headers are a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and they already exist.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p1-052 to p1-060 and p1-056-m1 record the headers.

requirements.statement: Security-header and cookie defects found on the way are not fixed by this programme: the CSP's connect-src lists 'wss' without a colon, the animals frontend sends no Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, COOP or COEP header, and the animals and plants frontends share one 'crumb' CSRF cookie on localhost.
requirements.why: These are problems in today's services that bringing the services up to the target design does not touch. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The Defra ID stub's own pages are not changed by this programme: its sign-in page ('Sign in using Government Gateway', user ID and password, 'Help signing in', the 'I have forgotten my password' placeholder, the CRN error message that names neither field as the wrong one, and its non-standard error summary), its title, phase banner and doubled service name, its signed-out page and its own security headers. The stub is observed through the security proxy but never attacked, and its error summary list is left out of accessibility scans, while the service's own sign-in and callback handlers stay in scope.
requirements.why: The stub stands in for Defra ID and is not one of the programme's repos. Its defects go to the report, and the suites already treat it as somebody else's code.
requirements.deltaNote: The stub's pages are as trace-e2e-p1-005 to p1-027 and repo-tests-p6-068, p6-070 and p6-071 record them; repo-tests-p11-084, p15-078 and p16-122 show the suites already exclude the stub's own markup and traffic from attack and from accessibility scans.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's accessibility suite holds every scanned page to WCAG 2.2 AA. Every test carries the @a11y tag and is reported under that standard, read from the fixture so the title and the rule set cannot drift apart, and every scan passes the five axe tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa explicitly, because axe's own default leaves target-size out. A scan waits for the DOM and then allows a bounded settling period, scanning anyway if that wait times out; it is recorded against the page's path; a test runs every one of its scans before failing and reports them together with each violation's severity, rule, description, node count and help link, attaching them to the report as JSON; a failing scan fails its test and a test that takes the scan but never runs one fails too. A test is allowed five minutes. Pages whose layout matters at small sizes are scanned again at 320 by 568 and at 568 by 320, and a narrow scan also proves the page does not scroll sideways once its tables are discounted. A scan may be narrowed per page, and the only exclusions are the two conditional-reveal radio groups whose aria-expanded attribute axe rejects and the sign-in stub's own error list: upstream disagreements in code the service does not own. A clean scan is not full conformance, and a state earns its own scan only where its value outweighs the set-up it needs.
requirements.why: Every page this programme changes must keep passing this suite, and a new scan has to be written to these rules. It already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: The tests repo's accessibility suite meets it today (repo-tests-p10-001 to p10-022 and p15-058 to p15-092). Those claims now sit in the test-suites area's working set, not this one's, so this area cites only the ruling that places the germinal set's accessibility specs beside the animals ones (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-062); the cross-area pass re-attaches the suite's own evidence to this id.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite walks the live-animals journey from the notification list to the declaration and scans every journey page as it first opens, and walks it again filling each page in and ending at the submitted confirmation, scanning every page with its answers on it. Each page is reached through the journey flow's own steps and page objects rather than by the spec's own navigation.

requirements.statement: Each frontend's own browser tests check accessibility in the repo as well. The animals frontend checks that a captioned page and the dashboard with its service navigation have no serious or critical WCAG 2 A or AA violations, excluding the conditional-reveal false positive. The INS frontend checks every page's initial render and validation-error state against WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA. The plants frontend builds every shared chrome component from GOV.UK Frontend apart from the Ministry of Justice date picker, and its own pages are checked the same way. Review cards and other grouped content get their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's accessibility proof are not closed by this programme. On the animals side no scan covers the permanent address page, four of the five party pickers and four of the five party edit pages, the contact address edit page, the sign-in page or the organisation picker, the add-address hand-off to the address book, or the germinal-products set, and the narrow-viewport scan of the notification list does not check for sideways scrolling. On the INS side the empty dashboard, the empty address book, the address book's load-failure state, the notification type page and every transporter page go unscanned, and the dashboard's narrow-viewport scans do not check for sideways scrolling. The organisation-scoped API refusals are proven by status code only, the sign-in error is proven only for present-but-invalid values, no test drives the organisation picker as a journey of its own, and nothing proves another organisation's user is refused a notification's view page as well as its overview.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suites, not differences from the target design. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's security suite is a traffic-driven OWASP ZAP scan of six services, each its own named ZAP context with its own address: the animals frontend, the animals admin, the INS frontend, the animals backend, the plants backend and the address book. Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through the proxy rather than letting ZAP crawl, so coverage is traffic-driven and the attacking corpus is curated by hand. There are two profiles: a passive one that runs the end-to-end suite without attacking, and an attacking one that runs only the @active corpus, is deliberate, runs on the compose stack alone and is refused on the deployed platform because its journeys delete records the scan then re-fires with fuzzed payloads. Anything but the exact attacking profile name is treated as passive. Identifiers in a page or API address are declared to ZAP as data rather than structure, from a context plan registered before any traffic exists; all three plans must declare the same contexts; diagnostics are excluded rather than scanned; the DOM cross-site-scripting rule is off; the uploader and the queue-consuming INS backend are out of scope with their reasons; and the three APIs are scanned because every API client inherits the run's proxy. The attacking corpus drives sign-in and sign-out, a whole submitted journey, the reason-gated pages and a private transporter, amend, copy, cancel and delete, a document upload with its scan and download, a draft validation error, the notification list's search, paging and sorting, the review page's Change trail, and the INS address book's whole record lifecycle with its role filter, its refused hand-off guard and the INS dashboard. A run fails on a FAIL-rated alert from the rules file (an unlisted alert failing only if it is high risk), on a scan that finished at or within half a minute of its 60-minute cap, or on a declared context that saw no traffic; a per-domain run gates only that domain's contexts and is labelled scoped, and an unknown domain is refused by name. Each run clears its report folder but never removes it, writes a landing page before failing with a row per site, its request count and alert counts, publishes ZAP's log and machine-readable report as HTML, and the pass-or-fail decision is made by the suite's own gate rather than by the plans.
requirements.why: Every route this programme adds or changes must be driven through this scan to be attacked, and a new spec has to be written to these rules. The suite already exists.
requirements.deltaNote: The tests repo's security suite meets it today (repo-tests-p11-037 to p11-102, p15-094 to p15-116 and p16-106 to p16-148). Those claims now sit in the test-suites area's working set, so this area cites only the ruling that places the germinal set's security specs beside the animals ones (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-062); the cross-area pass re-attaches the suite's own evidence to this id.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's security scan are not closed by this programme. No transporter route is driven through the proxy. Only the refused side of the address book's cross-service hand-off is in scope, because no accepted token can be seeded. The attacking plan's note that the animals frontend's upload identifier is never reached is out of date.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend serves a fixed list of routes, all behind sign-in: the dashboard at /, the notification type question at /notification-type, and the address book's list at /address-book, its add, address type, address view, edit and delete pages and its transporter type, private and commercial add and transporter view, edit and delete pages, each id in a path URL-encoded. It also serves /health, its sign-in routes under /auth/ and static files under /public/. Each page answers a GET at its path, and a POST at the same path when it has a form. It owns no notification set, journey, page engine, document upload or event publishing: choosing a type on the notification type question sends the user to the start of the animals or plants frontend, which creates the draft, and a live-animals notification's origin page can open the question for its own notification and come back to it.
