requirements.statement: In the plants frontend the journey asks which plant health authority a notification goes to and derives the region from the place-of-destination address.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants parked competent-authority routing because the routing, access parity and region derivation are backend work the plants backend cannot yet do, and this programme's repos do not include it. What the place of destination question says about a spot check is plants' own wording, which no row of this programme changes, and the confirmation page belongs to another area.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p8-020 shows every version of the destination question promising only that a plant health inspector may carry out a spot check; no claim in this working set records the journey asking which authority the notification goes to or deriving a region.

requirements.statement: The notification holds one transporter type for the consignment, either commercial or private, settled by the type the chosen transporter carries and by the type the trader picks when adding one.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page makes the transporter type a notification-level, single-select field the trader sets, with exactly one of a commercial or a private value, needed before the notification can be submitted. The page's two code values are its data values, not page labels: how the option and the Type column read stays the design's (req-393, req-418).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-050 settles the type from the chosen row and repo-frontend-p13-087 records it on every add, as one of the two values.

requirements.statement: A notification holds the details of one transporter: a commercial transporter record when the transporter type is commercial and a private transporter record when it is private, never both, each held once for the whole consignment and taken from what the trader chooses.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page makes each transporter record conditional on the transporter type, single per notification, notification-level and sourced from the trader. Today's obligation model already does this, so the page confirms the rule rather than changing it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-041 collects the type with a commercial and a private record and the list keeps only the chosen type's, but saving an add form writes only that form's record and the type (repo-frontend-p13-127), so a record of the other type already on the notification stays beside it until the list is saved again.

requirements.statement: Both transporter forms ask the Standard Address Block's fields and contact fields, with the Standard Address Block's formats and limits, and read with the design's labels, hints, section heading and question order; the commercial form asks a transporter authorisation number as well and the private form asks none.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page types both transporter records as the Standard address block, the commercial one with an approval number added, and points their field-level validation at that block. The 11 November ruling settles which source decides what: where the data dictionary specifies a field's format, limit, level or whether it is mandatory it decides those, and the prototype decides how the field reads.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's transporter forms ask the Standard Address Block's fields in Design Release 2.1's order with its labels (repo-frontend-p13-016, repo-frontend-p13-017) and the private form asks no authorisation number (repo-frontend-p13-115). The address book's own transporter forms, which become the one route (req-2264), read with the block's own labels and section headings instead, which req-2265, req-2266 and req-2267 change; that evidence is the transporter-records area's.

requirements.statement: The commercial transporters the transporter list offers are the approved transporters the service's approved-transporter list holds.
requirements.why: The Live Animals and Germinals Data Fields page says commercial transporters are consumed from a list of approved transporters, and leaves which list as its one open point, which the 6 November ruling parks with approved transporters.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the commercial transporters on the list are seed records shipped in the animals frontend, with no approved-transporter list behind them (req-2273, repo-frontend-p12-049).
requirements.blockedBy: Approved transporters are parked by ruling:ian-2026-11-06 decision 3: a list of approved transporters managed in MDM for every organisation, added on top of an organisation's own transporters, is not in scope now, and which list the commercial records come from is the ruling's one explicitly open point. The transporter area is re-distilled once approved transporters are unparked.

requirements.statement: The service holds the two worked transporter addresses the data specification gives: the nine-line Northern Ireland transporter whose last line is the approval number UK/NEWCA/T1/00090953, and the eight-line United Kingdom livestock services address.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the two addresses are worked examples showing each field's format, not records the service holds. The transporters the list ships are parked with approved transporters (req-397, req-398) and the rest are what a trader adds. Each example also carries a mailto link whose address differs from its visible text, which is the page's own typing rather than anything to build.

requirements.statement: The document reference, document type, date of issue and attachment are asked once for the notification as a whole, not per commodity line, per animal or per unit, and a document belongs to the notification rather than to any line on it.
requirements.why: The V4 data fields page puts all four accompanying document fields at Notification level, which is the level the real record already uses.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend stores documents in their own collection linked to a notification by its reference number, with nothing tying one to a commodity line (repo-backend-p3-016), and the page owns the one documents collection (repo-frontend-p1-035).

requirements.statement: The trader types the document reference and the date of issue and chooses the document type: the service fills none of the three in from the file or from the rest of the notification.
requirements.why: The V4 data fields page marks all three as supplied by the user, and the real page asks for each of them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-022, repo-frontend-p17-101 and repo-backend-p3-022 show the three details taken from the trader and nothing else today.

requirements.statement: Nothing on the upload documents page depends on the commodity: the same document types are offered and no document is demanded or hidden, whatever commodity, species or reason for import the notification carries.
requirements.why: Unlike the animal identifier fields, no accompanying document field on the V4 data fields page carries a commodity condition or an 'Applicable to' list, and the real page has no such rule either.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-023 offers the same list whatever the consignment, and repo-frontend-p17-033 shows the documents obligation carrying only a count and per-field mandatory markings, with no commodity rule.

requirements.statement: The attachment's file format is taken from the file the trader attaches and is never asked as a question; the format must be one of PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS and XLSX.
requirements.why: The V4 data fields page holds the attachment's format as data the notification captures and permits those eight formats, but neither Design Release 2.1 nor the real page asks the trader for it, and what a page asks is the prototype's (c-355).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-099 takes the format from the chosen file's extension against those eight types, with no question asking for it, and repo-frontend-p17-115 lists them as the attachment types a document may carry.

requirements.statement: Entering any one of the document reference, document type, date of issue or attachment makes the add-a-document form a document to add: Save and add another, Save and continue and Save and return to overview all check all four, hold the trader on the page with an error for each one that is missing or not valid, and keep everything already entered.
requirements.why: Sam's 26 October ruling says what a trader typed is never dropped and that a part-filled document is refused on every save button with an error for each missing detail; the V4 data fields page marks all four document fields all-or-nothing, and the accompanying documents group is the one all-or-nothing group it holds. Sam's ruling outranks the prototype's silent discard and the V4 page's own intro, which makes the other three mandatory only once a type is selected (c-351).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p5-017 refuses a form with only the reference typed, repo-tests-p5-019 refuses one with everything but the type, and repo-tests-p5-018 proves all three save controls do it the same way and keep what was typed.

requirements.statement: A document saved as Self-declaration, CITES permit/certificate or Packing list / species list is accepted, stored and published by its own code.
requirements.why: The document type list the business supplied on 29 October 2026 adds these three, and the V4 data fields page outranks the prototype's demo data on which values the field permits (c-348). The backend now holds a code for each.
requirements.deltaNote: The select offers all three (repo-frontend-p17-023, repo-tests-p5-008) and the backend holds SELF_DECLARATION, CITES_PERMIT_OR_CERTIFICATE and PACKING_OR_SPECIES_LIST among its thirteen codes (repo-backend-p3-001, repo-backend-p3-004, repo-backend-p3-007, repo-backend-p3-013).

requirements.statement: The backend holds a code for each of the thirteen document types the page offers and no others, the same list for every notification, and a saved document whose type the page has no label for shows 'Not provided' in its Document type cell.
requirements.why: The backend's codes and the offered list must agree, so every document the page saves can be stored and published; the 'Not provided' fallback keeps a document with an unlabelled type readable.
requirements.deltaNote: The backend's codelist is the thirteen offered types (repo-backend-p3-001), with no HEALTH_CERTIFICATE code any more, and repo-frontend-p17-130 shows 'Not provided' for a type with no label. The backend describes each code only in its API description, for example JOURNEY_LOG as Journey log and OTHER as Other supporting documents (repo-backend-p3-005 to repo-backend-p3-014); the labels the trader sees come from the frontend.

requirements.statement: The V4 data fields page records what its 29 October 2026 document type list update changed, and gives an accompanying document type example that is one of the values the field permits.
requirements.why: These are gaps in the policy page, which this programme reads rather than edits; they go to the report so the business can tidy them. Until then the list is taken as the business's latest and the example as stale.

requirements.statement: How the Notification submitted page lists the ITAHC as still to upload whenever no ITAHC was uploaded, whatever else was uploaded.
requirements.why: The documents area stops at how documents show on the review page; the confirmation page is the review and confirmation area's.

requirements.statement: On a live-animals or germinal-products notification, each of Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination holds exactly one address the trader has chosen, in the Standard Address Block shape the address book keeps and validates against its own field-level rules: the name, the address lines, the town, the county, the postcode, the country and the telephone number and email address. Each party is held once for the whole notification, not per commodity line, and a party counts as answered only once its stored copy carries a name.
requirements.why: The V4 data specification lists all five parties as Standard Address Block fields the user supplies at notification level, with the address block's own field-level validation, in both the animals and the germinals journeys. Writing it down keeps the picked copy's shape and its level tied to the specification rather than to the prototype's demonstration addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-052 shows a picked party stored as a copy of the record's name, telephone number, email address, addressLine1, addressLine2, townOrCity, county, postcode and ISO country code, repo-frontend-p14-058 one such answer per party at notification level, repo-frontend-p14-057 all five mandatory and always in scope, and repo-frontend-p14-032 that a party counts as answered only when its copy carries a name. The stored block holds two address lines rather than three (repo-frontend-p14-034-m1), which is the real service's own field shape and so stays as it is under ruling sam-2026-10-09. The germinal-products set's copy of the page and its pickers come with req-1827.

requirements.statement: A live-animals or germinal-products notification can be submitted only once Place of origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer and Place of destination each hold an address; any of them may be left blank while the notification is still a draft.
requirements.why: The V4 data specification marks all five parties mandatory to submit, in both the animals and the germinals journeys, so a trader fills the notification in any order but cannot send it a party short. What the review page says about an incomplete notification is the review-and-submit area's.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-057 binds all five parties as mandatory answers always in scope, repo-frontend-p14-106 shows a draft saving and continuing with none of them chosen, and trace-e2e-p8-069 shows an incomplete notification's review page carrying the addresses card's error.

requirements.statement: The data specification's own field labels and worked example addresses appear in the service: 'Place of Origin' and 'Place of destination' as the page's section names, and the German livestock exporter, UK importer and UK farm distribution addresses as content.
requirements.why: Out of scope: those labels and examples illustrate the Standard Address Block for the people writing the service, not copy or data the service shows. The page's section names, titles and hints come from the design (req-562, req-563), and every address shown comes from the trader's own address book (req-608). The Importer example's 'Crown Business Hall' against the Consignee's 'Crown Business Park' is a slip in an illustration with nothing turning on it.

requirements.statement: On the add-address page reached from a party picker, 'Save and return to address page' makes exactly the same checks as 'Save and select': with any answer missing or not valid the trader stays on the add-address page, sees an error for each one in field order, keeps every value they entered and every role they ticked, and nothing is written to the address book; the address is saved only once every answer passes. A germinal products notification's add-address page behaves the same way.
requirements.why: A second save button must not let a half-checked address into the trader's address book. The owner's 26 October decision is that the save buttons behave consistently, that a missing or invalid answer keeps the trader on the page with an error for each one, and that no page is an exception; the 10 November review restates that both save buttons make the same checks, and the owner's 27 November decision keeps that both save buttons on a page make the same checks in live animals, in the germinal products copy and on plants' pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Both save buttons are on the page today (repo-tests-p7-003) and a refused save keeps the page, lists the errors in field order and stores nothing; the tests drive that refusal from 'Save and return to address page' on the consignee route (repo-tests-p7-034, repo-tests-p7-035), while the design's suite lists the errors only from 'Save and select' (prototype-dr2-1-specs-p4-064) and its trace never shows the second save refused for the destination-side pages (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p7-073). What is left is proving the same refusal from 'Save and select' and from every role's page, and the germinal copy. The second save button itself is req-673 and the check set it applies is req-660 to req-668.

requirements.statement: On the contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets, the secondary button that saves and returns to the hub makes the same checks as 'Save and continue': with no address chosen, or with an address that is not in the list, the trader stays on the page with 'Select a contact address' in the error summary and on the radios, nothing is saved, and any contact already held is kept.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling has every save button on a page make exactly the same checks, with no page an exception, and the 27 November ruling confirms those checks are the page's own hard stops together with any answer the Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page marks mandatory to proceed, in live animals and the germinal products copy alike. That page marks the contact address mandatory to proceed, so a missing choice is refused whichever button the trader presses.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: While a notification is being amended, 'Save and return', 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' make exactly the same checks on the page's answers, on every page that offers them, in live animals, germinal products and plants: with any answer missing or not valid the trader stays on the page and sees an error message for each one, with what they entered still in the fields; with every answer given and valid, the button saves and goes where its own wording says. No page is an exception: on the CPH number, permanent address, contact address and plants consignment contact pages each of these buttons checks whatever the page needs before the trader moves on, and on upload documents a part-filled document is refused by every one of them, with an error for each missing detail, while a complete document is saved and kept.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling makes the save buttons behave the same as each other, so a trader who leaves a page by any of them is told what is missing or wrong instead of carrying an unchecked answer into the overview, and documents behave like every other page; the 27 November ruling keeps that default in live animals, the germinal products copy and plants' pages alike. The CPH number, permanent address and contact address pages, and the plants consignment contact page, take the same rule: what each of them needs before the trader moves on is unchanged, and every save control checks it alike.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Save and return to overview' while amending accepts a cleared mandatory answer and lands on the overview with no error, so the missing answer is reported only later on the review (repo-tests-p6-026), and the page's way out that discards an answer is a 'Cancel and return to overview' link (repo-tests-p6-013, repo-tests-p6-016). The 'Save and return' control itself does not exist yet (trace-e2e-p14-047), so its checks are built with it (req-1403, req-2068).

requirements.statement: A notification holds one CPH number for the whole notification, not one per commodity line or per animal; the trader enters it and it is held as a string of no more than 11 characters.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page puts the CPH at notification level with a single entry and types it as a string of at most 11 characters, which leaves room for the slash-separated form as well as the nine digits.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-026 stores the nine digits as one value and repo-frontend-p16-093 holds the CPH number as a single-field obligation of the notification, so there is one CPH for the notification and it is well inside 11 characters.

requirements.statement: The notification records a responsible person for the load, made up of the person's name, telephone number and email address and their organisation's name, address and telephone number, taken at notification level from the signed-in user's identity, in both the live-animals and germinal-products sets.
requirements.why: Out of scope. The goal is Design Release 2.1's look and feel together with the data the journey's own pages ask for, and this field is consumed on authentication: no page in this area asks for it, shows it or checks it. Two of its six values, the organisation's address and telephone number, would also need Defra ID to serve them, and the Defra ID stub is not one of the programme's repos. Its V4 field rows left this area in the re-extraction and the journey areas that would ask them now carry them, so nothing here backs the field; the id is kept so earlier citations still resolve, and it comes back into scope if a ruling adds it to the data shape.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source in this area's working set shows what the notification records from the signed-in user's identity, so nothing here says whether the six values are held already.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the origin page's caption, heading, fields and hints as the hub's own exit and change tests happen to record them.
requirements.why: The two end-to-end claims that recorded them are no longer in this area's working set, and the origin page's own copy is decided by req-012, req-048 and req-049; what the hub's tests drive is weighed where the hub is reconciled.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p4-004 and trace-e2e-p4-043 record the same caption, heading and internal reference hint from this area's own origin slice.

requirements.statement: Plants' stored late indicator reaches the plants backend's notification record as a field of its own for the regulator side, and an inspector reads a submitted plants notification live from that record.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants decisions d-007 and d-066 park both. Each needs trade-imports-plants-backend and regulator tooling, which are not the programme's repos, and Design Release 2.1 asks for neither. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification needs action, so is counted on the Germinal products 'Action needed' card and listed on the Action needed drill-down, when it is submitted and a document the germinal set requires is still missing; no animal identifier is asked of it, so none is tested.
requirements.why: The Action needed card and drill-down cover the germinal products category, and Sam's 10 November ruling makes the germinal pages take live animals as their reference for everything, so the live animals rule applies to the documents the germinal set asks for (c-366).
requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when. It also waits on the outstanding-actions banner design that Sam's 16 November ruling makes the only way outstanding actions are shown, and on the animals backend re-adding the rule that works out a notification's outstanding items with that banner under Sam's 19 November ruling; neither ruling says who designs the banner or when.

requirements.statement: On the address book list the delete success banner shows the address's name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, for example 'Green valley farm address deleted'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sentence-cases the name, but lower-casing a name the user typed changes how their own data is shown, and the reason is not visible (c-367).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner shows the name as entered (repo-insfrontend-p6-081, repo-tests-p12-044).

requirements.statement: When the request carries a search or a Type, the address book list's 'Filter addresses' disclosure is open as the page loads, showing the search term and the type the results are filtered by.
requirements.why: Once the filter is submitted to the server, a collapsed disclosure would hide what the shown results rest on (c-368).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the disclosure is closed whenever the page loads (repo-insfrontend-p4-009).

requirements.statement: The delete page's Address row leaves out any line that repeats one already shown, ignoring case, and falls back to fields split out of a free-text address.
requirements.why: The prototype holds a seeded address as one free-text string whose last part is its country, so it has to drop the repeat and split the string; the real record holds separate lines and an ISO country code looked up to a name, so no line repeats another, and dropping a line the user typed would hide part of what is being deleted.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page lists every filled-in part of the record's address in its one row (repo-insfrontend-p6-071).

requirements.statement: The address book list groups and labels the address types 'consignor or exporter', 'exporter', 'contact' and 'packer'.
requirements.why: These four types exist only in the prototype's seeded demonstration data, which maps the service's own consignment and contact addresses into the book. No exporter role exists and none is to be created, the roles question does not offer these four and the prototype's own Type filter gives them no option, so the real book never holds one; building a category membership and a column label for each would be dead work.

requirements.statement: Search on the Transporter tab also matches a transporter's approval number, so a trader finds a transporter by the number on its approval.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's search text for a transporter covers its approval number.
requirements.deltaNote: The Transporter tab's search also matches the country and the type label (repo-insfrontend-p4-055, repo-insfrontend-p4-056), but no claim records it matching the approval number.

requirements.statement: Going back from the add-details step to 'Choose an address type' and continuing again shows the address, the contact details and the ticked roles already entered, so nothing the trader typed is lost between the add's two steps.
requirements.why: Sam ruled that what a trader typed is never dropped and that saving behaves consistently from page to page; a two-step add that threw the entry away on the way back would lose it. The prototype keeps the in-progress address and roles for the add and clears them only when the add starts afresh or ends.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-096 and repo-tests-p13-014: after a refused save, going back and choosing the same address type again shows every field and the ticked role as entered.

requirements.statement: An address needs a postcode or Zip code whatever country is chosen, and it is free text of at most 12 characters.
requirements.why: The germinal data fields mark the Standard Address Block's postal or Zip code mandatory with no exception by country, and the add form and the address book already require one; whether a country with no postal code system is exempt, and whether 12 characters suit every country's format, is open, and the conflict carries the default.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-042, repo-addressbook-p1-023 and repo-tests-p13-092 already refuse a blank postcode on every address, whatever country is chosen, and repo-addressbook-p1-024 caps it at 12 characters.

requirements.statement: One flat address record holds the address wherever a field asks for a Standard Address Block, whatever level that field sits at: address line 1, an optional address line 2, town or city, an optional county, postcode and a country code, with no address line 3, city or free-text country.
requirements.why: The same flat block serves every address a notification or an address-book record holds, so a field at any level reads and writes the one shape.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-118 shows the stored address-book record holds one flat block, repo-tests-p9-026 the same block on a notification, and repo-backend-p1-038 the same fields in the backend's Address type, which an animal's permanent address also uses (p1-032). The V4 Address Block rows this also rested on left this area in the re-extraction and the address-book areas now carry them.

requirements.statement: On every live animals and germinal products template page that offers both 'Save and continue' and a return button, the two buttons make exactly the same checks: the trader sees an error naming each answer the page refuses, stays on the page with what they entered kept, and, where the page refuses nothing, has the answers saved to the template in progress and moves on as the button they selected does.
requirements.why: The owner's decision of 26 October: the save buttons behave consistently, Save and return to overview makes exactly the same checks as Save and continue, and no page is an exception. The ruling names the live animals and high-risk plants frontends; it reaches the germinal products set's template pages too, because each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals page and the ruling's point is that the buttons behave consistently. Plants has no template mode, so only the animals sets' template pages are covered here.
requirements.deltaNote: There is no template mode today, so no template page has either save button yet.
requirements.blockedBy: Sam decides to pick templates up again: templates are de-prioritised and the templates rows are parked and not built now (ruling:sam-2026-11-04), and templates are dropped for now (ruling:interaction-designer-2026-11-09), with no condition named for their return.

requirements.statement: An amendment keeps a copy of the notification's answers as they were when it started and compares the trader's answers with that copy, counting the notification as changed when they differ and never changed when no copy was taken, ignoring everything that is not an answer (errors, messages, the commodity search box, the status, the amend bookkeeping, version flags, drafts, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted references and address book additions).
requirements.why: Out of scope: this is the prototype's own session bookkeeping, and the prototype's source does not say what any page does with the result (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-084). The real service already holds the submitted answers as the amend snapshot and answers the same question with a yes-or-no value of its own (req-2366), so there is nothing of the prototype's comparison for the programme to build.

requirements.statement: Once the trader has saved an answer that differs from the submitted one during an amendment, the amend review's title and level-1 heading read 'Review before re-submitting'; until then they read 'Review your notification', in live animals, germinal products and plants.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the page for what the trader is about to do, so the heading tells the trader an amendment is waiting to be re-submitted rather than simply reviewed; the service holds a yes-or-no 'answers differ from submitted' value that says when it has happened (c-371).
requirements.deltaNote: Live animals already switches the heading once an answer has changed and keeps 'Review your notification' until then (repo-tests-p6-007, repo-tests-p6-008, repo-tests-p6-011, repo-frontend-p7-111); the trace of the earlier build kept one heading throughout (trace-animals-fit-p3-032, trace-animals-fit-p3-051), and no claim shows plants' view taking the second heading, so plants takes it with this requirement.

requirements.statement: An answer the data specification marks mandatory to proceed must be given before its page can be left by either save button. An answer marked mandatory to submit can be left blank while the notification is being filled in and is needed only before it is submitted. An answer marked optional can be left blank throughout. An answer marked conditional is needed only while its stated condition holds, judged at the level the answer applies at.
requirements.why: The data specification's Mandatory column is the policy on which answers are a page's hard stop and which only hold back submission. The owner's 10 November ruling drops the obligation model row that would have recorded it, because the service already tells a hard stop from a submission check and refuses a half-filled document group, so nothing is built for this on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an in-scope obligation is marked mandatory or optional only and a conditional gate that names no mandate counts as mandatory (repo-frontend-p1-137), and a mandatory answer is enforced by the review page's submit rather than on its own page: additional details is accepted with both questions blank and its row stays 'To do' (repo-tests-p4-132). The 10 November ruling drops the obligation model row that would add these markings.

requirements.statement: A group of answers the data specification marks all-or-nothing can be left blank as a whole, and once any answer in the group is given every answer in it is needed: the page refuses either save button with an error for each answer still missing from that group, and the group's row on the overview counts as complete only when all of the group is given or none of it is.
requirements.why: The data specification marks some answers as a group that must be filled in together, so a half-filled group is never stored or submitted. The owner's 10 November ruling drops the obligation model row that would have recorded it, because the service already refuses a half-filled document group, so nothing is built for this on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: Today no all-or-nothing rule across a notification's scalar answers exists; the nearest rules are the document and collection ones, which make all four of a document's details mandatory within that document (repo-frontend-p1-174) and hold a row back from reading complete while a required collection is empty (repo-frontend-p1-089).

requirements.statement: Whatever level an answer applies at, an answer the trader gives is checked before it is saved: the right format, within the length allowed, and one of the list's entries where the answer has a list. An answer that fails is refused with its own error and the trader's own entry is shown back.
requirements.why: The data specification makes validity a rule of every answer, whatever its level, and the real service cannot store a value that does not fit its field. The journey already works this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-050, repo-tests-p4-084 and repo-tests-p4-155: an answer that is too long or too large is refused with its own message, whatever level it applies at; repo-tests-p4-127: a refused page shows the trader's own entries back.

requirements.statement: A notification's answers sit at three levels, and each level's count holds. The answers true of the whole movement are given once for the notification and are not driven by the commodity chosen. A commodity line, one or more per notification, carries a commodity code with its species and quantities. A unit record, none or more per species line, carries one animal's or germinal product's own identifiers, such as an ear tag, a passport, a donor name or identifier and a collection date.
requirements.why: The levels decide which answers are asked once for the notification and which repeat per commodity line or per unit, and the record the journey writes already holds them that way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-022, p1-025 and p1-029 hold the three levels today (a list of commodities, each with a list of species lines, each with one animal-identifier entry per animal), repo-tests-p9-011, p9-018 and p9-144 prove the stored record keeps them, and confluence-6497338582-p1-026 states the notification level for a field that is not driven by commodity selection. The V4 rows that set the levels out left this area in the re-extraction and the journey areas now carry them.

requirements.statement: An answer the data specification sets out is asked in both the live-animals and the germinal-products sets unless the specification marks it for one of them, and where both sets ask it but allow different values each set offers its own list.
requirements.why: The data specification covers both sets in one page and marks the exceptions, so the germinal set's questions are the live-animals set's except where the specification says otherwise. The germinal set does not exist yet, so every one of its answers comes from this rule.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals frontend serves live animals as its only set (repo-frontend-p1-007, repo-perftests-p1-004), so no answer is marked by set and no set-specific value list exists.

requirements.statement: The data specification page's own bookkeeping is not built: its page version and title, its statement that the fields are agreed, the eight headings each field is specified under, the two spellings of the commodity level, and its change log's columns, its unnamed authors, its missing reasons for the six de-scopings and its silence on the address block.
requirements.why: These describe the specification document rather than anything a user, operator or other system can observe. Each field the change log records as de-scoped is weighed where that field's page is weighed.

requirements.statement: On every frontend, a page refused because an answer is missing or invalid comes back with what the trader typed still in its fields, beside the error summary and the inline messages, so nothing has to be typed again. This holds for whichever save control the trader pressed.
requirements.why: The owner's 26 October ruling makes keeping the trader's entry a rule of the service rather than a courtesy of a particular page: an answer refused on any save button comes back on the page instead of being dropped. The shared error pattern is where that is guaranteed for every page.
requirements.deltaNote: The INS frontend keeps the value the trader entered in the field the error summary links to (repo-insfrontend-p1-138), and plants keeps date text it cannot read as the trader typed it so the field can show it back (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-067). Where one page still drops an entry, that page's own row fixes it.

requirements.statement: The five-character limit on the region of origin code is checked whatever the answer to the region of origin code question is, so a longer code typed before switching to No is still refused.
requirements.why: The limit belongs to the field, not to the Yes branch, so a code that cannot be stored is never accepted through the other branch.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-029 shows the No branch applying the same length rule; no fit spec exercises it, so the builder keeps it when the page changes.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: clearing the subdivision and the region of origin code when the trader picks a different country of origin.
requirements.why: The claim that showed this behaviour was refuted on verification. The verified behaviour is narrower, blanking a saved country that has left the list with its territory and code, and req-031 carries it. No source shows or asks for clearing on a change of country, and no end-to-end trace drives the case (trace-e2e-p4-128), so nothing is built for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-035-m1 replaces the refuted claim and covers only a stale saved country.

requirements.statement: The internal reference box does not stop the trader typing past its limit: the 58-character rule is applied when the page is saved.
requirements.why: The target design caps nothing in the box either, and the limit is a server check whose error names it (req-050).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-039 and trace-animals-fit-p5-029 show the box with no maxlength today, as the prototype's own field has none (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-070).

requirements.statement: Choosing a type on the notification type question hands the trader to that type's service through the service's own start path, its sign-in and its sign-in callback, then the new notification's first page, and the other journey service is never visited on the way.
requirements.why: Each journey service signs the trader in and mints its own notification, so the hand-over goes through its start path rather than straight to a page; keeping the other service out of the hop proves the type decides the service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-058 shows the five-hop sequence for every option, repo-tests-p14-057 the animals draft opening at Origin of the import and repo-tests-p14-063 to repo-tests-p14-065 the plants drafts opening at the commodity type page.

requirements.statement: The hand-over between the INS front door and each journey frontend works in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack, each service taking the other's address from its own configuration and never from a hard-coded host or port, signing in through the Defra ID stub in the two Docker stacks and through Defra ID as each CDP environment configures it. The end-to-end suite proves the hand-over in the local and CI Docker stacks.
requirements.why: The 4 November ruling requires every link, redirect and form hand-over between services to work in all three places from each service's own config, which is what lets one build serve them all.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-037 to repo-insfrontend-p3-039 show each journey URL built from the frontend's configured base URL, and repo-tests-p14-057 the hand-over working against the stack the end-to-end suite runs, with both journey frontends up (repo-tests-p14-076). No separate check is built for CDP.

requirements.statement: A trader whose sign-in to the INS front door or to a journey service has lapsed while they were in the other one is signed in again on the way back and still lands where they were going: the type question with their chosen type selected, or the same notification's first page.
requirements.why: A hand-over that crosses two services crosses two sessions, and losing one must not lose the trader's place or start a second notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-074 and repo-tests-p14-075 show both recoveries proven end to end today.

requirements.statement: The end-to-end coverage of the notification type question runs both journey frontends, and every test that crosses from the INS front door into a service and back is given a longer time budget than an ordinary page assertion.
requirements.why: A cross-service journey is slower than a page, so the suite that proves the hand-over says so rather than failing on time.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p14-076 records the two frontends the hand-overs need and repo-tests-p14-096 the raised budget on every crossing test.

requirements.statement: The origin page's end-to-end page spec proves that page's rendering, interaction and validation at /live-animals/notifications/<reference>/origin, posting countryOfOrigin, regionOfOriginCodeRequirement, regionOfOriginCodeSuffix and internalReferenceNumber, and the overview's 'Where is this consignment coming from?' row is the route it takes to open the page from the overview.
requirements.why: The suite's page specs each stay inside one page's scope, so the origin page's rows are proven there and the overview row is how the spec reaches it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-020 and repo-tests-p1-022 show the page and its country control, and repo-tests-p1-054 the four answers posted.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the shared date picker the suite drives and the date formats it types and reads back.
requirements.why: The origin page asks for no date; the date picker and its formats are decided where the pages that ask dates are reconciled.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p1-017 and repo-tests-p1-018 record the Ministry of Justice date picker's bounds and button and the dd/mm/yyyy and d/m/yyyy formats the suite uses on the pages that ask dates.

requirements.statement: The commodity page shows the service's page-maturity banner while its behaviour is still being detailed, and Commodity details, whose behaviour is agreed, shows none.
requirements.why: The service marks each page's maturity so a reviewer can see what has been agreed; Design Release 2.1 has no such banner because the prototype does not model maturity. Commodity details being agreed also makes it a signed-off page, so a change to its agreed behaviour needs a person.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-002 marks Commodity details agreed, so it renders no banner, and -p10-004 marks the identification page still being detailed.

requirements.statement: The commodity search field shows its label and its hint and no placeholder text.
requirements.why: Only how a search list reads, its label, hint and placeholder included, follows the prototype, and Design Release 2.1's commodity search carries no placeholder.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-010 passes no placeholder to the search component and holds no placeholder key, and repo-tests-p1-131 records that nothing asserts one.

requirements.statement: One commodity search lists at most a hundred species, and the trader is told nothing about the species left out.
requirements.why: The real commodity list is far larger than the prototype's, which ships whole with the page, so the number of results a search can show is a real constraint the prototype cannot express; nothing in Design Release 2.1 or the data specification asks for a message about the cut-off.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-015 caps one search at a hundred species, the reference service's own largest page size (repo-referencedata-p2-005, -p2-021), and -p9-016 records that the results markup and the copy file hold no truncation message.

requirements.statement: In the search results each species is labelled with its common name and its Latin name in brackets (for example 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'), and with the Latin name alone where the list holds no common name for it.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels a species by the name a trader knows first, and sorts the results by that label. A species with no Latin name is never listed, so every label has one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the label puts the Latin name first and the common name in brackets, 'Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle)', with the Latin name alone where no common name is held (repo-frontend-p9-020, -p9-103); the reference service leaves out any species with no Latin name (repo-referencedata-p2-018).

requirements.statement: A posted commodity choice or removal the page cannot resolve to a species it has seen is refused or dropped rather than acted on: the page honours only a species a search returned to it or one already on the notification, a Remove naming a row the page does not hold is refused as a bad request and logged with its key, and a chosen key the page cannot resolve is left out of the selection with a warning logged.
requirements.why: A notification must not take a commodity line from a post the service cannot resolve, a real persistence and validation constraint the prototype does not model: Design Release 2.1 drops unknown species ids silently instead.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-034 refuses an unresolvable Remove as a bad request, -p9-039 drops an unresolvable chosen key with a warning, and -p9-108 and -p9-109 show the page honouring only the species it has stored from searches or the notification.

requirements.statement: Without JavaScript the results list ends with a secondary 'Add selection' button that commits the ticked species to the chosen list while running the typed search again and keeping its results on screen, and it is rendered only while results are listed.
requirements.why: The commodity search must work as a form a button submits, so a trader without JavaScript can tick species from one search and keep searching; with JavaScript the button is hidden because ticking commits at once.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-069 renders the button only with results and hides it while JavaScript is on, -p9-107 shows it posting the Search action, and -p9-070 and -p9-071 show the no-JavaScript Search, Remove and Clear all keeping the chosen list across posts.

requirements.statement: The commodity search results sit in a scrolling box at most 270 pixels tall, joined to the bottom edge of the search box with no border between them, each species row ruled the full inner width and lined up with its commodity heading, the first row under each heading shaded and then every other row after it, and a hovered tick box draws no ring.
requirements.why: The results list is a custom component with no GOV.UK equivalent, so its look is part of what a trader sees; Design Release 2.1 stripes the list the same way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-072 to -p9-075 hold the scrolling box, the joined edge, the row rules, the alternate shading and the ringless hover today.

requirements.statement: Pressing Escape in the commodity search closes the results list and empties the search field while the selection stays in the panel.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling 10 November puts commodity search in a separate ticket's hands rather than this work's, so how the search dismisses its results is that ticket's to decide.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Escape hides the results list and keeps what was typed, clicking the search box shows the list again, and clicking away hides it with the chosen species still chosen (repo-frontend-p9-062, -p9-063).

requirements.statement: The commodity search's button is a magnifying-glass icon beside the field whose only text, read to a screen reader, is 'Search'.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling 10 November puts the joined search button with the separate commodity-search ticket rather than this backlog, and the look of a search box belongs to EUDPA-635.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the button beside the search field reads 'Search' as visible text (repo-frontend-p9-011), and nothing asserts its accessible name beyond that word (repo-tests-p1-131).

requirements.statement: The commodity search's results list is labelled 'Commodity search results' for assistive technology, and the live region announces how many species are chosen ('1 option selected', '2 options selected') and is left empty after Clear all.
requirements.why: Out of scope: ruling 10 November puts commodity search in a separate ticket's hands rather than this work's, so its extra announcements and labels are that ticket's to decide, as the 9 November ruling left the country search's own component announcements to stand.

requirements.statement: A number inside a quantity error message is written with thousands separators in the UK style, so 2147483647 reads as 2,147,483,647.
requirements.why: A trader reads the limit the message names, and an unseparated ten-digit number is hard to read.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-049 formats the maximum quantity with UK thousands separators for both above-maximum messages, in English and in Welsh.

requirements.statement: Pressing Enter in a quantity field on Commodity details saves the page and moves on, rather than pressing a row's Remove button.
requirements.why: A trader who finishes typing a count and presses Enter must not lose a commodity, which the removal buttons sitting before the fields would otherwise do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-065 and -p10-164 show Enter in a quantity field saving the page and moving on to identification details, because the form opens with a hidden Save and continue ahead of every Remove button.

requirements.statement: On a phone the Selected commodities table stays inside the screen width.
requirements.why: The table has three columns and a row action, and a trader on a phone must be able to read it without scrolling the page sideways.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-068 checks the table stays within the screen width on a phone today.

requirements.statement: The identification details page, its heading and inset, what happens to a line's identifier records when its count is raised, and any cap on how many commodity lines or identifier records a notification holds.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: this area stops at animal identification, so the identification page's own content and what happens to a line's records when its count is raised belong to the identification and permanent address area. No source asks for a cap on lines or records beyond each line's own number of animals.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-003, -p10-069 and -p10-070 show the identification page as it is today, -p10-161 that nothing caps the lines or records, and -p10-162 that neither page says what a raised count does to the records already saved.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, choosing Transit reveals a 'Port of exit' question then a 'Destination country' question, and choosing Internal market reveals the purpose question; no exit date is ever asked, because the set does not offer Temporary admission horses.
requirements.why: The policy page marks the destination country, the port of exit and the exit date as applying to the germinals journey as well as the animals one, while the germinals reason list offers only Internal market and Transit; the exit date's own condition, Temporary admission horses, can therefore never be met in that set, and the listed conditions are the specification. The 27 November ruling confirms the set asks for no exit date and builds nothing for one, and the target design gives the germinal Transit reveal the same two questions and lists as live animals. The 9 October ruling makes germinal products a sibling set with its own copy of the page.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: The 'Destination country' and 'Port of exit' questions on the main import reason page are asked with the animals frontend's accessible autocomplete, which shows its whole list on focus, filters it as the trader types, says 'No countries found' or 'No ports found' when nothing matches and lets the trader pick again; without JavaScript each is a plain select whose first option reads 'Select one', and the chosen code and date still submit and are kept.
requirements.why: A follow-on ticket has already given both questions the frontend's accessible autocomplete, with a no-JavaScript fallback and accessibility proven, and the goal has a search box behave as the real frontend configures it. The 9 October afternoon ruling's clause that a field the prototype shows as a plain select stays a plain select reads two ways against that, so the question records the choice and the default keeps what is built.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-092, repo-frontend-p8-093 and repo-frontend-p8-114 show both questions already asked as type-aheads with their own no-match messages, and repo-frontend-p8-120 and repo-tests-p1-066 the plain-select fallback without JavaScript. Under the other reading of the ruling the component comes out and both questions go back to plain selects.

requirements.statement: The design decisions behind these two pages are recorded in the live-animals set's own design-decision record rather than in a ledger inside each page's folder.
requirements.why: The repo source was read for any decisions or rulings ledger these pages keep; the folders hold none, so there is no page-level ledger to reconcile against and none is added.

requirements.statement: A selected-commodities row whose species lines carry no number of animals shows an empty quantity cell.
requirements.why: A zero would read as a count of none the trader had declared; an empty cell says the count has not been given yet. The target design does not cover the case, and reading back a count nobody entered is a persistence condition it cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-076 shows an empty Number of animals cell rather than a zero for a row whose species lines carry no count.

requirements.statement: A saved animal row on a commodity line that has no species label is named 'Animal <number>'.
requirements.why: A commodity line can reach the page without a species label from reference data, which the target design does not express, so the row still names the animal it holds rather than showing a blank.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-111 shows the fallback 'Animal <number>' on a line with no species label.

requirements.statement: A refused save on the identification details page shows the page again with every identifier the trader typed still in its field, the cap-reached refusal of a line that filled up while the page was open included.
requirements.why: The 26 October ruling holds that what a trader typed is never dropped, and the target design shows a refused save with the typed values kept in that species' entry form; a trader told by the message that the line is full should not also have to type the animal again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a refused over-long value comes back in its field (repo-frontend-p10-127). For the cap-reached refusal, which is reported on the line's card (repo-frontend-p10-155), this run's frontend extract no longer says whether the typed values come back; the earlier extract found every field emptied, so the builder checks and keeps them.

requirements.statement: A species line's identifier records are held under that line, so removing the commodity line removes its animals with it.
requirements.why: A record left behind would count towards a line the notification no longer holds and could never be reached to remove. The target design keeps saved entries when a species goes, which the real model cannot, so persistence overrides it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-154 stores each species line's identifier records under that line, so they go with it; trace-e2e-p6-101 records that no trace shows what happens to the records when the line is removed.

requirements.statement: The identification details page lays its heading and inset text in a two-thirds column and its cards across the full width, and on a phone the selected commodities summary and a species card holding a saved animal stay inside the screen width.
requirements.why: A species card holds a table with a column for every identifier, which needs the full width, while running text reads best in a two-thirds measure; staying inside the screen width on a phone is an accessibility requirement the target design does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-148 shows the two-thirds column and the full-width cards, repo-frontend-p10-176 and repo-frontend-p10-177 the summary outside the form on the wider display surface, and repo-frontend-p10-150 the summary and a card with a saved animal staying inside a phone's screen width. Design Release 2.1 spans the panels across the full width too (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-067); its phone layout is not in the traces (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p5-078).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a new draft records 'Germinal products' as what the consignment is certified for, without asking the trader and with no way to change it.
requirements.why: Germinal products is a set of its own, so what the consignment is certified for follows from the set the trader started in rather than from a question; the option B plan the owner chose sets the answer when the draft is created and shows it with no Change link, which is why the set asks no certification question (req-181). Design Release 2.1 carries a certification purpose list (Breeding and/or production, Approved bodies, Other) on every germinal commodity that no germinal page reads.

requirements.statement: The transit countries page offers no confirmation step and no 'are you sure' page for adding or removing a country: the table of added countries is the whole interaction, and without JavaScript no message beyond the changed table tells the trader what happened.
requirements.why: Sam's 10 November ruling: nothing confirming that a transit country has been added or removed is needed where a row is added to a table, because the table is itself the confirmation, and no visible message is shown without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-094 shows no confirmation route or template in the feature folder, and trace-animals-fit-p17-056 shows a trader without JavaScript told only by the new table row.

requirements.statement: Save and continue takes the trader to the page that asks for an earlier answer the next arrival page needs: saving arrival details by road with only the country of origin answered opens 'What are you importing?' rather than a transport page, and the overview offers no transit countries row until a commodity is saved.
requirements.why: A notification is built in journey order, so the journey sends the trader to the answer it still needs rather than to a page it cannot yet ask.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-044 shows the commodity search opening instead of the next transport page and the transit row absent until a commodity is saved, and p11-086 shows the transit countries page sending the trader to the page that asks for a missing earlier answer, with the back trail carried.

requirements.statement: A means of transport already saved that has since left the reference list is refused with 'Select a valid option', the same message as an unknown value submitted on the page.
requirements.why: Validation is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and the service's default option message covers the stale case; no source asks for a message of its own here, unlike the port of entry and the arrival date, which each have their own saved-answer wording.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-029-m1 shows the default message shown for a stale saved means of transport, with no key for it in the copy module and no test in the slice exercising it.

requirements.statement: A transit country chosen in the search box but not added with 'Add country' is not saved: Save and continue and Save and return to overview keep only the countries already listed.
requirements.why: The list the page saves is the one it shows, and design's 13 November ruling keeps 'Add country' as the step that puts a country on that list. No source asks for a warning that an unadded choice will be lost.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-080-m1 shows the chosen but unadded country ignored on the save path, with no warning, and p11-078 shows the saved list taken from the countries already listed.

requirements.statement: A refusal shown on the transit countries page keeps the search box and the Add country button on screen even when twelve countries are already listed, so the trader can act on the error.
requirements.why: A trader shown an error must be able to reach the control the error names, which the cap would otherwise take off the page.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-092 and trace-animals-fit-p17-051 show the search box kept on the page beside the limit paragraph in the over-the-limit error state.

requirements.statement: A refusal the trader's own input causes on the arrival and transit pages, such as choosing nothing or choosing a country already added, is shown on the form and not logged, while every other refusal, each redirect out of the transit countries page and each missing earlier answer is logged with its reason.
requirements.why: A trader's mistake is not an incident, so the log keeps room for the refusals and redirects an operator needs to see.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-076 shows the trader's own refusals unlogged and every other one logged, p11-084 and p11-086 the logged redirect and missing answers, and repo-plantsfrontend-p5-083 and p6-051 the same rule on plants' arrival pages.

requirements.statement: The live animals arrival details and transit countries pages record maturity 'agreed', so their behaviour is signed off, while the high-risk plants arrival-status and arrival-details pages record 'exploring'.
requirements.why: A signed-off page's behaviour has been agreed by a person, so a change to it is raised for approval rather than made in passing; plants' arrival pages are not yet at that level.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p11-002 and p11-053 record both animals pages as agreed, and repo-plantsfrontend-p5-073 and p6-002 record both plants pages as exploring.

requirements.statement: In the plants frontend, the arrival date calendar's toggle is a GOV.UK-brand button with an inverse-text icon that darkens on hover and takes the GOV.UK focus colours, the open calendar ends above the time of arrival question, opening it with the mouse puts focus on the day it opened on, and opening it with the keyboard shows the focused day and a GOV.UK focus outline round the calendar body.
requirements.why: Plants styles the MoJ date picker inside the GOV.UK palette as animals does (req-288), and Design Release 2.1 shows nothing different.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p6-068 to p6-071 show the toggle's colours, the in-flow calendar and the mouse and keyboard focus behaviour today.

requirements.statement: In the plants frontend, a save that fails because the backend is unavailable brings the arrival-status and arrival-details pages back at HTTP 500 with a recoverable-error banner and every answer still filled in, while a programming failure reaches the service's catch-all error page instead.
requirements.why: A backend failure must not lose what the notifier entered, and a fault in the service's own code must not be dressed up as one the notifier can recover from.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p5-105 and p6-055 show the recoverable-error banner at HTTP 500 with the answers kept, and p5-106 and p6-056 the programming failure escaping to the catch-all.

requirements.statement: In the plants frontend, the arrival-status and arrival-details forms post with browser validation turned off and carry a cross-site-request token and the notification's concurrency token, and an action posted against a stale notification is redirected rather than saved.
requirements.why: Server-side validation, request forgery protection and optimistic concurrency are real constraints the prototype cannot express, as they are in the animals journey (req-334).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p5-108 and p6-067 show both forms carrying the tokens, and p6-067 the stale-action redirect.

requirements.statement: In the plants frontend, a refused arrival details page comes back at HTTP 400 with an error summary listing its errors in question order, arrival date then time of arrival then proposed place of landing, each summary link resolving to the control it names, every typed answer still in place and nothing saved; once every answer is given the summary clears and Save and continue reaches the place of destination.
requirements.why: The GOV.UK error pattern lets a notifier find and fix each problem, and one name per answer across the control, the error and the summary link keeps every link resolvable.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p6-047 and p6-048 show the refusal, the HTTP 400 answer and the error order, p6-077 the single name per answer, and p6-047-m1 and p6-048-m1 the recovery once every answer is given.

requirements.statement: The reference-data service reaches MDM and the Trade Platform token endpoint at the addresses its own configuration gives (MDM_SERVICE_URL and TRADE_PLATFORM_AUTH_URL, which default to the stub on port 8087), and each frontend reaches reference-data at the address its own configuration gives (TRADE_IMPORTS_REFERENCE_DATA_URL, port 8086 by default), so the country and port lists load in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack with no hard-coded host or port.
requirements.why: Sam's 4 November ruling: every link between services works in CDP, the local Docker stack and the CI Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use, each taking its address from that service's own configuration and none from a hard-coded host or port. Countries and ports come from real MDM in CDP test and from the stub locally and in CDP dev, so the address has to be configuration.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-034 and p3-035 show MDM and the token endpoint read from MDM_SERVICE_URL and TRADE_PLATFORM_AUTH_URL, defaulting to the stub at localhost:8087 (repo-stub-p2-034); p3-003 and p3-005 show the service on PORT (8086 by default) and the animals frontend calling it through TRADE_IMPORTS_REFERENCE_DATA_URL; p3-041 routes egress through HTTP_PROXY in CDP. p3-043 shows the stack's dependency on the stub locally. Earlier wording cited frontend claims this area's working set no longer holds; the statement now names the reference-data and stub links this area owns.

requirements.statement: The tests repo holds the transit countries page's screenshot check.
requirements.why: Sam's 10 November review ruling drops the transit countries screenshot from the live animals class-name row because it is already on the tests repo's main, so no row builds it again.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-sam-2026-11-10b-p1-033 records the transit countries screenshot as already on the tests repo's main, which is why p1-031 drops it from the row.

requirements.statement: The contact address page is opened from the overview's 'Contact address for this consignment' task, at the notification's consignment/contact/select path.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: the contact address page belongs to the consignment-parties area, which weighs it; it was seen in this area only because the transit countries specs sit beside it in the same part of the suite.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p7-001 and trace-e2e-p7-002 show the overview task and the path as recorded; the animals frontend's main has since removed the contact page altogether.

requirements.statement: A port whose MDM traffic value is missing, or is not Airport, Port or Rail, stays in the port of entry list with no type, in its own group after the rail ports, A to Z by name, and reference-data logs a warning once for each such port code and traffic value.
requirements.why: The 9 October ruling orders the list airports, seaports, rail from MDM's traffic field, builds every list against reference-data as it is, and keeps whatever MDM serves. Every port MDM serves today carries one of the three values, so this group is empty today; keeping any other port, rather than dropping it, keeps the list MDM's content.
requirements.deltaNote: Reference-data already does this: repo-referencedata-p1-034 lists such a port with type null, p1-036 puts ports of unknown type after the rail ports, p1-035 and p1-065 warn once per port code and traffic value, and p1-067 proves it with a 'Ferry' port and a port with no traffic. repo-stub-p2-030 shows every port in the stub's MDM capture is Airport, Port or Rail, so no port falls into this group today.

requirements.statement: A transporter is a record the address book service holds for one organisation, in its own transporters collection with its own document, controller, repository and route, reusing the service's organisation scoping, soft-delete status, optimistic locking and Standard Address Block field validation where the fields are genuinely the same; the address book is the system of record for transporters.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling settles the question the 9 October afternoon ruling left blocked: the address book manages transporters, saved per organisation exactly as every other address is, and it does so in a collection of its own rather than on the Address model. The ruling leaves the full field list to the service, which keeps the Standard Address Block fields with a phone and an email.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-001 and -002 hold transporters in their own transporters collection on their own route, repo-addressbook-p4-003 gives the record the Standard Address Block fields with phone, email, type and approval number, repo-addressbook-p4-005 locks it optimistically, and repo-tests-p15-052 proves a transporter can be created straight through the address book API.

requirements.statement: A transporter holds no address role and no address type, no seventh address role and no fourth role group is added for it, and the address book's address API is unchanged by transporters: a transporter request carrying roles or a role is refused on that field.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling: an address role says which records a notification's picker may offer for a slot, drives the receiving-roles-in-the-United-Kingdom rule and drives the address list's category tabs, and a transporter is none of the six roles and has one use, so a role would carry no information for it. The address book's own request shapes could not hold a transporter in any case: they require at least one role and refuse a type outright.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-025 and -026 refuse roles and role on a transporter request, repo-addressbook-p4-040 returns a transporter with no roles and no address type, and repo-tests-p15-012 holds a transporter's type as one of two values.

requirements.statement: A transporter record carries a required private-or-commercial type, PRIVATE or COMMERCIAL, stored on the record rather than worked out from anything else; a commercial transporter must have an approval number and a private one must not, a blank approval number counting as none; no address carries either.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling: a transporter's type is intrinsic because it decides the form, the field list and the country rule, so unlike an address's type it cannot be derived. The approval status the same ruling names is its own requirement (req-2263), because the address book does not hold one yet.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-023, -029 and -030 require the type and refuse any other value, repo-addressbook-p4-031 to -033 hold the approval number rules, repo-insfrontend-p7-038 and -038-m1 never ask or save one for a private transporter, and repo-tests-p15-028 and -038 store the type with the approval number only for a commercial one. repo-addressbook-p4-094 shows no approval status on the record today, which req-2263 adds.

requirements.statement: A transporter's approval status reads 'Approved' or 'New' on the transporter list and is held in a field of its own, separate from the record's soft-delete status, under a name the address book chooses.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling names the two values and says the approval status is not the address book's active-or-deleted soft-delete tombstone, so putting transporters and addresses on one service means the transporter document needs its own name for the concept. How a field is named in a service is that service's own design.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals frontend shows the two words and the two tags today (repo-frontend-p12-024, repo-frontend-p12-025) and marks a transporter it adds 'New' (repo-frontend-p12-060), and repo-tests-p7-111 reads the 'New' tag from the journey's list; the address book's transporter record holds no approval status of its own, which is the transporter-records area's evidence.

requirements.statement: 'Add a transporter' on the transporter list opens the address book's add-a-transporter pages in journey mode, with the controls the address add pages show in journey mode, and lands the trader back on the transporter list on save or on cancel, through the same hand-off the journey already uses to add an address; the animals frontend serves no transporter add pages of its own.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling makes the address book the system of record and has a journey that needs a new transporter open the INS front door's add pages in journey mode, using the hand-off already built for addresses rather than a second pattern of its own, with those pages living in the front door rather than in the animals frontend's three transporter add-page folders. Keeping those folders would be the second pattern it refuses, so their routes, fit specs and copy keys go with them; both journey details pages are signed off, so the change goes through the signed-off check. The address book's own transporter pages are all still exploring, so changing them trips no signed-off check.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's add pages always return to the address book filtered to transporters, on save (repo-insfrontend-p7-049, repo-tests-p15-026) and on cancel (repo-insfrontend-p7-045), with no journey return, and the animals frontend still serves its own type question and two details forms inside the journey. The address book's pages are at maturity 'exploring' (repo-insfrontend-p7-001).

requirements.statement: The name field on both transporter forms is labelled 'Name or organisation name'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label, which the prototype decides; the journey's own forms already use it.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's forms label it 'Name or organisation name' (repo-frontend-p13-019); the address book's transporter forms, which become the one route (req-2264), label it 'Name or organisation', which is the transporter-records area's evidence.

requirements.statement: The commercial transporter form's first field is labelled 'Transporter authorisation number'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's label, which the prototype decides; the journey's own form already uses it.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's form labels it 'Transporter authorisation number' (repo-frontend-p13-028); the address book's commercial transporter form, which becomes the one route (req-2264), labels it 'Approval number', which is the transporter-records area's evidence.

requirements.statement: Both transporter forms carry one section heading, 'Enter contact details', after the country and before the email address, and no heading above the address fields.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 groups only the contact questions under a heading, which the prototype decides; the journey's own forms already do it.
requirements.deltaNote: The journey's forms carry the single 'Enter contact details' heading after the country (repo-frontend-p13-031, repo-frontend-p13-032); the address book's transporter forms, which become the one route (req-2264), split under 'Address' and 'Contact details', which is the transporter-records area's evidence.

requirements.statement: The transporter list shows eight transporters a page, with GOV.UK pagination below the table that carries the search term and the chosen transporter in its links, no pagination where eight or fewer are found, and an inset between the search box and the table naming the transporter the trader has chosen, so a trader on another page still sees it.
