requirements.why: The 25 November ruling keeps pagination everywhere and says its removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, no requirement says an organisation's records are shown unpaginated, and every picker in both journeys pages at the one figure the INS address book list already uses, eight. Transporters are now records the address book holds per organisation, so the transporter list is such a picker, and the restatement comes back with the paging because the chosen row can be on another page again.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list shows every matching transporter in one table with no pagination control and no page size (repo-frontend-p12-030), and no trace shows a list long enough to need one (trace-animals-fit-p18-107); a ticked transporter already survives a search that hides it (repo-frontend-p12-042), which paging needs too. EUDPA-824, still to do, is the ticket that splits the list into pages of eight (ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 2).

requirements.statement: The transporter list says how many transporters it is showing, reading '1 transporter shown' for one and '<count> transporters shown' for more, and reads the count, or the no-matches line, out through a status region on the page.
requirements.why: A trader who has searched needs to know how many rows are left, and a screen-reader user needs to hear it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-033 holds both forms of the sentence, repo-frontend-p12-034 reads it out through a status region and repo-frontend-p12-035 carries one ready-made message per row. The per-row messages exist to let the browser announce a count while filtering in place, which req-389 stops, so the count is rendered with the page the server returns.

requirements.statement: A transporter row's only actions are the radio that picks the transporter and the 'View details' link: a transporter is changed or deleted from its own page in the address book, which offers Edit and Delete and a Back link to the address book filtered to transporters.
requirements.why: The journey picks a transporter; managing the record belongs with the service that holds it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-060, repo-tests-p15-049 and -050 put Edit and Delete and the Back link on the transporter's own page in the address book; the journey list's row actions are recorded by the transporters area.

requirements.statement: When the address book cannot be reached while checking that a saved transporter is still on the list, the transporter list falls back to the transporters the service ships and records a warning rather than failing the page.
requirements.why: A real cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express: the transporter list reads another service, which can be down.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-049 falls back to the shipped transporter list and records a warning instead of failing the page.

requirements.statement: A transporter saved on a notification comes back ticked on the transporter list, matched to the address book record it came from.
requirements.why: The address book gives every transporter a stable identifier of its own, so the list matches the saved pick to that record rather than to a name two transporters could share.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a stored transporter pick is matched back to the list by name rather than by id (repo-frontend-p12-048), so two transporters sharing a name cannot be told apart.

requirements.statement: The transporter list offers the signed-in organisation's own transporters from the address book together with the transporters the service ships, the shipped records after the organisation's own, and reads them with no filter of its own beyond the search term.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling parks approved transporters and leaves the eight records the service ships exactly as they are, so they stay where they are in the animals frontend while the list builds over whatever the organisation itself has added, which the address book holds. The ruling does not say what the transporter step's picker reads to offer transporters, and the list already reads the address book for the organisation's records.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-029 offers the transporters held for the signed-in trader's organisation in the order the address book returns them, and repo-frontend-p12-049 names the shipped list the frontend still holds.

requirements.statement: An organisation's transporters are the records the address book holds for it: no transporter captured before the address book became their system of record is carried over.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling leaves open what becomes of transporter records captured before the change, and there are none to carry over: the store it replaced kept them in one process's memory, so they were lost on every restart, and the records a trader adds already go to the address book.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-047 creates each transporter as a record in the address book and repo-tests-p15-052 proves the address book holds it, so nothing is left elsewhere to carry over.

requirements.statement: A commercial transporter's country is stored as the Northern Ireland country code the address book already uses and shown as 'Northern Ireland' by both the address book and the journey.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling forces a created commercial transporter to a Northern Ireland country code rather than looking one up, and keeps the code and its display name as constants in the service. Which code that is settles how the value is held rather than anything a trader sees, so the service's own choice stands unless the owner means the literal code the ruling names (c-388).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-063 and repo-insfrontend-p7-003 store the fixed country as the code GB-NIR, and repo-insfrontend-p7-059 and repo-tests-p15-036 show it as the words 'Northern Ireland'.

requirements.statement: 'A commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland' is enforced from the stored country alone, with no postcode parsing and no extra flag, because the Northern Ireland code is distinct from the United Kingdom's.
requirements.why: The 6 November ruling: storing a Northern Ireland code of its own keeps the rule enforceable from the value, and keeps a transporter's country the same type as the address book's country code rather than a display string.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p2-102 stores a commercial transporter's country as a code distinct from a private one's, and repo-frontend-p13-045 refuses a country other than Northern Ireland from the value alone. The tests repo names that code 'GB-NIR' (repo-tests-p7-114) where the 6 November ruling stores 'XI'; either is distinct from the United Kingdom's, so the rule holds (c-472).

requirements.statement: The address book refuses a commercial transporter whose country is not Northern Ireland with 'A commercial transporter must be in Northern Ireland', and the address book's commercial add and edit forms refuse a posted country other than Northern Ireland with the same message, always saving a commercial transporter with the Northern Ireland code.
requirements.why: The address book is the system of record for transporters, so a transporter written straight through its API cannot escape the rule; the 6 November ruling names the add form's hidden field and its refusal of a tampered value, and the service's own refusal on write stands beside it as a real validation constraint (c-389).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-034 refuses a commercial transporter whose country code is not GB-NIR with that message, as an exact match (repo-addressbook-p4-035), keyed by the field (repo-addressbook-p4-037); repo-insfrontend-p7-041 and -072 refuse a tampered post on the add and edit forms and repo-insfrontend-p7-042 always saves GB-NIR.

requirements.statement: Opened in journey mode, 'Add a commercial transporter' shows the notification's status above its heading, a 'Draft' tag and the notification reference, and neither 'Choose a transporter type' nor 'Add a private transporter' shows one.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the status block off two of the three add pages and shows it on the third, and the prototype decides what a page shows. Once the address book serves those pages the status has to reach them across services, which nothing yet shows the hand-off doing.
requirements.deltaNote: The animals frontend's own add pages already do exactly this (repo-tests-p2-088, repo-frontend-p12-074, repo-frontend-p13-054), but the pages the trader will reach are the address book's, and no claim shows the add-address hand-off carrying the notification's status into them.

requirements.statement: The transporters route the address book serves is designed in the address book's own conventions: its paths, its pages, its soft-delete and its paging, which takes a 1-based page defaulting to 1 and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, as the address list's does, and answers an object of items, page, page size, total items and total pages; an out-of-range or non-numeric page or page size is a 400 bad-request problem.
requirements.why: The prototype never decides a service's paths, field names or API, and the 6 November ruling gives the transporter its own controller, repository and route without saying what the surface is, leaving it to the service. The 25 November and 5 November rulings fix the paging bounds for every list the address book serves.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-046, -047, -049, -051 and -055 serve list, create, get, replace and delete under /organisation/{orgId}/transporters, and repo-addressbook-p4-065 to -067 page it with the address list's bounds.

requirements.statement: A transporter list opened from the notification view keeps that trail: its Back link returns to the view, its 'View details' links and its 'Add a transporter' route carry it, and a transporter saved from the add pages lands back on that same trailed list.
requirements.why: A trader who came from the review goes back to the review, not to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-028 passes the trailed list URL as the return on the View details links, repo-frontend-p12-083 and -084 carry it to the type question and back under the success banner, and repo-frontend-p13-096 lands a save on the same trailed list.

requirements.statement: What a trader has not saved while adding a transporter is kept apart from the notification's answers: the type chosen on the way to an add, and what was typed into a details form, come back when they return, and are cleared once a record is saved or the add is cancelled; a type chosen with no record saved reopens the type question with neither option chosen, and cancelling leaves the transporter the notification already had chosen still ticked and its task complete.
requirements.why: A trader who leaves an add half done loses nothing, and a notification's saved answers are not changed by an add that never finished.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-076 to -078 hold the chosen type, the part-typed form and the just-added name apart from the notification's answers, repo-frontend-p12-079 reopens the question blank when no add was saved, and repo-frontend-p13-090, -099 and -101 clear them on save or cancel while leaving the existing pick alone.

requirements.statement: A refused transporter type the trader actually sent, a redirect away from an add form because the stored type does not match, and a cancelled add are each recorded once for support, with the journey, the route and the type, and choosing nothing at all is not recorded.
requirements.why: Support needs to see a trader bounced out of an add without the log filling up with empty submissions.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-070 records a refused type only when a value was sent, repo-frontend-p13-007 records the guard's redirect once with the journey, route and stored type, and repo-frontend-p13-100 records a cancelled add once.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript switched off a trader can search the transporter list, pick a transporter the search found and save it, and can save or cancel either add form, each ending where it does with JavaScript on.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and JavaScript only enhances a page that already works.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p12-088 proves the list's search, pick and save with JavaScript off and repo-frontend-p13-106 the private form's save and cancel, but nothing proves the commercial form either way (repo-frontend-p13-110).

requirements.statement: The transporter list shows 'No transporters match your search.' in place of the table whenever no row is left, with no separate wording for an organisation that has no transporters of its own.
requirements.why: Out of scope as a difference to fix: while the service ships transporter records to every organisation the list always holds at least those (req-2273), so the empty state cannot be reached, and Design Release 2.1 never shows one. Wording for an organisation with no transporters at all is settled when approved transporters are unparked and the shipped records go.

requirements.statement: The additional-documents table inside the expander has the visually hidden caption 'Additional documents by type of consignment'.
requirements.why: A table needs a name a screen reader can hear; this accessibility duty overrides Design Release 2.1's captionless table (c-006).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-015 carries the caption today; Design Release 2.1's table has none (prototype-dr2-1-source-p10-018).

requirements.statement: Once a notification holds 15 documents the add control is shut: it keeps its place on the page and in the tab order, is marked aria-disabled, is described by the limit message and carries no form action, so no sixteenth file is sent to be scanned and stored.
requirements.why: The prototype stores no file, so it cannot express the cost of sending a sixteenth file to be uploaded, scanned and stored only to be turned away; refusing it at the control is a real constraint (c-075).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-055 and repo-tests-p5-026 shut the add control at the limit today.

requirements.statement: When the service cannot open an upload session the add form is closed and the page shows 'Documents cannot be uploaded at the moment. Reload the page or come back later.' in the error summary, linked to the add control, and a part-filled save is then told only what metadata is missing.
requirements.why: A real upload session can fail to open, which the prototype, which uploads nothing, cannot express; the trader has to be told rather than left with a control that does nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-057 shows the message and the closed add form today. When the form is shut both at the document limit and for a missing session, the limit message is the one shown (repo-frontend-p17-057-m1).

requirements.statement: A document whose file was taken on but not saved to the notification is recoverable: the page returns with 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. Your document was uploaded but has not been saved to this notification. Select <save action> to try again.', or with 'Sorry, there is a problem with the service. We could not check that every document you uploaded is saved to this notification. Select <save action> to try again.' when the service cannot be asked, and holds the trader on the page until the outstanding upload or removal is finished. A page shown after a service failure carries an internal-server-error status, and one shown after a refused add or continue a bad-request status.
requirements.why: A real upload can succeed while the save that follows it fails, which the prototype, which keeps documents in a session, cannot express; a trader must not lose a document they have already uploaded.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-105 to repo-frontend-p17-107 show both messages and the reconciliation behind them today.

requirements.statement: Each time the documents page is drawn the add control posts to a fresh upload session, a page the browser restored from its back or forward store is reopened from the service, and the page is served with no-store, so the add control never posts to a session that has already taken a file and a trader who comes back by Back can still add another document.
requirements.why: A one-use upload session is how the real upload handshake works, which the prototype cannot express; without this a trader returning to a stale page would post a second file to a spent session.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-095 and repo-tests-p5-052 give a fresh upload address on every render today, and repo-frontend-p18-071 reopens a restored page from the service.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript running, a file over the limit is caught in the browser before it is sent: the limit and the message come from the page itself, the message joins the page's one error summary as a link to the upload control with focus moved to the summary heading, the field shows it with the visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, a server-rendered message for the same field is replaced rather than repeated, each attempt clears the last attempt's browser-raised errors, and a page carrying no limit or no message posts the file for the server to judge. An oversize file left in the field also stops Save and continue.
requirements.why: Stopping a file the service cannot take before it is sent spares the trader a long upload, and doing it from wording the page carries keeps the browser and the server to one limit and one message. The prototype enforces nothing, so it cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p18-056 to repo-frontend-p18-070 and trace-animals-fit-p23-072 to trace-animals-fit-p23-077 show the browser-side check, its summary, its field error and its clearing today.

requirements.statement: The documents page refuses a request it cannot place: a Remove aimed at a position the notification holds no document at is refused with no page shown, a returning upload handle the notification never opened is ignored and the trader is simply returned to the page, an upload id or returning handle that is not of the shape the service mints is treated as absent, and a returning upload whose form started no document adds nothing.
requirements.why: The page's own addresses carry ids a trader can edit, so each has to be bounded before it reaches the upload service: a real security constraint the prototype, which posts only a filename, cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p17-078, repo-frontend-p17-096 and repo-frontend-p17-097 refuse or ignore each of these today. A replayed return for a document already listed adds nothing (repo-frontend-p17-098-m1).

requirements.statement: The CDP nginx ingress in front of the animals frontend accepts a request body of at least 50,001,024 bytes, and the service team records the confirmation against EUDPA-518.
requirements.why: It is a CDP platform change this programme does not make. It goes to the report because the 50MB limit is already in the animals frontend's code (req-509): deployed before the cap is raised, every file between about 10MB and 50MB passes the service's own checks and is then refused by the ingress, so the trader gets a platform error page and loses the document type, reference and date of issue they typed.

requirements.statement: The animals backend's document unit tests build a real DocumentService on stubbed repositories, and the local stack restarts the file uploader by itself.
requirements.why: Sam's 19 November ruling keeps both as they are: the unit tests follow the house rule of not mocking the service's own modules, and the uploader restart is wanted.
requirements.deltaNote: ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-014 and ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-017 record both as already built that way and name them as exceptions to the fixes the engineering review asked for.

requirements.statement: Two browser tabs open on one notification's documents page can each add their own document at the same time: both settle, both are listed, and neither tab's View file link serves the other tab's file.
requirements.why: A one-use upload session per render could otherwise let one tab claim the other's upload; the prototype, which uploads nothing and keeps documents in one session, cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p5-054 and repo-tests-p5-055 prove both tabs add and keep their own document today.

requirements.statement: Recorded gaps in the documents page this programme does not fix: nothing is announced to a screen-reader user when the page gives up asking for the scan statuses; the browser-side size check reads only the first chosen file; the page does not say whether the 50MB limit is per file or per notification; the documents page's behaviour is agreed, so a change to it needs a person; and the Welsh copy builds the accepted-file-types bullet differently from the English and reads badly for a rejected document whose file name is not known.
requirements.why: Real problems and recorded tensions in the animals frontend that Design Release 2.1 says nothing about and no adopted requirement here changes; they go to the report.

requirements.statement: What the suites do not prove about documents: no fit spec covers the browser-side oversize check or the reopen from the browser's back store; the tests repo proves no document reference rule, no bad date of issue, no file type beyond a PDF and a refused .txt, no wording for a refused file type, no hint, no stored record, no sixteenth-document post, no cross-organisation read of a file, and only two of the thirteen document types; a PNG fixture it names is missing; its scan-pending checks run only when the scanner has not already settled; and the documents page also carries a plain Continue button no spec places.
requirements.why: Coverage gaps in the fit and end-to-end suites, recorded so whoever builds a documents row knows what is unproven today; closing them is spec-cover's work, not a Design Release 2.1 difference.

requirements.statement: How the suites are run and what the notification view and amendment do around a document: which documents specs carry the compose, cross-browser and duplicated-in-frontend tags and so which run where, how long a run is given, how its references and notifications are recorded, and the notification view's reference heading, status tag, absent Change links and Back links.
requirements.why: Weighed here and left out: how the test suites are tagged and timed belongs to the tests repo's own conventions, and the notification view and amendment pages belong to the manage-notifications and review areas. Recorded so the tests repo's claims are weighed.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page and every party picker carry a cross-site request token and the notification's concurrency token with every submission. A submission of the consignment addresses page, or of a high-risk plants picker, made after the notification changed is refused and the trader is sent back to the same page rather than the newer answers being overwritten.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: two tabs or a slow connection must not lose a trader's answers, and the page cannot silently write over what another save has already stored.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-011 and repo-frontend-p14-014-m1 show the hidden crumb and concurrency token on the addresses page and its refusal of a stale submission; repo-frontend-p15-170 shows the crumb and token on the animals picker form; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-003 and -p9-004 show the same on every plants picker form. The animals pickers' own refusal of a stale save is not built today (repo-frontend-p15-151-m2) and is carried by req-2966.

requirements.statement: A same-as press is refused, with nothing saved and the trader returned to the consignment addresses page, when the pair is not one the page offers, when the source party has no address, or when the target party already has one, each refusal logged once; when the copy cannot be saved because the backend is briefly unavailable the page is shown again with its recoverable-error message and status 500.
requirements.why: A real constraint the prototype cannot express: a shortcut posted by hand, or pressed after another tab filled the party, must not overwrite an address or copy from an empty party, and a failed save must not look like a success.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p14-048 to repo-frontend-p14-050 show the three refusals and their log reasons, and repo-frontend-p14-051 the recoverable-error rendering at status 500.

requirements.statement: On the consignment addresses page, each party section that holds an address shows a 'Remove' button, styled as a link, beside its 'Change' link, whose visually hidden text names the party in lower case, so it reads 'Remove place of origin', 'Remove consignor', 'Remove consignee', 'Remove importer' or 'Remove place of destination'. The button submits the page's own form, so it works without JavaScript.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a trader empty a party filled by mistake from the page itself. The button is a submit inside the page's own form, as the same-as buttons already are. Plants has no consignment addresses page, so ruling sam-2026-10-09-pm leaves it unchanged.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a chosen party offers only 'Change' and 'Edit details', each naming the party in visually hidden text (repo-frontend-p14-035), with no way to empty it (repo-frontend-p14-040), and no test finds a remove control (repo-tests-p7-120).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants frontend's consignment contact picker's own question — its heading 'Contact address for consignment', its description, the absence of a section caption above it, its role-free list of the whole book, its own refusal wording, its three save controls and their Welsh, its task row and its place after the identification numbers page — is settled by this area.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: the contact address is the cph-permanent-and-contact area's, which carries that picker's own content. Only the paging and the chosen-address restatement that ruling ian-2026-11-25 sets for every picker in both journeys are this area's, in req-594 and req-595.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p7-067 to -p7-090 record the contact picker as it stands.

requirements.statement: The gaps in the evidence for this area, the test suites' own housekeeping and the frontends' internal mechanisms are requirements of this programme: that no test in the animals end-to-end slice yet asserts the pickers' page size, results sentence, chosen-address restatement, caption, heading, description, Change, Edit details or same-as actions in one part, nor the roles question or country message on the INS add page, nor the add-a-transporter pages; that the suite seeds the journey's parties as named address-book records and keeps one live record per name, tags some specs as duplicated in the frontend repo or as cross-browser, and still holds hub-worded controls no test uses; that every address-book record a test creates is named to a template and soft-deleted afterwards and a shared environment's book is cleared by name template; that the animals addresses page and its pickers are marked at maturity 'detailing' and show a maturity banner; that the page reads every party's stored answer at once and can render an address as one comma-separated line and keeps a test-support helper for its banner; that the plants stub book's search runs over every field of a record; and that the page's scope expects frozen parties it has no notion of.
requirements.why: Out of scope: each is either a hole in the evidence that needs nothing built, a test suite's own arrangement, or a frontend mechanism rather than something a user sees. They are recorded so every claim in this area's working set is weighed, and the gaps go to the report.

requirements.statement: Each party picker, in both animals sets and in the high-risk plants frontend, gets its page of eight by reading the role-filtered list the address book returns and cutting the page in the frontend, so the address book's own page and page-size parameters serve its other callers rather than a picker.
requirements.why: The owner's 27 November ruling keeps the default of the question on where the page of eight is cut: in the frontend, in the germinal products copy too. Ruling ian-2026-11-25 had set aside only the premise that a caller must read the whole book to filter by role, and ruling paul-2026-11-05 gives the list API's parameters and limits without saying how a picker pages.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p9-089 and -p9-090 show the plants picker taking the slice the page number names out of the whole list the address book returned, eight at a time, and working the page count out from the number found; repo-plantsfrontend-p9-100 shows it reading every page of the matches a hundred at a time first, and repo-plantsfrontend-p9-019 only the search term passed to the service. repo-frontend-p15-145 shows the live animals picker doing the same: it reads the whole role-filtered list and cuts its page in the frontend; the germinal products pickers are copies of it (req-1827).

requirements.statement: The add-address page asks for 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and the postcode field, which the trader may leave blank.
requirements.why: The ruling of 14 October 2026 keeps County on the address book's add-details step, which is the step the journey's add-address page is: the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County included, and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose that data on a round trip.
requirements.deltaNote: The page already offers 'County (optional)' in that position, as a half-width input the trader may leave blank (repo-tests-p7-015, trace-e2e-p9-062, trace-e2e-p9-062-m1). Its length cap is req-668's 100 characters.

requirements.statement: On the consignee, importer and place of destination party edit pages the Country select holds 'United Kingdom' alone and the saved country is United Kingdom; the place of origin and consignor edit pages, and plants' consignor and contact edit pages, offer the whole country list. The plants frontend's place of destination edit page holds 'United Kingdom' alone too.
requirements.why: The address book refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom and leaves the other roles unrestricted, so a copy edit that could set another country would make the notification hold an address the book itself would not accept.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all five live animals edit pages apply the same nine rules with the same full country list and nothing depends on which party is being edited (repo-frontend-p15-155, repo-frontend-p15-103), and plants' edit page accepts any country the address book lists, the United States included (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-107, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-069).

requirements.statement: On the party edit page a country the address book does not list is refused with 'Enter a country' in both the live animals and the high-risk plants frontends.
requirements.why: The two frontends show the same page and both take their labels and refusals from the address book, so one unlisted country must not read two ways.
requirements.deltaNote: Live animals refuses both a blank and an unlisted country with 'Enter a country' (repo-frontend-p15-116, repo-tests-p7-063, trace-e2e-p8-051), while plants refuses a blank one with 'Enter a country' and an unlisted one with 'Enter a valid country' (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-105, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-106).

requirements.statement: The party edit page's county field carries the browser autocomplete hint address-level1, as its other address fields carry theirs.
requirements.why: GOV.UK and WCAG 1.3.5 ask an input holding personal data to identify its purpose, and the county is the only address field on the page without a hint.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals edit form sets organization, address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, tel and email but nothing on the county (repo-frontend-p15-105, trace-animals-fit-p15-053); plants already sets address-level1 (repo-plantsfrontend-p8-075), so only live animals changes.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an exporter role on an address, and an 'Exporter' option among the add-address page's role checkboxes.
requirements.why: Ian's ruling of 16 November: there is no exporter role and none is to be created; the prototype's consignor-or-exporter is its own internal vocabulary, and the real service models the merged party as the single consignor role.

requirements.statement: The add-address hand-off between the animals frontend and the INS address book works in CDP, in the local Docker stack and in the CI Docker stack the pull request end-to-end runs use, each service taking the other's address from its own configuration and never from a hard-coded host or port; the end-to-end suite proves it in the local and CI Docker stacks, and no new check of it is built for CDP.
requirements.why: Every link, redirect and form hand-over between services has to work in all three places from each service's own config (ruling 2026-11-04 point 4), and this hand-off is a redirect out of one service and back again. The owner's 27 November decision on the INS-to-journey hand-over sets how such a hand-over is proved (c-398).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the hand-off is exercised where both frontends run, the compose stack and CDP, and skipped when the animals frontend runs in stub mode (repo-tests-p7-001, repo-frontend-p15-036, trace-e2e-p9-079); nothing names the CI Docker stack the pull request runs use as a place it is proven, and nothing shows either service reading the other's address from its own configuration.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: an add-address page reached from a consignment contact page, with its own primary button label.
requirements.why: The live animals journey holds five parties and no consignment contact party, so no add-address page is reached from a contact page, and the design shows no contact address page either; every add-address page reached from the journey is reached from a party picker and reads 'Save and select' (req-671). The DR1 contact-page add link has no page to sit on (c-399).
requirements.deltaNote: The live animals party list holds no contact party, so there is no contact picker, contact edit page or contact route into the add page (repo-frontend-p15-152).

requirements.statement: The tests that prove the review page's broken-copy error summary and its inline party errors find the review's cards by GOV.UK structure and role rather than by the words of a numbered heading.
requirements.why: The owner's 19 November decision is that live animals review tests find cards the way the plants tests already do, so renumbering or rewording a card heading does not break a test of the address errors.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the review's broken-copy errors are proven through the error summary and the party's own row (trace-e2e-p8-015, trace-e2e-p8-017), and the ruling records that live animals review tests still reach cards by heading words, which no test may depend on (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-010).

requirements.statement: The contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets shows eight branch-address records a page, with GOV.UK pagination ('Previous', 'Next' and numbered page links, and none where eight or fewer records were found), carries the page number in its paging links, opens on page one when the trader comes back, and lets a contact ticked on a later page be saved.
requirements.why: The 25 November ruling keeps pagination everywhere: every address book list and every address picker pages, no requirement shows a list of an organisation's addresses unpaginated, and every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses, which is eight. Organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, which is why the 5 November ruling kept paging even though Design Release 2.1 has none.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: The contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets shows an inset 'Selected address: <name>' for a ticked or saved contact, above the list of addresses, even on a page where that record is not listed.
requirements.why: The 23 November ruling brings the restatement back with the paging, because the chosen row can be on another page again and a trader on page two would otherwise have nothing on screen telling them what they have chosen; the 25 November ruling keeps it. The animals contact page has no search box, so the inset sits above the list rather than between a search box and the results.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address keeps each box within its own limit and refuses an over-long value with that field's own message, such as 'Town or city must be 100 characters or fewer': 255 characters for the name, address line 1 and address line 2, 100 for town or city and county, 12 for the postcode, 20 for the phone number and 254 for the email address.
requirements.why: The address the notification carries must fit the record that holds it, and the limits are the journey's own address limits, shared with its other address forms.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-048 caps the boxes at the journey's address limits and refuses an over-long value with that field's own message; repo-frontend-p16-106 records that those messages are the edit-address page's, naming the field 'Name', 'Postcode' or 'Telephone number'.

requirements.statement: A new permanent address refuses an email address that is not a correctly formed address, with the same message the journey's edit-address page uses.
requirements.why: The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page types the permanent address as the Standard Address Block and sends its field-level validation there, which checks the form of an email address; the journey's own edit-address page already does so, and a trader who mistypes an email on one page should be told on both.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-049: the permanent address page checks only that an email address is present and within its length, unlike the journey's edit-address page, which checks the form as well.

requirements.statement: Adding another animal to a commodity line that already holds a saved permanent address leaves the saved one as it is and offers the new animal a card with neither option chosen; removing that animal again leaves the first animal's address as it was, with no card for the one removed.
requirements.why: A trader who changes how many animals are on a line must not lose the addresses they have already given for it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-058 holds both halves, and repo-tests-p2-061 proves end to end that a hand-entered address for the first animal survives saving a second animal on the identification details page.

requirements.statement: A permanent address card carries no change or remove control of its own: an answer is changed by choosing the other option or retyping the address in the card, and the only change control is the 'Change' link in the consignment addresses page's permanent address section.
requirements.why: An animal that needs a permanent address needs one to submit, so there is nothing to remove it to; one change control in the section keeps the page to the question it asks.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-061 gives a card no change or remove control and leaves the section's Change link as the only one, and repo-frontend-p16-062 records that nothing in the page lets a trader remove a saved permanent address or says what should happen if they want to.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page posts every animal's answer in one form, each control named by the animal's commodity line and its position on that line, in the service's own naming conventions rather than the prototype's.
requirements.why: One page asks for several animals at once, so each animal's option and boxes need names of their own; the prototype never decides form field names.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-095: each card's option is named 'option-<line>-<animal>' and each address box '<field>-<line>-<animal>', so several animals' answers post together in one form.

requirements.statement: The CPH number and permanent address pages turn the browser's own validation off, so every rule on their fields is applied by the service and reported on the page.
requirements.why: A page must work the same with JavaScript and without, and a browser's own message is neither in the service's words nor in Welsh.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p13-024 shows the CPH form posting with browser validation off (novalidate); the extract that showed the permanent address page doing the same has left this area's working set, and repo-frontend-p16-066 shows that page's single save posting to the service.

requirements.statement: The live-animals hub is offered in Welsh with a Welsh entry for every English copy key it holds, including the task list heading, the five numbered section headings and the eleven task row titles, and the Welsh is marked as a machine draft that is not released without Welsh Language Standards sign-off.
requirements.why: The hub's copy changes in this programme, and a changed English string with no Welsh counterpart would leave a Welsh page half in English; the frontend already keeps the two copy files in step.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p5-079 shows the Welsh copy file carrying the same key tree as the English, the five section ids and the eleven row ids included, with no key missing and none extra, under a machine-draft warning, today.

requirements.statement: On the high-risk plants Overview the task list sits under a visible second-level heading reading 'Notification task list' (Welsh 'Rhestr dasgau'r hysbysiad'), below the 'Overview' heading and above the numbered groups.
requirements.why: The owner's 19 November decision has plants show the notification task list heading visibly, as live animals does, in the same words in both services.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-003 shows the 'Notification task list' heading at level 2 below the H1 in both languages, and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-011 shows it as the only level-2 heading in main and the name of the task list's region, today. The ruling leaves the heading's level and position open (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-039); the plants page already answers both the way live animals does.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants Overview names its addresses group and the rows inside it with the same wording as the live-animals hub's addresses section and its 'Consignment addresses' row.
requirements.why: The owner's 17 November decision gives the addresses wording to plants as well as animals, on the ground that plants matches animals on these pages; plants' Overview in fact holds three party rows of its own and no consignment addresses page, so what the decision asks of plants is open.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants third group already reads '3. Addresses' (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-016), so the section heading needs nothing; its three rows read 'Consignor', 'Identification numbers' and 'Contact address for consignment' (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-021, p2-059, p2-062, p2-066), and plants has no consignment addresses page or row to carry the 'Consignment addresses' title or the 'Complete consignment addresses' message.

requirements.statement: Each plants Overview task row works its status out from the answers its own pages collect, by the rule that row carries: the commodities row over the commodity type and the commodity lines, the arrival row over the arrival status and the arrival details (the status question being out of scope for potatoes), the destination and consignor rows over the party picked, the identification numbers row over the numbers its commodity type asks for, and the contact row over the contact address picked.
requirements.why: Out of scope: plants keeps its own questions, answers and data when a change is mirrored, and no row of this programme changes which answers a plants row is measured over.
requirements.deltaNote: Already true today: repo-plantsfrontend-p2-035 to p2-073 hold each row's own completeness rule, including the potato arrival row that skips the status question and the wood row whose identification numbers are optional, and p2-067-m1 the contact row reading Not yet started until a contact address is picked.

requirements.statement: The live-animals hub's behaviour spec and the plants Overview's are signed off, so their maturity reads agreed or ready for live.
requirements.why: Out of scope: promoting a page is its own reviewed pull request and never part of other work, so no row of this programme raises either page's maturity; the goal is to bring the pages up to Design Release 2.1, not to sign them off.
requirements.deltaNote: The live-animals hub page is at maturity 'detailing' (repo-frontend-p5-004) and the plants Overview at 'exploring' (repo-plantsfrontend-p2-010), so neither page's behaviour is signed off today and neither is promoted by this programme.

requirements.statement: No action in a notification's view header shares another's form: 'Amend this notification' is a link to the notification's amend confirmation page, 'Copy as new' posts a form of its own to the notification's copy path carrying the request token, the concurrency token and its copy origin, and Delete is a link to the delete page. All three work with JavaScript turned off, in the live animals and germinal products sets and in the high-risk plants frontend.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling gives no action another's form, and the 25 November ruling makes Amend a link like Delete, because the first click changes nothing once the amend confirmation page exists, and gives plants Copy as new so both journeys offer the same three actions.
requirements.deltaNote: Today 'Amend this notification' posts its own form to the notification's /amend path carrying only the request token (repo-frontend-p6-019, repo-plantsfrontend-p10-025, p10-177), and plants' header has no Copy as new (repo-plantsfrontend-p10-162).

requirements.statement: An unfinished Consignment addresses card's message is 'Complete consignment addresses', shown on the card and as its entry in the error summary.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling settles the addresses wording: the incomplete-card message reads 'Complete consignment addresses', the same words as the card title and the page's heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-098 gives the card that message against the addresses anchor, and repo-tests-p3-012 pins it in the refused review's list.

requirements.statement: The Uploaded documents section is never marked unfinished and never appears in the review's error summary.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 treats uploaded documents as optional, so their cards never show an error and documents never appear in the summary.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the documents card is one of the ten cards checked and listed, and shows 'Complete documents' when its task row is not ready (repo-frontend-p6-097, p6-100).

requirements.statement: Every review card is a region named by its own title, and a card action link carries its card's title in brackets as hidden text so two cards offering the same action read apart, except inside a species block's identification details, where the action carries no card title.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling gives review cards their accessible names the way the rest of the service does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-033 makes every summary card a region named by its own third-level heading, and p6-083 adds the card title to each action link.

requirements.statement: The review restates an answer without offering to change it in place: every value is read-only text and the only controls on a card are its Change or Edit details links; a card with no rows shows only its title, any error and its blocks or groups, with no empty summary list; a card's groups come after its rows and after any species blocks, each under its own sub-heading with its own summary list; and a numeric answer reads back as its digits.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's review is a restatement the trader can check, not a form, and a card that has nothing to list must not show an empty one.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-131 to p6-134 already behave this way, repo-frontend-p6-126 renders a recoverable error with no message of its own, and repo-tests-p3-111 reads every answer as a description-list term and value.

requirements.statement: Opening the review of anything but a submitted notification records that the trader has seen the notification as it stands, so a later change can be reported to them, and the review's address carries a refused marker when Continue has just been refused and a stale marker when the notification changed under the trader, which raises the shared 'notification has been updated' banner.
requirements.why: Real persistence the prototype cannot express: a trader must not be able to submit answers that changed after they checked them, and must be told when that happens.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-009 records the seen state and p6-010 carries the refused and stale markers that raise the shared banner, which repo-tests-p3-032 reads as the refused form of the address.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's whole-journey specs drive each journey through the browser front door as a trader does, and the live animals review tests find its cards by their GOV.UK structure and role, as the plants tests do, with no test depending on the words of a numbered section heading, the review page object offering a single heading, and the shared resume-in-the-UI and save-and-continue walk helpers carrying no overloads.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling makes the live animals review tests read the page the way the plants tests already do, and takes the overloads back off the two shared helpers.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a test asserts the numbered section headings by their words, '2. Description of the goods' among them (repo-tests-p3-124), and reads each answer as a description-list term and value pair (repo-tests-p3-111).

requirements.statement: Tests prove the review page's visually hidden text, its GOV.UK summary-card structure and the rendering of its last card, alongside the overview's totals box, buttons and caption line height.
requirements.why: The 10 November ruling moves these class-list checks out of the live animals class-name row and into the rows that rewrite the overview and review tests, so the pages that change prove their own structure.

requirements.statement: Whether an amendment's answers differ from the submitted version is a yes-or-no flag that is never absent, held on the notification record and read by the review to choose its heading, and the animals frontend's local stub holds the flag in the backend's own shape rather than working the value out itself.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling makes the flag a non-null yes or no that the local stub reads from the backend's shape, so the review's heading follows one recorded answer wherever it runs.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the animals frontend's local stub works the value out itself rather than taking it from the record's shape (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-026), while the review already switches its heading on it (repo-frontend-p6-005, p6-006).

requirements.statement: Outstanding actions on a submitted notification are shown through a banner-style alert, and the notification record carries the outstanding items left at submission and the rule that works them out for the banner to read.
requirements.why: The 16 November ruling replaces the action-required status with a banner-style alert the dashboard designs introduce, and the 19 November ruling re-adds the stored outstanding items and their rule with that banner.
requirements.blockedBy: The dashboard designs under test must settle the outstanding-actions banner before it can be built: the 16 November ruling names the banner as how outstanding actions are shown but gives it no wording, placement, appearance or trigger, and the 19 November ruling ties re-adding the stored items to it.

requirements.statement: Every refusal on the review, declaration and confirmation pages is logged once, naming the notification, its status and the reason, and never the message shown to the trader: an unlisted species refusal, a declaration refusal with both concurrency tokens, a confirmation asked for a notification that is not submitted, and plants' review-outstanding and submission-rejected refusals. A declaration refused only because the trader did not tick the box is not logged, because it is their own input error shown back on the form.
requirements.why: Operators need one log line per refusal to trace why a submit did not go through.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-049 and p7-057, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-030, p11-032 and p11-059 already log each refusal once with its reason, and p11-022 leaves the missed tick unlogged.

requirements.statement: Plants' review is built in one place from the notification's answers, the journey's scope and the request's evaluation: its sections, cards and rows, its notification header, each row's key, value and Change target, each card's anchor and message, and the check of every answered party's copied address. A row shows only where the journey asks for its field, a value's read-back follows its kind, and every value and every message is escaped, so text a trader typed cannot become markup.
requirements.why: One place to build the review is what keeps a row from appearing where the journey does not ask for it, and escaping every value is a security constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-165 to p10-173 build the page in one place from the answers and the journey's scope, and p10-063 and p10-063-m1 escape every address line, value and message.

requirements.statement: Plants' check answers groups its party cards under the section heading '3. Addresses', each party card keeping its own title.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling gives plants the same address wording as animals because plants matches animals on these pages, but plants' review has no single addresses card to carry the 'Consignment addresses' heading.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p10-038 already heads the section '3. Addresses', and p10-040 and p10-066 keep the place of destination, consignor, identification numbers and contact cards with their own titles.

requirements.statement: The review, declaration and confirmation pages keep to the service's existing patterns throughout, with four things left as they are: the local stack's automatic restart of the file uploader, the plants journey specification's deleted ruling, the tests repo's removed note on why cancel amend waits on the address, and the animals backend's unit tests that build a real document service on stubbed repositories.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling fixes every other atypical item the overview and review theme's engineering review found, and names those four as exceptions.

requirements.statement: The review, declaration and confirmation pages' recorded maturity levels, and the phase banner each one shows.
requirements.why: Maturity is the build loop's signed-off marker and changes only by its own promotion pull request; the phase banner belongs to the shared layout, not these pages.

requirements.statement: A rulings or decisions ledger in the animals set's four end-of-notification feature folders.
requirements.why: Out of scope here: the recorded-decisions-animals area weighs whether the animals frontend keeps a decisions ledger and where.

requirements.statement: How the review, declaration and confirmation work is grouped into increments, themes and branches, and which increment carries each moved test check.
requirements.why: Out of scope as a requirement: the rulings' grouping instructions are the backlog's shape, not behaviour anybody can observe. They go to the consolidator, which draws the increments and themes.

requirements.statement: The exit port is worded 'Port of exit' and the arrival date 'Arrival date at port of entry' wherever they appear in the live animals journey, the question page and check your answers alike, with no other name used for either; the high-risk plants journey keeps its own arrival wording, which follows the arrival state it asks about.
requirements.why: The 17 November ruling gives one name to each, everywhere, and names no service, ruling out 'Exit border control post' and 'Arrival date at destination'; plants asks its own arrival questions, so the goal's rule that plants keeps its own questions settles what 'everywhere' reaches.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p6-040 and p6-057 already read 'port of exit' and 'Arrival date at port of entry' on the review, and repo-plantsfrontend-p10-056 keys plants' arrival date row by its own arrival state. repo-tests-p4-031, repo-tests-p8-082 and -p8-082-m1 show the question page asking for a port of exit and a transit consignment's review card reading 'Port of exit'; repo-tests-p4-103, repo-tests-p8-077 and trace-e2e-p14-110 show the arrival question page and the review's Arrival details card reading 'Arrival date at port of entry'.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the INS front door's page titles other than the home's — the 'Error: ' prefix a page showing an error summary opens with, the page-not-found title, and where the title checks live between the end-to-end suite and the INS frontend's own tests.
requirements.why: This area covers the home and its drill-downs; the other pages' titles belong to those pages' own requirements, and which suite holds a title check is the test suites' business.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: what signing out of one frontend does to the trader's sessions with the other frontends.
requirements.why: No source says what it should do and nothing proves it today; cross-service sign-out belongs to the sign-in and session work rather than to the home.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: how the end-to-end suite is run and reports — each service addressed by a base URL given to the run, a missing one stopping the run with a message naming the setting, and each test reporting the reference numbers it created.
requirements.why: They are the suite's own mechanics, not behaviour of the home or its drill-downs.

requirements.statement: The additional filters' 'Status' select offers 'Action required' alongside 'Select one', 'Submitted' and 'Completed'.
requirements.why: The prototype's status filter lists 'Action required', while the 16 November ruling shows nothing action-required until the outstanding-actions banner lands; it waits on the answer. The prototype's own claims for the filter sit with the notification list's area this run.

requirements.statement: On plants' list a posting action sits in the card's own action list beside its title, in the same place as the link actions, as on the live animals card.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts every card action in one list beside the card's title, and the 9 October afternoon ruling gives plants' list the same card layout; the live animals card already renders its posting actions there as link-styled buttons.
requirements.deltaNote: Today plants' card adds a final 'Actions' row (Welsh 'Camau gweithredu') holding each posting action as a secondary button in its own form, while its link actions sit beside the card title (repo-plantsfrontend-p1-023, p1-024).

requirements.statement: When an amendment cannot be started from a card, the trader is returned to the list, which shows an 'Important' banner reading 'This notification could not be amended.' and leaves the notification as it was.
requirements.why: A refused amendment has to tell the trader why they are back on the list; this is a persistence and lifecycle constraint the prototype cannot express, so it stays on both lists although Design Release 2.1 shows no such banner.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p4-060 and repo-plantsfrontend-p1-035 and p1-051 (proven by repo-plantsfrontend-p1-086): both lists already show this banner as a landmark region named by its title, and plants leaves the notification untouched.

requirements.statement: Wording and helpers the lists carry but never show stay as they are: the unused 'Reference', 'Actions' and 'Not submitted' labels on both lists and their Welsh twins, the ungrammatical English fallback inside the results-count builder, the arrival-date helper nothing calls, and plants' duplicated previous-and-next helper.
requirements.why: None of these is a difference from Design Release 2.1 and none of them reaches a trader, so the programme does not tidy them; the removal of the results count and the card's dates leaves some of them further out of use still.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the animals frontend and the plants frontend as they are today.

requirements.statement: The way a notification is opened other than from a list's own 'Create new' button, and what each service logs when a notification is opened or an amendment started, are unchanged by the list's reframe: each set keeps its /start entry, which signs the trader in first when there is no session, records the front door as where they came from, and is not cached.
requirements.why: These are the set's other entry points and its logging, not the list's own content; the programme changes what the list page shows, so nothing here is built or changed.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the animals frontend and the plants frontend as they are today.

requirements.statement: The end-to-end suite's own waits around the notification list stay as they are: it retries the sign-in that lands on the list, and it reopens the list and searches again for up to 15 seconds before a newly created notification's card shows.
requirements.why: These are the suite's waits, not behaviour a trader sees, and no requirement of this programme changes them; they are recorded so the reframe's own tests know the list is not always immediate.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the tests repo as it is today.

requirements.statement: Every list of an organisation's addresses is served and shown a page at a time: the address book's list API takes a 1-based page number defaulting to 1 and a page size of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, refuses a page below 1, a size outside the bounds or a non-number with a 400 problem rather than clamping, and no caller is served an organisation's whole address book in one answer.
requirements.why: The 5 and 25 November rulings: organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses, so pagination is kept everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: ListPaging takes page from 1 and pageSize 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, refusing out-of-range values (repo-addressbook-p3-002 to repo-addressbook-p3-006), and the INS list always sends both (repo-insfrontend-p4-071).

requirements.statement: The address book's list API takes the roles an address must hold, repeatable so that holding any one of them is enough, and separately the roles a search term is widened by, so an address holding one of those roles matches a text search even when its own text does not; repeated values collapse, an unknown role is a 400, an address with no roles never matches a role filter, and both filters run in the service, alongside the organisation scope and the live-addresses-only rule, before the page is cut.
requirements.why: The 5 and 25 November rulings: one request serves a whole tab, and paging the API cannot make the role filter wrong.
requirements.deltaNote: role and searchRole are repeatable, collapse repeats, refuse unknown values and run inside the organisation and ACTIVE scope (repo-addressbook-p3-031 to repo-addressbook-p3-041, repo-addressbook-p3-063), proven end to end (repo-tests-p12-083, repo-tests-p12-084).

requirements.statement: An address saved through the address book is found by the next search of the address book list straight away.
requirements.why: A user who has just saved an address looks for it next, and another user of the organisation should see it at once.
requirements.deltaNote: The service reads primaryPreferred, so a read straight after a write sees it (repo-addressbook-p3-092), and a just-added address is found first by the next search (repo-tests-p12-035).

requirements.statement: The edit page follows a return path only when it is one the INS front door allows; a return pointing anywhere else is ignored, and the page's 'Back' link and 'Cancel' go to the address's own details page instead.
requirements.why: A return path a caller supplies would otherwise send a signed-in user off the service, which is an authentication and security constraint the prototype does not express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p13-060: a return on another site is ignored and both Back and Cancel go to the address's details page, while an allowed return is followed (p13-054, p13-055).

requirements.statement: The address book groups its six roles into sending (place of origin, consignor), receiving (place of destination, consignee, importer) and branch (branch address), the same three groups the add's 'Choose an address type' step offers; it refuses an address whose roles come from more than one group with 'An address can only have roles from one group', and refuses a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom, while a place of origin, a consignor or a branch address may be anywhere.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 5 November makes the grouping the address book's own rule, with each role in exactly one group, so the front door can always work one address type out of an address's roles; it also keeps the receiving roles in the United Kingdom.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book has two groups, sending and receiving, with no branch group (repo-addressbook-p1-046), already refuses roles from both with that message (p1-048), and restricts no role by country (p1-029).

requirements.statement: The address book's API carries no address category and no role grouping as fields: both stay inside the service, and the request and response hold the roles alone.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 5 November keeps category out of the API for now and makes the grouping of roles the address book's internal rule, to be added to the API only if it ever becomes a public concept.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-010, p1-047 and p1-056: the request and response carry roles and no category or group field, and the groups show only as a refusal; the API's description text names the groups (p1-050).

requirements.statement: A role a new notification type needs is added by changing the address book's code, each role in exactly one group.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 5 November says code changes to add new roles make sense, so the role vocabulary is not configuration a client can extend. The ruling says nothing about removing or retiring a role.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-044 and p1-047: the roles are fixed in the service's code and a new role cannot be added without a group.

requirements.statement: No address saved before roles were stored is kept: after the change is released the addresses collection is dropped in dev and in test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and a local stack is restarted, so every address in the book holds at least one role.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 5 November chooses deletion over a migration because none of the addresses already saved has any value, and the ruling names only dev, test and a local stack, so what every other environment gets waits on the answer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-003 and repo-tests-p13-112 have roles optional on the stored document, so a record saved before the change could still be held with none.

requirements.statement: An add reached from a notification journey asks 'What else should this address be used for?', with the hint 'This address is being added as a <role> address. Select any other roles or addresses this address should be used for.', offering only the other roles on the party's side, unticked, and leaves the question out when the party has no other role to offer; ticking none is allowed, and the address is saved with the party's own role plus any role ticked.
requirements.why: The journey always needs an address it can select for its party, so the party's role is applied without a tick, while the trader can still add the other roles of that side in one go (c-434).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-081 to p5-085 and p5-154: the journey-mode roles question already reads this way, and repo-tests-p13-107 proves the party's role saved without a tick.

requirements.statement: The INS end-to-end suite proves the address book's add journey in its steps, its roles question, its validation messages and its journey hand-off, and the edit page with its return, its refusals and its banner, with each record it creates soft-deleted afterwards, an other-organisation record created under a generated organisation id, and its seeded fixtures reconciled to one live record each.
requirements.why: The suite is what holds the add and edit pages to the behaviour these requirements name; a page that changes without it changes untested.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p13-118, p13-119 and p13-124: the suite already walks the three-step add through its own entry points and reconciles its seeded records before the journeys run; p13-132 and p13-133 record what it leaves unproven.

requirements.statement: An address is held per organisation in the address book, on its own rather than against a notification, a commodity line or a unit, and its values are the ones a user types on the add or edit form.
requirements.why: The V4 Address Block states neither an 'Applies at' level nor a source for its fields, so where an address is held and where its values come from are the real service's to settle, and the address book holds one organisation-scoped record filled in by hand.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p1-001 and repo-tests-p13-112: the record is owned by an organisation and holds the fields the form asks for, and p13-120 shows entry by hand as the only way in.

requirements.statement: The add-details step asks 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and the postcode field, free text of at most 100 characters that may be left blank.
requirements.why: Paul's ruling of 14 October keeps County on the add step: the V4 Address Block gives every address block the same fields, County among them, and ranks above the prototype, and an add form that cannot set a field the record, the view page and the edit form all carry would lose it on a round trip.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p5-027, p5-039 and p5-040 and repo-tests-p13-020: the add form already asks 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and the postcode, optional and capped at 100 characters.

requirements.statement: On a germinal products notification's view header, no action shares another action's form: 'Copy as new' posts a form of its own, and 'Amend this notification' and Delete are links to their own confirmation pages placed outside it, as on the live animals header.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling gives every posting button on the view header its own form and keeps Delete a link to its confirmation page; the 25 November ruling makes Amend a link to the amend confirmation page and applies the header rule to live animals, germinal products and plants alike. The germinal set's amend, copy and delete build on what the manage notifications theme lands (27 November ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set is walked or served today (repo-tests-p8-152), so the germinal copy of the view header is new.

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a notification's view header is a link to that notification's amend confirmation page, outside any other action's form, in the live animals, germinal products and plants frontends. Following it changes nothing: the notification moves into amendment only when the trader confirms on that page.
requirements.why: The 25 November ruling answers the header question: the first click on Amend changes nothing, a post that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-post on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by link in the same header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals view header's Amend posts a form of its own and the post starts the amendment at once, taking the record to AMEND and writing the snapshots (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-008, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-010). Plants' amend moves behind the same confirmation page (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-057).

requirements.statement: The animals backend records whether the answers of a notification being amended differ from the submitted ones as a yes-or-no value that is never empty, and the animals frontend reads that value from the backend's shape, in its local stub as against the real service, rather than working it out itself.
requirements.why: Duplicate: req-2333 carries this requirement, with its claims and conflicts folded in; the backend's own flag is req-2865.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the frontend works the value out itself rather than reading the backend's shape (ruling-sam-2026-11-19-p1-026), while already showing its effect on the amend review's heading (repo-tests-p6-008); a copy starts without the flag (repo-backend-p2-039).

requirements.statement: A document added during an amendment is not a changed answer: the amend review keeps the title and heading 'Review your notification' until an answer itself differs from the submitted one.
requirements.why: Uploading a document does not change what the notification says, so the heading waits for an answer to change.
requirements.deltaNote: Adding only a document during an amendment already leaves the review headed 'Review your notification' (repo-tests-p6-009).

requirements.statement: Amend, cancel amendment and delete are confirmed and carried out without JavaScript: each confirmation is an ordinary page of its own, reached by a full page load, whose confirm button posts a form and whose way back is a control that leaves the notification as it was, in live animals, germinal products and plants.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and the interaction designer's 9 November answer makes both amend and cancel amendment pages rather than dialogs, so no confirmation depends on a script. The design's own amend confirmation is a server-rendered page of GOV.UK components.
requirements.deltaNote: Cancelling an amendment already works with JavaScript turned off in both frontends (repo-frontend-p7-125, repo-plantsfrontend-p11-105, repo-tests-p6-044), and plants' four ending pages are each a page of their own (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-112); the amend confirmation page does not exist yet (req-1391).

requirements.statement: The tests repo documents why cancel amendment waits on the URL.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 19 November ruling leaves the deleted docs note as it is and records no interest in restoring it.

requirements.statement: The delete confirmation, cancel-amendment confirmation and notification-actions features carry a signed-off maturity level.
requirements.why: Out of scope: promoting a page is its own reviewed pull request rather than part of other work, and Design Release 2.1 does not ask for it, so each page keeps the maturity it has while its behaviour changes.

requirements.statement: The end-to-end suite's own fixtures change: the reference numbers it records against each run, the later-session helper that keeps only the sign-in cookie, the per-service session cookie names and the landing page each service opens after sign-in.
requirements.why: Out of scope: suite mechanics with nothing a user sees; Design Release 2.1 does not touch them, and they stay as they are while the specs above follow the changed behaviour.

requirements.statement: The delete, cancel-amendment and amend confirmations ask the trader to type nothing and tick nothing: each is a two-control Yes or No page with no field, so it has no option list, no validation and no error message, in every set.
requirements.why: The confirmation is the question, so pressing Yes acts and nothing can be submitted blank.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete and cancel-amend pages are already two-button pages with no radios, no errors key and no validate step (repo-frontend-p7-104, repo-frontend-p7-129), as plants' are (repo-plantsfrontend-p11-113); the amend confirmation page is built the same way.

requirements.statement: Each document a trader uploads for a notification is stored as one record of its own, in the animals backend's accompanying_documents collection, keyed to the notification by its reference number, with one record per upload; the file reaches the record through the real uploader and virus scan.
requirements.why: The uploaded file and its details are held beside the notification rather than inside it, so a document can be scanned, listed and published on its own.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-043 and p9-044 read the accompanying_documents collection and find exactly one record per upload; p9-055 shows the file travels through the real uploader and virus scan before the record is stored.

requirements.statement: An accompanying-document record holds the document reference the trader typed, an upload id in UUID form, the date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD calendar date, the document type as the code the type select submits rather than the label shown, a scan status, a version, a correlation id, an S3 bucket, created and updated timestamps, and a files list whose entries each hold the original filename, the declared content type, the byte length, an S3 key beginning with the notification's reference number and the upload id, the content type detected on scanning, a SHA-256 checksum and a per-file status.
requirements.why: PIMS, the documents list and support all read these fields, and the S3 key keeps each notification's uploads in their own path.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p9-045 to p9-052 read every one of those fields back from the stored record today.
