A commodity's heading in the results and in the tally reads as its name with its code in round brackets where the service knows a name for the code and as the code alone where it does not, while commodity details still names a commodity by its code, and a result shows the species label with the part the query matched in bold so a trader can see why it was offered. Results are listed in order, the commodity groups by their code and each group's species by the label they are offered under, over the page of results the search returned. With JavaScript, Escape in the search box or a click outside the search hides the list while keeping the term and every choice, and focusing or clicking the box shows it again, the list hiding once the click has landed so a click on a button below it is not moved out from under the pointer. The tally shows a chip per chosen species under its commodity's heading, the species' Latin name and a cross named to remove that name, with a control to clear everything beside the count, styled as a link and posting the page's form. The add-selection button and its wording are settled for now and come back to design with their no-JavaScript question.
requirements.why: A results list drawn as the design draws it, ordered by code and label, lets a trader scan a long catalogue, and hiding it only after a click has landed keeps a button below it clickable.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-276 to repo-frontend-p19-283 and repo-frontend-p19-292, with the open wording of the add-selection button recorded at repo-frontend-p19-275.

requirements.statement: A species reads as its Latin name with its common name in round brackets wherever it is listed or named, in the search results, on commodity details, in the selected commodities tables and in the identification details, and as its Latin name alone where the reference data holds no common name for it; the tally's chips carry the Latin name alone, as the design draws them. The permanent address rule and the identifier-column rule read the line's stored Latin name rather than the displayed label, so a species whose common name changes what it reads as still gates the same way. One commodity code can cover several commodities and hundreds of species, so each chosen species gets its own selected-commodities row named by the species on both commodity details and identification. The commodity heading on commodity details is set at the larger size because the commodity blocks are the substance of the page, the type stepping down from commodity to species to quantity labels, and the labels carrying a size so they do not read at the weight of their hints; the number of animals question has no hint because the page repeats it per species, so an example would repeat with it; and the commodity inset's second sentence stops a reader concluding that goods with no certificate need no notification.
requirements.why: Gating on the stored Latin name keeps a rule firing when a display label changes, and one row per species is what lets a trader give numbers and identifiers for each.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-284, repo-frontend-p19-285 and repo-frontend-p19-289 to repo-frontend-p19-293.

requirements.statement: The commodity tally offers a removal per chosen species, posting the page's form with the species' key in the button's value, so the entry pressed is the entry removed however the panel is ordered, and each removal on commodity details carries the entry it removes, the commodity's code on a code row and the line's key on a species row, so a repeated or stale removal is refused rather than taking another row. Because a tick box on screen carries no hidden value, a removal naming a choice the post no longer carries, the trader having unticked that box first, is honoured and nothing is logged, while a removal naming a key the stored search rows never held is refused as a bad request with one logged refusal, reachable by a tampered post and by a page left open across a save and a later removal of that commodity line, because a save empties the stored rows. A removal leaves the trader on commodity details while a line is left, with every number they had typed still in its field, because the page answers the removal itself rather than redirecting to it, and a removal that empties the selection goes to the commodity question, because that is where the next answer comes from; commodity details is one form opening with a hidden submit before the selected-commodities table so Enter hits it rather than the first removal, and ending with the save actions, and a removal is a post on that form with no load route so a link cannot trigger it.
requirements.why: Carrying the entry in the button's value is what makes the row pressed the row removed after the list has been reordered, and answering the removal on the page keeps the numbers a trader has already typed.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-286 to repo-frontend-p19-288 and repo-frontend-p19-294 to repo-frontend-p19-297.

requirements.statement: The consignment addresses page gives each party its own section, a medium heading, its hint, then either a named link to add that party's address or the chosen address in an inset with controls below it to change it and to edit its details, so the trader sees which full address they chose, its name and every address line; the county parish holding number follows the same section shape, its number read with slashes on one line and with no edit control. The inset shows the name in bold, then each street line on its own line, with the locality, county, postcode and country joining into the last line, the country being the name held on the notification's own copy of the party so the page never asks the address book. A section with no address may also offer a control that fills it from another party's address, place of origin filling the consignor and consignee filling both the importer and the place of destination, no other pair offering one and a section already holding an address never offering one; the page is one form so such a control posts it, and pressing one shows the page again with the target section filled and no success banner. Each section is a region named by its heading so a screen reader lists the parties, the add link names the party so it needs no hidden suffix, and the change, edit and fill-from controls keep a hidden suffix naming the party because two sections would otherwise offer the same control name. The section heading reads Addresses, the page's own heading, its task row and its review card title read Consignment addresses, and an incomplete card asks the trader to complete the consignment addresses. The backend names the place of destination destination where the journey names it place of destination, every other address role having the same name in both.
requirements.why: Reading the chosen address back in full on the page where it was chosen is what lets a trader see they picked the right one, and taking the country from the notification's own copy keeps the page working when the address book is unavailable.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-299 to repo-frontend-p19-304 for the sections and the inset, with the role names at repo-frontend-p19-450; the wording in the second-last sentence is ruling-sam-2026-11-17-p1-010 to ruling-sam-2026-11-17-p1-013, and whether the pages already read that way is the consignment-parties area's to say from the code.

requirements.statement: Every party link on the consignment addresses page carries where the trader came from, so a trader sent there from check your answers goes out to the picker or the edit page and comes back, with Save and continue there going on to the review page, and the county parish holding link carries it alone, its page's Back and its save always answering the consignment addresses page with no marker needed.
requirements.why: A trader sent from check your answers to fix one address must be able to get back to it after a round trip through a picker.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-451 and repo-frontend-p19-306.

requirements.statement: Each party picker searches the address book from a submitted search box with a medium search label, a hint naming what can be searched, and a square blue icon button joined to the box, the button named for screen readers and being the form's first submit so Enter in the box runs the search, the box and button taking half the content column's width. The picker is one form in which the search and the save are told apart by the value of the control pressed, a ticked row travels across a further search in a hidden field with no client script, and a page link is a load carrying the address the server already holds for the party rather than a row ticked on this visit and not yet saved. A control to add a new address sits as a secondary button beside the picker's heading, shown only outside stub mode, and because it leaves the journey for the address book it sits with the page rather than inside the search form.
requirements.why: A search that runs on a submit works without JavaScript, and carrying the ticked row in a hidden field is what keeps a choice through a second search with no script at all.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-307 and repo-frontend-p19-308; ruling-design-2026-11-13-p1-014 keeps the search on a submit rather than filtering as the trader types, and ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-015 records the joined blue button as already built.

requirements.statement: A party picker's results sit under a heading asking the trader to select an address, with the count straight under it, eight a page counted against every address the picker found, whether the role's whole list or the matches when a search narrows it, and the design system's pagination follows the table where more than eight were found, its links carrying the search term and the address held as chosen. An inset above the results names whichever address the picker currently holds as chosen, between the search box and the results, on every page and after a search, the address coming from the address in the request, the posted field or the party's saved answer so the name shows on a page that does not hold its row. The results table is one fieldset whose visually hidden legend repeats the heading so a screen reader names the group of addresses, and with no matches the message takes the place of the count.
requirements.why: An organisation's address book grows past one screen, so the picker pages, and naming the chosen address above the results is what tells a trader on the second page what they have already chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-311, repo-frontend-p19-314 and repo-frontend-p19-315, which the design record states as built; ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-022 pages the pickers at eight and ruling-ian-2026-11-23-p1-011 restores the restatement of the chosen address with the paging.

requirements.statement: The edit control on a section follows that section's address whether the picker copied it onto the notification or a fill-from control took it from the paired party, and with no address held the edit page sends the trader to the picker; reopening a party's picker pre-ticks the record that party's address was picked from while the role's list still holds it. A picker is reached from the consignment addresses page rather than the hub, so it ends with the primary control alone. A save with nothing chosen leaves without refusing and commits nothing, so the role stays empty or keeps the address it held; an address not in the book, or no longer in it, is refused with the role's own error; and a missing or deleted selection travels as no selection while the context a change link carried is kept on every way out of the picker.
requirements.why: A trader who opens a picker to look and leaves without choosing should not lose the address the notification already holds, and pre-ticking the record they picked from shows them where the address came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-309, repo-frontend-p19-310, repo-frontend-p19-312 and repo-frontend-p19-317.

requirements.statement: The permanent address section is a third section shape on the consignment addresses page, alongside the party sections and the county parish holding section, for a consignment carrying a cat, dog or ferret line, its hint being a lead-in sentence followed by two bullets rather than the party sections' single line. Once every animal needing one has a permanent address the section shows one address, every addressable animal being saved against the place of destination or only one animal needing one, and otherwise one line saying how many animals have an address added, counting the animals that need one. Either shape carries a control to change it and no edit control, because the address was hand-entered or copied from the place of destination on the permanent address page and never picked from the address book, so there is no record there to edit.
requirements.why: A hand-entered address has no address-book record behind it, so offering to edit that record would lead nowhere, and one line for many animals keeps the page readable.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-318 to repo-frontend-p19-320; which commodities the section applies to is the identification and permanent address area's to settle from the data dictionary.

requirements.statement: The county parish holding number page keeps its three part labels on screen, because three unlabelled boxes under one legend would be harder to use than the single field they replace, and the number being two digits of county, three of parish and four of holding, its example hint shows that grouping with no comma and no full stop; its help names the animal and plant health documents, then links to the guidance for checking a holding's details. The boxes set no character limit, so nothing typed or pasted is cut short: when the county box holds nine digits with or without spaces or slashes and the other two are empty the number is split into its three parts on save, and anything else goes through the per-part checks unchanged with every box keeping what was typed. Each box turns the browser's saved values off and asks for a digit keypad, nothing moves focus between the boxes, and one error message belongs to the group rather than to each box, the date-input row classes only sitting the boxes side by side. The page can be saved with every box empty: no number is saved, any number saved before is cleared, and the gap is held at submission rather than refused on the page. The number is stored as nine bare digits.
requirements.why: A trader copying a number off a document should be able to paste it whole, and holding the gap at submission lets them come back to the page without being blocked on it.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-321 to repo-frontend-p19-329; ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-013 has the boxes follow the date input with no script on top, which repo-frontend-p19-324 to repo-frontend-p19-326 record as built.

requirements.statement: The permanent address page is reached only from the permanent address section of the consignment addresses page, for a consignment carrying a cat, dog or ferret line, and its cards come from the animal identifier records already entered, one per animal, never from the line's animal count, because the address is stored on the identifier record so a card can only exist once that record does. When at least one line needs a permanent address and no line that needs one has an animal identified yet, the page shows no cards and a message takes their place: "Identify an animal on identification details before you can continue.", linking to the identification details page, when any such line carries a number of animals, and "Add the number of animals on consignment details before you can continue.", linking to the consignment details page, when none does. While the message shows, the save control still renders but writes nothing. Each card asks once, as its own radio group legend, whether the animal lives at the place of destination or at a new address, and the page carries no second question above the cards.
requirements.why: Driving the cards off the identifier records keeps the page from offering a card it cannot store an answer against, and asking once per card keeps the answer with the animal it belongs to.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-330, repo-frontend-p19-331, repo-frontend-p19-333 and repo-frontend-p19-452 to repo-frontend-p19-455; the permanent address feature's English copy holds both messages.

requirements.statement: Choosing to enter a new address on a permanent address card requires the name or organisation name, the first address line, the town or city, the postcode, an email address and a phone number, while the second address line and the county may be left blank, and every field's character limit and over-long message are the ones the owning address rules already build for the party edit page, the page stating only its own required messages and no format check on the email, the phone or the postcode. Choosing the place of destination before the notification has one is refused on that card's radio group, naming no animal on the field or in the summary, while an address field's refusal names the card's animal in the error summary and stays plain on the field itself. The new-address fields ask no country, a hand-entered address always recording the United Kingdom, and the phone field is the one field with a hint, because a trader giving an address outside the United Kingdom cannot otherwise know the number is dialled from here. An animal left with neither option chosen saves with no permanent address, the save still succeeding for the others.
requirements.why: Naming the animal in the summary is what lets a trader find the card that needs fixing on a page of many, and saving the cards that are answered keeps their work while they find the rest.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-334 to repo-frontend-p19-340.

requirements.statement: The documents file field is labelled as the attachment, the noun the review also uses, and the reference field has no hint. The status column reports the check's progress, scanning for a virus and the check being completed, and on a refusal names the reason the upload service gave where the page has wording for it, a virus found, the upload failing or the download failing, a reason it has no wording for staying as rejected rather than being named wrongly. A document is started by any of its reference, its type whether offered or not, its date of issue text or a chosen file, and any save control then keeps every answer typed, says what is missing and adds nothing, or adds the document when it is complete, rather than dropping the part-filled form; every field is mandatory per record and there is no edit page, so presence is checked when a document is added, and the error summary lists the fields in the order they appear on the page. The type list opens on its select text, which carries no value, so a form left on it submits an empty type, and one message covers both mistakes a list can make, being left on the select text or carrying a value the page never offered; the offered types are served by the service and primed at boot so the check is built for each add rather than frozen at module load, and the list's items, the add form's check and the vocabulary this service sends to the backend are one ordered list, so the order the page offers is the order that list states.
requirements.why: Keeping a part-filled document on the page rather than dropping it is what stops a trader re-typing a reference after a missed field, and one ordered list of types keeps the page, the check and the backend from disagreeing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-341 to repo-frontend-p19-343 and repo-frontend-p19-357 to repo-frontend-p19-360.

requirements.statement: The documents file size limit is whatever the documents upload configuration holds and nothing else states a figure, the page states that same figure and checks it in the browser for any submit that sends the file, so a trader learns a file is too large before spending time uploading it, and the upload service decides for itself whether to take a file and may refuse one as too large on receipt, which the page renders in its own wording. While the add form is open every save control posts the form and its file to the upload service's own scanning session rather than to this service, that session being opened with the size limit to enforce so the ingress body cap does not bound it; when the form is closed, or a taken-on document or a removal is waiting to be retried, the save controls post to this service and send no file, so the retry runs before anything else on the page. A file carrying no bytes is the right type and under the size limit, so it reaches the page rather than being stopped before it, and the page is where it is refused and nothing is added. A document saved by adding another or by the save-and-return control is followed by a redirect so a reload cannot replay the save, while one saved by Save and continue is answered on the returned request by the save choice, a reload of that response saving nothing twice because a document already listed is not added again, and nothing holds the trader for a scan still running. A render reuses the upload session the page is already showing while that session is still waiting for its file, carried in the refresh link and a hidden field, so a scan being polled does not leave a run of registrations behind; a render carrying no handle, and one whose session has already taken its file, opens a session of its own, which keeps two concurrent adds off one handle, and the carried handle is looked up on the notification rather than trusted alone, so a handle another notification opened reaches nothing. A form carrying a session that has already taken its file is answered by the upload service and never by this one, because the save controls post the file straight there, the page being served with no store and the feature's client bundle opening it again by its own address when the browser hands back a copy it kept. The query key the trader returns under is the trader-facing word for what they return from and its value is the correlation handle, because no upload identifier exists when the session opens, and the return path is relative because the upload service refuses an absolute redirect outside development. A well-formed upload identifier from another journey is answered as not found rather than as forbidden, so the journey never confirms that upload exists.
requirements.why: Posting the file straight to the upload service is what lets a large attachment past the ingress body cap, and looking a carried handle up on the notification is what keeps one trader's upload session out of another's notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-344 to repo-frontend-p19-350 and repo-frontend-p19-361 to repo-frontend-p19-368.

requirements.statement: The documents page uses the full-width surface so the added-documents table fits, its guidance and its fields keeping a two-thirds reading width, and with no documents the upload card shows no table and no sentence. The reference cell breaks a long unbroken reference onto further lines so the table stays inside the card, and each row's actions sit at its right-hand end. The reason the add control is shut sits before the control it refuses, and the control keeps its place in the tab order so the error summary can reach it; the limit error links to the documents already added rather than to the attachment field, because at the cap the add control is shut and pointing a trader at the file input would send them to a control they cannot use, while the table shows the documents they already hold. The drop zone's wording matches the design system's own defaults. A document's file is opened with a link rather than a submit so it needs no token, and a file is offered only once its scan has settled clean. The status tag carries a visually hidden name for the document it belongs to, so a screen reader hears what was checked. With JavaScript on, the upload control the page shows is not the original file input, so the oversize summary error points at the control a trader can focus rather than at the hidden input behind it.
requirements.why: Pointing an error at a control the trader can actually focus is what makes the error summary usable, and offering a file only once its scan is clean keeps an unchecked file from being opened.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-351 to repo-frontend-p19-356 and repo-frontend-p19-367 to repo-frontend-p19-372.

requirements.statement: A document the scan rejected holds the continue back, as does a document the upload service has taken on that the notification does not list, because otherwise the trader would carry on with a claimed document missing from the notification, while the exit to the overview waits for neither.
requirements.why: A trader must not reach the declaration believing a document is attached when the notification does not hold it, and a trader who only wants to stop should not be held by a scan.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-362.

requirements.statement: A trader's own uploaded document is served under a cache policy a decision has settled, saying what a shared or browser cache may keep of it.
requirements.why: The goal is the look and feel of the notification journey, and no source in this programme settles what a cache may keep of a trader's document: the design record carries it as still to be settled, with the page served with no store because a kept copy of it can post to a spent upload session, so the open decision is reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: The design record states that a document's file is served with no cache directive of its own and records what a cache may keep of a trader's own document as still to be settled (repo-frontend-p19-371).

requirements.statement: The arrival date's hint gives a fixed date showing the format rather than a date tied to the arrival window, the date widget's bounds and the out-of-range message policing the window, and the arrival details page reads the window once per request and hands it to both the widget and the checks, so the two cannot disagree across midnight, a reading with no widget taking the window as it stands.
requirements.why: A hint that moved with the window would read as part of the rule, and reading the window once is what keeps the widget and the refusal from disagreeing at midnight.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-373 and repo-frontend-p19-374.

requirements.statement: The port search shows a placeholder asking the trader to select a port in its empty box, in the same words as the select text that is the first entry of the list shown without JavaScript. The means of transport options read air, rail, road and sea, and each stores its own reference code. The transport identification hint is a lead-in and one bullet per alternative, so the number of choices shows at a glance.
requirements.why: Using one wording in the box and in the list keeps the question the same on both paths, and one bullet per alternative shows a trader at a glance what they may give.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-375 to repo-frontend-p19-377.

requirements.statement: A transit country is added to the table when the trader presses the add control, and removing one submits the page's form so the token travels with it and no load can trigger it, the country's code riding in the button's value so the row pressed is the row removed however the list has been reordered since the page rendered. The status message region ships empty and the page's script writes the message into it just after load, because a live region already holding its text when the document is parsed is read as ordinary page content, both adding and removing being full form submits so the message arrives with a fresh document every time. The added-countries list names each country rather than its code, because the list is the whole record of the answer the trader reads back, and the cap is not stated up front: the search goes when the last country is added and the status message says why. The page's browser title is the short task name rather than its question heading, the search's select text asks for a choice while its empty-box text asks for a search, because the two do different things, and a country already added stays in the list and a repeat is refused by name, which tells the trader more than a country quietly missing from the list. The page offers the same countries and territories as the country of origin page, each territory named with its country, rather than every code the label lookup resolves. An empty list is a valid answer because the question is optional, while a list holding a country not offered is refused, on submit as not from the list and on a stored answer as no longer available, and a stored list is checked against the page's rules when it opens, a banner naming any country no longer offered before the continue saves the filtered list. The page names the choice once, a heading above the search box and the table with the fieldset round the table carrying the same words visually hidden, so a screen-reader user hears the group named and a sighted user reads the words once.
requirements.why: The table is itself the confirmation that a country was added or removed, and refusing a repeat by name tells a trader why their choice did not appear instead of leaving them guessing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-378 to repo-frontend-p19-390; ruling-design-2026-11-13-p1-003 keeps the add control and ruling-sam-2026-11-10-p1-008 makes the table its own confirmation, both of which the record states as built.

requirements.statement: The transporter list shows its facts in headed columns with a status tag, green for an approved transporter and magenta for a newly added one, and a transporter with no approval number reads as not applicable in that column. Searching the list filters it in place: nothing is checked or committed, and a picked row stays picked when the search leaves it on the list. With JavaScript the list narrows in the page as the trader types, because the page already holds the whole list and needs no endpoint, the matching letters in each shown cell being bold and a polite live region saying how many rows are shown, and pressing the search control or Enter runs the same filter and posts nothing, so the page keeps the whole list to filter again; without JavaScript the search is a submit on the page's own form and the server returns the narrowed list, the pick travelling through a search in a hidden field and the search and the save being told apart by the value of the control pressed. A transporter picked and then filtered out of view stays picked, the filter hiding rows and never clearing a choice. The search matches the name, the address, the approval number, the type and the status, ignoring case and accents, so a trader typing plain letters finds an accented name, and a transporter with no approval number is matched by the words its column shows; a term running across two cells, such as an address into an approval number, still finds its row, and because no single cell holds the whole term nothing is bold. The control to add a transporter sits on the search row, right-aligned above the table, dropping below the search on a phone, and the tab order is the search box, the search control, the add control, then the rows.
requirements.why: Filtering a list the page already holds keeps a trader's choice while they look for another, and matching across cells is what finds a row when a trader pastes something spanning two columns.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-391 to repo-frontend-p19-397, with the in-place filter at repo-frontend-p19-381. Where transporter records are held is the transporter area's to settle.

requirements.statement: The transporter type question warns the trader to check the transporter list before adding a new transporter, so they do not add a duplicate, offers private first with no hint and commercial with an explanation of the Northern Ireland condition, and its one control is a continue rather than a save. Each add form opens only for the type it belongs to, opening or posting it for any other stored type, or none, returning the trader to the type question. A commercial transporter added by hand can only be from Northern Ireland, so its country is shown rather than asked and a posted value naming anywhere else has been tampered with and is refused, and the commercial form opens with the authorisation rules the transporter list states, read from the list's own copy. Both forms close the address at the country, then head the contact details with the email before the phone, and both hint the international dialling code. A transporter typed in by hand joins the organisation's list as new rather than approved, and a private transporter's country is held as both the display name and its code, so neither storing it nor reading it back needs a lookup.
requirements.why: Warning the trader before they add is cheaper than de-duplicating a list afterwards, and showing a country that can only be one value saves a question that has one answer.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-398 to repo-frontend-p19-405; ruling-ian-2026-11-06-p1-038 forces a commercial transporter's country with no reference-data lookup, which repo-frontend-p19-401 records as built. How that country is stored, and where a transporter record lives, are the transporter area's to settle against the service.

requirements.statement: The link that adds a transporter carries where the trader came from, and the add form's own save carries it on to the transporter list, so a trader sent from check your answers goes on from the list like any other start. Saving a complete record on either add form returns the trader to the list with the saved transporter as the first row, already chosen, under a one-time success banner titled for success and reading the transporter's name with only its first letter capitalised followed by the words that a transporter was added, the banner showing on that one view only and a reload or a later return showing the list with no banner. Values entered on a form whose save was refused are shown again in its fields the next time the trader opens that form, until the form is saved or cancelled, while the secondary control on each form discards them, commits nothing to the notification and takes the trader to the dashboard, wherever the notification list lives. The transporter type question and the private add form carry no status strip, while the list and the commercial add form do. Where the stored type was not changed on the way into an add form, the transporter chosen before the add began is still chosen after cancelling, and a trader who changed the type at the type question on the way in is left with the type they chose and no transporter, the type question's own purge having removed the other type's stored transporter before the add form opened.
requirements.why: Showing the saved transporter first and already chosen is what saves the trader finding it again, and keeping refused values until the form is saved or cancelled is what stops them re-typing an address.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-406 to repo-frontend-p19-410, with the trail carried at repo-frontend-p19-382 and the status strip at repo-frontend-p19-400.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's own code-quality rules bind every change to it: a comment describes only the lines below it and only where a name or an extraction cannot, making no claim about callers, other modules, the backend, a library or a test and carrying no counts; no ticket key, backlog or ruling identifier, release name or session word appears in code, comments or test titles; no history is kept in code, so there is no before-and-after narration, no removed constants and no note of a rename; a name predicts what the code returns and changes, with no positional boolean flags, no metaphors and one name per concept, a rename covering the whole vocabulary; and set-up used by two tests lives in the shared helper, promoting a helper deleting the local copies. The lint script enforces the identifier, silent-catch, error-log and platform-layer rules through the repository's own lint rule module, and the identifier rule in template comments through a second one, and the canonical text of the rules lives in the workspace rather than in the repository.
requirements.why: Lint refusing a ticket key or a ruling identifier in code is what keeps a programme's own vocabulary out of the service, and one canonical text keeps every repository answering to the same rules.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-411 to repo-frontend-p19-416 and repo-frontend-p19-419: the repository records the rules and names the lint that enforces them.

requirements.statement: Every branch that changes an outcome logs once through the request's logger with the identifiers support searches by, logging the error object rather than only a message, and no request or response body is logged at information level. A test's title states what its assertions prove, and the test fails without the change it covers.
requirements.why: One log line per outcome with the identifiers support searches by is what makes a trader's report traceable, and a test that passes without its change proves nothing.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-417 and repo-frontend-p19-418.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend requires at least Node 26.13.1 and npm 11.6.2, the floor set in its engines field. It keeps its session in a Redis-backed cache when deployed and in memory for local development, which the cache engine setting overrides, the in-memory cache being unsuitable for production because it is neither shared between instances nor kept across a restart, while every deployed instance of a service shares one Redis store and a frontend may use only the keys prefixed with its own service name. Its Redis client pins the RESP2 wire protocol, because the client library defaults to RESP3 and the session store talks RESP2 to the managed Redis service. A forward proxy is set up by default and calls made with the platform fetch use the proxy dispatcher, a client that uses another HTTP library providing the dispatcher itself.
requirements.why: A session that is not shared between instances loses a trader's work on a deploy, a client speaking a protocol the store does not answer breaks every session, and a call that misses the proxy dispatcher fails only once it is deployed.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-456, repo-frontend-p19-421, repo-frontend-p19-457, repo-frontend-p19-457-m1 and repo-frontend-p19-428.

requirements.statement: For every page request it handles, the animals frontend counts the calls that request made to its journey backend, the times it read the signed-in session record from the session store, and every call it made to an HTTP dependency, by dependency and operation, the journey backend included, commands sent to the session store not counting as dependency calls. A page request is every request except the health check, the site icon, the static asset route and the counts endpoint itself, so a form post, a redirect, a rendered page, the not-found page and the document scan poll all count; a backend call is one call to the journey backend through the shared fetch helper, counted once even when a refused or slow connection is retried, and a session resolution is one read of the session record by the authentication plugin or by the view context, the session state the session library loads not being counted. A request's counts live in a per-request async store, the counts plugin running each request's lifecycle methods inside it because the server framework offers no public hook that runs a whole request in one async context, and because a view renders outside that context a session resolution is counted against the request it is read for rather than through the store. Running totals are kept per route and served from a counts endpoint, which a delete clears, answering with the service name, the time counting began, the totals and a list per route by method and path, each holding page requests, backend calls, session resolutions and external calls, the last keyed by dependency and then by operation; the performance suite reads them and reports the ratios. The endpoint is on by default for local development and off when deployed, and needs no sign-in, while the metrics are off locally and on when deployed, writing one metric document per page request carrying the backend calls and session resolutions marked as a page request.
requirements.why: Counting a request's backend and session reads is what shows a page that has quietly started making one call per row, and the performance suite's ratios are read from those counts.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-458 to repo-frontend-p19-465, with the page-request definition at repo-frontend-p19-423, the endpoint at repo-frontend-p19-425 and the performance suite's use at repo-frontend-p19-427.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's pre-commit hook is cheap, running the staged-file formatter and lint auto-fix on the staged files only, with no build and no tests, so a fix lands in the commit that caused it, while the pre-push hook is the full gate, running the format check, lint and the unit suite, which builds the frontend first. The slow half of the gate sits on the push rather than the commit because the suite is thousands of tests with coverage on top of a production build, mostly fixed startup cost that does not shrink for a small change, and charging that to every commit is what teaches people to skip the hooks, which skips the cheap format and lint checks as well, while a push is the first point the work affects anyone else. Installing dependencies installs both hooks. The whole gate, or just its fast half, can be run by hand at any time, and when the workspace's quality gate has already run the format check, lint and the suite for the exact commit and left a marker naming the verified revision, the pre-push hook skips rather than repeating it, while without that workspace the full gate always runs locally; the workspace gate runs its cheap checks before the build, so a formatting slip fails in seconds instead of after a full suite. The SonarCloud analysis the gate uploads is set up in the repo's own Sonar project properties file.
requirements.why: A cheap commit and a thorough push is what keeps people using the hooks instead of skipping them, and the shared marker stops the same suite running twice for one revision.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-429 to repo-frontend-p19-432 and the three notes beside them, with the SonarCloud set-up at repo-frontend-p19-437-m1.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend builds a development image and a production image from its Dockerfile, each run with the container's port 3000 published on the host's port 3000. The recommended path for local cross-service development is the workspace Docker stack, held in the trade imports workspace repository, which stands the identity stub up alongside the frontend with the right environment wiring and needs no host-file edits, while a standalone run against that stub needs its own environment file naming the sign-in configuration address, client identifier, client secret, service identifier and policy; the full local environment, the database, the file store, Redis, the stubs and every animals service including this one, is that stack, which can also be started built from local source or with this service left out to run natively. The session cookie's same-site setting is fixed at strict in the authentication plugin while the identity state cookie is lax by default and set by its own variable, because the identity callback is a cross-site top-level navigation on which a strict state cookie is not sent, so sign-in fails.
requirements.why: A strict state cookie silently breaks sign-in, so the reason it is lax has to be recorded beside the setting, and naming the stack as the local path saves each developer wiring the stubs by hand.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-433 to repo-frontend-p19-435, with the two images at repo-frontend-p19-435-m1 and the workspace that holds the stack at repo-frontend-p19-466.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's accessibility and performance floors are checked by running Lighthouse locally against the workspace stack on the service's port, the address list, the score floors and the steps for contributing to them living in the set's own guide.
requirements.why: A recorded floor and a recorded address list are what make the check repeatable by anyone, rather than a number one person remembers.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-436.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's information is licensed under the Open Government Licence version 3, and its attribution statement is cited in a product or application that uses it.
requirements.why: A public service's licence and attribution have to travel with its information.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-437.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's readme names the workspace that holds the Docker stack, the identity stub wiring and the pre-push marker, and names the same workspace everywhere it refers to it.
requirements.why: The goal is the look and feel of the notification journey, so a pointer in a readme is not a difference this programme changes. The readme now names the trade imports workspace for the Docker stack and the full local environment, so the stale pointer once reported here has gone and nothing is left to report.
requirements.deltaNote: The readme names the trade imports workspace repository for the Docker stack it recommends and for the full local environment (repo-frontend-p19-466).

requirements.statement: Where the animals frontend's design record names an exception to a house rule, the rule it names can be read from where the record says it lives.
requirements.why: The goal is the look and feel of the notification journey, so a citation that leads nowhere in the repository's own record is not a difference this programme changes: the one recorded exception to the rule against custom styling cites a rule file the repository does not hold, that rule living in the workspace instead, which is reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: The design record's recorded exception to the no-custom-styling rule cites a rule file the repository does not hold: its agent directory holds only its settings and the secrets hooks, and that rule lives in the workspace (repo-frontend-p19-439).

requirements.statement: A decision already taken on the animals frontend can be looked up by its identifier in the repository that holds it.
requirements.why: The goal is the look and feel of the notification journey and no source in this programme asks for a machine-readable ledger: the repository keeps its decisions only in its two prose records, the platform's architecture decisions and the set's per-page design record, so nothing in it can be queried for a decision by identifier, which is reported rather than built.
requirements.deltaNote: The repository keeps no machine-readable decisions ledger: its recorded decisions live only in the platform's architecture decisions and the set's per-page design record (repo-frontend-p19-440).

requirements.statement: Each departure from a house rule or a shared journey rule in the animals frontend is named in the set's own record with the reason for it: the documents reference cell's break-anywhere styling class, because the design system's own word-break class leaves a table cell's minimum width at the unbroken reference so a reference of the maximum length pushes the table past its card; the county parish holding sub-page's fixed Back target, against the general rule that a page takes its Back from where the trader came from; origin of the import being the one page the overview links to without the return controls; and the two transporter details forms ending with their own primary and a control that returns the trader to the dashboard.
requirements.why: An exception that carries its reason can be reviewed on that reason, while one that does not reads as an oversight and gets swept away with real atypicality.
requirements.deltaNote: Met by repo-frontend-p19-355, repo-frontend-p19-133, repo-frontend-p19-180 and repo-frontend-p19-184: the set's records name each exception with its reason. Whether the sweep of every other atypical item reaches these named exceptions rests on c-446.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's decisions ledger holds an entry for every decision that changes a plants behaviour the ledger already rules on, added as a new numbered entry naming the entry it supersedes, with the earlier entry kept in the ledger marked superseded and the subject it rules on re-stamped with the new resolution, who decided it and the new entry's id.
requirements.why: The ledger is the only place a plants ruling lives, and every conflict entry and every behaviour carries a pointer to it rather than its own answer, so a plants page changed without its entry leaves the set's own record saying the opposite of what the service does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the ledger's 97 entries carry no decision from this programme at all: they settle no content, wording, layout or component question of the design release, name neither the notification list's reframing nor a party picker's page size, and the seven superseded entries were every one of them replaced by the set's own owner rulings (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-005, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-183-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-184). The Copy as new action on the notification view header (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-017) is the first such decision: it supersedes the ledger's park of reusing a previous consignment and the 'minus Copy as new' clause of the post-submission action set, both of which today say plants has no Copy as new.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey specification's entry for each page, obligation and behaviour says what that page, obligation or behaviour does in the service, so a reader of the specification and a user of the journey see the same thing.
requirements.why: The specification is the plants set's contract and the tests linked to its scenarios are its evidence, so an entry that still reads the old way makes the contract false and the evidence point at behaviour nobody has.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the specification states the journey as it stood before this programme: the overview page is headed Overview with four numbered groups and five row statuses, the read-only view carries no Copy as new and a reuse behaviour says there is none, the page order ends at check your answers from the contact page, and the picker, list and status-strip entries describe today's layout (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-019, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-020, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-050, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-070, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-078, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-080). It also still marks all seven of its sources as being extracted from one 6 September snapshot, says the whole-journey fixture and the contract-test table do not exist when both do, and holds an empty happy-path fixture beside it (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-010, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-010-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-227, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-228, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-229). It disagrees with itself or the code in four places: a copied banner on the list against no Copy as new on the view, the Address book link pointing at '#' while the layout links the real address book, two Ministry of Justice Frontend versions while the repo pins 12.0.1, and the consignor stored as a copy while the ledger's d-089 says a reference (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-080-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-084-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-118-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-207-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants conflicts register's entry for a recorded disagreement names the decision that settled it, with that decision's resolution and who made it.
requirements.why: The register carries a pointer to the ledger and never its own answer, so an entry left pointing at a withdrawn decision reads as settled when it is not.
requirements.deltaNote: Today all 40 entries point at the set's own panel or owner rulings, 33 to the panel and 7 to the owner, and none of them points at a decision of this programme (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-008, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009). One entry also contradicts itself: c-011's resolution says the contact number and contact email fields were taken off it, while its field list, and c-025's, still name both (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-120-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants panel's evidence stays as it is when a ruling changes: its eight dockets, its 83 rulings with their rationale, spec changes and dissent, its reconciliation entries, its critic report and its panel README.
requirements.why: They record why each plants decision was taken, so a reopened question starts from the argument rather than the outcome; editing them would rewrite the reasoning instead of adding to it.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's own rule already says that changing a ruling leaves rulings.json and critic.json alone and edits the ledger and its subject in one commit (repo-plantsfrontend-p17-005).

requirements.statement: A document in the high-risk plants set's docs folder that states a behaviour of the journey says what the journey does, and changes in the same increment as the behaviour it describes.
requirements.why: The set's own documentation-drift work records that a document stating something the code does not do is a defect, because a second, false specification is read as though it were current.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the guides describe the journey as it stood before this programme: the served-surface reference's dashboard and picker description, the flow guide's sections, task rows, Back rules and caption map, the features guide's save-actions and view-header description, and the copy-status table (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-002, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-090, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-108, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-116, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-125, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-155, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-189). Each increment that changes one of those behaviours brings its sentence in step.

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants frontend the consignment contact page's two return controls read "Save and return to overview" and "Cancel and return to overview".
requirements.why: A return control names the page it opens, which is headed Overview, and every other page in the plants and live animals journeys names it that way.
requirements.deltaNote: Today they read "Save and return to hub" and "Cancel and return to hub", the one plants page where the internal name Hub reaches the screen (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-077, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-079).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants notification view header offers the same three actions as the live animals header: Amend this notification, Copy as new and Delete. Copy as new posts a form of its own, no action shares another action's form, and Copy as new carries the notification's own plants answers into the new draft.
requirements.why: A trader moving between the two journeys finds the same actions in the same place, and every layer beneath the button (the plants backend's copy endpoint, the frontend's real and stub persistence and the engine's copy) already exists, so only the header action and its route are missing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the plants read-only view's header carries the reference heading, the status tag, the date line, Amend, Delete notification and the import reference numbers, with no Copy as new, and the list offers View, Amend and Delete with no Copy as new anywhere (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-050, repo-plantsfrontend-p15-131, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-027). The copy machinery beneath it is already on main (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-020, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-028).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants address picker lists eight addresses a page, pages beyond eight, restates the address already chosen in an inset above the results, ticks the chosen row, and reads "No addresses match your search." when a search finds none.
requirements.why: Every picker in both journeys pages at the one figure the address book list already uses, and the inset keeps the chosen address on screen when its row is not on the page being read.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants served-surface reference already describes eight addresses a page, GOV.UK pagination beyond eight and the inset naming the chosen address (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-006, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-008).

requirements.statement: A change mirrored into the high-risk plants journey changes its structure, wording patterns, components and behaviour, and never which questions it asks, which values a field offers or which commodities a rule covers.
requirements.why: The plants journey's data comes from its own statute and policy paper, so a look-and-feel change that moved a question or a value would put the service outside the law it implements.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants set's own standing rulings already say so: the fourth ranks the policy paper and its draft statute above the Confluence pages, the Mural board and the prototype, and the fifth keeps the animals shape only where no plants source gives a reason to diverge (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-007, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-004).

requirements.statement: An increment that changes a high-risk plants page reads that page's maturity level from the page's own page identity module, and treats a page at agreed or readyForLive as signed off.
requirements.why: A change to a signed-off page needs a person's agreement, so an increment has to know which plants pages are signed off before it changes one.
requirements.deltaNote: The engine already reads a page's level and shows it in the phase banner, and agreed or readyForLive already counts as signed off, but the set's docs do not say which pages are at which level (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-064, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-067, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-385).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page's maturity level changes only through its own reviewed pull request.
requirements.why: Promotion is a person's judgement that the page's behaviour is agreed, so it cannot ride along inside a change that alters the behaviour.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's features guide already says a page's maturity level changes only through a reviewed pull request (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-066).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants notification's late flag is set once, at its first submission from draft, and the confirmation page, the read-only view and the list card read the stored value; a resubmission after an amendment moves the submitted date and leaves the flag alone, and a cancelled amendment restores the snapshot carrying it.
requirements.why: Lateness is judged against the timing the trader was held to when they first notified, so recomputing it from a later submission would change a recorded fact about a submitted notification.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the late flag a stored system value committed immediately before submitting while the notification is a draft, and read back rather than recomputed (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-018, repo-plantsfrontend-p17-025).

requirements.statement: Every label, hint, option text and error message on a high-risk plants page lives in its own feature's copy pair, and a display-shaped key in the obligation model stops the service starting.
requirements.why: One home for the words means a wording change is a copy change, and the boot guard makes the rule enforceable rather than a convention a change can quietly break.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's obligation-model guide and its boot guards already hold this: obligations carry no display copy and the purity check fails the server start (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-053, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-054, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-263-m1), and user-facing text lives in each feature's English and Welsh copy modules (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-071).

requirements.statement: A string added to or changed on a high-risk plants page lands in both its feature's English and Welsh copy files with the same leaf paths and value kinds, the Welsh a machine draft headed as unreviewed with no Welsh invented, and the copy-convention and copy-parity checks run over every pair.
requirements.why: The service owes a Welsh version it cannot yet publish, so every string is captured in both files as it is written rather than retrofitted when a translator arrives.
requirements.deltaNote: Every templated plants feature already needs both copy files of the same shape under the parity and convention checks, with machine-drafted Welsh marked as not reviewed by a translator (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-072, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-190, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-277).

requirements.statement: A number more than one high-risk plants feature shows, such as a timing window or a length limit, is written once as a named constant and reaches the copy as a function argument.
requirements.why: A reissued policy paper then changes one constant rather than every sentence that quotes it, and no second copy of the number can drift.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's features guide already keeps a value more than one feature reads in a cross-feature constant module and passes numbers to copy functions as arguments (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-060, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-074).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page reached from the overview ends with Save and continue and its own save-and-return control side by side as the only buttons in one button group, with its cancel link on its own line below the group; a page reached from another page ends with the primary button alone.
requirements.why: A trader sent from the overview can stop and go back to it from where they were sent, while a sub-page leaves the way the trader came in.
requirements.deltaNote: The shared save-actions partial already owns how every plants page ends, in that order, and a test holds the order (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-075, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-212).

requirements.statement: While a high-risk plants notification is being amended, every page except check your answers ends exactly as it does on a draft, and the status strip shows the Amend status with its Cancel amend link.
requirements.why: A trader amending a notification is doing the same work as a trader filling in a draft, so the page behaves the same way and only the strip says which it is.
requirements.deltaNote: A plants test already renders every task-row page in both states and fails if their endings differ (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-324).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page answers a validation failure with HTTP 400, one error summary titled "There is a problem" carrying a link per field error, an "Error:" prefix on the page title, the message beside each field, and the trader's own answers kept.
requirements.why: A trader who gets something wrong sees what to fix without losing what they typed, and the status code tells a monitor the request was refused.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants already answers every validation failure with a 400 rather than the live animals mixture of 200s (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-072).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is built from GOV.UK Frontend and Ministry of Justice Frontend components and utility classes only, with no hand-rolled component and no custom CSS.
requirements.why: A tested government component is accessible and maintained, and a bespoke one has to be proved from scratch every time it changes.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's recipes already render every field with GOV.UK and MoJ macros inside the govuk-frontend toolbox and prefer server-rendered controls (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-276, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-333, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-102).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is checked for accessibility on its first render and on its validation-error state against the five rule sets covering WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 A and AA, failing on any serious or critical violation, and no page narrows that list.
requirements.why: The machine-checkable 2.1 and 2.2 rules only run when their tags are asked for, and a page allowed to narrow the list would hide the very rules the service is held to.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants fit harness already builds its check with the five tags, so the ruling and the code agree (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-174).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page is audited by Lighthouse from a registered route the seeding step can reach, under a report name no other route claims, on a seed shape whose own categories admit its country of origin, and the floors stay a performance score of 0.60 and accessibility and best-practices scores of 0.70 with no search-engine assertion.
requirements.why: A page whose prerequisites are unmet redirects and would silently audit the overview instead, and a lowered floor hides the regression it was put there to catch.
requirements.deltaNote: The audit's targets step, its route-derived URL list and the three floors are already in the repository (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-236, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-243, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-246).

requirements.statement: A change to the high-risk plants journey ends with the set test run, the whole-repo test run, the format check, the lint run and the feature browser suite green, and the whole-journey browser suite too when the change touches the whole journey or the shared browser helpers.
requirements.why: The set run does not cover composition, dispatch, the fulfilment registry or the copy checks, so a green set run alone can hide a broken journey.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's testing guide already names those runs, and green already means every command exits zero with a suite that matched files (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-233, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-234).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page carries browser coverage of its first render, a happy-path save and redirect, persistence on reload, every validation rule, the answers kept after an error, every error-summary link moving focus, Back, Save and return, Cancel and Change navigation, the purge when an answer leaves scope, its check-answers rows and its overview row states.
requirements.why: A change to a page's wording, layout or controls can break any of those without failing a unit test, so the page's own browser spec is where the change is proved.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's recipes already require that list of a page's and a feature group's browser specs (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-325, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-345).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants page's Back link goes to the place the trader came from, carried on the link or the form rather than held in the session, falling back to the overview, to the dashboard on the first page until an answer is entered, and to the notification list on a submitted notification's review.
requirements.why: A trader who arrived from the overview, a Change link, a list card or the type question expects Back to return there, and a trail held in the session would get it wrong in a second tab.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants flow guide already holds this rule: Back is carried on the page's links and form posts, the session holds no record of how a notification was started, and a trail naming an unknown place falls back as described (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-106, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-125, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-140).

requirements.statement: A new high-risk plants page joins the journey's one page order and its task row, is filed in the caption map or listed there as bare, and is registered in the dispatch and routes barrels, its binding bundle and its review card.
requirements.why: Each of those registrations is checked at boot or by a test, so a page that misses one either fails to start the service or renders without its caption, its row or its review card.
requirements.deltaNote: The set's recipes already limit a new page's registration to those five steps, with a coverage test failing until the caption decision is made either way (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-338, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-304).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants overview takes its groups from the journey's flow sections in order and appends the check-and-submit group, and a task row groups pages for submit readiness and decides nothing about where Save and continue goes.
requirements.why: Keeping the page order and the overview's grouping separate means a change to one does not silently move the other.
requirements.deltaNote: The set keeps feature group, flow section and task row as three separate things and derives the overview's groups from the sections (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-326, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-123).

requirements.statement: Save and return to overview on a high-risk plants page makes the same checks as Save and continue and changes only where a valid save goes.
requirements.why: Two buttons that save the same page must either both accept an answer or both refuse it, or a trader can save past a check by choosing the other button.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants records already describe it that way: Save and return to overview commits the page and opens the overview whichever page it is pressed on, under the same page-level checks as Save and continue (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-061, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-106).

requirements.statement: An answer on a high-risk plants notification that leaves scope is purged and never restored, scope is worked out afresh on every read and write rather than stored, and a page whose every question is out of scope is passed over by Save and continue.
requirements.why: A notification must hold only what its consignment needs, so an answer kept out of sight would be submitted as part of a record the trader was never shown.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants ledger already rules the wipe and the fresh evaluation on every read and write (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-062, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-103).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants place-of-destination or consignor picker lists its own role's addresses together with any address saved with no role, and the consignment contact picker asks for no role and lists every address in the book.
requirements.why: An address saved before the record carried roles would otherwise be invisible to the picker that needs it, and the contact can be any address the organisation holds.
requirements.deltaNote: Each plants picker already narrows the organisation's book to its own role plus any address saved with no role, and the stub book holds one such record to prove it (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-009, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-225).

requirements.statement: A high-risk plants picker stores a copy of the record it picks, a later address-book edit or deletion never changes the notification, and a copied address that breaks the address rules makes check your answers refuse Continue and the declaration refuse Submit.
requirements.why: A submitted notification must say what the trader saw when they submitted it, while an address that can no longer be saved must not be carried into a submission unnoticed.
requirements.deltaNote: Plants already copies the chosen record onto the notification, refuses an id the book no longer holds, throws on an address-book outage rather than reading it as a deletion, and lists copied-address errors on the review (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-011, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-016, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-017, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-092).

requirements.statement: The organisation whose address book a high-risk plants picker reads comes only from the verified session, never from the submitted form.
requirements.why: Otherwise a trader could reach another organisation's addresses by posting an identifier.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants specification already records that the organisation is taken only from the verified session (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-079-m1).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the behaviours its own specification records: its entry guard, its one page order, its save-and-return and Back rules, its scope purge, its two-page commodity collection, its own session cookies, its lenient page validation, its four system-populated values, its layout chrome and its boot guards.
requirements.why: They are the platform behaviour every plants page is built on, so a look-and-feel change is made inside them rather than against them.
requirements.deltaNote: The specification's behaviours block already holds all of them (repo-plantsfrontend-p15-060 to repo-plantsfrontend-p15-171), and the entry guard the backlog extras record as inert already redirects to the commodity type page in the code (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-189).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the data, validation and behaviour its own decisions ledger and conflicts register have settled: its commodity vocabulary and lists, the per-category origin narrowing, the per-line fields and their formats, the arrival matters, the identification numbers, the single contact pick, the declaration statements, the reference number, the four-value status vocabulary and the two timing windows.
requirements.why: Those decisions rest on the plants statute and policy paper rather than on any design, so a change made for look and feel leaves them exactly as they are.
requirements.deltaNote: The 97 ledger entries and the 40 register entries already hold these decisions, each subject carrying a pointer to the entry that settled it, and the rulings that describe submission name the same submit step the engine calls (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-001, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-009, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-188).

requirements.statement: A change to the high-risk plants frontend follows the set's own served-surface reference and its obligation-model, features, flow-and-gates, services, limits, copy-status, testing and Lighthouse guides, and its four recipes for adding a field, a page, a section and a collection.
requirements.why: The guides and recipes are how a plants change is made in that repository's conventions, and a change made some other way fails a boot guard, a convention test or a coverage test rather than merging quietly.
requirements.deltaNote: The set already carries the reference, the eight guides and the four recipes, with boot guards and coverage tests behind them (repo-plantsfrontend-p18-023-m1, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-287, repo-plantsfrontend-p18-338).

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants set's own engineering-hygiene increments stay the plants team's work: its continuous-integration parity and workflow fixes, the multi-architecture and non-gating-audit publish changes, the Lighthouse scripts, the dependency-update configuration, the architecture-lint baseline, the removal of the unused platform services, the collection exemplars, the documentation-drift sweep, the unauthorised view's copy and the dashboard's empty submitted date.
requirements.why: The goal is what a user sees in the journeys that exist, and the set's own build hygiene lies outside it; most of these are in any case done in the code since the ledger recorded them (the Lighthouse scripts and workflow, the end-to-end, arm64, concurrency, security-audit, weekly, SonarCloud and FIT workflow changes, and a generated Dependabot configuration that departs from the recorded ESLint policy), and the end-to-end increments' recorded assertions, such as a picker paging at five, are the plants team's to refresh.

requirements.statement: The drift between the high-risk plants set's records and its code stays as it stands wherever this programme changes neither: entries recording work already done, the entry-guard entry describing a condition the code does not have, the recipes and guides calling registration modules, the sections folder and the evaluation barrel empty when they hold five sections, seven task rows, seven section modules and ten bindings, and the guides that disagree with each other about the flow-only keys and the captioned sections.
requirements.why: This programme keeps true the records of what it changes and no more; the owner has already declined one such tidy-up, and the rest is the plants team's own hygiene.

requirements.statement: The high-risk plants records' structural gaps stay as they are: the conflicts register has no state for an unsettled disagreement, no entry says who may reopen a ruling or on what evidence, the parked questions have no owner and no date, the panel evidence names no judge or chair and does not say which ledger entry each of its rulings became, and three of the five standing rulings are nowhere stated in their own words.
requirements.why: This programme keeps its own open questions and decisions in its own records, and the plants panel's evidence belongs to the work that produced it.

requirements.statement: The questions the high-risk plants set has parked stay parked: users, sign-in models, agents, delegation and plant-operator registration; internal-user login; bulk upload and importing from existing documents; regulator, inspector and analyst screens; list maintenance, risk classification and spot-check scheduling; document uploads; the outbox and event publishing; a combined animals and plants list; competent-authority routing; the notification reference's type-code prefix; the service name, feedback address and helpdesk lines; guidance and a before-you-start page; the previous scheme and the Northern Irish and Irish precedents; the lawful basis, privacy notice and retention period; a live Welsh service; a meaning for "sustainable"; and parity of internal access.
requirements.why: Each waits on a policy answer nobody has or on capability nobody is building, and the goal is the look and feel of the journeys that exist.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area's working set that state one plants page's own content, questions, options, hints or error messages are weighed in that page's area: the commodity type and commodity pages, origin, arrival status and arrival details, place of destination, the consignor and contact pickers, the identification numbers, the overview, check your answers, the declaration, the confirmation, the notification list, and the delete and cancel-amendment pages.
requirements.why: Each page's area reads the same claims against the plants code and the design, and one requirement per difference a user can see belongs there rather than in the record of what the set has settled.
