requirements.statement: The high-risk plants journey keeps the four decisions its ledger has already landed in the code: no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and no contact-details page, so the contact section is the one address-book pick; the commodity-type save keeps the lines the new type allows, counts the rest as removed and opens the commodities list with that count; the declaration carries its three plants statements, the last covering failing to notify, notifying late and giving incorrect details; and the arrival-status page asks whether the consignment has arrived in Great Britain.
requirements.why: A change made for the look of a page must not quietly undo a decision the set has already built, and these four are the ones where the ledger and the code have been checked against each other.
requirements.deltaNote: Each was checked against the code and found in place: the obligations manifest holds no use, contact-number or contact-email obligation and there is no contact-details feature folder; the commodity-type controller reconciles and redirects with the removed count; the declaration copy holds the three statements; and the arrival-status copy asks about Great Britain (repo-plantsfrontend-p16-178, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-179, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-180, repo-plantsfrontend-p16-181).

requirements.statement: A journey page is told where the trader came from by the trail the service writes into the page's own address: the places already saved, newest last, named in the service's own words (the dashboard, the overview, the Import Notification Service and the review page). The trail shortens by one as Back is followed, is dropped when it names a place the journey does not have, and carries through a page's own in-page actions.
requirements.why: The return and Back rules need a context the service can read on a page it serves by URL. The save and continue work that has since merged writes that trail in both frontends, which the 9 October ruling's wording did not foresee; whether it stays is an open question (c-451).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-002, repo-tests-p8-005 and repo-tests-p8-012: a live animals journey page's address already carries the places the trader came by as a comma-separated trail, newest last, starting from the overview, the dashboard or the Import Notification Service; repo-plantsfrontend-p14-002 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-016: plants carries the same trail and shortens it as Back is followed; repo-plantsfrontend-p14-109: a page opened straight by its address carries none.

requirements.statement: A trader who opens a journey page before the answers it needs have been given is offered the page that asks for the earliest missing one instead, with the page they asked for and every missing answer recorded, and the page they came from kept so Back returns to it. The answers a later page is held back for are the country of origin and at least one commodity line in the animals sets, and the commodity type and the country of origin in the plants set; an answer whose own page comes later in the journey never holds an earlier page back.
requirements.why: A notification's pages are reachable by URL, so a page whose earlier answers are missing must offer somewhere that works rather than render half a journey. Both frontends already do this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p1-061 to repo-frontend-p1-063: the two enforced answers, the redirect to the page that asks for the earliest missing one, and the record of the page asked for with every missing answer; repo-plantsfrontend-p2-088 and repo-plantsfrontend-p2-089: plants does the same and keeps the page the trader was on on the trail.

requirements.statement: A page whose question does not apply to the consignment is not shown: opening it by its own address shows the page that owns the choice instead, and a save posted to it after the choice has changed is not taken.
requirements.why: A notification's pages are reachable by URL and a trader can leave one open while the answer that brings it into scope changes, so an out-of-scope page must send the trader somewhere that applies rather than collect an answer the notification does not want. Both frontends already do this.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p4-011 and repo-tests-p4-012: the transit countries page shows the overview instead when no means of transport, Air or Sea is saved, and a country added on a page left open after the means changed is not saved; repo-tests-p4-019 and repo-tests-p4-054: the CPH number page shows the addresses page and the identification page shows the commodity selection page; repo-plantsfrontend-p12-017: a plants picker whose question does not apply redirects to the overview.

The section keeps its number and the overview row keeps its hint.

A notification whose every task is complete still reads 'Draft' until it is submitted.

The end-to-end suite proves the hand-over in the local Docker stack and the continuous-integration Docker stack; no new check of it is built for CDP.

requirements.statement: Every page of the animals, plants and INS frontends carries a page-maturity banner, a GOV.UK phase banner directly under the Alpha one and above the Back link, saying how settled the page's design is. The four states read 'Exploring' ('This page is an early idea. It may change a lot or be removed.'), 'Detailing' ('We're keeping this page. We're still working out the detail.'), 'Agreed' ('Users and the business have agreed this page. Changes need a reason.') and 'Ready for live' ('This page is ready for live.'), with an orange, purple, teal or green tag and the banner row behind it in the same colour at a lighter tint. A page declares its level in its feature's page descriptor, which travels with its route, and a page that declares none shows as Exploring. A screen reader hears 'This page's status:' before the tag and a full stop after it. The banner is left off an error page and off any route that carries no page descriptor, the whole banner can be switched off for an environment and is on by default, and its prefix and all four states have Welsh copy with the same keys as the English ('Statws y dudalen hon:', 'Archwilio', 'Manylu', 'Cytunwyd' and 'Yn barod i fynd yn fyw').
requirements.why: The maturity banner is how a reader of a page can tell whether its design is settled, which the prototype has no way to express and says nothing about. It already exists on both journey frontends and nothing in the target design or the rulings removes it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-071-m1, p2-072 to p2-077 and p2-157 give the banner on animals, its states, colours, screen-reader prefix, where it is left off, its switch and its Welsh copy; repo-plantsfrontend-p13-018 and p13-035 put it between the phase banner and the Back link on plants; repo-insfrontend-p1-022, p1-053 and p1-068 to p1-079 give the same banner on the INS frontend, its sign-in pages at Exploring.

requirements.statement: A page shows its banners before anything else in its content column, in one order: the recoverable-error banner first, then the stale-notification banner, then the notification's status strip, then the page's own content. A page may also open with a green success banner carrying its own title and message.
requirements.why: The order is what makes a trader read the problem before the page, and it is the same on both journey frontends today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p13-101 gives the order on plants, repo-insfrontend-p1-027-m1 the recoverable banner above the journey strip on INS, and repo-frontend-p2-021, p2-022 and p2-023 the same three banners and strip on animals, with the green success banner in repo-frontend-p2-026.

requirements.statement: A refusal is recorded once in the service's logs with the notification id, the route and the keys of the fields refused, never the messages the trader was shown; a refusal that is not the trader's own correctable input also records any reason or ids it turned on. A save that fails on a backend error the trader can wait out is recorded once with the notification id and the failure, and the page answers with its own fallback. A save refused because the notification changed is recorded once with the notification id and the concurrency token the page posted. A save that opens the page asking for a missing earlier answer instead of the next page is recorded once with the page saved, the page opened and the missing answers. A trail or return marker naming anywhere the journey does not have is recorded once a request as a warning, cut to at most 200 characters of what was received, and a page's own named fallback for Back records nothing.
requirements.why: A support request is answered from the log, so the log carries the ids support searches by and never a trader's answers or the words they were shown.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-050, p2-154, p2-155, p2-057 and p2-059 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-064, p13-096, p13-098, p13-099, p13-075, p13-075-m1 and p13-079 log each case once; the animals frontend logs the recoverable fallback at info (repo-frontend-p2-154) and plants at warning (repo-plantsfrontend-p13-064), a level no user sees. The INS frontend logs a failed service call once (repo-insfrontend-p1-149).

requirements.statement: The service shows no pop-up or dialog of its own in the shared chrome: every message a page gives is a banner, an error summary, an inline message or a hidden live region, and a confirmation, cancelling an amendment included, is its own page at its own address. A control that posts can be shown as a link, in the GOV.UK link colours including hover and active, so an action that needs a form still reads as a link; the shared remove action is such a button inside the page's form, its visible text followed by visually hidden text naming the item it removes.
requirements.why: The owner's 9 October afternoon ruling says pop-ups are not built and a confirmation stays a page, and the interaction designer's 9 November answers make amend and cancel amendment their own pages rather than dialogs over the page behind them. Both journey frontends already work this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-151 shows the shared chrome has no pop-up or dialog, p2-025 the Cancel amend link to its own page, and p2-113, p2-166 and p2-167 the posting controls shown as links; the rulings keep it that way (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-078, ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-021 to p1-023), and the Ministry of Justice modal is not an accepted component (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-040).

requirements.statement: On the animals and plants frontends a list a trader pages through starts at page 1, and a page number in the address that is not a whole number of 1 or more is ignored rather than refused. Previous and Next controls are shown only when the list runs to more than one page, Previous left off the first page and Next off the last, each taking its words from the list's own copy and linking to the page before or after through the list's own link builder. The shared paging helper holds no default page size and no upper or lower bound on one: it takes the page and the number of pages already worked out, so each list sets its own size.
requirements.why: Pagination is kept everywhere, so every list needs the same shared controls, while how many rows a page holds is each list's own answer rather than a shared default.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-125 to p2-127 and p2-176 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-070 to p13-072 give the shared paging rules on both journey frontends, and repo-frontend-p15-041 and p15-044 show a party picker applying them. The owner's 25 November ruling keeps pagination everywhere (ruling-ian-2026-11-25-p1-002, p1-007); each list's own page size and how its controls look are weighed where that list is weighed.

requirements.statement: Shared styles that reach no page are not relied on and are safe to remove: the extra spacing set for a main content wrapper whose class no template carries, and the link style that hides the underline until hover that nothing uses.
requirements.why: These are dead rules in today's stylesheet, not differences from the target design. They go to the report so a reader does not take them for live styling.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-152 and p2-153 record the two unreachable style rules. The notification list's own Previous and Next styles do reach a page (repo-frontend-p2-118) and are weighed with that list.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's visual-regression suite guards rendered composition: layout, spacing, colour and typography as the user sees a page, by comparing screenshots against committed baselines and failing when pixels differ outside the masked regions. Every spec carries the @visual tag and forces a headless browser for itself, because headed mode uses the operating system's own font rendering; on macOS the browser is launched with always-shown scroll bars and a coarse pointer so a Mac shot matches the Linux baseline. Each shot is committed twice, once for each platform, and both are regenerated when a visual change is intended, the Linux ones from a container that reaches the stack by its host name; regeneration can be narrowed to one spec or title, or write only missing baselines. A shot is taken at 1280 by 1000 pixels unless the test resizes the viewport. Content that moves with the clock or the run is pinned: a full-page shot of a notification page masks the whole status strip rather than the reference alone, so the masked box stays a fixed size, while the notification view and declaration shots overwrite the reference number and the dates with fixed text; a calendar shot stops the browser clock on a fixed day and moves the served earliest and latest dates by the same number of days. Only the animals and plants domains have visual specs.
requirements.why: A change to shared page chrome is exactly what this suite exists to catch, so every chrome change either keeps the baselines or regenerates both platforms' baselines in the same increment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p11-001 to p11-010 and p16-096 to p16-105 define the suite, its dual baselines, its headless and macOS rules, its viewport and its masks; repo-tests-p16-102 and p16-102-m1 give the regeneration commands and how to narrow them.

requirements.statement: Which pages and states the visual suite pins, and its coverage gaps, are weighed where those pages are weighed: the origin page on first load and with its region code revealed, the import reason page in its transhipment, transit, temporary admission, error and no-JavaScript states, the arrival details page, the transited countries page empty and with one country, the identification card, the accompanying documents page with one scanned document, the consignor picker's search row, the arrival date picker's button at rest, hovered and focused and its calendar opened by mouse and by keyboard, the overview's totals, the notification view of a ready draft at desktop width down to the Consignment addresses card, the refused review at desktop and phone width and the declaration. No baseline covers the germinal-products set, the notification list, the confirmation page, the commodity pages, the address book or the INS front door, and the review has a desktop baseline but no phone one.
requirements.why: Each baseline pins one page's own composition, so the page's area weighs it against the target design; the missing baselines are gaps in today's suite rather than differences from the design, and go to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p11-011 to p11-036, p11-109 and p11-110 list the baselines, and p11-103 and p11-104 the gaps.

requirements.statement: The tests repo has exactly two targets, the deployed services and the docker-compose stack, one config file each, extending one shared config that holds the projects, the reporters, one retry and a trace on the first retry with a screenshot only on failure. One default project, chromium, runs every domain, and five opt-in projects run only when named: branded Chrome, Firefox, WebKit, an emulated iPhone 17 and an emulated Pixel 10. The four desktop projects render at 1280 by 1000 and the two mobile ones take their device's viewport. A deployed run gives each test 60 seconds and each expectation 15 seconds because each page load is a real network hop, a compose run keeps Playwright's defaults, and a test that needs longer sets its own through a helper that leaves a debug run untimed. Each flow step waits up to 30 seconds for its page's heading so a transient gateway error fails the step that hit it and names the page. Tests run fully in parallel, a run on CI refuses a test marked only, and how many browsers run at once is capped by a setting that takes a whole number or a percentage and stops the run with both accepted forms when it is anything else. Every run refuses to start against production, a missing service base URL or a domain with no base URL stops the run naming what was missing, a compose run from a workspace clone that does not own the stack stops before the first test unless told to carry on, a compose preflight fails fast when the animals frontend, backend or admin does not answer its health check, and a containerised compose run adds a host-resolver rule so the stack's localhost redirects resolve. Local service ports and deployed per-service subdomains are fixed; a laptop run against a deployed environment names the environment, and its back-end calls go through the protected gateway with a developer API key over the department's VPN; calls that leave the platform for the internet go through the platform proxy, while journey and service calls stay direct.
requirements.why: Any new end-to-end, accessibility or visual proof runs under these settings, and a change that needs a new route, port or longer budget has to be made here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-025 to p16-033 and p16-068 to p16-078 give the configs, the projects, the timeouts, the retries and the guards; p16-060 to p16-067-m1 the addresses of every service on both targets; p16-197 the compose preflight and p16-152 the proxy rule.

requirements.statement: The tests repo is run by named scripts, one per suite and target, and by a profile on the deployed platform. Against the deployed services there are end-to-end, accessibility, Dynamics, cross-browser, BrowserStack, passive-security and active-security scripts, and against the compose stack end-to-end, accessibility, visual, cross-browser, BrowserStack, passive-security and active-security scripts plus a CI script for the workspace stack job; each excludes the type tags it does not run, and only the compose security scripts run the gate. Per-domain copies limit a run to that domain's own directory and are named to match the platform's profiles; a dash in the per-domain table means that domain has no specs of that test type yet. A deployed run picks its suite with a profile value, an unset profile running the default; a profile can be prefixed with a domain; a profile for a test type the domain has no specs of fails as no tests found, one whose directory does not exist stops the container naming the directory, and an unknown profile stops it listing every allowed value and domain, while the domain prefix never reaches the test runner. An active-security profile asked for on the deployed platform is refused, recorded in a failure marker and answered with a report page saying the profile only runs against the compose stack. A run that exits non-zero has its reason appended to that marker and the container exits 1 printing it; a security profile publishes the scan's report directory with the scan's own summary as its index and skips the Allure step, while every other profile publishes the Playwright report, copying it to the configured object store with a zip of its results, failing when the path is unset or the report is missing, and exiting with the publish step's code if publishing fails. A run can be narrowed with the runner's own parameters, and the report is opened or generated by its own commands.
requirements.why: A new suite, domain or test type has to be reachable by one of these scripts or profiles, and a chrome change that breaks a run shows up through this entrypoint.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-002-m1 to p16-024, p16-275 and p16-276 list the scripts and what each leaves out, and p16-135 to p16-151 with p16-136-m1 and p16-148-m1 the deployed profiles, their refusals and how each publishes its report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo holds end-to-end, accessibility and security tests for the animals frontend, its admin portal, the high-risk plants frontend and the INS front door with the address book, in four domains, each a functional area served by one or more services. A domain is selected by the directory its specs live in, which also gives them their base URL; a spec outside a known domain directory stops the run naming the four. Within a domain, specs are grouped as accessibility, end-to-end (with feature, page, journey and visual sub-folders) and security folders, but a folder only organises: the test type is selected by one of five tags and a suite is a domain's directory or one test type within it, each path ending in a slash because the runner reads it as a regular expression. A service tag is a different thing: it names a service whose pull request should also run the spec, whatever its test type or domain, and eight are recognised, each belonging to the domains that already run it by path. Linting fails a spec whose tags disagree with its test-type directory, and one that carries the service tag of a service whose pull request already runs its domain by path; the check asks the runner to list the tests so it reads the tags a test really has, names each offending test by file, line and title, and otherwise reports how many it checked. A further tag marks an end-to-end spec whose behaviour a frontend's own suite also proves.
requirements.why: A new spec has to sit in the right domain and carry the right tags, or the lint fails it and the pull-request runs either miss it or run it everywhere.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-079 to p16-092 give the domains, the folders, the five type tags, the eight service tags and the lint that enforces them; p16-001 the four services the suite covers.

requirements.statement: A spec in the tests repo is written to the suite's own conventions. It reaches a page through a named step in its domain's journey file rather than its own clicks, and a sequence two tests share becomes such a step with the local copies deleted; a flow or page object holds no assertion and an assertion two specs share lives in a shared checks module; a journey spec is never seeded, seeding being only for the set-up of a one-page assertion; test data is copied from real canned data and never invented, and a value that has a home is imported rather than retyped; answers are plain data apart from the steps that drive the pages, in named mandatory and full sets, and a spec starts from a set and overrides single values rather than changing the steps. A spec asserts which page is open through the page object's own URL pattern, opens a page on a trail through the page object, and never types a trail itself. Support code sits in named folders for specs, flows, page objects, domain constants, fixtures, adapters, canned data and cross-domain helpers, and shared code may not import a domain's page objects, flows or constants. A test title says what its assertions prove and a test must fail without the change it covers; a name predicts its return value and side effects and one concept has one name. A comment describes only the lines below it and only where a name cannot, the code carries no history, and a spec carries no ticket key, backlog or ruling id, release name or tracking wording in a comment, a title or a tag: the lint fails it and tells the author to say what the code does, or what the assertions prove, instead. A catch that drops its error is refused, as is an error or warning logged with only a string while a caught error is in scope; the lint also runs type-checked rules and refuses a floating promise. A test run is redirected to a file rather than piped. Lint, the formatting check and the type check run before a commit, with a pre-commit hook on the staged files.
requirements.why: Every new proof is reviewed against these rules, and the ban on ticket keys, release names and ruling ids in a spec is why a requirement's words have to say what the behaviour is rather than which decision produced it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-209 to p16-229 give the lint rules and the code-quality conventions, p16-094, p16-094-m1 and p16-095 how a spec asserts a page and where a shared assertion lives, and p16-218 to p16-226 the folder layout and the answer sets.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's cross-browser set is existing end-to-end specs selected by one tag, with no specs of their own in the cross-browser folders, run in branded Chrome, the runner's Firefox and WebKit builds, an emulated iPhone 17 and an emulated Pixel 10, against the deployed services or the compose stack, one project at a time by naming the project with an equals sign and adding the tag filter, because a named project without it would run every test. On a hosted device service the tagged tests run in real Edge on Windows 11 and the runner's WebKit on the newest macOS, and a second tag selects short single-context flows for real Safari on the two current iOS versions, on an iPhone 18 Pro and an iPhone 17; a test keeps that tag only if it passes on both iPhones, and on a hosted run a test without its platform's tag is skipped naming the tag. A test is tagged only if it runs against the deployed services and renders a page the set does not already cover, chosen so that together the set renders as many pages as possible in each engine, preferring a journey walk and then one test per page the walks do not reach, and leaving out validation, back-end, visual, accessibility and security specs; a tagged test still runs in the default run. The animals and INS domains have cross-browser commands and the admin domain has none. Real Android browsers, real Firefox, real macOS Safari and Chrome on Windows and macOS are deliberately not covered, real Android being checked by hand before a release; branded Chrome ships only in the amd64 image. On the hosted service session reuse is off because a real iPhone allows one browser context, each run uses one session per processor up to the team limit, the local tunnel cannot open localhost from Safari or WebKit so those platforms run only against the deployed services, network logs and the service's own accessibility checking are off, credentials come only from the environment and a run stops before starting if either credential or every platform is missing; the hosted service is not run from GitHub Actions. On an iPhone user agent the accessible autocomplete adds a hidden position counter, so a spec must not assume a fixed viewport. The set is reviewed against the government's browser guidance when that list changes, a new iOS or macOS arrives, Windows 11 reaches end of support or the runner is upgraded.
requirements.why: A page that changes keeps or earns its cross-browser tag under these rules, and the shared chrome is what every tagged test renders.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-277 to p16-298 give the projects, the hosted platforms and their tags and rules, and what is deliberately left out; p16-171 to p16-193 how a test is chosen and run. The accessible autocomplete adds a hidden position counter on an iPhone user agent (repo-tests-p16-183).

requirements.statement: The tests repo's Dynamics integration checks, which prove a submitted notification reaches a domain's Dynamics instance through the Dataverse Web API, stand as they are: they run only through their own profile, are left out of every other run, skip on the compose stack, read their settings by function rather than at load so one domain's missing setting cannot fail another's tests, fail at once naming a missing variable and never its value, and are given a longer base timeout; on the deployed platform their calls go through the platform proxy, which must allow the sign-in host and the Dynamics host.
requirements.why: Design and chrome changes reach no Dynamics field, so the programme leaves these checks as they are; they are weighed where notification publishing is weighed, not here.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-153 to p16-162 describe the suite, its profile, its credentials and its timeouts as they stand.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's own build and delivery stand: a test image built on the official runner image with the London time zone, curl, zip, a Java runtime and the cloud CLI, dependencies installed from the lockfile with lifecycle scripts skipped, run as a non-root user, built for one architecture because of that CLI, and carrying a copied security-scanner install with the add-on that needs a browser profile removed. A push to the default branch builds and publishes the image to both registries, tagged with the computed next version and latest, labelled with the repo, the suite name, the build run and the commit, declared as a platform test suite run as a job, and commits the version tag; a pull request publishes a branch image through the workspace's branch-publish workflow with a layer cache the main publish writes. End-to-end tests run in continuous integration through the workspace's reusable workflow, which starts the workspace stack probing for the branch's images and runs the published test image against it, publishing reports; that workflow runs only for a pull request whose image publish succeeded or on manual dispatch with a branch to probe, keeps one run per branch, and reports a pending check and then the result back to the pull request. A pull request also runs the formatting check, the lint and the type check, and the same job runs weekly. The dependency audit is a separate job, so a newly published advisory does not gate the merge or block the pull request carrying the fix, and every allowlist entry must carry an advisory id, be active, give a reason and an owner and have a real expiry no more than three months away, an expired entry failing the check. The suite runs on its pinned runtime, is driven by its pinned test runner with the accessibility, reporting, device-service, database, queue and audit clients it declares, keeps non-secret settings in the platform's app config and credentials as platform secrets, clears its previous results and saved sessions at the start of a run, can seed a notification from a script of its own, documents the four workspace commands that start, build, stop and rebuild the stack, publishes its reports and cleans them up when a pull request closes, and is licensed under the Open Government Licence version 3 with its attribution kept.
requirements.why: A chrome change that breaks a run is caught by these checks, and an increment that adds a route or a fixture has to keep the image, the workflows and the audit green.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-194 to p16-208 give the image, the publishes and the workflows, p16-203 and p16-204 the audit's own rules, p16-264-m1 where settings and secrets live, and p16-265 to p16-271 the pinned runtime, dependencies, seeding script and stack commands.

requirements.statement: Documentation drift and housekeeping defects in the tests repo stand as they are: the run table that leaves out the two deployed security scripts; the accessibility documentation and the accessibility folder's README, which name no conformance standard, no viewport, no list of pages that must be scanned and no run command; the per-domain and profile tables that do not say whether the plants and admin domains' missing suites are planned or deliberately out of scope; the attacking plan's out-of-date note that the upload identifier is never reached; the security report's title, which names the animals service although the report covers six services; and the absence of any decisions ledger, so the only rulings the repo carries are the ones its prose states.
requirements.why: These are documentation and housekeeping defects in today's suite, not differences from the target design, so the programme does not fix them. They go to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-012-m1, p16-272 to p16-274, p10-152, p11-072, p11-107 and p11-108 record the drift as it stands. The excluded-tag list, the runtime prerequisite and the exclusion table's selector names now agree with the code (repo-tests-p16-002-m1, p16-265, p15-132), so they are no longer listed.

requirements.statement: A notification belongs to the organisation that created it, and a signed-in user of another organisation reaches none of it. Opening a notification's page by its address shows the standard 404 Page not found page, which leaks neither its Overview heading nor its reference number; on the backend API, reading a submitted notification's fulfilments is refused with 403, every change to a notification (amend, save, submit, copy, soft delete and cancel amend) is refused with 404, and listing notifications by a reference the organisation does not own returns no rows rather than a refusal. The organisation a request acts for is carried on the backend API in its own header.
requirements.why: Organisation scoping is a real authorisation constraint the prototype cannot express, and it is what makes the shared error page the right answer to another organisation's address. It already works and is proven with a real second sign-in.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-082 to p6-089 prove the refusals, the header that carries the organisation and the second sign-in the proof uses, and repo-frontend-p2-179 binds the signed-in organisation to every animals request.

requirements.statement: The animals admin portal's own pages are weighed where the admin portal is weighed, not with the journey services' shared chrome: that a notification submitted in the animals journey is listed there and can be found by its reference, that it reads notifications through the animals backend so finding one there proves the journey app and the admin app agree, and that its replay-all and delete-all banners show only once its call to the gateway has succeeded, which is how its dead-letter specs prove the two are wired together.
requirements.why: The admin portal is a separate internal interface with its own chrome and its own area; this area covers the shared chrome of the journey frontends and the INS front door.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p6-090 and p6-091 record the admin portal's own proof as it stands.

requirements.statement: An end-to-end proof that creates an address or a transporter follows the suite's own rules for shared state. Every name it creates carries a timestamp or unique suffix so a search finds only that run's record, and the accessibility walks that add a transporter in parallel give it a name no other running test uses; the address-book fixtures delete every address and transporter they created when the test ends, pass or fail and on every retry, logging a failed delete with the record's id without failing the test; a transporter saved through the user interface is deleted only if the spec tracks it by name, and an address added on the add-address page or through the cross-service hand-off is not deleted at all. The shared journey addresses are seeded in global set-up through its own client so no test's clean-up removes them, and a spec that edits or deletes an address makes its own record instead; a record whose country is a name rather than a listed code is the one way, through the services alone, to copy an address the notification refuses. Because the book is shared and never wiped locally, a spec that counts rows searches for a token only its own run created or writes to an organisation whose book starts empty; because the picker lists records newest first and other workers are adding records, a spec that needs a record off page one creates enough newer records to fill page one and then follows Next until its record shows. On the deployed environments addresses expire about seven days after they are created where that is switched on, and the compose stack switches it off. A reset script brings a deployed environment's shared organisation back to a small known state, soft-deleting only records whose name matches a name a test creates, keeping the seeded journey addresses and the performance suite's records, run from a developer's own machine with their API key and never from continuous integration, reporting and deleting nothing by default, deleting addresses only when told to and transporters only when asked, printing the environment and organisation first, refusing production, and reporting in its dry run how many records it would delete and keep with the deletes by name and the commonest kept names.
requirements.why: The address book the navigation leads to is shared state that every worker reads, so a new proof has to create, name and clean up its records this way or it breaks other specs.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-035 to p16-044 and p16-246-m1 give the fixtures' clean-up and the shared-state rules, and p16-045 to p16-048 the reset script's own guards.

requirements.statement: How a commodity line is named and found in a test is weighed with the commodity pages, not here: the commodity page's tick-box label of scientific name then common name in brackets under a commodity-code heading, with the scientific name alone where reference data holds no common name; that one scientific name can sit under several commodity codes so a line is identified by code as well as name; that the aggregated notification's commodity label uses the first trade line's description; that the stack's reference-data stub answers only the searches saved from it, the first page of results holds 100 entries and only a species a search showed can be saved, so a seeded journey posts the search first; and that each line is named by search term, code, scientific name and common name, a spec building its expected label from that line or, where it needs the live answer, reading it through the reference-data client and handing it to the same helper.
requirements.why: These are the commodity pages' own content and the reference lists behind them, which the commodities area weighs against the target design and the data specification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-049 to p16-052 and p16-051-m1 record the labels, the stub's limits and the line constants as they stand.

requirements.statement: What the end-to-end suite proves about one page's own content or one journey's own answers is weighed in that page's area, not here: that a brand-new notification opens at the origin page with nothing answered, the entry guard admits it on an answer the trader entered, and starting a notification answers origin and opens the overview; the arrival date's window and its unpadded display form and a temporary admission's later exit date; how an accompanying document is added and waited for, and the budgets its list and scan are given; the import reason's conditional purpose; the transporter pages' order, their add forms, where each save lands, and why two tests adding a transporter of the same name can refuse a list's save; the overview's two sets of task rows in their fixed order; the rail, cat and poultry consignments' own answers and where each walk ends; the permanent address page's place in the journey and the holding number answered on the consignment addresses page; what the animals API seed unlocks; a party picker's refusal of a record without the role, its server round trip and how a party's row and a summary card's links and subsections are found; how a species tick box and a transit port of exit are chosen; every named walk a spec starts from; and the admin portal's replay and delete banners that prove it is wired to the gateway.
requirements.why: This area stops at any one page's own content and answers; those pages' areas weigh the same behaviours against the target design and the data specification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-232 to p16-262 and their missed claims record those pages' own behaviour and the suite's facts about them as they stand.

requirements.statement: A plants page that changes in the same increment as its animals twin is proved by the suites the plants domain has.
requirements.why: The owner's rule is that a change to something plants also has changes plants in the same increment, but the plants domain has end-to-end and visual specs only, so what counts as proof for a changed plants page is not settled.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants domain has compose scripts for end-to-end and visual only and none for accessibility or security (repo-tests-p16-018), a plants accessibility profile finds no tests (repo-tests-p16-138), and no attacking spec drives the plants journey (repo-tests-p11-105).

requirements.statement: Every page of every frontend is rendered and usable before any script runs: the service stylesheet loads in the head and the service script loads as a module at the end of the body. The animals stylesheet is built from GOV.UK Frontend plus the Ministry of Justice date picker and search components before the service's own variables, helpers, core, components and partials, and the INS frontend loads the Ministry of Justice frontend for its sub navigation only. Where JavaScript runs, the pages get the GOV.UK button, tick box, error summary, radio, service navigation and skip-link behaviours, the Ministry of Justice date picker, and the service's own enhancements, and nothing else: a behaviour is built from GOV.UK Frontend first, then another tested government library, and otherwise goes back to design. Anything a page can only offer with JavaScript is hidden when the GOV.UK JavaScript has not run, so a trader without it is never shown a control that would do nothing, and nothing a trader needs is shown only by script.
requirements.why: The owner's 9 October afternoon ruling makes every page work fully without JavaScript, with CSS and JavaScript only enhancing a page that already works, and limits the libraries a behaviour may come from. Both journey frontends already load their assets and hide their script-only controls this way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-028, repo-insfrontend-p1-035 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-030 load the stylesheet and the script so a page is usable first, repo-frontend-p2-111, p2-112 and p2-124, repo-insfrontend-p1-143, p1-144 and p1-151 and repo-plantsfrontend-p13-095 list the libraries and hide the script-only controls, and the ruling holds every page to working without JavaScript (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p1-033).

requirements.statement: The shared copy gives one date hint, 'For example, 27/3/2026', and shows 'Not applicable' where an answer does not apply.
requirements.why: These are two strings every page shares rather than each page's own wording, so one change to either changes every page that shows it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-060 and p2-061 give the hint and the words.

requirements.statement: The shared search box, the submitted search, the multi-select search, the transporter filter, the country dialling prefix and the page-specific styling of lists, totals and icon buttons are weighed where the pages that use them are weighed, not with the shared chrome: the autocomplete over a native select with its options, its matching that ignores capitals, accents and surrounding spaces, its bold matched letters, its square blue magnifier hidden from assistive technology, its room for that button, its assistive hint and Welsh announcements, its typography, focus and error borders and its pinned upstream licence; the submitted search's text box with its icon-only submit button, its term shown back, its lack of a clear control and its working without JavaScript; the multi-select search's ticked results, its server-rendered matching, its refresh timing, queueing, kept ticks, focus handling and announcements, its fall back to a plain form post and recovery through browser history, its no-JavaScript update button, its hidden clear cross and its bordered result list with chips and Clear all; the seven long-list fields of the live-animals journey and how each is proven, with and without JavaScript, at phone width and against a real GOV.UK input; the transporter list's in-page filter with its announcements; the prefix that changes with the country; the live region announced a moment after a page loads; and the notification list's filter panel, toolbar, sort row, Previous and Next control and its hover underline, the commodity totals panel, the service's icon button styling, a task row's status staying on one line while a long hint wraps, a table cell holding an unbroken reference breaking rather than widening the table, and the red bar down a summary card with answers still outstanding.
requirements.why: Each of these is one page's own control or one page's own styling, and the pages' areas weigh them against the target design, the owner's ruling that a search box uses the accessible autocomplete with the reference list's own entries, and the rule that the version without JavaScript is built first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-078 to p2-110, p2-138 to p2-150, p2-159 to p2-164, p2-168 to p2-175 and p2-089-m1 record the search controls and their proof as they stand, and p2-117 to p2-123, p2-177 and p2-178 the page-specific styling.

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend a date is asked for in one box about ten characters wide, as day/month/year text with a small label and the Ministry of Justice date picker beside it. A date is read as day, month and year only when it is one or two digits, a slash, one or two digits, a slash and four digits; a box left blank or holding only spaces is read as an empty date, and anything else is kept as typed and shown back to the trader. The picker's calendar opens below the field rather than floating over the page, at most 360 pixels wide, and its toggle is a blue icon button.
requirements.why: This is the shared date field of the animals page kit, the same field plants has, and the interaction designer's 9 November answers keep the Ministry of Justice picker for every date in both frontends.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-114 to p2-116 and p2-115-m1 describe the field and its picker, and the interaction designer keeps that picker as the one every date already uses (ruling-interaction-designer-2026-11-09-p1-040).

requirements.statement: On the animals frontend, a journey page's primary button reads 'Save and continue' unless the page gives the shared save controls its own primary label and styling, and beside it sit a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and, below them, a 'Cancel and return to overview' link to the notification's overview. A page can leave out both return controls and show only its primary button, and can add one more secondary button of its own beside the save controls, posting its own name and value; a page with no post handler answers a GET only. On a page that takes a file, every save button posts the form to the upload path as multipart, so a chosen file is sent whichever save the trader presses, and a page can put a hidden implicit-submit control ahead of its other buttons so pressing Enter in a field activates the control the page intends. Pressing 'Save and return to overview' on any journey page goes to that notification's overview; pressing 'Save and continue' goes to the next page of the journey that applies to the notification, to the review page when none is left, and to the page that asks for a required earlier answer the notification does not have when the next page needs one.
requirements.why: These are the animals frontend's shared save controls, the twin of the plants ones, and the owner's 26 October ruling makes both save buttons run the same checks on every page that has them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p2-034 to p2-040 give the controls and the two ways a page varies them, p2-135 a page with no post handler, and p2-046 to p2-048 where each save lands.

requirements.statement: The accessibility suite scans the INS front door and its address book: the blank address-type question, the blank add-address form, the add form fully entered with an optional second address line, a county and its roles ticked, an address's view page for a record with the required fields only and again for one with the extra fields, the edit form filled with a stored address, the delete confirmation, the address-type question, the add form and the edit form each with their error summary showing, the populated list and the list with the success banner after an address is added, the list's second page reached by seeding nine addresses and following Next, the dashboard in its default populated and sorted views, the not-found page, the dashboard with a search that matches a reference and again with one that matches nothing, the dashboard's paginated view where there is more than one page, the sign-in page on first load from a cold session and again with an error, with the sign-in stub's own error list excluded, and the unauthorised page. The address book's and the dashboard's longer pages are scanned again at both narrow viewports.
requirements.why: The INS front door and the address book are where the navigation leads, and every page that changes there must keep passing these scans.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p15-061 to p15-079 define the INS scans, the states each covers and the two narrow viewports.

requirements.statement: The notification type question takes a germinal products notification back to its own journey: opened for one, it shows Germinal products already selected, and only that one; continuing with Germinal products returns the trader to that notification's origin page in the germinal products set, without creating another draft; choosing a different type starts a new notification of that type in its own set or service, and the germinal products notification keeps its reference, its Draft status and every answer already given.
requirements.why: The germinal products set is the live-animals set's sibling and is reached through the same question, so its origin page's Back link to the question must bring the trader back to the same notification, as live animals does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today only a live animals notification can be taken back, its origin page being the only return page (repo-insfrontend-p3-028); a notification of any other type opens the question with nothing chosen and a warning logged (repo-insfrontend-p3-029), and the question has no Germinal products option (repo-insfrontend-p3-035).

requirements.statement: The notification type page is open only to a signed-in user with an organisation, is sent with Cache-Control: no-store, and its form posts with a CSRF crumb and with browser validation turned off, so the server makes every check.
requirements.why: The question starts a notification for an organisation, so it needs that organisation's sign-in, must not be cached, and must be checked by the server the same way with or without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-017, repo-insfrontend-p3-018 and repo-insfrontend-p3-018-m1 show the no-store header, the crumb and the server-side check on the INS front door's question today, and repo-insfrontend-p3-044 the signed-in user with an organisation it needs.

requirements.statement: Each hand-over from the notification type question is logged at info with the organisation id, the CRN, the chosen type and the destination, and a return to a notification with its reference and type too; a returning notification whose type cannot be taken back is logged as a warning with the organisation id, the reference and the type, and the choice is handled as a new notification.
requirements.why: Support staff trace a trader's start of a notification across two services by these log lines.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-025 and repo-insfrontend-p3-032 show the hand-over and return logs today, repo-insfrontend-p3-034 the warning for a type that cannot be taken back, and repo-insfrontend-p3-029-m1 that a blank notification id means no returning notification and no warning.

requirements.statement: On every journey page from the origin page onwards, in the live-animals and germinal products sets, the journey strip shows the blue 'Draft' tag followed by the notification type's name and the reference joined by ' - ': 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX' in the live-animals set and 'Germinal products - GBN-AG-26-XXXXXX' in the germinal products set, the short name rather than the type question's longer 'Germinal products (semen, ova, embryos)'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the notification's type beside its reference, so a trader with notifications in both sets can see which one they are in.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows the blue 'Draft' tag and the reference in bold, with no type name (trace-e2e-p4-003, trace-animals-fit-p6-042). The real service keeps its own strip component (trace-animals-fit-p5-007) in place of the prototype's custom block (trace-prototype-dr2-1-p1-073).

requirements.statement: On the high-risk plants frontend's journey pages that show the Draft strip, the strip takes the same shape, naming the notification's own commodity type as plants labels it once that type is chosen on plants' commodity type page, and showing the tag and the reference alone before then.
requirements.why: Plants mirrors the animals journey's wording patterns in the same increment, but it learns its type on its own commodity type page rather than from the type question.

requirements.statement: A journey in another frontend borrows the INS address book by passing four values, journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token, in the query or the form, each trimmed before it is checked. With none of them the address book is used on its own. A hand-shake missing any one is refused with 400 Bad Request ('Incomplete journey handshake'), and one whose journey type is not registered or whose fulfilment id is not listed for it with 404 Not Found, each logged as a warning with the journey type, notification id and fulfilment id and never the token. The token is only required to be present and is passed back on return. A valid hand-shake is kept in the trader's session and a posted one replaces it. Two journeys are registered, gbn-ag returning under /live-animals and gbn-ag-germinal-products returning under /germinal-products, both on the animals frontend, and no plants journey is.
requirements.why: The live-animals and germinal products party pickers add addresses through the address book and must come back to the same notification.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-048 to repo-insfrontend-p3-058 show the hand-shake, its refusals, its session handling and the two registered journeys in the INS front door today.

requirements.statement: When a journey borrows the address book for one party, the five party fulfilment ids, the same for both journeys, name the role asked for: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer or place of destination. The other roles offered are the rest of that party's group: place of origin and consignor offer each other, and consignee, importer and place of destination offer the other two. An address saved for the journey always keeps the role asked for, plus any other role chosen from that group, and the roles question carries a hint built from the asked-for role's label.
requirements.why: An address added from a party picker must be usable for the party the trader was choosing, and the group rule keeps sending and receiving roles apart.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-059 to repo-insfrontend-p3-064 show the fulfilment ids, the roles each offers and the kept role in the INS front door today.

requirements.statement: A trader leaving the address book for a borrowing journey is redirected to <animals frontend base URL><set base>/notifications/<notification id>/address-return, the notification id encoded as one path segment, carrying the fulfilment-id, the handshake-token, the chosen addressId when there is one, and a landing value: select after adding an address, return when the trader pressed the return action, and cancel when they cancelled the add. No success message is shown on the way back; cancelling from the address book alone goes to the address book list.
requirements.why: The journey needs to know which party, which address and how the trader left to put them back on the right picker.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-065 to repo-insfrontend-p3-069 and repo-insfrontend-p3-082 show the return URL, its values and the landings in the INS front door today.

requirements.statement: Address book pages honour a return parameter only when it is a path on the INS front door (a /live-animals path being sent to the same path on the animals frontend) or a full URL on the animals frontend's own origin; any other return, a URL on another site, a protocol-relative URL, a repeated parameter or one holding a backslash or line break, is ignored and logged at info, and in stub mode a return to the animals frontend is ignored. An honoured return is carried to the next address book page, except a return to the list, and leaving a record's pages, its edit page or a dead link goes to it, else to the record or the list. A record id must be 24 hexadecimal characters, or the trader is redirected and the failure logged. After an add, an edit or a delete, a one-time success message shows once on the address book list.
requirements.why: The return parameter is how a journey brings the trader back, and refusing anything off the two services keeps it from being used to send traders elsewhere.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p3-070 to repo-insfrontend-p3-084 show the return rules, the record id check and the success message in the INS front door today, and repo-tests-p14-098 the address book journey the end-to-end suite walks.

requirements.statement: Wherever the commodity search and its selected panel name a commodity, as '<commodity name> (<code>)', the name is the commodity's description as MDM gives it, passed with each result group by trade-imports-reference-data, falling back to the bare code where MDM gives none.
requirements.why: A commodity's name is part of the commodity reference list, which ruling 11 November makes MDM's content reaching the service through reference-data and never edited in code, and the data fields page names MDM's commodity list as the source of the commodity selection. MDM already returns a description for each commodity; the reference service does not yet pass it on.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the reference service's result groups carry only the commodity code, with no description (repo-referencedata-p2-026, -p2-028), so the name in 'Cattle (0102)' comes from a list the frontend holds itself (repo-frontend-p9-018, repo-tests-p1-118); MDM's commodity record gives 0102 the description 'Live bovine animals' (repo-referencedata-p2-055).

requirements.statement: trade-imports-reference-data's commodity search, GET /commodities, takes a search term q, a zero-based page (default 0, never below 0) and a size (default 100, from 1 to 100), answering 400 for a page or size that is not valid and 503 when MDM is unavailable; it trims the term, answers no species for a term shorter than two characters without asking MDM, leaves out any MDM row with no commodity code and any species with no Latin name, lists the same species under the same code once, groups species by commodity code in MDM's order, counts every match on the MDM page it read, asks MDM afresh on every call, and counts and logs each lookup and what it left out.
requirements.why: The commodity search the commodity page reads is a real service with real limits the prototype's embedded list cannot express; these are the behaviours its tests prove today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p2-004 to -p2-008, -p2-014, -p2-024 and -p2-052 hold the parameters, the two-character floor, the dropped rows and the uncached MDM call, and -p2-060 to -p2-071 and -p2-077 to -p2-080 prove them by test.

requirements.statement: trade-imports-reference-data's species check, POST /commodities/species-check, takes a list of commodity lines, each a non-blank commodity code and Latin name, and returns, in the order sent, every line whose Latin name, matched exactly with case, MDM does not list under its code, reading every page of each distinct code's species once; it answers 400 for a body that is not a list of complete lines, 503 when MDM is unavailable, calls MDM not at all for an empty list, applies no germinal rule, and counts each check and logs each unlisted line.
requirements.why: A notification's commodity lines are checked against MDM before they are relied on, because MDM's species list can change after a line is saved; the check is the reference service's real behaviour today.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p2-031 to -p2-043 describe the endpoint and its rules, and -p2-072 to -p2-076 and -p2-075-m1 to -m4 prove them by test.

requirements.statement: The commodity page shows the service's page-maturity banner for a page still being detailed rather than agreed.
requirements.why: The commodity page's behaviour is not yet agreed, so traders and testers are told the page may still change; promoting it is its own reviewed change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-002 marks the page as still being detailed, which renders the maturity banner.

requirements.statement: The commodity page has no serious or critical accessibility violations when empty, when showing results with species chosen and the help open, and when showing the 'Select a commodity' error.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint the prototype cannot express, and the page's custom search component must still pass the automated check.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-076 checks all three states with axe, and trace-animals-fit-p8-057 shows the results state passing.

requirements.statement: Every post from the commodity page carries the service's cross-site request token and the journey's concurrency token, and the form turns the browser's own validation off so every refusal is the service's own message.
requirements.why: Saves are guarded against forged posts and against two edits of one notification overwriting each other, real persistence and security constraints the prototype does not model.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-077 and -p9-078 hold both tokens and the switched-off browser validation, and trace-e2e-p5-042 shows the concurrency token rising as the notification is saved.

requirements.statement: When Commodity details or the animal identification page sends the trader to the commodity page with a return marker, a valid save returns them to that page; a return marker naming any other page is ignored, and a link with no marker carries the trader on through the journey.
requirements.why: A trader who leaves a later commodity page to change their choice goes back to where they were rather than walking the journey again.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-052 and -p9-053 honour only those two pages' return markers, -p9-049 and -p9-051 return there and log it, and -p9-110 continues the journey when no marker is given.

requirements.statement: The overview's 'What are you importing?' task counts as answered once the notification holds at least one commodity line.
requirements.why: A commodity choice is a choice of species: a notification with no species chosen has not answered what is being imported.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-085 counts the question answered once one commodity line is held.

requirements.statement: On Commodity details the Selected commodities table, headed 'Commodity code' and 'Species', with 'Number of animals' where the count is shown and a hidden 'Actions' heading where a row can be changed or removed, lists the saved lines grouped by commodity code in the order the codes first appear: a commodity's chosen species share one row, their labels separated by a comma and a line break, unless the commodity is one whose species are listed individually, when each species has its own row; each Change or Remove names its row to a screen reader by the commodity code and species labels, and a page that names the species shows its Latin name capitalised on its own and in lower case inside a sentence.
requirements.why: The trader checks what they chose before giving the details of each line; these are the real service's table rules today, and DR1 gave per-species rows to the commodity code whose species are listed individually.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p9-081 to -p9-084 and -p9-089 build the table, its headings, its hidden row names and the recased Latin name today; trace-e2e-p5-045 captured an earlier 'Commodity code', 'Common name' and 'Actions' heading set (c-374).

requirements.statement: On Commodity details each commodity line asks for 'Number of animals' and 'Number of packages (when required)', hinted 'Such as crates, bags or boxes', each in a narrow numeric input with no unit shown, both empty until the trader answers them, and adding a further species adds a line beside the ones already saved.
requirements.why: The data fields page records a number of animals, mandatory to proceed, and an optional number of packages on each commodity line; these are the fields the real page asks today.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p5-049 to -p5-053 show both inputs, the hint, their empty start and a valid save, repo-frontend-p9-094 the blank quantities on a new line, and trace-e2e-p5-054 a further species adding a line.

requirements.statement: The commodity search also matching hidden search terms, other spellings of a Latin name, full tariff codes and an English animal-names file that no row names (so 'polar bear' finds Other Carnivora, 'cattle' finds insects and travelling circus animals, and 'Bos' finds Gaur and Yak).
requirements.why: Out of scope: the search terms, tariff codes and common names are the prototype's own catalogue build, not content MDM serves, and ruling 10 November hands the commodity search control to a separate ticket; the real search matches what MDM's product search matches.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's commodity search reading germinal commodities from MDM through trade-imports-reference-data.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the germinal catalogue the search reads is the separate commodity-search ticket's (EUDPA-569, ruling 10 November); the germinal set's own pages go ahead on the commodity data it holds today, which the germinal-products area covers.

requirements.statement: In the search results the bold covers the whole word that begins with the typed text, so typing 'Bos' bolds 'Boselaphus' in full.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 bolds the matched word rather than only the letters typed, and how the search list reads follows the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each matched run of the typed text is bolded and nothing more (repo-frontend-p9-023).

requirements.statement: Wherever Commodity details and identification details name a chosen species (the Selected commodities Species cell, the species sub-heading, the Remove button's hidden text and the count-drop error), it reads '<common name> (<Latin name>)', for example 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', or the Latin name alone when the species has no common name or its common name repeats the commodity name or the Latin name; a species with no Latin name held shows its common name alone.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names a species by its common name with the Latin name in brackets, and drops the common name where it would only repeat the commodity's name; one species label serves every place the two pages name a species.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a species is labelled with its Latin name and its common name in brackets ('Bos taurus (Domestic Cattle)'), the Latin name alone when no common name is held, and nothing at all when no Latin name is held, in every heading, table cell and message on both pages (repo-frontend-p10-013, -p10-014, -p10-017, repo-tests-p1-077, -p1-078).

requirements.statement: On Commodity details the Number of animals, Number of packages and germinal Quantity (unit/pieces) fields are GOV.UK text inputs ten characters wide, with a numeric keypad.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 sizes every count field at width 10.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both live-animal fields are numeric inputs five characters wide (govuk-input--width-5, trace-animals-fit-p9-025, -p9-027; repo-frontend-p10-038 calls the field narrow).

requirements.statement: Commodity details lays its content out in the full-width grid column.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the page the full width, which holds the Selected commodities table's three columns and its row action.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the page sits in a two-thirds grid column (trace-animals-fit-p9-076).

requirements.statement: The notification status strip above the caption shows the 'Draft' tag followed by the notification's type and reference, '<type> - <reference>': 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-0FI8DO' in the live-animals set and 'Germinal products - <reference>' in the germinal products set.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the kind of notification the trader chose beside its reference on every journey page.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows the 'Draft' tag and the reference in bold, with no notification type (trace-animals-fit-p9-005).

requirements.statement: When Commodity details is shown with errors its browser title begins 'Error: ', and each inline message carries a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix.

requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-060 shows the 'Error: ' title prefix and -p9-058 the hidden inline prefix today.

requirements.statement: A Remove post naming an entry the selection no longer holds shows Commodity details as it now stands, or the commodity page when nothing is left, and one naming a single species under a code whose species are not listed individually is refused as a bad request.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-026, -p10-027 and -p10-027-m1 show the refusal, the page shown as it stands with a warning logged, and the hop to the commodity question when the selection is empty.

requirements.statement: The Welsh wording of Commodity details and identification details, including the Welsh count-drop message's plural forms.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the Welsh copy is a machine draft marked not to be shown to users before Welsh Language Standards sign-off, and Design Release 2.1 has no Welsh. That the Welsh count-drop message does not singularise its counts is for the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-158 to -p10-160 show the Welsh bundle as it is today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's own mechanics behind Commodity details: its form field names (numberOfPackages reused for the germinal quantity, germinalPackages, the removeCommodity and removeSpecies keys), its hidden from=hub marker, its session storage and what it saves or clears there on submit, the totals it works out for other pages, the package type it clears on save, its /design-release-2.1 mount, and how the real page names its own fields and hands species over from the commodity page.
requirements.why: Out of scope: field names, data shapes, paths and code structure are the real service's architecture, which the prototype never decides, and no increment changes an existing real path or code structure to match it. The real service keeps its own per-line field names and storage.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p9-072 shows the real commodity page handing species over in its own shape today.

requirements.statement: The prototype's germinal commodity catalogue content (its 18 embryo, ova and semen entries and their codes) as a source of which germinal commodities Commodity details shows.
requirements.why: Out of scope: commodity and species names and codes are a reference list, MDM's content reaching the service through reference-data, never edited in code to match the prototype; the prototype's app/data catalogue is a demo fixture.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, Commodity details lets a blank field pass and flags only an entered value that is not valid.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets a template leave answers for the trader to fill in later. The templates rows are parked in their own theme, so this is built with them.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's Commodity details has the same back link, caption, heading, Selected commodities table and commodity groups as the live-animals page, with one table row per germinal commodity listing all its chosen species (for example '05111000 | Cattle, Semen | Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)'), each group headed '<commodity name> (<commodity code>)' such as 'Cattle, Semen (05111000)', and a section break between the species sections inside a germinal commodity group.
requirements.why: Each germinal page is a copy of its live-animals twin plus Design Release 2.1's germinal differences, and Design Release 2.1 separates germinal species within a commodity.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set each species whose commodity the data fields page's package-count list names (its semen, embryo and ova lines) also asks 'Number of packages', after Quantity (unit/pieces), with no hint and no '(when required)'. It is optional, but a value given must be a whole number of 1 or more, otherwise 'Number of packages must be a whole number greater than 0', linked to that species' field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives germinal species an optional package count with its own message, and the data fields page decides which commodities a package count applies to.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's Commodity details asks one 'Temperature' question for the consignment, after all commodity groups behind a section break: radios with the legend 'Temperature' at label size, the hint 'How the products will be stored.' and the options 'Ambient', 'Chilled' and 'Frozen' in that order. It is optional: left unanswered, no error is shown.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the storage temperature once for a germinal consignment, and ruling 2026-10-09 makes the germinal set always ask it; the data fields page makes it optional.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, a valid Save and continue on Commodity details, reached in the journey, goes on to the next page the journey puts after Commodity details (Identification details where a chosen species needs identifiers), with no page between them asking a total gross weight for the whole consignment: each species' total gross weight is asked in that species' own block on Commodity details.
requirements.why: Ruling 27 November keeps the germinal total gross weight per species, and it ranks above Design Release 2.1, which now asks one total gross weight for the consignment on a page of its own after Commodity details (c-461, as c-231 and c-486 settle the same difference for the weight field and the hub row).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists in the real frontend today.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's main import reason page, the Internal market reason's hint reads 'For consignments intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'
requirements.why: The target design gives the germinal page its own hint for this reason, worded for consignments, and it wins by default on copy; nothing overrides it. The 9 October ruling makes germinal products a sibling set with its own copy of the page.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's main import reason page, the Transit reason's hint reads 'For consignments moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'
requirements.why: The target design gives the germinal page its own hint for this reason, worded for consignments, and it wins by default on copy; nothing overrides it.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today; the live-animals page carries the animals wording (repo-frontend-p8-068).

For example, animals that have been sold and are being moved to a new owner or will be sold once in Great Britain, purchases from a breeder/shop overseas and where an animal is being moved to a new owner with no sale involved (for example a gift).'
requirements.why: The target design gives the germinal purpose its own hint and wins by default on copy. Its second sentence still speaks of animals; the design renders it that way, so it is built as written.

This includes animals and germinal products intended to contribute to the genetic pool of a breeding program, improve livestock quality, or produce offspring.'
