requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's internal market purpose question, Research carries the hint 'Animals and germinal products for use in scientific or medical research.'
requirements.why: The target design gives the germinal purpose its own hint and wins by default on copy; nothing overrides it.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today; the live-animals purpose carries the animals wording (repo-frontend-p8-078).

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's internal market purpose question, Production carries the hint 'Animals and germinal products that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'
requirements.why: The target design gives the germinal purpose its own hint and wins by default on copy; nothing overrides it.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today; the live-animals purpose carries the animals wording (repo-frontend-p8-082).

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set's main import reason page reads as the live-animals page does apart from its reasons, purposes and hints: the h1 and title 'Main import reason', the caption 'About the consignment', the visually hidden legend 'What is the main reason for importing the animals?', the 'Purpose in the internal market' question, the 'Port of exit' and 'Destination country' questions under Transit, the Back link to What are you importing and the same three journey controls; its status strip names the notification as germinal products.
requirements.why: The target design swaps only the reason and purpose lists and their hints for germinal products and keeps one legend and the rest of the page, and it wins by default on copy and layout. The 9 October ruling makes germinal products a sibling set with its own copy of the page.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today; the live-animals page shows this heading, caption and legend (repo-frontend-p8-063).

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set's main import reason page, Internal market with no purpose, or with a purpose other than the four the set offers, is refused with 'Select a purpose in the internal market'; Transit with no port of exit or no destination country is refused with 'Select a port of exit' and 'Select a destination country', port first; a valid answer goes on to Commodity details.
requirements.why: The target design refuses the germinal page's answers with the same messages as the live-animals page and counts a purpose outside the germinal four as not chosen; the policy page makes these follow-ups mandatory to proceed once their reason is chosen.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists in the real frontend today; the live-animals page refuses with these messages (repo-frontend-p8-100, repo-frontend-p8-102).

requirements.statement: An open conditional reveal on the main import reason page keeps GOV.UK Frontend's standard conditional reveal styling, with its grey left border and indent, in both sets.
requirements.why: The target design restyles the open reveal with no left border and 18px of padding, and its snag photographs are the designers' record of that look, while the 9 October afternoon ruling makes GOV.UK components the toolbox and the real page is built from them unaltered. Neither is ranked above the other on how a standard component is styled.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p7-074 shows the page built from govuk-frontend radios with conditional reveals and no custom reveal classes today. Under the other reading the open reveal loses its border and takes the design's padding.

requirements.statement: In the temporary admission horses reveal, the exit date and port of exit questions sit one above the other with 30px between them, in the error state too.
requirements.why: The target design settles this spacing in its S12 snag and wins by default on layout; nothing overrides it.

requirements.statement: The additional details page's form sits in the two-thirds grid column.
requirements.why: The target design places this page in the two-thirds column, unlike the full-width commodity and identification pages, and it wins by default on layout.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p12-062 shows the page's components today but no today source shows its column width, so the builder checks it and sets two-thirds where it differs.

requirements.statement: No rule switches a notification's reason or purpose lists, or re-judges a saved reason, by which species are chosen, and no mixed live-animal and germinal-products consignment is handled on these pages: each set's copy of the page offers its own lists.
requirements.why: The target design decides germinal or live from the species chosen, gives a mixed consignment the live lists and re-judges a saved reason if the notification turns germinal-only. That is its own architecture: the 9 October ruling puts germinal products in a sibling set whose notifications never hold live animals, so a notification never changes set.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the identification page's heading carries the caption 'Description of the goods'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 captions the identification page 'Description of the goods' when every selected commodity is a germinal product, where the live-animals page keeps 'About the consignment'. Each set holds one category, so the germinal set always shows this caption.

requirements.statement: In the live-animals set, each species panel that asks for an animal's details shows the hint 'Enter at least one identifier.' under its entry heading. A germinal products panel, which takes one set of details per species, shows no such hint.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader on every live-animal panel that one identifier is enough, which is the bar the service applies, and leaves the hint off germinal panels.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a card holds the counter, the identifier fields and the save button with no hint of its own (repo-frontend-p10-106).

requirements.statement: Wherever the identification page names a species, in the summary's Species column, the panel title, the entry heading and the saved-animal rows, the species label leads with the species' common name with the Latin name in brackets, such as 'Domestic cattle (Bos taurus)', and shows the Latin name alone when the species has no common name or its common name only repeats the commodity name or the Latin name. Both names are the ones reference data serves.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leads with the name a trader knows. The names themselves are MDM's content through reference data and are never edited in code to match the prototype (its 'Equus cabalus' is its own data); only how the label reads follows the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a species label leads with the Latin name, with the bracketed name after it, such as 'Bos taurus (Cattle) 1' on a saved row (repo-frontend-p10-110), and the species display name used elsewhere is the Latin name with only its first letter in capitals (repo-frontend-p10-184).

requirements.statement: The horse name field is labelled 'Equine name', in its field label, its saved-animals column heading and its length error 'Equine name must be 58 characters or less'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels the field 'Equine name', and the 11 November ruling leaves labels to the prototype; V4 still decides that the field is captured, for horses only, up to 58 characters.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the field reads 'Horse name' (repo-frontend-p10-092, trace-animals-fit-p10-036) and its error 'Horse name must be 58 characters or less' (repo-frontend-p10-126).

requirements.statement: A species asked for the free-text identifiers is asked for 'Description' first, then 'Identification details'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 asks the description before the identification details wherever it shows both, and the 11 November ruling leaves question order to the prototype.
requirements.deltaNote: Today an ostrich line, a commodity with no declared identifier, is asked for Identification details then Description (repo-frontend-p10-180).

requirements.statement: On a species panel that asks for one identifier only, such as the 'Ear tag' of a sheep or goat panel, pressing the panel's save with that field blank shows 'Enter an ear tag', naming the field, in the error summary and inline, linked to the field.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 names the field when a panel has only one that counts and says 'Enter at least one identifier' otherwise. The article follows GOV.UK grammar, where the prototype's generated wording would read 'a ear tag'.
requirements.deltaNote: Today every blank card shows 'Enter at least one identifier for this animal' (repo-frontend-p10-121), and a sheep or goat line asks for an ear tag alone (repo-frontend-p10-098).

requirements.statement: The saved-animals table has a column for every identifier the species is asked for, whether or not a saved animal filled it in.
requirements.why: Today's table, kept until the owner says the prototype's habit of hiding unused columns should be built for the real identifier sets.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p10-109 and trace-animals-fit-p10-061 show a column for every identifier the species is asked for today, a blank one showing as an empty cell.

requirements.statement: Identification fields beyond the specified identifiers on the identification page: Identification number, Flock ID, Classification with its option lists and 'Select a classification' dropdown, Breed/category, Bird breed, Leg ring/band, Mark/clip, Unique code, Egg mark, Identification mark, Batch number, and Hatching date with its calendar and hint; species-by-species field sets hard-coded per commodity; and one set of details per flock or batch rather than per animal.
requirements.why: Out of scope: V4 is the source of truth for data under the 11 November ruling. It specifies six animal identifiers, each held per animal, and these fields, option lists and per-flock entries come only from the prototype's app/data demo fixtures, which are evidence of nothing about what a notification captures, which values a field offers or which commodities a rule covers.

requirements.statement: While a template is being created or edited, a species panel's save with no identifier filled is accepted.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the 4 November ruling parks the templates rows, so nothing is built for template mode now.

requirements.statement: A separate 'What is the total gross weight of the consignment?' page after Commodity details, asking one required total gross weight for the whole consignment, with the caption 'Description of the goods', the hint 'This includes the weight of all the commodities in the consignment and their packaging.', its own back links, completeness rule and form actions.
requirements.why: Out of scope: the owner's 27 November ruling, given after the prototype moved to this page, keeps the germinal total gross weight per species on Commodity details (req-121, c-231), and V4 makes the weight optional (c-232). The page's mechanisms (pre-filling from earlier per-species net weights, minting a prototype reference on visit, saving without checks on Save and return) exist for the prototype's own session data. What still holds from the page is carried per species: the number rule and trimming (req-1784), decimals (req-1786) and continuing to Identification details (req-1790). Live animals have no total gross weight in either reading.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the Internal market reason's hint reads 'For consignments intended for sale or use in Great Britain (England, Scotland or Wales).'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the germinal reason hints for consignments, since germinal products are not animals; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the Transit reason's hint reads 'For consignments moving through Great Britain for direct travel to a third country, that will enter Great Britain at one port or airport and leave from a different one within England, Scotland or Wales.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 words the germinal reason hints for consignments; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Transfer of ownership - Sale/gift' has the hint 'Any movement of a consignment that has as its aim the sale of or the transfer of ownership of the consignment from one person or entity to another.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Breeding' has the hint 'Consignments for reproduction. This includes animals and germinal products intended to contribute to the genetic pool of a breeding program, improve livestock quality, or produce offspring.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Research' has the hint 'Animals and germinal products for use in scientific or medical research.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the internal market purpose 'Production' has the hint 'Animals and germinal products that are farmed for the production of meat, milk, eggs, wool or any other animal product or by-product.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives each germinal purpose its own hint; the prototype decides wording.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set asks transit countries on the same condition as the live-animals set: its transit countries page and overview task appear when the means of transport is rail or road, with the same question, list, cap and rules.
requirements.why: The data dictionary contradicts itself on whether transit countries apply to germinal products: one condition bullet says animals only, while its impacts cell marks the field for germinals too. Sam's 10 November ruling has the germinal pages take live animals as their reference point for everything, so the germinal set asks it as live animals does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today only the live-animals set has a transit countries page (repo-frontend-p11-053), reached for rail or road (repo-frontend-p11-043); the germinal set does not exist yet.

requirements.statement: While a live-animals or germinal template is being created, Save and continue on arrival details goes on with no means of transport chosen, raising no error for it.
requirements.why: A template is reused across consignments and Design Release 2.1 does not require the means of transport while one is created. The 9 October templates ruling lets template mode's validation differ from the notification journey on the same pages.
requirements.deltaNote: Today a missing means of transport is always refused with 'Select a means of transport to the port of entry' (repo-frontend-p11-028), and there is no template mode.
requirements.blockedBy: The owner decides to pick the parked templates rows up again: the 4 November ruling parks them unbuilt and the interaction designer records templates dropped for now.

requirements.statement: While a live-animals or germinal template is being created, arrival details and transit countries end with 'Save and continue', a secondary 'Save and return to template' button and a 'Cancel and return to template' link, and both return controls go to the template's review page.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's wording for template mode on these pages. Its button reads 'return to template' and its cancel link goes to the template review, and the 9 October templates ruling has the way back follow the context a page was opened in, so the button goes where its label says.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both pages always end with 'Save and continue', 'Save and return to overview' and 'Cancel and return to overview' (repo-frontend-p11-042), and there is no template mode.
requirements.blockedBy: The owner decides to pick the parked templates rows up again: the 4 November ruling parks them unbuilt and the interaction designer records templates dropped for now.

requirements.statement: When the notification has a transporter saved, the transporter list shows it under the sub-heading 'Selected transporter' as GOV.UK inset text: the transporter's name, then its address, 'Approval number: <approval number>' and its type, each of those three only when it has a value, in place of the search box, 'Add a transporter' and the table. The search box, 'Add a transporter' and the table show instead when the trader has chosen Change, has searched, or the page has an error. Saving from the summary keeps the same transporter.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the chosen transporter on its own once it is chosen, so the trader sees what is saved without reading a table, and the prototype decides how a page looks. A private transporter the trader added shows 'Approval number: Not applicable' (req-399).
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list is the only view: coming back to it shows the table with the saved transporter's radio checked (repo-frontend-p12-052, trace-animals-fit-p18-061), and no 'Selected transporter' summary exists.

requirements.statement: The selected-transporter summary has a 'Change' link, with the visually hidden text ' transporter', that shows the search box, 'Add a transporter' and the table again with the saved transporter's radio checked.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's way back to the list from the summary, so the trader can pick another transporter or add one.
requirements.deltaNote: Today there is no summary and so no Change link on it; the list always shows the table (repo-frontend-p12-052). How the link carries its state is the service's own: the prototype's '?change=1' is not used, the real service already using that word for its review trail (req-423).

requirements.statement: The selected-transporter summary has a 'Remove' button styled as a link, with the visually hidden text ' transporter', which clears the notification's chosen transporter at once, with no confirmation page and no banner, and shows the transporter list again with the search box, 'Add a transporter' and the table and nothing chosen.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader clear the transporter. A transporter is still mandatory to proceed (req-402), so a save after removing one is refused until another is chosen, and the transporter task is no longer complete.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the list offers no way to clear a saved transporter: it ends with 'Save and continue' and the journey's return controls only (repo-frontend-p12-053).

requirements.statement: A transporter the trader ticked before a search that hides its row is still the one 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' save, with or without JavaScript, until the trader ticks another.
requirements.why: Searching saves and validates nothing (req-391), so it must not lose the trader's pick either; with the search done on the server alone (req-389), the pick has to survive the re-rendered page, as it must survive moving to another page of the list (req-2268).
requirements.deltaNote: With JavaScript the rows are only hidden, so the pick survives (repo-frontend-p12-042, repo-tests-p2-073); without it a server search keeps the pick as a hidden value but the save reads only the ticked radio, so a pick searched off the list is refused with 'Select a transporter from the list' (repo-frontend-p12-042-m1), though one still on the narrowed list stays ticked (repo-frontend-p12-098).

requirements.statement: For a germinal products notification, the transporter list shows only the heading and 'This is the person or company responsible for transporting the consignment.' under it, with no transporter authorisation guidance: no DAERA or APHA lead-in, no conditions list, no economic-activity link and no document validity statements.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows the transporter authorisation guidance only for live animals, which is what it is about.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists today; the one transporter list, the live-animals one (repo-frontend-p12-001), always shows the guidance (repo-frontend-p12-007).

requirements.statement: The success banner after adding a transporter shows the transporter's name exactly as the trader entered it.
requirements.why: Re-casing what a trader typed is a change to how user-entered data is shown, and nothing says why the banner does it: it lower-cases every letter after the first, so 'Lough Livestock Ltd' reads 'Lough livestock ltd'. It is a question whose default is not to build the re-casing.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the banner lower-cases the name after its first letter, so 'Jean Dupont' reads 'Jean dupont transporter added' (repo-frontend-p12-104, repo-frontend-p12-057).

requirements.statement: For a germinal products notification, 'Add a commercial transporter' shows no 'Important' transporter authorisation banner; for a live animals notification it shows the banner with its 'Help with transporter authorisation' guidance.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 leaves the live-animal authorisation help off the germinal products journey, as it does on the transporter list (req-2638). Whether the address book's add page knows which set it serves rests on what the journey-mode hand-off carries, which is open.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set exists today; the animals frontend's commercial form always shows the banner (repo-frontend-p13-046).

requirements.statement: 'Add a private transporter' offers a postcode lookup: 'Name or organisation name', then a field labelled 'Enter a UK postcode' with the hint 'For example, AB12 3CD', a 'Find address' button and an 'Enter address manually' link-style button, calling the same INS backend address lookup as the other address searches.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader find a UK address by its postcode rather than type it, using the GOV.UK Addresses pattern, which is look and feel the prototype decides. It waits on the address lookup like every address search.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the private form has no address lookup: every field is typed by hand (repo-frontend-p13-016).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local and not wired in (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34). Address search is also parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is re-distilled with the rest of address search once the lookup lands.

requirements.statement: On both add-a-transporter pages, 'Find address' with a postcode that has addresses shows a step titled and headed 'Select an address', showing 'Postcode' with the postcode entered and a 'Change postcode' link-style button, then a select labelled 'Select an address' whose first option counts the matches ('1 address found', '2 addresses found') followed by each address as one comma-separated line, a 'Continue' button and an 'Enter address manually' link-style button.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's results step for the postcode lookup. Its entries are whatever the INS address lookup returns.
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither add form has an address lookup (repo-frontend-p13-017).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34), and address search is parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is built with the add pages' postcode lookups.

requirements.statement: On both add-a-transporter pages, 'Find address' with no postcode shows the error 'Enter a postcode', linked to the postcode field, and stays on the postcode step; it does not check the name.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's error for a missing lookup postcode.
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither add form has an address lookup (repo-frontend-p13-017).

requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's error for a malformed lookup postcode; the lookup postcode is the only postcode it checks for shape (req-439).
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither add form has an address lookup (repo-frontend-p13-017).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34), and address search is parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is built with the add pages' postcode lookups.

requirements.statement: On both add-a-transporter pages, a UK postcode with no matching addresses shows the error 'No addresses found for <postcode>. Check the postcode or enter the address manually', with the postcode formatted, and stays on the postcode step.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's error when the lookup finds nothing, pointing the trader to manual entry.
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither add form has an address lookup (repo-frontend-p13-017).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34), and address search is parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is built with the add pages' postcode lookups.

requirements.statement: On both add-a-transporter pages, 'Continue' on the 'Select an address' step with no address chosen shows the error 'Select an address', linked to the select, and shows the list again.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's error for an unchosen lookup result.
requirements.deltaNote: Today neither add form has an address lookup (repo-frontend-p13-017).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34), and address search is parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is built with the add pages' postcode lookups.

requirements.statement: On 'Add a private transporter', choosing a looked-up address fills address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and the postcode from what the lookup returns and sets the country to United Kingdom, keeping the name the trader typed; 'Change postcode' goes back to the postcode step and 'Enter address manually' to the details step, each clearing the address fields and any errors.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves the trader typing what the lookup knows. A looked-up address is a UK address, so the country follows.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the private form has no address lookup to fill from (repo-frontend-p13-016).
requirements.blockedBy: The INS address lookup becomes a real feature (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claim 34), and address search is parked as concept work (ruling:sam-2026-11-09 point 2). It is built with the private transporter's postcode lookup.

requirements.statement: Until the private transporter's postcode lookup is built, and always without JavaScript, every address and contact field on 'Add a private transporter' shows from the start, so a trader can always enter the address by hand.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript, manual address entry never waits on the address lookup, and the 9 November ruling keeps every field shown from the start on the add-address pages, as main has them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p13-016 asks every address and contact field on the private form, in order, with nothing hidden.

requirements.statement: The add pages' address lookup lists Companies House registered office addresses with repeated entries listed once, and a commercial save fills any field the trader emptied back from the looked-up address.
requirements.why: Both are the prototype's mechanism over its own canned lookup data, not look and feel: the entries are whatever the INS address lookup returns, and what the trader leaves in a field is what is saved.

requirements.statement: A notification started from a template finds its transporter again on the list by its name and approval number.
requirements.why: The prototype's mechanism for its session data, which keeps a template's transporter details but not its id. The real service matches a saved transporter to its address book record by id (req-2272), and templates are parked (ruling:sam-2026-11-04).

requirements.statement: While a template is being created, the transporter list shows 'Save and return to template' and 'Cancel and return to template'.
requirements.why: Templates are parked and not built now (ruling:sam-2026-11-04), and the prototype's own controls disagree about where they land.

requirements.statement: The transporter list's form post ignores the search box's value, leaving search to the browser or a search term in the address.
requirements.why: The prototype's mechanism behind its in-page filter, which design did not keep: the real list searches on the server when the trader presses Search or Enter (req-389).

requirements.statement: The address book sets a transporter's id, its organisation (from the caller's identity header), its live status and its created and modified times itself; any of them sent in a request body is accepted and ignored.
requirements.why: The system of record owns its server fields, so no caller can place a transporter in another organisation or back-date it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-004, -027 and -061 set the server fields and ignore those sent, proven by the service's create tests.

requirements.statement: The address book refuses, as a 400 validation problem keyed by the field, a transporter whose name or address line 1 is blank or over 255 characters, whose address line 2 is over 255, whose town or city is blank or over 100, whose county is over 100, whose postcode is blank or over 12, whose country code is blank, whose phone is blank or over 20, whose email is blank, malformed or over 254, or whose approval number is over 50; the postcode, phone and approval number are checked for presence and length only, and the country code is stored as given.
requirements.why: The address book is the system of record, so its own rules hold for a transporter however it is written; they are the Standard Address Block's limits the 6 November ruling reuses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-007 to -024 hold every rule, proven by the request validation tests, and repo-tests-p15-041 stores an NI/TA approval number unchanged.

requirements.statement: A transporter the address book returns carries, in camelCase, its id, name, address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county, postcode, country code, phone, email, type, approval number, organisation id, a deleted flag and its created and modified times, with an unset address line 2, county or approval number written as null; it never carries roles, an address type, the internal soft-delete status, its expiry date or its version.
requirements.why: Every consumer reads one shape, and soft deletion is shown only as a deleted flag so the internal tombstone status can change without breaking a caller.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-039 and -041 to -044-m1 give the response's fields, proven by the mapper and response tests.

requirements.statement: The address book's transporter list holds only the caller's organisation's live transporters, newest first by creation time and then by id; a soft-deleted transporter leaves the list.
requirements.why: The list is what every picker and the Transporter tab read, so it shows what the organisation holds now, most recent first.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-068 and -069 order and filter the list, proven by the service and delete tests.

requirements.statement: The transporter list's search term is trimmed and matched as literal text, ignoring case, against any part of a transporter's name, address lines, town or city, county, postcode or approval number, never its country code, phone, email or type; repeatable country codes and search types match a transporter in any given country or of any given type; a transporter matching the term, a country or a search type is listed; and an absent or blank term, country code or search type adds nothing, repeats counting once.
requirements.why: The Transporter tab's single search box finds a transporter by its name, address, approval number, country name or type word, which the front door turns into the term, country codes and search types.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-070 to -075 and -078 hold the search, proven by the transporter search tests.

requirements.statement: A repeatable type filter on the transporter list keeps only transporters of the given types across every page and narrows the search; an unknown type or search type value is a 400 bad-request problem with no errors map.
requirements.why: The Transporter tab's Type filter narrows the whole tab on the server rather than one page of it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-076 and -077 are proven by the transporter search tests.

requirements.statement: Reading a transporter by id returns it to its own organisation, a soft-deleted one included and marked deleted; an unknown id and another organisation's id both answer the same 404 'Transporter not found', so the service never confirms that another organisation holds an id.
requirements.why: A notification can still show a transporter that was later deleted, and nothing leaks another organisation's records.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-049, -050 and -083 are proven by the service, delete and scoping tests.

requirements.statement: Replacing a live transporter replaces every field the caller sends, clearing an optional field left out, keeps its id, organisation, status, created time and expiry date, and moves its modified time on; replacing a soft-deleted, unknown or another organisation's transporter answers 404, and a save from a stale copy is refused as a 409 conflict rather than overwriting a later change.
requirements.why: Optimistic locking keeps two editors, or a late write after a delete, from silently overwriting each other.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-051 to -054 and -005 hold the replace and the lock; the 409 is documented but not driven by a test (repo-addressbook-p4-006). The API lets a replace change the type (repo-addressbook-p4-053), which the front door's edit form never sends.

requirements.statement: Deleting a transporter soft-deletes it and answers 204 with no body: its status becomes deleted, its modified time moves on and its approval number stays; deleting it again answers 204 and changes nothing, and deleting an unknown id answers a 404 not-found problem.
requirements.why: The address book's soft-delete rule holds for transporters exactly as for addresses, so a submitted notification's transporter stays readable.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-055 to -060 are proven by the transporter delete tests.

requirements.statement: Every transporter operation needs the trusted organisation id header and is authorised against the path organisation: a missing header is a 400, a header that disagrees with the path answers 404 and changes nothing, and one organisation never lists or reaches another's transporters.
requirements.why: Transporters belong to an organisation, as addresses do, and the 6 November ruling reuses the address book's organisation scoping for them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-080 to -082 are proven by the scoping tests, and repo-tests-p15-030 shows another organisation's address book holding none of them.

requirements.statement: The transporters collection has one index besides its id, on organisation, status and creation time, and the live list query uses it rather than scanning the collection.
requirements.why: Organisations in test environments hold thousands of records, so the list stays fast as the collection grows.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-085 is proven by the transporter index test.

requirements.statement: Outside prod, when a time to live is configured, a new transporter expires that many days after it is created, and a later update or soft delete keeps that date; in prod transporters and their tombstones are kept indefinitely.
requirements.why: The address book's expiry rule holds for transporters exactly as for addresses, so test environments do not fill up.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-086 and -088 hold the rule, reusing the address time-to-live setting.

requirements.statement: Each transporter operation, and the list's database query, is timed as a metric, and the list logs whether a search term was given, never its text, with the page, page size, country codes and types.
requirements.why: The transporters route is observed like the address routes without logging what a trader searched for.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-089 and -090 name the metrics and the log line.

requirements.statement: The address book's OpenAPI contract documents the five transporter operations under a transporters tag, 'An organisation's transporters, scoped to its address book', with name, address line 1, town or city, postcode, country code, phone, email and type as the request's required fields.
requirements.why: Callers of the system of record build against its published contract.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-addressbook-p4-091 and -093 are in the locked contract.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: minor inconsistencies in the address book's transporter validation and contract that no trader sees, namely the generated contract giving required string fields a minimum length of 0, a request with no type and an approval number also being refused as private, and a blank commercial country getting two messages on one field.
requirements.why: None of them reaches a trader through the front door's forms, which validate first, and none changes what is stored; they go to the report rather than into an increment.

requirements.statement: Choosing Transporter on the address book's 'Choose an address type' question opens the transporter type question afresh, clearing any transporter part-way through being added.
requirements.why: Starting again from the address type question should never carry over half-entered details from an earlier attempt.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-005 and -006 open the question at its start and clear the in-progress entry, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-106 and repo-tests-p15-001.

requirements.statement: The address book's 'Choose a transporter type' page has the caption 'Add a new transporter', the heading and title 'Choose a transporter type', the warning text 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.', a visually hidden legend 'Choose a transporter type', the radios 'Private transporter' with no hint then 'Commercial' with the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.', and one 'Continue' button.
requirements.why: The address book's type question is the one route to adding a transporter, and it already reads as the journey's type question does.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-007 to -014 hold the copy and repo-tests-p15-002 to -007 prove it end to end.

requirements.statement: Continuing on the address book's 'Choose a transporter type' with no option chosen re-shows it with status 400 and the error 'Select a transporter type', inline against the radios and in a 'There is a problem' summary whose link moves focus to 'Private transporter', with and without JavaScript.
requirements.why: The address book's type question becomes the one route (req-2264), so it takes the design's refusal wording that the journey's own question carries today; this is the same change as req-420 on the page that remains.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the address book's question refuses with 'Select what kind of transporter it is' (repo-insfrontend-p7-016, repo-tests-p15-010); the status, summary and focus already match.

requirements.statement: On the address book's type question, 'Private transporter' opens 'Add a private transporter' and 'Commercial' opens 'Add a commercial transporter'; the chosen type is remembered so the question shows it chosen on return, and values already typed on a form are kept when the type is changed.
requirements.why: A trader who goes back to change the type should not lose what they have typed.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-017, -017-m1 and -018 hold the routing and memory, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-108 and repo-tests-p15-013 and -032.

requirements.statement: Opening or posting the address book's private or commercial add form with no transporter type chosen, or a different one, sends the trader to 'Choose a transporter type' and saves nothing.
requirements.why: The form a trader fills in must match the type they chose, because the type decides the fields and the country rule.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-020 guards both forms, proven by repo-insfrontend-p7-112 and -117 and repo-tests-p15-022.

requirements.statement: The address book's add forms carry the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and title 'Add a private transporter' or 'Add a commercial transporter'.
requirements.why: The address book's add forms are the one route and already read as the journey's do.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-021 to -023 hold the copy, proven by repo-tests-p15-014, -015 and -033, and the private form's opening in the cross-browser and iOS runs too (repo-tests-p15-135).

requirements.statement: The address book's add and edit forms ask, in order, the name, the approval number on a commercial form only, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, and Phone number with the hint 'For international numbers include the country code'; the name and address line 1 are required and at most 255 characters, address line 2 at most 255, town or city required and at most 100, county at most 100, postcode required and at most 12, email required and at most 254, phone required and at most 20, and the approval number required and at most 50; every value is trimmed of surrounding spaces before it is checked and saved.
requirements.why: The forms ask the Standard Address Block's fields and contact fields with its limits, as the 11 November ruling settles; the name and approval number labels and the section headings are their own requirements (req-2265, req-2266, req-2267).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-025 to -035 and -039 hold the fields, their order, the phone hint, the limits and the trimming; repo-tests-p15-017 and -018 prove the fields end to end. Today the name reads 'Name or organisation', the approval number 'Approval number' and the fields sit under 'Address' and 'Contact details' (repo-insfrontend-p7-024, repo-tests-p15-016), which the label and heading requirements change.

requirements.statement: The address book's transporter form fields carry the browser autocomplete hints address-line1, address-line2, address-level2, postal-code, email and tel, with town, county, postcode and country at half width and phone at two-thirds width.
requirements.why: Autocomplete hints help every trader and are a WCAG input-purpose requirement; the widths follow GOV.UK guidance for the expected length.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p7-034 sets the hints and widths.

requirements.statement: A blank name on the address book's transporter forms shows 'Enter a name or organisation name'.

requirements.statement: The plants consignment contact page has the h1 'Contact address for consignment' with no section caption, then the body text 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.', then the sub-heading 'Select an address' above its results, in English and Welsh.

requirements.deltaNote: The plants contact page already has the heading with no caption; the intro and the 'Select an address' sub-heading are added. This area's working set carries no plants frontend extract, so the evidence is the ruling's plants clause alone.

requirements.statement: Outside amend, the plants consignment contact page ends with 'Save and continue' and 'Save and return to overview' side by side in one button group, and 'Cancel and return to overview' on its own line below them. While a notification is being amended, it shows 'Save and return', which goes to the review page, a secondary 'Save and continue' and a link-styled 'Save and return to overview', with no cancel link and no cancel-amend dialog.
requirements.why: The plants contact page is linked from the overview, so it keeps the three return controls, and the 2026-10-09 afternoon ruling gives plants' pickers the same amend buttons as the animals pages. The 27 November ruling builds prototype changes that reach amending on the manage-notifications theme's branch.
requirements.deltaNote: The controls outside amend are already built; the amend set is new. This area's working set carries no plants frontend extract, so the evidence is the rulings' plants clauses alone.

requirements.statement: Once a CPH number is saved, the consignment addresses page's CPH section shows it with a 'Change' link and a 'Remove CPH number' link; removing it clears the saved CPH number, and the section offers 'Add a CPH number' again.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the CPH section shows the saved number in its slashed form with a 'Change' link only (repo-frontend-p16-027, trace-e2e-p6-076), and nothing removes it.

requirements.statement: Once a permanent address is saved, the consignment addresses page's Permanent address section offers 'Remove permanent address' beside its 'Change' link; removing it clears every animal's saved permanent address, and the section offers 'Add a permanent address' again.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 lets the trader take back the permanent addresses in one go, for example after the animals change.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p16-062: nothing in the permanent address slice lets a trader remove a saved permanent address today.

requirements.statement: On the permanent address page the warning, the guidance and the error summary sit in a two-thirds column, and the question and the animal cards below them span the full width, each card a section labelled by its heading.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps the reading text at a readable width while giving each animal's card the room for its address form, and labelling each card by its heading lets assistive technology move between animals.
requirements.deltaNote: Today each animal is a GOV.UK summary card (repo-frontend-p16-039), not a labelled section in a full-width column.

requirements.statement: The CPH number and permanent address pages' behaviour while a notification template is created or edited is not built now: the 'Save and return to template' and 'Cancel and return to template' controls, the permanent address page raising no errors, and 'Save and return' going to the consignment addresses page rather than the template review.
requirements.why: Out of scope: templates are dropped for now and their rows stay parked in their own theme.
requirements.deltaNote: The service has no template journey through these pages today.

requirements.statement: In the status strip above the page heading, the notification reference is preceded by the notification's type label and ' - ': 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P' in the live-animals set and 'Germinal products - <reference>' in the germinal-products set. In the high-risk plants frontend the strip reads the label plants' own commodity type question gives the chosen type, then ' - ' and the reference, and the reference alone until a commodity type is chosen. The strip is shared, so the hub and every other page that shows it read the same.

requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip shows the status tag and the reference alone, with no type label: repo-frontend-p5-061 and trace-animals-fit-p4-003 in live animals, repo-plantsfrontend-p2-008 in plants.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, the 'Units/pieces' card shows the total of the quantity (units or pieces) answers saved against the notification's commodity lines that are positive numbers, and '0' when the total is not above zero.
requirements.why: The design's rule for the germinal quantity card; the quantity it totals is the data specification's commodity-line quantity in units or pieces, not the prototype's storage.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set or quantity card exists today. The prototype sums its own numberOfPackages answers for this card (prototype-dr2-1-source-p12-116 note); the real card totals whatever field the germinal set stores the quantity in.

requirements.statement: In the germinal-products set, section 2 holds 'Commodity details', then 'Identification details' where a chosen commodity needs identifiers, and no other row: there is no 'Additional details' row and no 'Total gross weight' row, the total gross weight being asked for each species on the commodity details page and counted by the 'Commodity details' row.

requirements.deltaNote: No germinal-products set exists today.

requirements.statement: A notification's view header gathers its actions in an 'Actions' button menu built with the Ministry of Justice button menu, which shows its items as a row of buttons when JavaScript is off: 'Amend this notification' (submitted notifications only), then 'Copy as new', then Delete, in the live animals and germinal products sets and in the high-risk plants frontend. The menu offers no 'Make template'.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 holds the viewed notification's actions in one Actions menu, and the 9 October afternoon ruling admits a tested government library's component where GOV.UK Frontend has none, provided the page works without JavaScript. Templates are parked, so Make template is not built. What each action opens is the manage-notifications area's.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the actions are separate buttons in a GOV.UK button group under the heading: Amend primary, Copy as new secondary or default, and Delete a warning button (repo-frontend-p6-017, p6-018); plants has Amend and Delete notification only (repo-plantsfrontend-p10-020-m1, p10-023).

requirements.deltaNote: Today only the live-animals confirmation applies the rule (repo-frontend-p7-064); the germinal set's copy of the page is new.

requirements.statement: The live-animals declaration page is titled and headed 'Declaration' and sets out three statements as headings, word for word: 'I am the contact for the authorities and located in the UK.' with 'I am complying with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2017/625 including on animal health and welfare.'; 'I confirm I am responsible for this consignment.' with 'I am responsible from the submission of this notification to when it enters Great Britain. And I am responsible until it has either:' and the bullets 'cleared official checks at the border' and 'reached the Place of Destination as stated on the health certificate or notification'; and 'I confirm that I am accountable for:' with the bullets 'any payment for the official controls at the border', 'any arrangements to re-dispatch the consignment', 'any costs needed for quarantine or isolation of consignments' and 'any costs needed for destruction and disposal of consignments, when instructed by the authorities', ending with 'I am authorised as being accountable for these things if raising notifications on behalf of a third party.' and 'I can legally act on behalf of a third party in relation to the conditions of this declaration.'
requirements.why: It is the design's declaration, and the real page already says it word for word.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-008 and p7-012 to p7-020 give the heading and every statement word for word, and repo-tests-p3-002 asserts the heading.

requirements.statement: The live-animals declaration page shows no status strip and nothing above its 'Declaration' heading, for a draft and for an amendment alike.

requirements.statement: The live-animals declaration and confirmation pages, and plants' declaration (with and without its error), confirmation and the read-only view of a late notification, have no serious or critical accessibility violations.
requirements.why: Accessibility is a real constraint every page must meet.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p7-052 and p7-082, and repo-plantsfrontend-p11-023, p11-039 and p11-062 run axe on each page and find none.

requirements.statement: Every English string on the declaration and confirmation pages, in live animals and plants, has a Welsh counterpart under the same key, marked as an unreviewed machine draft.

requirements.statement: The prototype keeps a failed declaration's error in the session until a successful submit, so reopening the declaration still shows the error summary.
requirements.why: A prototype mechanism that exists because the prototype holds state in its session; the real service re-renders the error only on the refused post.

requirements.statement: How the declaration and confirmation tests are organised: the frontend's test-only route that replays the review post to reach the declaration, the tests repo's duplicated-in-frontend tags, and what the end-to-end suite leaves unasserted on the confirmation page.
requirements.why: Test support and test tagging, not behaviour a user sees; the programme's rows prove their own changes.

requirements.statement: On the Action needed, Status updated and Inspection required drill-downs, a submitted notification's status reads 'Submitted' as plain text and a notification being amended shows its Amend tag; no card shows an 'Action required' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 shows a submitted notification's status as text on the drill-downs and keeps a tag for Amend. These lists hold only submitted notifications, so a draft never appears on them and its tag is not built here. Sam's 16 November ruling withdraws the 'Action required' status and its tag, a submitted notification reads 'Submitted', and nothing action-required is shown until the outstanding-actions banner is designed (c-494).
requirements.deltaNote: The drill-downs do not exist today; the INS home's table shows each status as its raw code in a plain cell (trace-ins-fit-p4-025).
requirements.blockedBy: Sam's 9 October rulings block the INS dashboard's summary information (the overall home's per-category sections, counts and glance cards, the status-change cards and their drill-downs) until its requirements firm up and are agreed; the area is then re-distilled. The rulings do not say who firms them up or when.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the prototype's dashboard scripts that scroll the list tabs into view and clear the search.
requirements.why: The programme writes no custom JavaScript to copy the prototype, and no prototype test drives these scripts, so what they do is not shown; the drill-downs work as plain GET pages without them.

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's root renders the germinal products notification list in the same form the live animals list has today: the 'Dashboard' caption, a heading and introduction worded for germinal products, the start button, the keyword or reference search, the sort with its 'Update sort' button, the results count, the summary cards with their facts, status tags and status-driven actions, Previous and Next paging, the empty-list text and the deletion banner, with its start button starting a germinal products notification.
requirements.why: The 27 November ruling ships the germinal products set without waiting for the animals dashboard theme: its list, its cards and its delete message copy the live animals list as it is on main today (c-495). The wording names germinal products where the live animals list names live animals, because a germinal trader reads it.

requirements.statement: The 'Submitted' tab's subheading is followed by the description 'Notifications you have submitted. You can still change them and add documents.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader what the tab holds and what they can still do with it.

requirements.statement: The 'Draft and Amend' tab's subheading is followed by the description 'Notifications you have started but not submitted, and notifications that are being amended.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader the tab holds both unfinished drafts and notifications being amended.

requirements.statement: The 'Past' tab's subheading is followed by the description 'Notifications that have been processed. They move here 2 weeks after the commodity arrival date.', and the tab lists notifications by their completed status.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's copy for the tab; the prototype files a notification under 'Past' by its completed status and no code moves one there by date, so the description is shown as designed while membership follows the status (c-498).

requirements.statement: The live animals list's additional filters end with an 'Apply filters' button that submits the list's one search form, with the search, sort and every filter.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 closes the filter panel with its own submit button, so a trader who has chosen filters need not go back to the search button; it is a real submit button of the GET form (9 October afternoon ruling).

requirements.statement: When a status filter is set on the live animals list, the tabs are not shown and every notification matching the filters, from every tab, is listed under the h3 'Filtered results' with no description.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 drops the tabs while a status filter narrows the list, because the filter already says which notifications the trader wants.

requirements.statement: While a status filter is set and the search field is empty, the filtered results show a status line, announced to assistive technology, giving the number of matching notifications across every page: 'No notifications match your filters.', '1 notification matches your filters.' or '<n> notifications match your filters.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells the trader how many notifications their filters found, and says so when none match.

requirements.statement: The filtered results have a 'Clear filters' link that goes back to the list keeping only the tab and the sort, so the tabs come back.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 gives the trader one step back to the unfiltered list.

requirements.statement: The additional filters have a 'Needs action' checkbox, 'Only show notifications that need action', which keeps only notifications needing action.
requirements.why: Not built: the 16 November ruling shows nothing action-required until the outstanding-actions banner design is agreed, and a notification submitted with something outstanding is submitted like any other, so there is nothing for the checkbox to find (c-418).

requirements.statement: Where a card's links lead and what those pages show stay as managing notifications sets them: the review page a 'View' opens, the amendment a resumed card opens, and the copy and amend addresses the prototype works out for its notification hub.
requirements.why: Out of scope for the list: what each card action does belongs to managing notifications, which builds on its own branch (27 November ruling).

requirements.statement: The k6 journey script's steps beyond the notification list stay as they are: creating a draft and reading its id, the hub, the notification view, the declaration and confirmation, amend and cancel-amend, sign-in through the front door, returning visits, the backend fulfilments read and replay, and its traffic model and reporting.
requirements.why: Out of scope for the list: none of these steps reads the list, so the list's reframe changes nothing they request; any change to them belongs to the area whose pages they open.
requirements.deltaNote: Recorded from the performance tests repo as it is today.

requirements.statement: The address book list has a fourth tab, 'Branch', after 'Transporter', headed 'Branch addresses', listing the addresses holding the branch address role. Its Type filter offers 'Select one' and 'Branch Address', the Type column labels the role 'Branch', and the role reads 'Branch Address', after a divider, with the hint 'This is the contact address of the person responsible for the consignment from when it enters Great Britain until authorities complete their checks.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 draws a Branch category, and the rulings of 5 and 16 November describe a six-role vocabulary that includes the branch address; EUDPA-776 has since removed both the role and the tab from main with the consignment contact (c-499).
requirements.deltaNote: The list has no Branch tab and the address book refuses BRANCH_ADDRESS as an unknown role (repo-tests-p12-149, repo-tests-p12-161, repo-insfrontend-p4-025, repo-insfrontend-p4-085).

requirements.statement: When the view page is opened with an honoured return to a page outside the address book, such as the dashboard or a notification's journey page, it shows an inset under the heading reading 'You can only edit this address in the address book', and still shows the Edit and Delete buttons.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 tells a user who arrives from elsewhere that changes are made in the address book; the real service knows where the user came from by the honoured return.
requirements.deltaNote: The view page shows no inset; it already honours an INS return such as the dashboard for its Back link (repo-insfrontend-p6-015).

requirements.statement: The delete page shows an inset between its heading and the Address summary reading 'This will not remove the address from existing notifications.'
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's reassurance, and it is true of the real service: a notification holds its own copy of an address and a deleted address stays readable by id.
requirements.deltaNote: The delete page goes from its heading straight to the summary, with no inset (repo-insfrontend-p6-070, repo-insfrontend-p6-071).

requirements.statement: The prototype's side effects of editing a seeded address in the session: the list's Address column, Name column and delete page still showing the old lines or name, an edited address moving category by its first ticked use, an edited branch's Type reading 'Branch address', a transporter's type becoming 'Transporter', and the view page splitting a free-text address into fields.
requirements.why: They come from the prototype holding seeded addresses as free text and merging edits over them in the session; the real book stores each field and saves the whole record, so none of them can happen, and an address's category is decided by its roles (c-172).

requirements.statement: The prototype's /design-release-2.1 mount for the address book, its rewriting of an unversioned /address-book return, and its shared views across design releases.
requirements.why: A design prototype decides look and feel, never URL paths or code structure; the real address book keeps its own paths (ruling of 9 October).

requirements.statement: Outside prod, the address book removes addresses, tombstones included, a configured number of days after they were created, so test data does not build up: expiry is off unless both its days and its index switch are set, a zero, negative or blank setting stops the service starting, and two safeguards keep it off in prod. Updating or deleting an address keeps its expiry date, which is never returned on the wire, and transporters expire the same way.
requirements.why: Today's operational behaviour of the address book; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it, and it keeps the shared test organisations' books small enough to page.
requirements.deltaNote: ADDRESS_TTL_DAYS, ADDRESS_TTL_EXPIRY_ENABLED and ENVIRONMENT drive the expiry with two prod safeguards (repo-addressbook-p3-071 to repo-addressbook-p3-077), and expired records are removed by the TTL index (repo-addressbook-p3-081, repo-addressbook-p3-084).

requirements.statement: The address book list is served by one compound index on organisation, status and creation time with no collection scan, and the service reads with primaryPreferred and writes with majority concern, over TLS, with a bounded connection pool.
requirements.why: Today's storage behaviour behind the list; nothing in Design Release 2.1 changes it.
requirements.deltaNote: The org_status_created index serves the list and the Mongo client is configured this way (repo-addressbook-p3-088, repo-addressbook-p3-089, repo-addressbook-p3-093 to repo-addressbook-p3-095).

requirements.statement: The address book's API is held to its locked contract: camelCase JSON and query parameters, RFC 9457 problem responses with a traceId, the four address and transporter paths with their operations, parameters, enums and required lists, and a committed generated spec the build byte-checks against the live API; the build fails on any drift the compliance test compares.
requirements.why: Any change to the list, read or delete API in this programme must change the locked contract and its generated spec with it.
requirements.deltaNote: docs/openapi/api-contract.locked.yaml and ApiContractComplianceIT hold the contract (repo-addressbook-p5-001, repo-addressbook-p5-046 to repo-addressbook-p5-057), with Jackson set to camelCase (repo-addressbook-p5-070).

requirements.statement: The edit page shows the inset text 'Changing the address here will not affect existing notifications' under its heading, above the form.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 copy. It is true of the real service: a journey commits its own copy of a picked address, so editing the address book record leaves notifications that used it as they were.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the edit page shows no inset (repo-tests-p13-043 lists its heading, sections and fields only).

requirements.statement: One address is read with GET /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}, which answers 200 with every field of a live address, and 200 with deleted true for a soft-deleted one; an unknown id and another organisation's id both answer 404 with the not-found problem, so the service never confirms another organisation holds an id; a 404 is never a deletion signal, and outside prod it can also mean the address has expired.

requirements.statement: An address is soft-deleted with DELETE /organisation/{orgId}/addresses/{id}, which answers 204: the address is kept with status DELETED, drops out of the list and is still readable by id with deleted true; a repeat delete answers 204 and changes nothing; an unknown id or another organisation's address answers 404 and stays as it was; and a stale write can never bring a deleted address back.
requirements.why: Soft delete lets a consumer tell a deleted address from an unknown one; persistence and authorisation constraints the prototype cannot express.
