requirements.statement: The stray trailing comma after the country on the last address line of the prototype's template page is not reproduced.
requirements.why: A prototype defect from joining the postcode and country, not part of the design; the address lines read as the notification review shows them.

requirements.statement: The prototype's ways of fitting its seeded templates to its own pages are not built: matching a template's species names loosely against its commodity catalogue, mapping the seeds' certified-for wording onto its options, and copying a seeded template's one place of origin into every party with its last line read as the country.
requirements.why: These exist only because the seeded templates store labels and a single free-text address; a real template stores the notification's own answers in the notification's shape, so using one seeds each answer as it was saved (c-183, c-186).

requirements.statement: On the delete and amend confirmation pages, every word of a species' Latin name in the Commodity row is shown with a capital letter (for example 'Bison Bison').
requirements.why: The design re-cases the species names it shows; the reason is not visible, and the real service's species names come from its reference data as held, so nothing is built until the question is answered (c-510).

requirements.statement: In the germinal products set, the deletion success message on the set's notification list reads 'Notification has been deleted.'.
requirements.why: The germinal list copies the live animals list as it is on main, delete message included, while the germinal set's delete builds on what the manage notifications work lands, and that work changes the live animals message; which of the two the germinal list shows is open (c-511).

requirements.statement: The amend confirmation page identifies the notification being amended in a GOV.UK summary list with the rows 'Reference number', 'Commodity', 'Number' and 'Origin' (the country of origin), worked out from the saved notification, in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's amend confirmation shows the same rows as the delete confirmation, so the trader confirms they are amending the right notification (c-512).

requirements.statement: Below the summary the amend confirmation page says 'Confirm that you want to amend this notification.', in every set that amends.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1's confirmation wording for amending, matching the delete page's (c-512).

requirements.statement: The germinal products set's amend, cancel amendment, copy as new and delete are copies of the live animals features as the manage notifications work leaves them, with the germinal differences the requirements name.
requirements.why: The 27 November ruling builds the germinal set's actions on what the manage notifications work lands, because that work is in flight, and sends the design's later changes to that work rather than into germinal products; each germinal page is a copy of its live twin (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-p1-014).

requirements.statement: The cancel-amendment confirmation reads 'Cancel this amendment?' and 'Any changes you have made to this notification will not be saved.', with the summary rows and a back link to where the trader came from, and a GET to cancel amendment cancels at once.
requirements.why: Out of scope: that page belongs to the prototype's Testing 3 and Testing 4 rounds and is not reached in Design Release 2.1, whose cancel confirmation is the wording the cancel-amendment requirements give; a GET that changes state is not built, because every state change is a form post (c-189).

requirements.statement: Each notification holds a flag saying whether its answers differ from the answers it was submitted with, always yes or no, never empty: no on a new notification and on a record stored without it, worked out again on each content save during an amendment from the notification content alone (uploaded documents and the fulfilments payload never count, and an answer put back reads as unchanged), no for an amendment with no stored submitted version, and reset to no when the amendment is submitted or cancelled. The fulfilments view returns it, and it is not published on any notification event.
requirements.why: The view tells the trader whether an amendment has changed anything before they resubmit, and the owner's 19 November ruling makes the flag a non-null yes or no that the backend's shape owns and the frontend's stub copies.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-015 and p1-016 (answersDifferFromSubmitted, always true or false), p2-014 to p2-016 (worked out on each amendment save over the notification fields), p2-046 and p2-058 (reset on submit and cancel), p1-069 (the fulfilments view returns it) and p4-174 (not published in the GBN-AG body).

requirements.statement: A notification only ever moves between four statuses: DRAFT on create, SUBMITTED on submit or cancel amend, AMEND on amend and DELETED on soft delete. A DELETED notification cannot be saved, submitted, amended or copied, and a SUBMITTED notification's content cannot be saved until it is moved to AMEND.
requirements.why: Every page and every published event relies on the lifecycle moving only along these paths.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-125 (every status change the service makes), p2-126 and p2-127 (what DELETED and SUBMITTED refuse), and each operation's allowed statuses: p2-009 save, p2-027 copy, p2-042 submit, p2-050 amend, p2-056 cancel amend, p2-061 and p2-063 soft delete.

requirements.statement: Every trader notification route, and every document-uploads route bar the scan-result callbacks, scopes the record to the organisation named in the caller's Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header and refuses a request without a non-blank one with 400 and the detail 'Missing required header Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id'; a new notification belongs to the organisation in the header at creation, and the organisation recorded on an event and its actor is that organisation.
requirements.why: One organisation's traders see and change only that organisation's notifications.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p1-005, p1-089, p2-085, p2-086 and p2-088 (TraderOrganisationHeaderFilter and the stored organisation), p4-022 (the event's organisationId) and repo-tests-p9-126 (every call names the organisation).

requirements.statement: The PURPOSE clause publishes each reason for import as its purpose code: internalMarket as INTERNAL_MARKET, transhipmentOrOnwardTravel as TRANSHIPMENT_OR_ONWARD_TRAVEL, transit as TRANSIT, reEntry as RE_ENTRY and temporaryAdmissionHorses as TEMPORARY_ADMISSION.
requirements.why: PIMS reads the reason for import as a code from the GBN-AG purposes list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-093 to p4-097 (Clause's purpose codes).

requirements.statement: The INTERNAL_MARKET_PURPOSE clause publishes each purpose in the internal market as its code: transfer-of-ownership-sale-gift as TRANSFER_OF_OWNERSHIP_SALE_GIFT, transfer-of-ownership-rescue as TRANSFER_OF_OWNERSHIP_RESCUE, breeding as BREEDING, research as RESEARCH, racing-competition-show-or-training as RACING_COMPETITION_SHOW_OR_TRAINING, approved-premises-or-body as APPROVED_PREMISES_OR_BODY, companion-animal-not-for-resale-or-rehoming as COMPANION_ANIMAL_NOT_FOR_RESALE_OR_REHOMING, production as PRODUCTION, slaughter as SLAUGHTER, fattening as FATTENING and restocking as RESTOCKING.
requirements.why: PIMS reads the internal market purpose as a code from the GBN-AG internal market purposes list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-098 to p4-108 (Clause's internal market purpose codes).

requirements.statement: The GOODS_CERTIFIED_AS clause publishes each certified-for answer as its code: further-keeping as FURTHER_KEEPING, slaughter as SLAUGHTER, confined-establishment as CONFINED_ESTABLISHMENT, germinal-products as GERMINAL_PRODUCTS, registered-equine-animal as REGISTERED_EQUIDAE, travelling-circus-animal-act as TRAVELLING_CIRCUS_ANIMAL_ACT, exhibition as EXHIBITION, event-or-activity-near-borders as EVENT_OR_ACTIVITY_NEAR_BORDERS, release-into-the-wild as RELEASE_INTO_THE_WILD, dispatch-centre as DISPATCH_CENTRE, relaying-area-purification-centre as RELAYING_AREA_PURIFICATION_CENTRE, ornamental-aquaculture-establishment as ORNAMENTAL_AQUACULTURE_ESTABLISHMENT, technical-use as TECHNICAL_USE, quarantine-or-similar-establishment as QUARANTINE_OR_SIMILAR_ESTABLISHMENT, live-aquatic-animals-for-human-consumption as LIVE_AQUATIC_ANIMALS_FOR_HUMAN_CONSUMPTION and other as OTHER.
requirements.why: PIMS reads what the goods are certified as as a code from the GBN-AG goods-certified-as list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-109 to p4-124 (Clause's goods-certified-as codes).

requirements.statement: The rules of the copy, amend, cancel-amendment and soft-delete endpoints themselves (their tokens, refusals, documented responses and what they keep) are specified and proven by the manage-notifications area, not this one.
requirements.why: Out of scope for this area: amend, cancel-amend, copy and soft delete are manage-notifications' to own; this area keeps only the record, the statuses and the events they write.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p2-026, p2-028, p2-029, p2-049, p2-053, p2-055, p2-057, p2-065 and p2-128 record those endpoints today; the 25 November ruling moves the amend state change behind the amend confirmation page's confirm button, which changes the frontend and not the backend's amend.

requirements.statement: Reference-data's GET /countries answers 200 OK with a JSON array in which each country has a code (MDM's effectiveAlpha2, such as DE), a name (MDM's effectiveAlias, such as Germany) and a subDivisions list of code and name (such as ES-CN, Canary Islands); MDM's other country fields and each subdivision's blocs are not passed on, and a country with no subdivisions has an empty list.
requirements.why: The origin, transit, destination, transporter and address-book country lists all read this one shape, and a territory reaches callers as a subdivision of its parent country.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-004 to p1-012 give the shape and mapping; p1-052, p1-053 and p1-055 prove it (DE / Germany, Spain with ES-CN, Austria with an empty list).

requirements.statement: A subdivision MDM gives without a code is left out of its country's subdivisions, and the subdivisions that remain keep the order MDM gives them.
requirements.why: A subdivision without a code cannot be chosen or stored, and reference-data sorts only the countries themselves.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-010 drops subdivisions with no code; p1-073 shows subdivisions come back in MDM's order.

requirements.statement: The countries list runs A to Z by name and never holds the United Kingdom or its subdivisions, such as Northern Ireland, so the unfiltered list holds 249 of MDM's 250 country records.
requirements.why: Imports into Great Britain never come from the United Kingdom itself; the one frontend list that needs the United Kingdom (an address country) adds it itself.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-013 sorts by name and p1-014 drops GB and its subdivisions, proven by p1-051, p1-054 and p1-060. The stub's capture holds GB with no effectiveAlias and an unnamed GB-NIR subdivision (repo-stub-p5-085 to p5-091), which never reach callers.

requirements.statement: GET /countries takes one optional blocks value: when given, a country is listed only if MDM gives it a block of exactly that name marked includeCountry true, or gives it no blocks at all; when not given, every country but the United Kingdom is listed.
requirements.why: Each country list keeps the MDM block it uses today (GBNAG_SPS_EX where it is filtered), and a change of block is a content question for the list's owner.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-015 to p1-017 give the filter, and p1-060 and p1-061 prove it (Martinique dropped when its GBNAG_SPS_EX block says includeCountry false; nothing dropped with no blocks value).

requirements.statement: Reference-data asks MDM for countries at GET /mdm/geo/countries with system GBNAG and the caller's blocks value, and for ports at GET /mdm/trade/bcp/poes with system GBNAG, each call carrying the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header and a bearer token from the Trade Platform token endpoint that is reused until it expires.
requirements.why: This is the contract the real MDM through APIM and the stub both answer, so the lists are the same shape in every environment.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-020 to p1-023 give both calls, proven by p1-059 and p1-063; p3-035-m1 shows the token reused until its expiry.

requirements.statement: Reference-data's GET /ports-of-entry takes no query parameters and answers 200 OK with a JSON array in which each port has MDM's code and name and a type; MDM's port id is not passed on.
requirements.why: The port of entry and port of exit lists read this one shape, and the type is what orders the list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-027 to p1-030 give the endpoint, proven by p1-069 ({"code":"GB ABD","name":"Aberdeen Harbour","type":"seaport"}) and p1-064.

requirements.statement: Every port MDM returns for system GBNAG is in the ports list: the list is never narrowed by port type or by what a port may handle, and only the whole country and port lists are served, never a single country or port by its code.
requirements.why: MDM carries no approved-for-animals flag on a port, so no exit-only or commodity-only port list is built.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-039 and p1-072 show no filter between MDM's result and the response; p1-071 shows each controller has one root GET and no lookup by code.

requirements.statement: Every country, territory and port name in the lists is MDM's own, served unchanged: country names in MDM's ISO short-name style (such as 'United States of America (the)', 'Moldova (the Republic of)', 'Western Sahara*' and 'Curacao'), territories MDM holds both as a country's subdivision and as a country record of their own (such as Martinique and the Canary Islands), and port names with MDM's duplicates and misspellings (such as two 'Port of Sheerness', two 'Pembroke Port', 'Teestort', 'TILBURY' and 'Portsmouth  Port').
requirements.why: A reference list's content is MDM's, reaching the service through reference-data; where it differs from the design that is MDM's content to change, never a reason to edit a list in code or to block a row. The duplicate and misspelt ports are in real MDM and go to the MDM team.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-006 and p1-031 pass MDM's names through unchanged; repo-stub-p3-014 to p3-016, p5-116 to p5-119 show MDM's country spellings, p4-009-m1 and p5-111 the territories held twice, and p6-024 to p6-030 the duplicate and misspelt ports, all as MDM serves them.

requirements.statement: When MDM or the token endpoint cannot be reached, takes longer than 3 seconds to connect or to answer, answers 502, 503 or 504, or answers the countries or ports call with no body or no result list, reference-data answers 503 with the title 'Service Unavailable' and the detail 'Reference data is unavailable. Please try again later.'
requirements.why: A caller can tell a passing MDM outage from a fault, and the page that reads the list can show its own error rather than an empty list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-019, p1-040 and p1-041 treat a missing body or result as MDM unavailable, p3-024 to p3-026 and p3-028 answer it 503, and p3-038 sets the 3-second timeouts.

requirements.statement: When MDM returns no countries, GET /countries answers 200 OK with an empty list.
requirements.why: An empty list is a valid answer from MDM, unlike a missing body.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-018 answers an empty MDM result with an empty list, and p1-057 shows the next request asks MDM again.

requirements.statement: Every error reference-data answers itself is an RFC 7807 problem detail with a type, a title, a detail and, when the request has one, a traceId: 400 'Validation Error' or 'Bad Request' for a bad request, and 500 'Internal Server Error' with 'An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.' for any other MDM or token endpoint error and any unexpected fault, never the fault's own message.
requirements.why: Callers handle one error shape, and nothing internal leaks into an answer.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-020 to p3-023 and p3-030 give the problem details; p3-027 and p3-029 send other MDM and token errors to the 500 handler. p3-031 and p3-032 note the unreachable 404 and 409 handlers and Spring's own 404 for an unknown path, which stay as they are.

requirements.statement: Reference-data caches MDM's countries, separately for each blocks value, and MDM's ports for 60 minutes by default (CACHE_MDM_TTL_MINUTES), at most 20 entries each, never caches an empty or missing answer, and sorts and maps the cached lists on every request.
requirements.why: The lists change rarely, so callers are not held up by MDM, while a change in MDM reaches callers within the hour.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-042 to p1-048 give the caches, proven by p1-056, p1-058 and p1-070.

requirements.statement: Reference-data counts and times every countries and ports-of-entry request, logs MDM's trace id from the x-ms-middleware-request-id header when MDM sends one and warns when it does not, and exposes /health (with no details and no dependence on MDM), /metrics, /info and /cache.
requirements.why: Operators can follow a list request into MDM, and an MDM outage never restarts the service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-049 and p1-050 count lookups, p1-025 logs the trace id, and p3-042 and p3-042-m1 give the actuator endpoints.

requirements.statement: Reference-data is the one shared service for MDM-sourced reference lists: it serves countries, ports of entry and commodities from MDM and holds none of its own, serves no border control posts beyond ports of entry, owns no notification, address or user data, and records its decisions as ADRs under doc/adr/.
requirements.why: ADR 0002 keeps reference domains in one service until one grows large enough for its own, and MDM is the source of truth for every list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-013 to p3-018 give ADRs 0001 and 0002; p3-008 to p3-011 give what the service does and does not hold.

requirements.statement: The reference-data workspace page and ADR 0002 describe the service as it is: the ports list grouped by port type, the animals frontend's port list call, and ports of entry and commodities as domains it serves.
requirements.why: Out of scope: a documentation correction, not a behaviour or a page the design changes. The page says both lists are sorted by name while the README and the code group ports by type, the page leaves ports out of the animals frontend's calls, and ADR 0002 still lists ports and commodities as planned. It goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-012 shows the page saying both lists are sorted by name; p3-014 shows ADR 0002 not updated.

requirements.statement: Reference-data serves a transporter list, an accompanying document types list and a certification purposes list.
requirements.why: Out of scope: no source asks reference-data to serve these lists. Each organisation's transporters are its own records in the address book, a commercial transporter's country is set to Northern Ireland with no reference-data lookup, and an approved-transporters list managed in MDM is parked, so nothing asks reference-data for transporters; the document type and certification purpose options are fields V4 specifies, which their own areas carry.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-044 to p3-046 show no endpoint, model or MDM call for any of the three.

requirements.statement: Commodity search and the species check in reference-data match MDM's search behaviour: prefix and word-start matching, a page size from 1 to 100, and MDM's own punctuation.
requirements.why: Out of scope for this area: the commodity catalogue and commodity search wait until commodities come from MDM, and the commodities area carries the search contract. Recorded here because the reference-data contract page holds it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p3-040 and p3-012-m1 to m5 describe today's commodity search contract and MDM's behaviour.

requirements.statement: GET /countries lists a country MDM gives with no name rather than failing the whole request, and a port MDM gives with no name sorts after the named ports of its group.
requirements.why: Out of scope: no record MDM serves today triggers either case. The United Kingdom is the only country with no effectiveAlias and is dropped before the sort, and every port has a name. It is a latent fault in a service the programme does not otherwise change, so it goes to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-referencedata-p1-013-m1 shows a country with no effectiveAlias fails the sort; p1-037-m1 shows a nameless port sorts first in its group.

requirements.statement: The stub reads each saved MDM response once, when it starts, answers every call from that copy with the header x-ms-middleware-request-id: stub-trace-id, and fails to start, logging the file's name and 'Failed to read from json file: <file>', when a saved response is missing or unreadable.
requirements.why: Reference-data reads MDM's trace id header, and a broken fixture shows at start-up rather than as a wrong list.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-stub-p2-014 and p6-010 load once at start; p2-015 and p6-008 send the trace header; p2-018 and p2-031 give the read failure.

requirements.statement: The stub's README lists the two integrations it stands in for reference-data: trade-token, the Trade Platform OAuth token endpoint at POST /tenant/oauth2/v2.0/token, and mdm, 'MDM reference data through APIM: countries, border control posts and products', owned by the MDM / data platform team, with no added delay by default and interim SLA targets of p50 100 ms, p95 400 ms and p99 1,000 ms, each overridable.
requirements.why: Perf runs set the stub to the SLA latency, and the interim targets stand until the volumetrics page confirms MDM's latency.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-stub-p2-034 to p2-041 give the README's integration entries, latency profile and SLA defaults.

requirements.statement: The stub offers an error, empty or slow ports answer and inactive port records to test against, and its tests cover an invalid saved file, a block named in another letter case, the count of Port records, the order beyond the first record and the ignored system value.
requirements.why: Out of scope: no source asks for it. The stub mirrors MDM's real data, which holds no inactive port, and the goal changes no stub behaviour beyond the tidy-up. The gaps go to the report.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-stub-p6-035 and p6-036 show no inactive port and no failure answer; p2-032, p2-033 and p6-034 show the untested cases.

requirements.statement: The status strip above each journey page's heading shows the status tag and the reference prefixed with the notification type's label and a hyphen, for example 'Live animals - GBN-AG-26-7K8M2P' or 'Germinal products - GBN-AG-26-…'; with no known type, the reference shows on its own.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 labels the reference with the notification type so a trader can tell the sets apart; the prototype decides how the strip reads.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the strip holds only the status tag and the bare reference (repo-tests-p1-010, trace-e2e-p13-006, trace-e2e-p13-007).

requirements.statement: Starting a notification from a set's own list creates the draft and opens its first page, origin of the import, without asking the notification type question again.
requirements.why: The set's list already says what is being imported, so Design Release 2.1 skips the type question there.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p13-003: 'Start a new notification' creates the notification, mints its reference and redirects straight to its origin page.

requirements.statement: A live animals notification's opening run, from its origin page, takes Save and continue through the pages in this order, skipping any whose question does not apply to the consignment: Origin of the import, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Identification details, Additional details, Arrival details, Transit countries, Transport details, Upload documents and Consignment addresses.
requirements.why: This is the question order the target design walks in every live animals journey, and the order the real service already walks; both frontends' suites and the tests repo hold the journey to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-121 and repo-tests-p8-157: Save and continue already carries a new notification from the origin page through these pages in this order, and repo-frontend-p3-123 checks each landing by its slug and heading.

requirements.statement: Starting a germinal products notification opens its Origin of the import page straight away, with no notification type question, and the notification is labelled Germinal products from that page onward.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's accessibility suite holds every scanned page, animals and INS alike, to WCAG 2.2 AA. Every test carries the @a11y tag and is reported under that standard, read from the fixture so the title and the rule set cannot drift apart, and every scan passes the five axe tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa explicitly, because axe's own default leaves target-size out. A scan runs with axe's legacy mode off, so cross-origin iframes are scanned, and may be narrowed or widened per page with include, exclude and disabled rules. A scan waits for the DOM and then allows a bounded settling period, scanning anyway if that wait times out; it is recorded against the page's path; a test runs every one of its scans before failing and reports them together with each violation's severity, rule, description, node count, help link and first target, attaching them to the report as JSON; a failing scan fails its test and a test that takes the scan but never runs one fails too. The suite proves its own scanner on a real service page: with an unnamed button and two adjacent eight-pixel links injected, the scan reports button-name and target-size, and a test expected to fail is never retried. A test is allowed five minutes, and the accessibility runs use the same two configs as every other test type. Pages whose layout matters at small sizes are scanned again at 320 by 568, the reflow width, and at 568 by 320, for orientation and the reflow height, set for the whole test, and a narrow scan also proves the page does not scroll sideways once its tables are discounted, taking the same scan options as any other scan. A clean scan is not full conformance, and a state earns its own scan only where its value outweighs the set-up it needs.
requirements.why: Every page that changes must keep passing this suite, and a new scan has to be written to these rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p10-001 to p10-022 and p15-058 to p15-086-m2 define the suite and its narrow-viewport scans, and p10-142 to p10-144 with p15-080 and p15-081 prove the scanner catches a real fault.

requirements.statement: An accessibility scan leaves out only markup whose finding is an upstream disagreement in code the service does not own, and only the elements that carry it, never a page or a rule as a whole: the origin page's region-of-origin-code radio and the import reason page's radios that open a conditional reveal, because govuk-frontend sets aria-expanded on such a radio and axe's aria-allowed-attr rule rejects it; the accompanying documents page's file upload button, in every state of that page and at both narrow viewports, because axe's label-content-name-mismatch rule joins the button's status text and its Choose file text without a space while the browser's accessible name contains the visible text and so meets Label in Name; and, on the INS sign-in page with an error, the sign-in stub's own error list. The file upload button exclusion is deleted once a release of axe or govuk-frontend no longer reports the finding. The three journey exclusions are kept in one shared module, which the accessibility documentation names, and no INS scan uses them.
requirements.why: Every page this work changes keeps being scanned whole apart from these elements, and a new exclusion has to meet the same bar.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's accessibility proof stand as they are. On the animals side no scan covers the permanent address page, four of the five party pickers, four of the five party edit pages, the sign-in page or the organisation picker, or the hand-off from a party picker to the address book's add-address page, and the narrow-viewport scan of the notification list does not check for sideways scrolling; the journey has no contact address page left to scan. On the INS side the empty dashboard, the empty address book and the address book's load-failure state are deliberately left unscanned, and the notification type page and every transporter page go unscanned.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suites, not differences from the target design, so the programme does not close them. They go to the report. The germinal products set's missing scans are not among them: a separate requirement places its accessibility specs in the animals project.

requirements.statement: The tests repo's security suite is a traffic-driven OWASP ZAP scan of six services, each its own named ZAP context with its own address from its own setting: the animals frontend, the animals admin, the INS frontend, the animals backend, the plants backend and the address book. Playwright drives real signed-in journeys through the proxy rather than letting ZAP crawl, so coverage is traffic-driven and the attacking corpus is curated by hand; the three APIs are scanned because every API client inherits the run's proxy. There are two profiles: a passive one that runs the end-to-end suite without the attacking specs and is safe against a deployed environment, and an attacking one that runs only the @active corpus, runs on the compose stack and in a weekday scheduled GitHub Action whose password-protected report is pruned after seven days, and is refused on the deployed platform because its journeys delete records the scan then re-fires with fuzzed payloads. Anything but the exact attacking profile name is treated as passive. Identifiers in a page or API address are declared to ZAP as data rather than structure, from a context plan registered before any traffic exists; all three plans must declare the same contexts; diagnostics are excluded rather than scanned; the DOM cross-site-scripting rule is off; the sign-in stub is observed but never attacked while the service's own sign-in handlers are in scope; and the uploader and the queue-consuming INS backend are out of scope with their reasons. A run fails on a FAIL-rated alert from the rules file (an unlisted alert failing only if it is high risk, and no alert ignored today), on a plan error or a plan running past five hours, on a scan that finished at or within half a minute of its 60-minute cap, or, in the attacking profile, on a declared context that saw no traffic; a per-domain run gates only that domain's contexts and is labelled scoped, the full run being the authoritative clean bill of health, and an unknown domain is refused by name. ZAP listens on a loopback port outside the workspace's port ranges with a local default key, runs as a container beside the stack locally and as an in-process daemon pointed at each per-service subdomain on the deployed platform, using the same plans and gate. Each run clears its report folder but never removes it, writes a landing page before failing with a row per site, its request count and alert counts and notices for a cut-short, partial or scoped run, publishes ZAP's log and machine-readable report as HTML with the whole Playwright report beside it, and never runs the gate against a spec run that failed or refused to start.
requirements.why: Every route that is added or changed must be driven through this scan to be attacked, and a new spec has to be written to these rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p11-037 to p11-102, p15-094 to p15-115 and p16-106 to p16-134 define the suite, its profiles, its contexts and its failure conditions; p16-144 to p16-148 give how a deployed run starts ZAP itself and publishes its report.

requirements.statement: The attacking corpus drives through the proxy: the animals sign-in round trip with a refused user and a sign-out, from a cold start; a whole submitted live-animals journey to its confirmation; the reason-gated pages for Transit and Temporary admission of horses with additional details saved and returned from the overview, and a private transporter typed by hand; amend and copy as new, then cancel amendment and delete; a document upload waited through its scan and then opened; a draft validation error on the origin page; the notification list's search, paging and sorting; the review page's Change trail; the INS address book's whole record lifecycle with a role-filtered tab and the dashboard opened at the end; the add page's cross-service hand-off parameters, of which only the refused side is proven; and the INS sign-in round trip, which holds the suite's only check that the INS front door renders its 'Log out' link.
requirements.why: A page or route that changes keeps being attacked only while a spec in this corpus still drives it, so a change to any of these journeys updates the spec that drives it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p11-087 to p11-095 and p11-112 to p11-115 give the animals and INS attacking specs, p15-098 to p15-106 and p16-125 to p16-127 the INS ones in detail.

requirements.statement: Gaps in today's security scan stand as they are. No attacking spec drives the high-risk plants journey, so the plants backend is a declared context that nothing reaches and a full attacking run cannot pass the no-traffic gate as things stand; only a per-domain run avoids it. No transporter route is driven through the proxy. Only the refused side of the address book's cross-service hand-off is in scope, because no accepted token can be seeded.
requirements.why: These are coverage gaps in today's suite, not differences from the target design, so the programme does not close them. They go to the report.

requirements.statement: The tests repo signs each worker in once per domain and its tests restore that session, the saved state holding only the auth cookie and never written until a fresh context has proved it restores to a signed-in landing page; sign-in waits for the landing page or the sign-in failure page before deciding to try again. A spec that must start unauthenticated opts out with a cold-start state, a spec that needs the same user in a new session carries only the auth cookie into a new context, and session reuse can be switched off, which caps the deployed run's workers. Reuse was proved against one deployed environment by a probe that mints one session and reuses it across twenty fresh contexts, refuses to run against production, and is to be re-run before relying on reuse elsewhere. The suite signs in as two stub identities mirroring the sign-in stub's data, a default single-organisation user and a second user with two organisations for organisation choice; the password comes from the environment with a local stub default and is never written into a trace, the sign-in fixtures have their own longer timeout, and no spec wipes the database because every spec creates the state it asserts on.
requirements.why: Any new end-to-end proof of sign-in or navigation has to work within these existing suite rules.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p16-053 to p16-059 give the session rules, p16-163 to p16-167 the identities and password handling, p16-034 the sign-in retry and p16-093 that nothing is wiped.

requirements.statement: Every page of every frontend shows the refreshed GOV.UK brand the design uses: the current GOV.UK header, logo and colours that GOV.UK Frontend applies by default.
requirements.why: The design is built on the rebranded GOV.UK Frontend styles, and look and feel follows the design.
requirements.deltaNote: Each frontend builds its chrome from GOV.UK Frontend components (repo-frontend-p2-124, repo-plantsfrontend-p13-095, repo-insfrontend-p1-143), on a release that applies the refreshed brand by default, where the prototype has to switch it on (prototype-dr2-1-source-p1-101). No today claim records the brand itself, so the first increment that touches the layout confirms it on a rendered page.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's content security policy lets its forms post to the journey frontends and to the browser-facing Defra ID origin, so a hand-over from INS to a journey can pass through sign-in.
requirements.why: The type question and the address book hand the trader to the animals or plants frontend, and a hand-over that the browser refuses to post never arrives.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-166 sets the form-action sources.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend takes the address of every service it calls or sends the browser to from its environment configuration: the address book, reference data, the INS backend, the animals frontend and the plants frontend, with no hard-coded host or port. Each outbound connection waits up to one second per address before trying the next, as the animals and plants frontends do.
requirements.why: Links and calls between services have to work in the local Docker stack, the CI Docker stack and CDP alike, which only configuration per environment can give.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-165 names the five settings and p1-169 the connection wait; the owner keeps every hand-over on each service's own configuration (ruling-sam-2026-11-27-p1-014).

requirements.statement: On the INS frontend a list page reads its page number from the address, treating a missing, non-numeric or below-1 value as page 1 and a page beyond the last as the last page. A results line gives the range shown and the total, and is left out when there are no items. A list of one page or fewer shows no pagination; otherwise Previous shows except on the first page and Next except on the last, with the first page, the pages either side of the current one, the current page and the last page numbered, the current page marked and an ellipsis wherever numbers are skipped. The helper sets no page size: each list passes its own.
requirements.why: The INS address book pages, and the owner keeps pagination on every list of an organisation's addresses.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-insfrontend-p1-115 to p1-121 give the INS list-page rules as they stand; each list's own page size is weighed where that list is weighed.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's hidden Defra ID test pages are not changed by this programme: the sign-in page with its 'Sign in with Defra ID' start button, the signed-in page listing the ID token's and access token's claims and the token response, and the signed-out page. They are English-only internal pages linked from nowhere in the service, served only when the Defra ID discovery settings are configured and discovery succeeds, and they never change the service's own signed-in identity.
requirements.why: These are internal diagnostic pages for checking the real Defra ID in CDP dev, not pages a trader sees, so the design has nothing to say about them.

requirements.statement: The INS frontend's temporary address lookup spike, a page served only in the dev and local environments that searches by postcode or free text through the INS backend and saves nothing, is not changed by this programme, and neither are the gaps it shows between the lookup's results and the address form.
requirements.why: Address search waits until the INS address lookup is a real feature, and until then every add-address page offers manual entry only.

requirements.statement: Pages after the commodity page opening with no commodity chosen, because a missing-commodity guard never redirects.
requirements.why: The prototype's missing-commodity guard is a stub that always lets the trader through: a mechanism of the prototype, not a designed behaviour. Which pages a set's journey guards, and what each guard needs, is the real journey's own architecture, which the prototype never decides, so nothing is built from it.

requirements.statement: The animals frontend's own private and commercial transporter details pages, signed off at maturity agreed, and the fit test data that adds a Northern Ireland commercial haulier and a French private transporter through them.
requirements.why: Out of scope for arrival and transit: this area stops at the transporter pages. The 6 November transporter ruling moves adding a transporter to the address book hand-off, so these signed-off pages and their test data go with that move, which the transporters area carries (req-2264) through the signed-off check.
requirements.deltaNote: Today both pages carry maturity agreed (repo-frontend-p13-003) and the fit test-support adds the two sample transporters (repo-frontend-p13-116).

requirements.statement: In live animals each of the five parties (place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination) is chosen on its own picker page, reached from that party's add link on the consignment addresses page, or from its Change link once an address is chosen. Each picker lists only the organisation's addresses offered for that party's role, together with any address that carries no role yet, in the address book's own order, which paging keeps; an address the same-as button copied onto the consignor from the place of origin is not listed on the consignor picker unless its record also carries the consignor role, while the consignor section still shows it.
requirements.why: A trader picks each party from the addresses their organisation saved for that role, so a picker never offers an address meant for a different part of the consignment.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: five picker pages at <party>/select, each reading the address book under its own role (repo-frontend-p15-001, repo-frontend-p15-002, repo-frontend-p15-004), reached from the add and Change links (repo-frontend-p15-006, repo-frontend-p15-080), listing only the role's addresses plus role-less ones (repo-frontend-p15-078) in the book's order (repo-frontend-p15-079), and leaving a same-as copy off the consignor list (repo-frontend-p15-086). The consignment parties area carries the same behaviour as req-608 and req-612.

requirements.statement: Each live animals party picker shows the caption 'Addresses' above its heading naming the party, and the party's hint as a paragraph under the heading: Place of origin 'The address where the animals begin their journey to Great Britain'; Consignor 'This is the sender of the consignment.'; Consignee 'This is the receiver or buyer of the consignment being shipped or transported.'; Importer 'This is usually the same as the consignee. You can select a different person if needed.'; Place of destination 'This is where the animals will be unloaded and accommodated for at least 48 hours. If a health certificate is required, it will show this address.'
requirements.why: The picker repeats the section's own wording, so the trader knows which party they are choosing and what it means.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with this caption and these five hints (repo-frontend-p15-007, repo-frontend-p15-010 to repo-frontend-p15-014, repo-frontend-p15-161). The germinal products set's own place of origin and place of destination hints are req-2720 and req-2721.

requirements.statement: Each live animals party picker's Back link returns to the consignment addresses page, carrying the trail the trader arrived on.
requirements.why: The picker is a step out of the consignment addresses page, so Back takes the trader to where they came from.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-015).

requirements.statement: Each live animals party picker has a search box labelled 'Search' with the hint 'Name, address or country', joined to a search button whose accessible name is 'Search'. Submitting it, by the button or by pressing Enter, narrows the list on the server with no JavaScript needed, opens the first page of matches and keeps the term in the box, also when nothing matches; searching with the box cleared lists the party's whole list again from its first page; a search saves nothing and keeps the address already chosen, still named above the results.
requirements.why: A trader with many saved addresses needs to find one quickly, and the search must work without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: the labelled box and hint with its joined button (repo-frontend-p15-017, repo-frontend-p15-018), the server search that works without JavaScript and keeps the term (repo-frontend-p15-019, repo-frontend-p15-020, repo-frontend-p15-081, repo-frontend-p15-165), the cleared search (repo-frontend-p15-082) and a search keeping the choice (repo-frontend-p15-053-m1).

requirements.statement: Below the search box each live animals party picker heads its results 'Select an address' as a level-two heading, which also names the radio group as its visually hidden legend, with 'Showing <shown> out of <total> results' straight under it.
requirements.why: The heading and count tell the trader what the list is and how much of it they are seeing, and the legend makes the radios one choice to a screen reader.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-021, repo-frontend-p15-022, repo-frontend-p15-024-m1, repo-frontend-p15-084).

requirements.statement: Each live animals party picker lists its addresses in a table with a visually hidden 'Select' column, then 'Name', 'Address' and 'Country'. The address cell leaves out any blank part, with no empty line and no stray comma, so a Danish consignor reads 'Havnegade 21' then 'Copenhagen, 1058'; the country column shows the country's name, not its code. Each row's control is a small GOV.UK radio, all sharing one name so only one address can be chosen, whose value is the record's id and whose visually hidden label reads 'Select <name>'; the first radio's id lets an error summary link reach it.
requirements.why: The trader compares addresses by name, address and country and picks exactly one, and every row must be announced clearly to a screen reader.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-025, repo-frontend-p15-028 to repo-frontend-p15-033).

requirements.statement: Each live animals party picker shows eight addresses a page, with GOV.UK pagination only when its addresses run past one page: 'Previous' and 'Next' links, the first page, the pages either side of the current one, the current page marked as current, and the last page, with an ellipsis wherever the numbers skip. Every page link carries the search term, the page, the chosen address and the trail the trader arrived on. A picker always has at least one page, even with no addresses; a page number that is not a whole number of one or more serves the first page, and one past the last page serves the last, each logged. The picker offers no sort and no choice of page size.
requirements.why: Organisations can hold many addresses for one role, and eight a page is the figure the INS address book list already uses over the same records.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: eight a page with the GOV.UK pagination and its links (repo-frontend-p15-038 to repo-frontend-p15-049, repo-frontend-p15-083, repo-frontend-p15-156, repo-frontend-p15-157), and no sort or page-size control (repo-frontend-p15-144). The consignment parties area carries the same behaviour as req-594.

requirements.statement: When a live animals party picker holds a chosen address, including one reopened from the party's Change link, it names it in an inset reading 'Selected address: <name>' between the search box and the results heading and ticks its radio when its row is on the page shown. The choice is carried in a hidden field and in the page links, so it stays named while the trader pages away from its row and a save made from another page still saves it; the page the trader is on is carried too, so a refused save shows the same page of results again.
requirements.why: With the list split across pages, the trader must still see which address they chose and must not lose it by paging or searching.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-050 to repo-frontend-p15-054). The consignment parties area carries the same behaviour as req-595 and req-602.

requirements.statement: Outside an amendment, each live animals party picker ends with a single 'Save and continue' button and offers no 'Save and return to overview' control.
requirements.why: The picker is a step inside the consignment addresses task, whose own page carries the return to the overview.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-061). The consignment parties area carries the same ending as req-605.

requirements.statement: Saving a live animals party picker with an address ticked records it on the notification and returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, carrying the trail. Saving with nothing ticked, after a search that matched nothing as well, saves nothing, shows no error or prompt and returns the trader to the consignment addresses page, where the party still offers only its add link.
requirements.why: A party may be left blank while the notification is a draft; completeness shows in the task status and is checked at submission.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-062, repo-frontend-p15-064, repo-frontend-p15-065, repo-frontend-p15-162). The consignment parties area carries the same behaviour as req-603 and req-606.

requirements.statement: Saving a live animals party picker with an address that is not in the organisation's book, or not offered for the party's role, saves nothing and shows the picker again with status 400, no radio ticked and the search term kept, with the party's own message: 'Select a place of origin from the list', 'Select a consignor from the list', 'Select a consignee from the list', 'Select an importer from the list' or 'Select a place of destination from the list'. The message is in an error summary whose link moves focus to the first radio, or to the search box when nothing is listed, and is repeated above the results with a visually hidden 'Error:' prefix, the results group marked as in error and described by it; when nothing is listed it sits under 'No addresses match your search.' in a form group marked as in error.
requirements.why: A choice the trader's organisation cannot use for that party must never be saved, and the refusal follows the GOV.UK error pattern.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today with these five messages and this error pattern (repo-frontend-p15-066 to repo-frontend-p15-075, repo-frontend-p15-073-m1, repo-frontend-p15-163, repo-frontend-p15-164). The consignment parties area carries the same refusal as req-604.

requirements.statement: A live animals party picker save the service cannot store shows the picker again with status 500, marked as a recoverable error, with the chosen address still ticked.
requirements.why: A brief backend failure must not lose the trader's choice.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-076). The consignment parties area carries the same behaviour as req-607.

requirements.statement: Each animals party picker, in both animals sets, refuses a save made after the notification changed since the picker was shown, and sends the trader back to the same picker to see the current answer, as the party edit page does.
requirements.why: A real persistence constraint the prototype cannot express: a save from a second tab or a slow connection must not silently write over an answer another save already stored, and the picker should behave as the edit page beside it does.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the picker form carries the crumb and the concurrency token (repo-frontend-p15-170, recorded in req-2298), but its routes are declared by hand with a bare POST handler, so a stale save does not get the redirect back to the page that the party edit page gets (repo-frontend-p15-151-m2). The germinal products pickers are copies of the live animals ones (req-1827).

requirements.statement: A live animals party picker offers no control to clear a chosen address: it has no 'none of these' option and no remove control.
requirements.why: The picker chooses one address; clearing a party is done from the consignment addresses page.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-143). The Remove button on the consignment addresses page is req-2300 and req-2715.

requirements.statement: A live animals party picker saved with nothing ticked is logged as an outcome naming the journey and the party, and a refused save is logged as a refusal naming the party and the address id that was refused.
requirements.why: Operators can see how often traders leave a party blank and which addresses are refused, without reading the notification.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-166, repo-frontend-p15-167).

requirements.statement: The live animals consignment addresses page and every live animals party picker have no serious or critical accessibility violations: the page empty, complete and with the same-as buttons showing, at desktop and phone width; the picker empty, after a search, with no matches and after a refused save.
requirements.why: The service must meet WCAG 2.2 AA under the public sector accessibility regulations.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today by the frontend's own checks (repo-frontend-p15-085, repo-frontend-p15-095). The consignment parties area carries the same quality as req-620.

requirements.statement: Every piece of wording on the live animals consignment addresses page and its party pickers, and on the high-risk plants frontend's place of destination page, has a Welsh counterpart; the animals addresses feature's Welsh is marked as a machine draft not yet reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Every page must be ready for Welsh, and an unreviewed machine draft must be flagged until a translator signs it off.
requirements.deltaNote: Present today in both frontends (repo-frontend-p15-141, repo-plantsfrontend-p8-129). The consignment parties area carries the same as req-619.

requirements.statement: The live animals party pickers and party edit pages show the same maturity as the consignment addresses page they belong to.
requirements.why: The pickers and edit pages are part of the addresses task, so they are marked at the same stage of readiness.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today: both take their maturity from the addresses page (repo-frontend-p15-160).

requirements.statement: The live animals consignment addresses page shows its intro and one headed section per party, each with the party's hint and a named add link, and ends with 'Save and continue'; its Back link returns to the overview.
requirements.why: The page gathers every party of the consignment in one place, each with its own way in.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-087, repo-frontend-p15-088). Today the page also shows the fraud warning, which the consignment parties area moves to the place of destination picker (req-558).

requirements.statement: A chosen party shows on the live animals consignment addresses page as its name in bold, its address lines, and a last line joining the town or city, county, postcode and country with commas, leaving out any blank part, with a 'Change' link and an 'Edit details' link, each naming the party to a screen reader.
requirements.why: The trader sees the copy the notification holds and can replace it or correct it from the section.
requirements.deltaNote: Built today (repo-frontend-p15-090, repo-frontend-p15-171). The consignment parties area carries the same as req-571 and req-572.

requirements.statement: Choosing an address for every party marks the consignment addresses task Complete on the overview, for a consignment that is asked for no CPH number and no permanent address.
requirements.why: The task status tells the trader the addresses are done.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p15-089). How the CPH number and the permanent address count towards the status is req-584.

requirements.statement: With JavaScript turned off, the live animals consignment addresses page shows its sections, an add link opens the party's picker, and the same-as button fills the consignor from the place of origin.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p15-092).

requirements.statement: A live animals consignment of poultry is asked for a county parish holding number on the consignment addresses page, with the section's hint and add link, and a saved number shows in its slashed form, such as 12/345/6789, with a 'Change' link; a consignment of horses or of ostriches is not asked for one.
requirements.why: The CPH number applies only to the animals that need it.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p15-093). The CPH section's wording and rules are req-573 and req-574, and its Remove button req-2716.

requirements.statement: The live animals consignment addresses page shows a permanent address section for a cat consignment and none for a cattle consignment.
requirements.why: A permanent address applies only to animals that need one.
requirements.deltaNote: Proven today (repo-frontend-p15-094). The section's wording and content are req-575 and req-2719.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the prototype's page path for the permanent address page behind 'Add a permanent address'.
requirements.why: The prototype decides look and feel, never URL paths; the target keeps its own routes, and the permanent address page is built in its own area.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: one part of the tests repo exercising no party edit form.
requirements.why: A hole in one part's evidence that needs nothing built: the party edit form is proven by other parts of the tests repo and the frontend's own checks (req-681 to req-693). Recorded so the claim is weighed, and the gap goes to the report.

requirements.statement: The contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets shows the notification's 'Draft' tag and reference above the heading, as the other journey pages do.
requirements.why: The trader always sees which notification they are changing, as on the CPH number and permanent address pages (req-704).
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: The contact address form in the live-animals and germinal-products sets posts back to its own URL with a CSRF crumb and the notification's concurrency token, and every save of the page, an unchanged choice included, is counted as a save of the notification.
requirements.why: The real service's persistence and concurrency constraints, which the prototype cannot express, apply to every journey form, as they do on the CPH number and permanent address forms (req-723).
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: The contact address page in the live-animals and germinal-products sets has no WCAG 2 A/AA axe violations, clean and in its error state: the radios group's accessible description names the page's hint and, on error, the error message after it, the group takes the GOV.UK error style on error, and each radio is described by its own one-line address hint.
requirements.why: The service must be accessible; the prototype does not test this.
requirements.deltaNote: On the animals frontend's main the contact address page, its edit route and the notification's contact party have been removed (EUDPA-776), so none of this exists today. The row is built only if the contact address question is answered so that the live-animals journey asks for a contact address again.

requirements.statement: The notification records a responsible person for the load, made up of the person's name, telephone number and email address and their organisation's name, address and telephone number, taken at notification level from the signed-in user's identity rather than entered by the trader, in both the live-animals and germinal-products sets.
requirements.why: Out of scope, as req-2190 already records for the same field: no page in this area asks for it, shows it or checks it, because it is consumed on authentication, and two of its six values, the organisation's address and telephone number, would need Defra ID to serve them, which is not one of the programme's repos. The Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields page gives it no type and no mandatory marking (N/A). The cross-area pass folds this into req-2190.
requirements.deltaNote: No today source in this area's working set shows what the notification records from the signed-in user's identity.

requirements.statement: Out of scope: the prototype's dashboard date formatter that rewrites ISO timestamps and arrival-style dates into the declaration date format, shows 'Not applicable' when empty and passes unreadable text through.
requirements.why: It is prototype mechanism for its own demo data: Design Release 2.1's notification card does not use it, and the real drill-down cards reuse the category list's own card, whose date format belongs to the notification list's requirements.

requirements.statement: The notification dashboard has a secondary 'Use template' button beside the primary 'Create new' button, which opens Manage templates.
requirements.why: Not built in this programme: templates are parked, treated as concept work and dropped for now, so neither the INS home nor the live animals and germinal products lists offer a way into them. The home button is already settled out of scope by c-416 (req-964) and the list button by c-420 (req-1038); this records the same button as the templates journeys' own traces and specs show it, so the cross-area pass may fold it into req-1038. The /templates path is the prototype's architecture, not a requirement. It is built only when templates are picked up again and this area is re-distilled.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area that describe another page's own content are weighed in that page's own area rather than here: the notification view page's header, Actions menu, dates, Import reference numbers section and Copy buttons, answer cards, read-only and draft states, error summaries and Back link (review and submit); the Make template action (templates); the phase banner (layout); the port of entry search (arrival); the outstanding items on the notification submitted page and the stale declaration (declaration and submitted); the hub's Review and submit button (notification hub); and the list's reference search (notification list).
requirements.why: This area covers the actions on an existing notification and stops at the review page itself and at the notification list. These claims arrived with the manage notifications traces and specs, but each describes a page another area owns and builds; weighing them twice would write duplicate requirements.

requirements.statement: What the design's traces and specs for these actions do not show is recorded, not built: Make template being followed from a notification, the import reference Copy buttons being used, the action-required Continue or a draft's Continue being pressed, how the list and view show a notification after an amendment is resubmitted, what delete and make template do with an unknown or missing reference, and the seeded port the amend review happens to show.
requirements.why: A gap in the design's evidence decides nothing on its own: the actions' behaviour is set by the requirements that cite what the design and today's services do show (resubmitting, the guards, delete), and seeded demo data is not a specification.
